words.en: If you enquire about something, you ask for information about it.

words.ex: He wrote a memorandum about the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一份关于会议的备忘录。
words.en: A memorandum is a written proposal or reminder, especially in a business context.

words.ex: The table has a rectangular shape.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是矩形的。
words.en: Something that is rectangular has the shape of a rectangle.

words.ex: He drank water to help his kidney work better.
words.ex_cn: 他喝水以帮助肾脏更好地工作。
words.en: One of the two organs in your lower back that separate waste products from your blood and make urine.

words.ex: From my standpoint, this plan is too risky.
words.ex_cn: 从我的立场来看，这个计划太冒险了。
words.en: A standpoint is a particular way of considering something, or a particular attitude towards it.

words.ex: The curative treatment helped him recover quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种医疗治疗帮助他迅速康复。
words.en: Curative means having the ability to cure or heal, especially of a disease or medical condition.

words.tr: phrase. 第一印象；初次见面时留下的印象
words.ex: His first impression was that she was very kind.
words.ex_cn: 他的第一印象是她非常善良。
words.en: The initial opinion or feeling that you have about someone or something when you first see or meet them.

words.tr: phrase. 作为介绍；作为开场白
words.ex: He spoke briefly by way of introduction.
words.ex_cn: 他简短地讲了几句作为介绍。

words.tr: phrase. 小型车；紧凑型汽车
words.ex: He bought a compact car to save fuel.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆小型车来节省燃油。

words.tr: phrase. 精炼的叙述；简洁的叙事
words.ex: The movie has a compact narration that tells the whole story in 10 minutes.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影有着精炼的叙述，能在10分钟内讲完整个故事。

words.ex: The compactness of the apartment makes it perfect for one person.
words.ex_cn: 这个公寓的小而紧凑让它非常适合一个人住。
words.en: The quality of being closely and neatly packed together; the state of being concise.

words.ex: The forest is dense with trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林树木茂密。
words.en: Something that is dense contains a lot of things or people in a small area.

words.ex: Soil compaction is a major concern in agriculture.
words.ex_cn: 土壤压实是农业中的一个主要问题。
words.en: Compaction is the process of making something more dense or compact, often by applying pressure.

words.ex: The police opened an enquiry into the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方对这起事故展开了调查。
words.en: An enquiry is a question you ask in order to get some information.

words.ex: The box has a rectangle shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是长方形的。
words.en: A rectangle is a four-sided flat shape where every interior angle is a right angle (90°). Opposite sides are parallel and of equal length.

words.tr: v. 趟水；涉水；艰苦地进行
words.ex: He wades through the shallow river.
words.ex_cn: 他涉水走过浅河。
words.en: To walk through water or another liquid or soft substance that impedes movement.

words.tr: phrase. 帝国大厦（位于美国纽约市的著名摩天大楼）
words.ex: The Empire State Building is an iconic symbol of New York City.
words.ex_cn: 帝国大厦是纽约市的标志性象征。
words.en: A 102-story Art Deco skyscraper in Midtown Manhattan, New York City, completed in 1931, known as a symbol of the city and a popular tourist attraction.

words.tr: v. （从水、泥等）蹚，走过，跋( wade的现在分词 )
words.ex: He is wading through the shallow river.
words.ex_cn: 他正在涉过浅河。
words.en: Walking through water or another liquid, typically with difficulty.

words.ex: The city is predominantly populated by young people.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市主要由年轻人居住。
words.en: If something is predominantly true, it is true to a much greater extent than it is false.

words.tr:
v. 抓住；攫住
n. 紧抓；离合器；一窝雏；一小群；紧要关头
words.ex: He clutched the rope tightly when he slipped.
words.ex_cn: 当他滑倒时，他紧紧抓住了绳子。
words.en: To clutch something means to hold it tightly, usually because you are afraid or anxious. In a vehicle, the clutch is a pedal that you press with your foot to change gears.

words.ex: She combines flour and water to make dough.
words.ex_cn: 她把面粉和水混合在一起做面团。
words.en: To combine means to join or merge two or more things together to form a single entity.

words.ex: The teacher showed a chart of temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 老师展示了一张温度图表。
words.en: A chart is a graphical representation of data, in which the data is represented by symbols, such as bars in a bar chart, lines in a line chart, or slices in a pie chart.

words.ex: He has asthma and cannot run fast.
words.ex_cn: 他有哮喘，不能跑快。
words.en: A respiratory condition marked by spasms in the bronchi of the lungs, causing difficulty in breathing. It usually results from an allergic reaction or other forms of hypersensitivity.

words.ex: He signed his name with a clear signature.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的签名签了名字。
words.en: A signature is a person's name written in a distinctive way as a form of identification in authorizing a document or letter.

words.ex: She wore a dress for the occasion.
words.ex_cn: 她为了这个特殊场合穿了一条裙子。
words.en: An occasion is a particular time when something happens, or a special event.

words.tr: adj. 无价的；非常宝贵的；
words.ex: Her advice was invaluable to me.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对我而言是无价的。
words.en: If you describe something as invaluable, you mean that it is extremely useful.

words.tr: v. 恢复；重新获得；复原；
words.ex: He will recover from the illness soon.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就会从疾病中恢复。
words.en: If you recover from an illness or an injury, you become well again. If you recover something that has been lost or stolen, you find it or get it back.

words.ex: The dominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间占优势的颜色是蓝色。
words.en: Someone or something that is dominant is more powerful, successful, influential, or noticeable than other people or things.

words.ex: The predominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的主导颜色是蓝色。
words.en: If something is predominant, it is more important, noticeable, or powerful than the other things in a situation.

words.tr: adj. 引人注目的；显著的； v. 打击；“strike”的现在分词；
words.ex: The painting has a striking color scheme.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有着引人注目的配色。
words.en: Something that is striking is very noticeable or unusual.

words.ex: The salient point in the report is the cost increase.
words.ex_cn: 报告中最显著的要点是成本上升。
words.en: The most noticeable or important.

words.ex: He dominates the conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他主宰了谈话。
words.en: To dominate means to control or govern someone or something, or to be the most important or noticeable feature of something.

words.ex: They live in a quiet suburb outside the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在城市外一个安静的市郊。
words.en: A suburb is a residential district located on the outskirts of a city.

words.ex: They live on the outskirts of the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在城市的郊区。
words.en: The outskirts of a city or town are the parts of it that are farthest away from its center.

words.tr: phrase. 将 a 与 b 结合；把 a 和 b 混合在一起
words.ex: You can combine A with B to create a new product.
words.ex_cn: 你可以将A与B结合，创造出一种新产品。
words.en: To join or merge two or more things together.

words.ex: The lock uses a simple combination of three numbers.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁使用三个数字的简单组合。
words.en: A combination is a mixture of things or people that are combined.

words.ex: The bar chart shows the number of students in each class.
words.ex_cn: 条形图显示了每个班级的学生人数。
words.en: A bar chart is a type of chart that presents categorical data with rectangular bars with heights or lengths proportional to the values that they represent.

words.ex: He drew a flow chart to show the steps.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一个流程图来展示步骤。
words.en: A flow chart is a diagram that represents a process or algorithm, showing the steps as boxes of various kinds, and their order by connecting them with arrows.

words.tr:
v. 潦草地写；匆匆地写；乱涂乱画
n. 潦草的字迹；涂鸦
words.ex: He scribbled his name on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上潦草地写了名字。
words.en: To scribble means to write or draw something quickly or carelessly.

words.ex: They rejoice when the sun comes out.
words.ex_cn: 当太阳出来时，他们欢呼。
words.en: To feel or show great joy or delight.

words.ex: The children were rejoicing after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在赢得比赛后很高兴。
words.en: Rejoicing is the expression of great happiness or joy, often because something very good has happened.

words.ex: The old toy is worthless now.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧玩具现在毫无价值。
words.en: If something is worthless, it has no use or value.

words.tr: adj. 无价值的；不值钱的；微不足道的
words.ex: The old toy is valueless now.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧玩具现在没有价值。
words.en: Having no value; worthless.

words.ex: The painting is priceless.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是无价的。
words.en: If you say that something is priceless, you are emphasizing that it is worth a very large amount of money, or that it is very important to you and you could not replace it.

words.tr: adj. 有价值的；贵重的；值钱的；
words.ex: This old book is valuable to historians.
words.ex_cn: 这本旧书对历史学家来说很有价值。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as valuable, you mean that they are very useful and helpful.

words.ex: This broken phone is useless.
words.ex_cn: 这部坏掉的手机毫无用处。
words.en: If something is useless, it is not able to do what it is supposed to do or is not effective.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.tr: phrase. 恢复镇定；重新控制自己
words.ex: After the loud noise, he took a deep breath and recovered himself.
words.ex_cn: 在巨大的噪音之后，他深吸一口气，恢复了镇定。

words.ex: He will recover from the flu next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周会从流感中康复。
words.en: To recover from something means to return to a normal state of health, mind, or strength after experiencing an illness, injury, or emotional distress.

words.ex: He needs time for recovery after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他手术后需要时间恢复。
words.en: The process of becoming well again after an illness or injury, or the process of returning to a normal condition after a period of difficulty.

words.ex: He eats sweets with moderation.
words.ex_cn: 他吃甜食很适度。
words.en: Moderation is the quality of doing something within reasonable limits; not too much or too little.

words.ex: He submitted the documentation for his project.
words.ex_cn: 他提交了项目的文件。
words.en: Documentation refers to the act of providing documents or the documents themselves, which serve as evidence or records of something.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；批判性的；关键的；危急的；临界的；
words.ex: Water is critical for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you are critical of someone or something, you show that you disapprove of them. In a critical situation, things are very serious and dangerous. A critical time or event is extremely important because it will affect future events.

words.ex: He is learning vocational skills to become a mechanic.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习职业技能以成为一名机械师。
words.en: Relating to the skills you need to do a particular job.

words.ex: He gave a summary of the story at the end.
words.ex_cn: 他在结尾对故事做了总结。
words.en: A summary is a brief statement or account of the main points of something.

words.ex: Please remove the trash from the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 请把厨房的垃圾去掉。
words.en: To take something or someone away from a place or off a surface.

words.tr: adj. 一定会；密切相关的；有义务的； v. “bind”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is bound to win the race.
words.ex_cn: 他一定会赢得比赛。
words.en: If one person, thing, or situation is bound to another, they are closely connected with each other, and it is difficult for them to be separated or to escape from each other. If you say that something is bound to happen, you mean that you are sure it will happen, because it is a natural consequence of something that is already known or exists.

words.tr: n. 小装饰品；廉价首饰
words.ex: She bought a small trinket at the market.
words.ex_cn: 她在市场上买了一个小饰物。
words.en: A trinket is a small ornament or item of jewelry that is of little value.

words.ex: My passport will expire next month.
words.ex_cn: 我的护照下个月到期。
words.en: If something such as a contract or a visa expires, it comes to an end or is no longer valid.

words.ex: He ate a moderate amount of food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了适量的食物。
words.en: If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent, or if you moderate a discussion, you help the people in it to reach an agreement.

words.ex: Eat sweets in moderation.
words.ex_cn: 适量吃甜食。
words.en: In amounts that are not excessive.

words.tr:
n. 纪录片；
adj. 文书的；
words.ex: We watched a documentary about pandas last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚看了一部关于熊猫的纪录片。
words.en: A documentary is a film or television or radio programme that gives factual information about a particular subject.

words.tr:
n. 文件；公文；文献；
v. 记录；为…提供证明；
words.ex: He submitted the document to the office.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件提交给了办公室。
words.en: A document is a piece of text or graphics, for example a letter, that is stored as a file on a computer and that you can access in order to read it or change it.

words.tr: phrase. 对某事持批评态度的；对某事挑剔的
phrase. 极其重要；至关重要
words.ex: Water is of critical importance for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: To be extremely important or essential.

words.ex: Critical thought helps us solve problems wisely.
words.ex_cn: 批判性思维帮助我们明智地解决问题。

words.ex: The water reached a critical point and started to boil.
words.ex_cn: 水达到了临界点，开始沸腾。
words.en: A critical point is a moment or stage at which the quality, state, or condition of something changes significantly, especially for the worse.

words.tr: phrase. 关键期；临界期（指在发展过程中对特定刺激或经验特别敏感的时期）
words.ex: Children learn language best during the critical period.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在关键期学习语言效果最好。
words.en: A critical period is a specific time during an organism's development when it is particularly sensitive to certain environmental stimuli, and certain abilities or characteristics are most easily acquired.

words.tr: adj. 不加辨别的；不加批判的
words.ex: He accepted the news uncritical.
words.ex_cn: 他毫不质疑地接受了这个消息。
words.en: If you describe someone as uncritical, you mean that they do not judge whether someone or something is good or bad, right or wrong, before supporting or believing them.

words.tr: adv. 严重地；批评地；危急地；
words.ex: The patient is critically ill.
words.ex_cn: 病人病情严重。
words.en: In a way that involves the objective analysis and judgment of the merits and faults of a work of literature, music, or art.

words.tr:
n. 研究所；学院；协会；
v. 建立；制定；
words.ex: He works at a research institute.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家研究所工作。
words.en: An institute is an organization set up to do a particular type of work, especially research or teaching. It can also refer to the act of starting something such as a system or an official process.

words.ex: In summary, he likes apples and oranges.
words.ex_cn: 总之，他喜欢苹果和橙子。
words.en: used to introduce a short statement of the main points of something.

words.ex: Can you summarise the story in one sentence?
words.ex_cn: 你能用一句话总结这个故事吗？
words.en: If you summarise something, you give a summary of it.

words.tr: n. 概括; 摘要，概要
words.ex: He wrote a summarization of the book in one page.
words.ex_cn: 他用一页纸写了一个这本书的摘要。
words.en: The act of making a summary or the process of summarizing.

words.tr: phrase. 与某事相去甚远；与某事毫无关联

words.ex: Salt is soluble in water.
words.ex_cn: 盐可以溶于水。
words.en: A substance that is soluble can be dissolved in a liquid.

words.ex: He uses a nail remover to take off polish.
words.ex_cn: 他用指甲卸甲液来去掉指甲油。
words.en: A substance or device used to remove something, such as a stain or a piece of furniture.

words.ex: The bounds of the rectangle are 5 cm and 10 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个矩形的边长是5厘米和10厘米。
words.en: 1. Limits or borders. 2. To leap or spring.

words.tr:
n. 租契；
v. 出租；
words.ex: He signed a lease for the apartment.
words.ex_cn: 他签了公寓的租契。
words.en: A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.

words.ex: The expiry of the contract will be next month.
words.ex_cn: 合同的满期将在下个月。
words.en: The end of the period for which something is valid.

words.tr: phrase. 用完；耗尽；跑出去；到期
words.ex: We run out of milk every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 我们每星期天都把牛奶喝光了。
words.en: If you run out of something, you have no more of it left.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.tr: adj. 易接近的；可使用的；简单易懂的；可进入的；
words.ex: The park is accessible by bus.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园乘公交车可达。
words.en: If a place or building is accessible to people, it is easy for them to reach it or get into it. If an object is accessible, it is easy to reach.

words.ex: The wind turbine spins to make electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风力涡轮机旋转以发电。
words.en: A turbine is a machine or engine which uses a stream of air, gas, water, or steam to turn a wheel and produce power.

words.ex: He is the backbone of the team.
words.ex_cn: 他是团队的中坚。
words.en: The backbone is the most important part of something, providing support and strength.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: The magnitude of this decision will affect everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定的重要性会影响每个人。
words.en: Magnitude refers to the great size or extent of something, or the importance of something.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.tr: n. 企业家；创业者；承包人；
words.ex: He is an entrepreneur who started a small coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位创办了小型咖啡店的企业家。
words.en: An entrepreneur is a person who organizes and operates a business or businesses, taking on greater than normal financial risks in order to do so.

words.ex: He made a proposal to improve the school lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了一个改善学校午餐的提案。
words.en: A proposal is a plan or suggestion, especially a formal one that is put forward for people to think about and decide upon.

words.tr:
n. 教练；长途客运汽车；
v. 训练；培训；
words.ex: The coach taught the team how to win.
words.ex_cn: 教练教球队如何获胜。
words.en: A coach is someone who trains a person or team in a particular sport. It also refers to a large, comfortable bus that carries passengers on long journeys.

words.tr:
n. 流浪汉；流浪乞丐；徒步旅行
v. 步行；踩；踏
words.ex: The old tramp slept on the park bench.
words.ex_cn: 那个老流浪汉睡在公园的长椅上。
words.en: If you tramp somewhere, you walk there slowly and with regular, heavy steps, especially for a long time.

words.ex: The lab is ultraclean to prevent contamination.
words.ex_cn: 实验室非常洁净，以防止污染。
words.en: Extremely clean; free from dirt, impurities, or pollutants.

words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。

words.tr: phrase. 将……归因于；把……归咎于

words.ex: They ascribe his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他们把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you ascribe an event or condition to a particular cause, you say or consider that it was caused by that thing.

words.ex: The quality of this phone is very high.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机的质量很高。
words.en: The standard of something as measured against other things of a similar kind; the degree of excellence of something.

words.ex: They stargaze on clear nights in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 他们在晴朗的夜晚在乡下观星。

words.tr: n. 天文爱好者；耽于幻想的人
words.ex: The stargazer looks at the stars every night.
words.ex_cn: 观星者每天晚上都看星星。
words.en: A stargazer is someone who observes the stars or someone who is always dreaming and not paying attention to what is happening around them.

words.ex: The comet shines brightly in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 彗星在夜空中明亮地闪耀。
words.en: A comet is a celestial object consisting of a nucleus of ice and dust and, when near the sun, a 'tail' of gas and dust particles pointing away from the sun.

words.tr: phrase. 能共存的；兼容的；能和睦相处的
words.ex_cn: 这台打印机与我的笔记本电脑兼容。
words.en: able to exist or occur together without conflict; able to be used together.

words.ex: This small enterprise makes handmade toys.
words.ex_cn: 这家小企业生产手工玩具。
words.en: An enterprise is a company or business, often a large one, or a difficult or important project, especially one that involves a lot of planning and organization.

words.ex: The corporation sells smartphones worldwide.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司向全球销售智能手机。
words.en: A corporation is a large company or group of companies that is controlled together as a single organization.

words.ex: The incorporation of new ideas improved the plan.
words.ex_cn: 新想法的结合改进了这个计划。
words.en: Incorporation is the process or result of forming a legal corporation, or the inclusion of something as part of a whole.

words.ex: He works for a small company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小公司工作。
words.en: A company is a business organization that makes money by producing or selling goods or services.

words.ex: He propose to go to the park after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他提议午饭后去公园。
words.en: If you propose something, you suggest it as a plan or course of action.

words.ex: The accident was fatal.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是致命的。
words.en: If an action or event is fatal, it causes someone's death.

words.ex: The currency in Japan is the yen.
words.ex_cn: 日本的货币是日元。
words.en: The system of money in general use in a particular country.

words.tr: v. 不赞成；反对；不同意
words.ex: My parents disapprove of my choice.
words.ex_cn: 我的父母不赞成我的选择。
words.en: If you disapprove of something, you have a negative opinion of it, often because you think it is wrong or not suitable.

words.ex: He complains about the loud noise every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都抱怨噪音太大。
words.en: To express dissatisfaction, pain, or resentment, usually because of a particular situation or someone's actions.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；鲁莽的；大胆创新的
words.ex: He made an audacious plan to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个大胆的计划，独自攀登那座山。
words.en: If you describe someone as audacious, you mean that they take risks in order to achieve something and show a willingness to challenge conventional ideas.

words.ex: The storm disrupted the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴中断了火车服务。
words.en: To disrupt a system, process, or event means to prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.ex: The price of bread went up because of inflation.
words.ex_cn: 由于通货膨胀，面包的价格上涨了。
words.en: Inflation is a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.

words.tr: 短语. 享受当下；珍惜现在
words.ex: We should enjoy the present and not worry about the future.
words.ex_cn: 我们应该享受当下，不要担心未来。
words.en: To appreciate and take pleasure in the current time.

words.ex: She learns to enjoy present moment by walking in the park.
words.ex_cn: 她通过在公园散步来享受当下时刻。

words.tr:
adj. 目前的；在场的；
n. 目前；礼物；
v. 呈现；提出；
words.ex: The present situation is very difficult.
words.ex_cn: 目前的形势非常困难。
words.en: If you say that someone is present at an event, you mean that they are there.

words.ex: His presence made everyone feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 他的存在让每个人都感到平静。
words.en: The state or fact of existing, occurring, or being present in a place or thing.

words.ex: A fatal accident happened on the highway yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天高速公路上发生了一场致命的事故。

words.ex: The car depreciates every year.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车每年都会贬值。
words.en: If something such as a currency depreciates or if something depreciates it, it loses some of its original value.

words.ex: He paid with paper currency instead of coins.
words.ex_cn: 他用纸币支付，而不是硬币。

words.ex: He complains about the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 他抱怨那噪音太大。
words.en: If you complain about a situation, you say that you are not satisfied with it.

words.tr: phrase. 大胆的精神；无畏的气魄
words.ex: The child showed an audacious spirit by climbing the tall tree.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子爬高树时表现出大胆的精神。

words.ex: The storm caused a disruption in the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴扰乱了火车服务。
words.en: Disruption is a situation in which something is prevented from continuing in its usual way because of problems or difficulties.

words.tr: adj. 破坏性的；引起混乱的；
words.ex: The new technology caused disruptive changes in the market.
words.ex_cn: 这项新技术给市场带来了破坏性的变化。
words.en: Causing or tending to cause disruption.

words.ex: The storm was destructive and broke many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴具有破坏性，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: Causing great and irreparable harm or damage.

words.ex: The company will reinstate his job next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将恢复他的工作。
words.en: If you reinstate someone, you give them back a job or position which had been taken away from them.

words.ex: He will restore the old bike.
words.ex_cn: 他将修复这辆旧自行车。
words.en: To restore something means to bring it back to its original condition or to a state of health, efficiency, or good management.

words.ex: He reverted to his old habits after the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 假期后，他恢复了旧习惯。
words.en: To return to a former state, practice, topic, etc.

words.ex: He tries to invert the numbers to find the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图将数字倒过来以找到答案。
words.en: To invert something means to turn it upside down or to reverse its position, order, or relationship.

words.ex: The company made a statement about the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 公司就新政策发布了一项声明。
words.en: A statement is something that you say or write which gives information in a formal or definite way.

words.tr:
n. 数量；数额；
v. 总计；等于；
words.ex: The amount of water in the bottle is small.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子里的水量很少。
words.en: An amount of something is how much there is of it, or how much you have, need, or get.

words.tr: v. 给予；发出；“give”的过去式；
words.ex: She gave me a book.
words.ex_cn: 她给了我一本书。
words.en: Past tense of give, which means to freely transfer the possession of something to someone.

words.ex: Given that it is raining, we will stay inside.
words.ex_cn: 鉴于正在下雨，我们会待在室内。
words.en: You use given that to introduce a fact or situation that you are taking into account when making a statement.

words.tr: adj. 先进的；高级的； v. 提前；前进；“advance”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This school uses advanced technology in classrooms.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校在教室里使用先进的技术。
words.en: An advanced system, method, or design is modern and has been developed from an earlier version of the same thing.

words.ex: Graduating from high school was a big milestone for him.
words.ex_cn: 从高中毕业对他来说是一个重要的事件。
words.en: A milestone is a significant event or stage in the development of something.

words.tr:
n. 曲柄；怪人；脾气坏的人
v. 用曲柄转动
adj. 古怪的；易怒的
words.ex: He turns the crank to start the old engine.
words.ex_cn: 他转动曲柄来启动旧引擎。
words.en: A crank is a device for transmitting rotary motion, consisting of a handle or arm attached at right angles to a shaft. It can also refer to a person who holds unorthodox opinions or behaves in an eccentric manner.

words.ex: The town holds a music festival every summer.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇每年夏天都举办音乐节。
words.en: A festival is an organized series of events such as musical concerts or drama productions, often happening annually in the same place.

words.ex: The king will instate a new prime minister next week.
words.ex_cn: 国王下周将任命一位新的首相。
words.en: To instate someone in a position or job means to formally establish them in that position or job.

words.ex: The boss appointed Tom as the new manager.
words.ex_cn: 老板任命汤姆为新经理。
words.en: If you appoint someone to a job or official position, you formally choose them for it.

words.ex: He contradicts what she said.
words.ex_cn: 他反驳了她的话。
words.en: If you contradict someone, you say that what they have just said is wrong, or you suggest that it is wrong by saying something different.

words.tr: 短语，表示“……的数量；……的总量”
words.ex: He drank a small amount of water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一点水。
words.en: The quantity of something, especially the total of a thing or things in number, size, value, or extent.

words.ex: The savings amount to $500.
words.ex_cn: 这些储蓄加起来是500美元。
words.en: If something amounts to a particular total, all the parts of it add up to that total. If an idea, feeling, or action amounts to something, it has the same effect or importance as that thing.

words.tr:
adj. 特指的；特殊的；挑剔的；
n. 细节；详情；
words.ex: He wants a particular book, not any other.
words.ex_cn: 他想要一本特指的书，不是别的。
words.en: You use particular to emphasize that you are talking about one thing or one kind of thing rather than other similar ones.

words.ex: The amazonian bird sings loudly in the rainforest.
words.ex_cn: 这只亚马逊鸟在雨林中大声歌唱。
words.en: Relating to the Amazon River or the Amazon rainforest; resembling or characteristic of an Amazon, especially in being strong and aggressive.

words.ex: He is a lexicographer who writes dictionaries.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位编写词典的词典编纂者。
words.en: A lexicographer is a person who writes, compiles, or edits dictionaries.

words.tr: n. 一束；一串；一群；大量
words.ex: A bunch of birds flew over the tree.
words.ex_cn: 一群鸟飞过树顶。
words.en: A bunch of things is a group of them. A bunch of people is a group of them who are together or who are connected in some way.

words.ex: He wore a funny costume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为派对穿了一套滑稽的服装。
words.en: A costume is a set of clothes in a style typical of a particular country or historical period, or a set of clothes worn by an actor for a particular role.

words.ex: The loud noise scared the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音吓到了孩子。
words.en: If something scares you, it frightens or worries you.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.tr:
adj. 青少年的；幼稚的；
n. 少年；
words.ex: The book is written for juvenile readers.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是为青少年读者撰写的。
words.en: A juvenile is a child or young person who is not yet old enough to be considered an adult.

words.ex: The rainbow is a natural phenomenon.
words.ex_cn: 彩虹是一种自然现象。
words.en: A phenomenon is something that is observed to happen or exist, especially something that is unusual or interesting.

words.ex: The freight train carried boxes to the city.
words.ex_cn: 货运列车把箱子运到了城市。
words.en: Freight refers to goods transported in bulk by truck, train, ship, or aircraft. It can also mean the charge for such transportation.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.ex: He works in lexicography at a dictionary company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家词典公司从事词典编纂工作。
words.en: Lexicography is the activity or profession of writing dictionaries.

words.ex: He checked the lexicographical order of the words.
words.ex_cn: 他检查了这些单词的词典顺序。
words.en: Relating to the compilation or study of dictionaries and word lists.

words.ex: He gave her a bunch of flowers.
words.ex_cn: 他送给她一束花。
words.en: A large number or quantity of something.

words.tr:
n. 诱饵；（诱捕鸟兽的）动物
v. 引诱
words.ex: The hunter used a decoy to attract ducks.
words.ex_cn: 猎人用假鸭子来吸引鸭子。
words.en: A decoy is a person, thing, or action that is used to trick someone into doing something or going somewhere, especially by making them think they are going to get something they want.

words.ex: The burglar broke into the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 窃贼在夜里闯入了房子。
words.en: A burglar is a person who illegally enters buildings and steals things.

words.ex: The bandit stole money from the bank.
words.ex_cn: 强盗从银行偷了钱。
words.en: A bandit is a person who robs people, especially one of a group of people who attack travelers.

words.ex: The hijacker forced the pilot to change course.
words.ex_cn: 劫机者强迫飞行员改变航线。
words.en: A hijacker is a person who illegally takes control of a vehicle, especially an airplane, by force, often in order to reach a particular destination or to demand something.

words.tr:
v. 处理；操纵；
n. 把手；柄；
words.ex: He can handle difficult problems easily.
words.ex_cn: 他能轻松处理难题。
words.en: To deal with or control a situation or problem.

words.tr:
n. 索具装备；钻探设备；装备
v. 配备索具；操纵；舞弊
words.ex: He uses a rig to hold the camera steady.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个支架来固定相机。
words.en: To rig something means to arrange or set it up in a particular way, often in a temporary or makeshift manner. It can also refer to the equipment used in drilling for oil or gas, or the sails and ropes on a ship.

words.ex: He shifted the gear to slow down the car.
words.ex_cn: 他换挡以减慢车速。
words.en: Gear refers to a toothed wheel that works with others to alter the relation between the speed of a driving mechanism (such as the engine of a vehicle) and the speed of the driven parts (the wheels). It can also mean equipment that is used for a particular purpose.

words.tr:
n. 精巧动作；军事演习；花招
v. （熟练地）移动；操控；算计
words.ex: The dancer's maneuver was breathtaking.
words.ex_cn: 舞者的精巧动作令人叹为观止。
words.en: A maneuver is a movement or series of movements requiring skill and care.

words.tr:
v. 移动；操控；
n. （熟练地）移动；
words.ex: He manoeuvred the car into a small parking space.
words.ex_cn: 他把车开进了一个小停车位。
words.en: A manoeuvre is a movement or series of movements requiring skill and care, especially in military tactics or in driving a vehicle. It can also refer to a clever or cunning plan or action designed to turn a situation to one's own advantage.

words.ex: The coach changed his tactic to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 教练改变了战术以赢得比赛。
words.en: A tactic is a method or plan chosen to bring about a desired future, such as achieving a goal or solving a problem.

words.ex: The team made a smart strategy to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队制定了一项聪明的策略来赢得比赛。
words.en: A strategy is a plan that you use in order to achieve something.

words.ex: His childish laugh made everyone smile.
words.ex_cn: 他孩子气的笑声让每个人都笑了。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially an adult, as childish, you disapprove of them because they behave in an immature way.

words.ex: He is still immature and often cries when upset.
words.ex_cn: 他仍然不成熟，生气时经常哭。
words.en: If you describe someone as immature, you are criticizing them because they do not behave in a sensible or responsible way, or because they have not developed emotionally or mentally to the level that is normal for their age.

words.ex: The youngster rode his bike to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个年轻人每天骑自行车去上学。
words.en: A youngster is a young person, especially a child or teenager.

words.tr: n. （十三到十九岁的）青少年
words.ex: The teenager walks to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个青少年每天步行上学。
words.en: A teenager is someone who is between thirteen and nineteen years old.

words.tr: phrase. 易受……影响的；对……脆弱的；易遭受……伤害的
phrase. 弱势群体；易受伤害的群体
words.ex: Children are a vulnerable group in society.
words.ex_cn: 儿童是社会中的弱势群体。
words.en: A vulnerable group refers to a group of people who are more susceptible to harm, exploitation, or discrimination due to factors such as age, disability, or socioeconomic status.

words.ex: The system has a vulnerability that hackers can exploit.
words.ex_cn: 这个系统有一个黑客可以利用的脆弱性。
words.en: The state of being exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally.

words.tr: adv. 脆弱地；易受伤害地
words.ex: He spoke vulnerably about his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他坦诚地谈到了自己的恐惧。
words.en: In a manner that is susceptible to being hurt, attacked, or criticized; in a fragile way.

words.tr: adj. 可攻击的；有隙可乘的
words.ex: The old wall is assailable by strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 这堵旧墙容易被强风摧毁。
words.en: If something is assailable, it is capable of being attacked or criticized.

words.ex: He is strong enough to lift the box.
words.ex_cn: 他很强壮，足以举起这个箱子。
words.en: Someone who is strong is healthy with good muscles and can move or carry heavy things, or do hard physical work.

words.tr: adj. 艰苦的；强硬的；严厉的；
words.ex: The hike was tough but beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 这次徒步旅行很艰苦但很美丽。
words.en: A tough person is strong and determined, and can tolerate difficulty or suffering.

words.tr: v. 攻击；困扰；抨击；袭击
words.ex: The storm assailed the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴袭击了这个小村庄。
words.en: If someone assails you, they attack you violently, either physically or with words.

words.ex: The police investigated the assault on the old man.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了对那位老人的攻击。
words.en: An assault is a physical attack on someone, or a military attack on a place.

words.ex: The resilient child bounced back quickly after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这个适应力强的孩子在事故后很快恢复了。
words.en: Something that is resilient is strong and not easily damaged by being hit, stretched, or squeezed.

words.ex: The kettle produces steam when the water boils.
words.ex_cn: 水烧开时，水壶会产生蒸汽。
words.en: Steam is the hot mist that forms when water boils. It can be used to power machines or to cook food.

words.tr: adj. 有价值的；贵重的；值钱的；
words.ex: This old book is valuable to historians.
words.ex_cn: 这本旧书对历史学家来说很有价值。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as valuable, you mean that they are very useful and helpful.

words.ex: He is presumably at home now.
words.ex_cn: 推测起来，他现在在家。
words.en: If you say that something is presumably the case, you mean that you think it is very likely to be the case, although you are not certain.

words.tr: n. 避难所；庇护所；庇护；
words.ex: The birds found sanctuary in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟在森林里找到了避难所。
words.en: A sanctuary is a place where people or animals are protected from danger or trouble.

words.tr:
n. 请求；要求的事；
v. 要求；请求；
words.ex: He made a request for help.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了一个帮助的请求。
words.en: If you request something, you ask for it politely or formally.

words.ex: Add a dash of salt to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 给汤里加一点盐。
words.en: If you dash somewhere, you run or go there quickly and suddenly. A dash is a straight, horizontal line used in writing, for example to separate two main clauses whose meanings are closely connected.

words.ex: The doctor gave him proper treatment for the infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他提供了针对感染的适当治疗。
words.en: The act or manner of treating someone or something, especially in a medical context.

words.ex: The sandpaper feels coarse to the touch.
words.ex_cn: 这张砂纸摸起来很粗糙。
words.en: Coarse things have a rough texture because they consist of thick threads or large pieces.

words.tr: adj. 不安全的；无保障的；缺乏自信的；无把握的
words.ex: He feels insecure when he is alone at night.
words.ex_cn: 当他晚上一个人时，他感到不安全。
words.en: If you are insecure, you lack confidence because you think that you are not good enough or are not loved.

words.ex: Rock contains many minerals.
words.ex_cn: 岩石中含有许多矿物。
words.en: A mineral is a solid substance that occurs naturally and has a specific chemical composition and structure.

words.ex: The steam engine moved the train on old tracks.
words.ex_cn: 蒸汽机车在旧轨道上行驶。
words.en: A steam engine is a heat engine that performs mechanical work using steam as its working fluid.

words.tr: adj. 无价的；非常宝贵的；
words.ex: Her advice was invaluable to me.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对我而言是无价的。
words.en: If you describe something as invaluable, you mean that it is extremely useful.

words.tr: phrase. 贵重物品；有价值的财产
words.ex: She kept her valuable belongings in a safe box.
words.ex_cn: 她把贵重物品放在保险箱里。

words.ex: I presume he will arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假设他明天会到。
words.en: If you presume that something is the case, you think that it is the case, although you are not certain.

words.ex: I assume it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假定明天会下雨。
words.en: If you assume that something is true, you accept that it is true without proof.

words.ex: The bird sanctuary protects many kinds of birds.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类保护区保护许多种类的鸟。
words.en: A protected area where birds are safe from harm and can thrive.

words.ex: The wildlife sanctuary protects endangered animals.
words.ex_cn: 野生动物保护区保护濒危动物。

words.tr: phrase. 寻求庇护；逃往避难所
words.ex: The family sought sanctuary in a church.
words.ex_cn: 这家人寻求在教堂里避难。

words.tr: phrase. 寻求公众关注；炒作自己
words.ex: He seeks publicity by posting wild videos online.
words.ex_cn: 他通过在网上发布疯狂的视频来寻求公众关注。

words.tr:
v. 潦草地写；匆匆地写；乱涂乱画
n. 潦草的字迹；涂鸦
words.ex: He scribbled his name on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上潦草地写了名字。
words.en: To scribble means to write or draw something quickly or carelessly.

words.ex: He spoke in a hoarse voice after shouting all day.
words.ex_cn: 他喊了一整天后，声音变得沙哑。
words.en: If your voice is hoarse or if you are hoarse, your voice sounds rough and unclear, for example because your throat is sore.

words.tr:
v. 使模糊；使看不清；弄污
n. 模糊
words.ex: The rain made the lights blur.
words.ex_cn: 雨使灯光变得模糊。
words.en: If something blurs your vision, it makes you unable to see things clearly.

words.ex: The experiment demonstrates that water boils at 100°C.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验证明水在100摄氏度时沸腾。
words.en: To demonstrate means to show something clearly by giving proof or evidence.

words.ex: He votes in a democratic election.
words.ex_cn: 他在民主选举中投票。
words.en: A democratic country, government, or political system is governed by representatives who are elected by the people.

words.ex: People vote in democracy to choose their leaders.
words.ex_cn: 人们在民主制度下投票选择他们的领导人。
words.en: A system of government by the whole population or all the eligible members of a state, typically through elected representatives.

words.tr: phrase. 不安全的投资；风险较高的投资
words.ex: Buying stocks without research is an insecure investment.
words.ex_cn: 不加研究地购买股票是一种不安全的投资。

words.ex: He felt insecurity when he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 当他失去工作时，他感到不安全感。
words.en: Insecurity is a feeling of uncertainty or anxiety about oneself or one's situation.

words.ex: She washed the linen in cold water.
words.ex_cn: 她用冷水洗亚麻布。
words.en: Linen is a kind of cloth that is made from the fibers of the flax plant. It is used to make clothes, sheets, and tablecloths.

words.ex: The painting gave me inspiration.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画给了我灵感。
words.en: Inspiration is a feeling of enthusiasm you get from someone or something, which gives you new and creative ideas.

words.ex: He gave a generous donation to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨地捐钱给穷人。
words.en: A generous person gives more of something, especially money, than is usual or expected.

words.ex: Farmers cultivate rice in the fields.
words.ex_cn: 农民在田里种植水稻。
words.en: To cultivate land means to prepare it and grow crops on it. To cultivate a particular quality, skill, or attitude means to try hard to develop it and make it stronger.

words.tr: n. （政治、商业或社会性）活动；运动；
words.ex: The city launched a campaign to reduce plastic waste.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市发起了一项减少塑料垃圾的活动。
words.en: A campaign is a planned set of activities that people carry out over a period of time in order to achieve something such as social or political change.

words.ex: The room was in complete disorder.
words.ex_cn: 房间一片混乱。
words.en: A disorder is a state of confusion or untidiness, or a medical problem that affects the mind or body.

words.tr:
n. 地点；场所；斑点；
v. 发现；识别；
words.ex: This is the spot where we met for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们第一次见面的地方。
words.en: A spot is a particular place or point. It can also refer to a small mark or stain, or a small amount of something. As a verb, it means to see, notice, or recognize someone or something.

words.ex: The outcome of the game was a tie.
words.ex_cn: 比赛的结果是平局。
words.en: The outcome of an activity, process, or situation is the situation that exists at the end of it.

words.ex: He was cautious when crossing the busy street.
words.ex_cn: 他过繁忙的街道时很小心。
words.en: If you are cautious, you are careful and avoid taking risks.

words.tr: adj. （言行）谨慎的；不显眼的；朴素的
words.ex: He was discreet about his personal life.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的私生活很低调。
words.en: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.ex: The two groups are discrete and do not overlap.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体是分离的，没有重叠。
words.en: Something that is discrete is separate and distinct in form or concept.

words.tr: adj. 分散的；散落的； v. 散布；分散；“scatter”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The books were scattered on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 书散落在地板上。
words.en: If something is scattered, it is spread out or distributed over a wide area in an irregular way.

words.tr: v. 加浮雕花纹于；饰以浮饰；使凸出
words.ex: He embosses the card with his name.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字压印在卡片上。
words.en: To decorate a surface by making raised designs or patterns on it.

words.ex: He engraves his name on the ring.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在戒指上。
words.en: To engrave means to cut or carve a design or letters into a hard surface, or to be strongly impressed in someone's memory.

words.ex: The ancient stone has an inscription in Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这块古老的石头上有一段拉丁文碑文。
words.en: An inscription is a piece of writing or a short message that is written or carved on something, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.ex: The answer is not guesswork; it's based on facts.
words.ex_cn: 这个答案不是猜测，而是基于事实的。
words.en: Guesswork is the process of trying to find the answer to something by guessing, rather than by using any exact method or calculation.

words.tr: adj. 鼓舞人心的；给予灵感的；
words.ex: Her speech was inspirational and made everyone feel hopeful.
words.ex_cn: 她的演讲鼓舞人心，让每个人都感到充满希望。
words.en: Something that is inspirational provides encouragement or new ideas for what you should do.

words.ex: His generosity helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的慷慨帮助了那个贫困的家庭。
words.en: Generosity is the quality of being kind and generous.

words.ex: He gave her a generous gift for her birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他送给她一份慷慨的生日礼物。

words.ex: Parents should foster good habits in children.
words.ex_cn: 父母应该培养孩子的好习惯。
words.en: To foster something means to encourage and promote its development.

words.tr:
n. 教养；养育；培育；
v. 培养；
words.ex: Her parents gave her good nurture.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母给了她良好的教养。
words.en: To nurture someone or something is to care for and encourage their growth or development.

words.ex: Mother's milk nourishes the baby.
words.ex_cn: 母乳滋养婴儿。
words.en: To nourish someone or something means to provide them with the food and other substances they need in order to live, grow, and be healthy.

words.ex: The police enforce the law.
words.ex_cn: 警察强制执行法律。
words.en: If people in authority enforce a law or a rule, they make sure that it is obeyed, usually by punishing people who do not obey it.

words.tr: phrase. 发起一场活动；开展一项运动；启动一场宣传活动
words.ex: The company plans to launch a campaign to promote its new product.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划发起一场运动来推广其新产品。
words.en: To start a planned series of activities, especially in politics or business, intended to achieve a particular aim.

words.tr: phrase. 竞选资金；用于政治竞选活动的经费
words.ex: He used campaign funds to buy posters.
words.ex_cn: 他用竞选资金购买了海报。
words.en: Money raised for use in a political campaign.

words.tr: adj. 不整齐的；混乱的；骚乱的；无秩序的
words.ex: The room was in a disorderly state.
words.ex_cn: 房间处于一片混乱之中。
words.en: If you describe something as disorderly, you mean that it is untidy, irregular, or disorganized.

words.tr: phrase. 火锅；一种将薄片食材在滚烫汤底中涮煮的中式烹饪方式
words.ex: We eat hot pot with friends on cold nights.
words.ex_cn: 我们在寒冷的夜晚和朋友吃火锅。
words.en: A dish consisting of a simmering metal pot of stock at the center of the dining table, with a variety of raw ingredients placed beside it to be cooked in the pot.

words.tr: phrase. 热点；热门地点；高发区；（无线网络）热点
words.ex: The city has many hot spots where tourists like to visit.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有许多游客喜欢去的热闹地区。
words.en: A hot spot is a place of significant activity or danger, especially one that is popular or problematic.

words.ex: He answered the question on the spot.
words.ex_cn: 他当场回答了问题。
words.en: If you do something on the spot, you do it immediately without any delay.

words.ex: The scenic lake attracted many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 风景优美的湖泊吸引了许多游客。
words.en: Relating to or resembling scenery; picturesque.

words.ex: We visited a scenic spot near the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 我们参观了山附近的一个风景点。
words.en: A scenic spot refers to a place of interest or a tourist attraction known for its natural beauty or cultural significance.

words.tr: phrase. 名胜古迹；旅游景点；有趣的地方
words.ex: This park is a place of interest for tourists.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园是游客的景点。
words.en: A place of interest is a location that is popular with tourists because of its beauty, historical significance, or other attractions.

words.ex: Loud noise aggravates his headache.
words.ex_cn: 噪音加重了他的头痛。
words.en: If someone or something aggravates a situation, they make it worse.

words.ex: The rain will worsen the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 雨会加重交通拥堵。
words.en: If a situation worsens or something worsens it, it becomes more difficult, unpleasant, or unacceptable.

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.ex: Smoking can exacerbate asthma.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会使哮喘加重。
words.en: If something exacerbates a problem or bad situation, it makes it worse.

words.ex: His deception fooled everyone at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他的欺骗骗过了派对上的所有人。
words.en: Deception is the act of deceiving someone or the state of being deceived.

words.ex: Practice can sharpen your skills.
words.ex_cn: 练习可以提高你的技能。
words.en: To make or become sharp or sharper.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；实际的；实践的；
words.ex: This tool is practical for everyday use.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具日常使用很实用。
words.en: relating to what is real rather than to what is possible or imagined; likely to succeed or be effective in real circumstances; involving or concerned with experience or actual use; not theoretical

words.ex: The plastic is pliable and easy to bend.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料柔韧，容易弯曲。
words.en: A pliable object or material is easy to bend or shape without breaking.

words.ex: The baby ate the tender broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝吃了嫩的西兰花。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as tender, you mean that they are kind, gentle, and sympathetic. If meat or other food is tender, it is easy to cut or chew. To tender something such as a service or a resignation means to formally offer or present it.

words.ex: The disposal of waste is important for the environment.
words.ex_cn: 废物的处理对环境很重要。
words.en: The act or process of getting rid of something, especially by throwing it away or selling it.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.ex: The pattern of the wallpaper is very simple.
words.ex_cn: 墙纸的图案非常简单。
words.en: A pattern is the repeated or regular way in which something happens or is done.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.tr:
n. 遗嘱检验；遗嘱认证
v. 核实（或检验）遗嘱
words.ex: The lawyer is handling the probate of the estate.
words.ex_cn: 律师正在处理遗产的遗嘱认证。
words.en: Probate is the legal process in which a will is reviewed to determine whether it is valid and authentic.

words.ex: The drought aggravates poverty in the village.
words.ex_cn: 干旱加剧了这个村庄的贫困。

words.tr: phrase. 使情况恶化；加剧局势
words.ex: He made jokes to aggravate the situation.
words.ex_cn: 他开玩笑使情况更糟。
words.en: To make a difficult or unpleasant situation worse.

words.ex: The noise caused aggravation to his headache.
words.ex_cn: 噪音加重了他的头痛。
words.en: An aggravation is a situation or condition that makes a problem or an illness worse or more serious.

words.ex: The heavy workload became a burden for her.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量成了她的负担。
words.en: A burden is a heavy load that is difficult to carry, or a duty or responsibility that is hard to bear.

words.tr:
v. 增加；增多；
n. 增加；增长；
words.ex: The company increased its profits last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年增加了利润。
words.en: To increase something means to make it larger in size, amount, or degree.

words.tr:
n. 减少；
v. 减少；降低；
words.ex: There was a decrease in rainfall last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月降雨量减少了。
words.en: If something decreases or you decrease it, it becomes less in quantity, size, or intensity.

words.ex: Try to lessen your sugar intake.
words.ex_cn: 试着减少你的糖摄入量。
words.en: If something lessens or you lessen it, it becomes smaller in size, amount, degree, or importance.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.tr: v. 使安静；安慰；使缓和
words.ex: She sang a song to soothe the baby.
words.ex_cn: 她唱了一首歌来安抚婴儿。
words.en: To soothe someone means to make them feel calmer and less anxious, upset, or angry.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.ex: He deceived his friend with a lie.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个谎言欺骗了朋友。
words.en: If you deceive someone, you make them believe something that is not true, usually in order to get some advantage for yourself.

words.tr: phrase. 故意的欺骗；蓄意的欺诈
words.ex: His intentional deception fooled everyone at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他的故意欺骗骗过了会议上的所有人。

words.ex: He sharpens pencils before the test.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前把铅笔削尖。

words.tr: phrase. 实践经验；实际经验
words.ex: He learned coding through practical experience.
words.ex_cn: 他通过实践经验学习编程。
words.en: Knowledge or skill that is acquired through doing something rather than learning about it in a classroom.

words.tr: phrase. 实用价值；实际用途
words.ex: The practical value of this invention is immense.
words.ex_cn: 这项发明的实际价值是巨大的。
words.en: The usefulness or importance of something in real situations or contexts.

words.tr: phrase. 实用材料；实际可用的材料；实践资料
words.ex: He uses practical material to learn how to fix cars.
words.ex_cn: 他使用实用的材料来学习如何修理汽车。
words.en: Substance or information that is useful and effective in a real-world situation or for achieving a practical goal.

words.ex: He disposed of the old books.
words.ex_cn: 他处理了那些旧书。
words.en: To dispose of something means to get rid of it, especially by throwing it away.

words.ex: His disposition is calm and kind.
words.ex_cn: 他的性情平静而善良。
words.en: Someone's disposition is the way that they tend to behave or feel.

words.ex: You need to pay a 40-yuan deposit to rent the bike.
words.ex_cn: 租自行车需要支付40元押金。
words.en: A deposit is a sum of money which is part of the full price of something, and which you pay when you agree to buy it. It is also a sum of money that you pay into a bank account.

words.tr: n. 沉积（物）；革职；宣誓证词；作证书
words.ex: Sediment deposition forms layers on the riverbed.
words.ex_cn: 沉积物在河床上形成层状结构。
words.en: The act of depositing something, especially a layer of a substance formed by natural processes, or the giving of testimony under oath.

words.tr: phrase. 由某人做主；由某人随意支配
words.ex: The keys are at your disposal.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙随你使用。
words.en: If you have something at your disposal, you are able to use it whenever you want and for whatever purpose you want.

words.ex: The city improves waste disposal to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市改善了废物处理以保护环境。
words.en: The process of getting rid of waste materials, especially to prevent harm to the environment.

words.ex: His opinion is subordinate to the manager's.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见比经理的次要。
words.en: If someone is your subordinate, they have a less important position than you in the organization that you both work for.

words.tr:
adj. 隶属的；附属的；与…有正式关系的；为…工作的
v. 隶属于；并入；联合；“affiliate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The hospital is affiliated with a university.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院与一所大学有关联。
words.en: If an organization is affiliated with another larger organization, it is officially connected with the larger organization or is a member of it.

words.ex: The subsidiary unit operates independently but reports to the parent company.
words.ex_cn: 该附属单位独立运营，但向母公司报告。
words.en: A subsidiary unit is a smaller, controlled company that is owned by a larger parent company.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary company in China.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司在中国拥有一家子公司。
words.en: A company that is controlled by a larger parent company.

words.ex: The local company is an affiliate of the big global brand.
words.ex_cn: 这家本地公司是这个全球大品牌的分公司。
words.en: If an organization is affiliated with another larger organization, it is officially connected with the larger organization or is a member of it.

words.ex: The tree has many branches.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树有许多分支。
words.en: A branch of a tree is one of its parts that grows out from its trunk. A branch of a business or organization is one of its offices or shops that are in different places.

words.ex: The ground began to subside after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨之后，地面开始下陷。
words.en: If a feeling or noise subsides, it becomes less strong or loud.

words.ex: The government gives a subsidy to farmers.
words.ex_cn: 政府向农民提供补贴。
words.en: A subsidy is money that is paid by a government or other authority in order to help an industry or business, or to pay for a public service.

words.ex: The club has an affiliation with the university.
words.ex_cn: 这个俱乐部与大学有从属关系。
words.en: An affiliation is a close connection or association with a particular group, organization, or institution.

words.ex: The hikers struggled across the rough terrain.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者艰难地穿越了崎岖的地形。
words.en: Terrain is used to refer to an area of land or a type of land when you are considering its physical features.

words.ex: He kneel to pray every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跪下祈祷。
words.en: To kneel means to go down into a position where one or both knees are on the ground.

words.tr: v. 使不知所措；使无法解决；击败；压垮；淹没
words.ex: The homework overwhelms her every night.
words.ex_cn: 每天晚上的作业让她感到不堪重负。
words.en: To overwhelm means to bury or drown beneath a huge mass of something, or to defeat someone completely.

words.ex: He looked at the lie with contempt.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you have contempt for someone or something, you have no respect for them or think that they are unimportant.

words.ex: I recognize her face from school.
words.ex_cn: 我从学校认出了她的脸。
words.en: If you recognize someone or something, you know who or what they are because you have seen or heard them before.

words.ex: He wears a badge on his shirt.
words.ex_cn: 他衬衫上戴着一枚徽章。
words.en: A badge is a small piece of metal, plastic, or cloth which you wear in order to show people that you have a particular rank, job, or belong to a particular group.

words.ex: The economic situation is getting worse.
words.ex_cn: 经济状况正在恶化。
words.en: Economic means concerned with the organization of the money, industry, and trade of a country, region, or society.

words.tr: adj. 虚弱的；衰弱的；无力的；
words.ex: The old man gave a feeble smile.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人露出虚弱的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as feeble, you mean that they are weak.

words.ex: Honesty is a great virtue.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种伟大的美德。
words.en: A virtue is a good quality or way of behaving.

words.ex: The village is in a hilly area near the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于靠近山地的多小山地区。
words.en: A hilly area has a lot of hills.

words.ex: The mountain is a natural landform.
words.ex_cn: 这座山是一个天然的地貌。
words.en: A landform is a natural feature of the Earth's surface, such as a mountain, valley, or plateau.

words.ex: The landscape after the rain is very beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 雨后的景色非常美丽。
words.en: A landscape is all the visible features of an area of land, often considered in terms of their aesthetic appeal.

words.ex: The mountain scenery is very beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 山景非常美丽。
words.en: The natural features of a landscape considered in terms of their appearance, especially when picturesque.

words.tr: adj. 压倒的；无法抗拒的；势不可挡的； v. “overwhelm”的现在分词；
words.ex: The crowd's cheers were overwhelming.
words.ex_cn: 人群的欢呼声压倒了一切。
words.en: If something is overwhelming, it affects you very strongly, and you do not know how to deal with it.

words.ex: The ship's crew discovered a stowaway in the cargo hold.
words.ex_cn: 船员们在货舱里发现了一个偷渡者。
words.en: A stowaway is a person who hides in a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle in order to travel secretly or without paying.

words.ex: He showed disdain for the lazy students.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些懒惰的学生表现出蔑视。
words.en: If you feel disdain for someone or something, you dislike them because you think that they are inferior or unimportant.

words.ex: He despises lying.
words.ex_cn: 他鄙视撒谎。
words.en: If you despise something or someone, you dislike them and have a very low opinion of them.

words.tr:
n. 蔑视
v. 蔑视
words.ex: He looked at the lie with scorn.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you scorn someone or something, you feel or show contempt for them.

words.ex: The price of oil soared last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月石油价格骤升。
words.en: To rise or increase dramatically in amount or level.

words.ex: He is recognized as a great teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他被公认为一位优秀的老师。
words.en: To be acknowledged or identified as a particular thing or in a particular way.

words.tr: n. 有价值的人或物；长处；
words.ex: He is an asset to the team because he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有价值的人，因为他工作努力。
words.en: An asset is something valuable that an individual, corporation, or country owns or controls with the expectation that it will provide a future benefit.

words.ex: He carries a briefcase to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天带着公文包去上班。
words.en: A briefcase is a flat, rectangular container with a handle, used especially for carrying papers and documents.

words.tr: n. 象征物；标志；代金券；代币；
words.ex: The dove is a token of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征物。
words.en: A token is something that represents or stands for something else, especially a piece of metal or plastic that you can use instead of money in some machines or as a symbol of a particular feeling or event.

words.tr:
n. 记号；分数；痕迹；
v. 做标记；（使）留痕迹；评分；
words.ex: He put a mark on the map to show the place.
words.ex_cn: 他在地图上做了一个记号来表示那个地方。
words.en: A mark is a small area or spot on a surface which is different in colour or texture from the area around it. If you mark something, you make a mark on it in order to identify it or to give information about it.

words.ex: Bees help to fertilize flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂帮助花朵受精。
words.en: To fertilize means to make soil or land more fertile or productive by adding substances to it, or to cause an egg, female animal, or plant to develop a new individual by introducing male reproductive material.

words.ex: He uses fertilizer to help his plants grow.
words.ex_cn: 他用肥料帮助植物生长。
words.en: A substance that is added to soil to improve the growth of plants.

words.tr: phrase. 经济形势；经济气候
words.ex: The economic climate is bad for small businesses.
words.ex_cn: 经济环境对小企业不利。
words.en: The overall condition and performance of an economy.

words.tr:
n. 寓言；神话传说；无稽之谈
v. 虚构
words.ex: The old man told a fable about a fox and a crow.
words.ex_cn: 老人讲了一个关于狐狸和乌鸦的寓言。
words.en: A fable is a short story that typically features animals as characters and conveys a moral lesson.

words.ex: He passed the test by virtue of his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他凭借努力学习通过了考试。
words.en: Because of or as a result of something.

words.ex: He was accepted in virtue of his excellent grades.
words.ex_cn: 他因优异的成绩被录取。
words.en: Because of; by means of.

words.ex: He depends on his brother for help.
words.ex_cn: 他依靠他哥哥帮忙。
words.en: To rely on someone or something for support, help, or supply; to be determined or influenced by something.

words.ex: He relies on his brother for help.
words.ex_cn: 他依靠弟弟帮忙。
words.en: To depend on with full trust or confidence.

words.ex: The sentence has ambiguity because it can mean two things.
words.ex_cn: 这句话有歧义，因为它可以有两种意思。
words.en: If you say that there is ambiguity in something, you mean that it is unclear or confusing, or it can be understood in more than one way.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.tr: adj. 虚拟的；几乎的；实际上的；事实上的；
words.ex: He played a virtual game on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他在电脑上玩了一个虚拟游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as virtual, you mean that it is so nearly true that for most purposes it can be regarded as true.

words.tr: adj. 品行端正的；品德高的；
words.ex: He is a virtuous man who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个品行端正的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Having or showing high moral standards.

words.ex: Smartphones are ubiquitous in modern life.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机在现代生活中无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as ubiquitous, you mean that they seem to be everywhere.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.ex: They live in a quiet suburb outside the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在城市外一个安静的市郊。
words.en: A suburb is a residential district located on the outskirts of a city.

words.ex: They live on the outskirts of the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在城市的郊区。
words.en: The outskirts of a city or town are the parts of it that are farthest away from its center.

words.tr: v. 粉碎；磨成粉；彻底击败；摧毁
words.ex: The machine will pulverise the rocks into dust.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器会把岩石碾成粉末。
words.en: To pulverise something means to crush it into a powder or to defeat someone completely.

words.ex: The farmer fertilise the soil before planting.
words.ex_cn: 农民在种植前给土壤施肥。
words.en: To fertilise means to make soil or land more fertile or productive by adding substances to it, or to cause an egg or female animal to become pregnant by introducing male reproductive material.

words.tr:
n. 定量；配给量
v. 配给；定量供应
words.ex: He gets a small ration of food each day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天得到少量的食物配给。
words.en: A ration is a fixed amount of something such as food or fuel that is officially allowed to each person, especially when there is not enough of it available.

words.ex: She is an attractive woman.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有吸引力的女性。
words.en: An attractive person or thing is pleasing or appealing to look at.

words.ex: The conquest of the mountain took three days.
words.ex_cn: 攻克这座山花了三天时间。
words.en: The act of conquering a place or people.

words.tr:
n. 老于世故的人；见多识广的人
v. 使复杂；使变得世故
words.ex: He is a sophisticated who knows how to handle difficult people.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个老于世故的人，懂得如何应对难缠的人。
words.en: To make someone or something more knowledgeable, complex, or refined, especially through experience or education.

words.tr:
n. 快照；
v. 突然断裂；猛然咬；
adj. 突然的；匆忙的；
words.ex: He took a snap of the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他拍了一张日落的快照。
words.en: If something snaps or if you snap it, it breaks suddenly, usually with a sharp cracking noise. | A snap is a photograph. | If someone snaps, or if something snaps inside them, they suddenly stop being calm and become very angry.

words.tr:
v. 表达；表示；
adj. 明确的；
n. 特快列车；快件服务；
words.ex: He can express his feelings clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的感受。
words.en: If you express an idea or feeling, or express yourself, you show what you think or feel.

words.tr:
v. 交配繁殖；饲养；
n. 品种；
words.ex: The farmers breed cows to get more milk.
words.ex_cn: 农民让奶牛交配繁殖以获得更多牛奶。
words.en: If you breed animals or plants, you keep them for the purpose of producing more animals or plants with particular qualities, in a controlled way.

words.ex: He left school at 15, which was too premature.
words.ex_cn: 他15岁就离开了学校，这太早了。
words.en: Happening or done before the usual or expected time; not fully developed or mature.

words.tr:
adj. 成熟的；
v. 成熟；
words.ex: He is a mature student who works full-time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成熟的学生，全职工作。
words.en: When something or someone matures, they become fully grown or developed. In finance, a mature investment is one that has reached the end of its term and is ready to be paid out.

words.ex: The farmer collects fertilized eggs for hatching.
words.ex_cn: 农夫收集受精的鸡蛋用于孵化。
words.en: An egg that has been combined with sperm to begin the development of an embryo.

words.tr: v. 异花授粉；交叉受精；交叉影响
words.ex: Bees help to cross-fertilise the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂帮助花朵异花授粉。

words.ex: It is rational to save money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 为未来存钱是合理的。
words.en: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.

words.tr: n. 基本原理；基础理论；
words.ex: The rationale for the new rule is to save time.
words.ex_cn: 这个新规则的基本原理是节省时间。
words.en: The fundamental reasons or logical basis for a course of action or belief.

words.ex: The ratio of boys to girls is 3 to 2.
words.ex_cn: 男孩与女孩的比例是3比2。
words.en: A ratio is a relationship between two numbers indicating how many times the first number contains the second.

words.tr:
n. 率；速度；比率；价格；费用；
v. 被评价；定级；（被）认为；
words.ex: The interest rate is very low this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年的利率非常低。
words.en: A rate is the speed at which something happens or changes, or the amount or number of something that happens or changes in a particular period.

words.ex: The mature breeding bird built a nest in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 这只成熟的繁殖鸟类在树上筑了一个巢。

words.ex: The ostrich runs very fast on the grassland.
words.ex_cn: 鸵鸟在草原上跑得很快。
words.en: An ostrich is a large African bird that cannot fly and has long legs and a long neck.

words.ex: Each family received the weekly meat ration on Friday.
words.ex_cn: 每个家庭在周五领取每周的肉类配给。

words.tr: phrase. 实行配给制；定量供应

words.ex: The factory has a quota of 1000 units per day.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂每天有1000件的配额。
words.en: A quota is the limited number or quantity of something which is officially allowed.

words.tr: phrase. 有吸引力的提议；诱人的条件
words.ex: The company made an attractive offer to hire her.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司提出了一个有吸引力的提议来聘请她。

words.ex: She has an attractive personality.
words.ex_cn: 她有迷人的个性。
words.en: An attractive personality refers to a set of characteristics that make a person appealing and likable to others.

words.ex: Her attractiveness made everyone smile.
words.ex_cn: 她的吸引力让每个人都笑了。
words.en: The quality of being pleasing or appealing to the senses.

words.tr: adv. 有吸引力地；动人地
words.ex: She dressed attractively for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对穿得很有吸引力。
words.en: In a way that is pleasing or appealing to the senses.

words.ex: The old house looks unattractive with its peeling paint.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老房子油漆剥落，看起来没有魅力。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as unattractive, you mean they are not pleasant to look at or do not have qualities that make them pleasant to be with.

words.tr: phrase. 军事征服；武力占领
words.ex: The ancient empire expanded through military conquest.
words.ex_cn: 这个古代帝国通过军事征服扩张。

words.tr: phrase. 恢复清醒；突然摆脱（某种状态）
words.ex: He finally snapped out of his daze after the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 在巨大的噪音后，他终于恢复了清醒。

words.tr: phrase. 抢购； 匆匆吃下； 抢先弄到手
words.ex: People snapped up the discounted shoes quickly.
words.ex_cn: 人们迅速抢购了打折的鞋子。
words.en: To buy something quickly and eagerly, often because it is cheap or in limited supply.

words.ex: His expression showed he was happy.
words.ex_cn: 他的表情显示他很快乐。
words.en: The act of making your thoughts, feelings, etc., known by speech, writing, or some other method.

words.ex: Her expressive eyes showed all her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 她富有表情的眼睛展现了她所有的感情。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as expressive, you mean that their behaviour clearly indicates their feelings or intentions.

words.tr: adj. 可识别的；可辨认的；
words.ex: The stolen bike is identifiable by its red handlebar.
words.ex_cn: 这辆被盗的自行车可以通过它的红色车把识别出来。
words.en: If something or someone is identifiable, they are able to be recognized.

words.ex: He accepted a nominal fee for the service.
words.ex_cn: 他为这项服务收取了微不足道的费用。
words.en: If you say that something is nominal, you mean that it is very small in comparison to the real value or importance of something.

words.ex: He acquired a new skill last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了一项新技能。
words.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

words.tr:
v. 注册；登记；
n. 登记簿；
words.ex: He will register for the course next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周会注册这门课程。
words.en: If you register something, you officially record it or list it.

words.tr: adv. 非常地；极其地；极端地；
words.ex: The weather is extremely cold today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气非常冷。
words.en: To an extreme degree; very.

words.ex: The apple will rot if left in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 如果把苹果放在太阳下，它会腐烂。
words.en: If something rots, or if it is left to rot, it decays and falls apart because of natural processes. Rot can also refer to a state of decay or decomposition.

words.ex: The ambulance arrived quickly to help the injured man.
words.ex_cn: 救护车迅速到达以帮助受伤的男人。
words.en: An ambulance is a vehicle equipped to transport the sick or injured, especially to a hospital.

words.ex: He felt miserable after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到很悲惨。
words.en: If you are miserable, you are very unhappy.

words.ex: The dog has identifiable characteristics like brown fur and a curly tail.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗有可识别的特征，比如棕色的毛和卷曲的尾巴。

words.tr: phrase. 名义上的首领；名义上的负责人
words.ex: He is the nominal head of the company, but the manager makes all the decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他是公司的名义上的首领，但所有决策都由经理做出。

words.tr: phrase. 名义资产；指账面上按面值或历史成本计价，但实际价值可能与市场价值相差较大的资产
words.ex: The company listed its nominal assets on the balance sheet.
words.ex_cn: 公司将其名义资产列在资产负债表上。

words.tr: phrase. 名义上的费用；象征性的费用
words.ex: He paid a nominal fee to join the club.
words.ex_cn: 他支付了一笔名义上的费用来加入俱乐部。

words.tr:
n. 金额；总数；
v. 概括；
words.ex: The sum of the bill is fifty dollars.
words.ex_cn: 账单的金额是五十美元。
words.en: A sum is an amount of money, or the total amount of two or more amounts of money added together.

words.tr: adv. 有名无实地；名义上地
words.ex: He is nominally the boss, but others make the decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他名义上是老板，但实际决策由别人做出。
words.en: If something is nominally true, it is true according to the name or title, but it may not really be true in fact.

words.tr: adj. 名义上的；有名无实的
words.ex: He is the titular head of the company.
words.ex_cn: 他是该公司的名义上的负责人。
words.en: Holding or constituting a purely formal position or title without any real authority.

words.tr:
adj. 次要的；轻微的；小的；小调的；
n. 未成年人；
words.ex: The mistake was a minor error.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误是一个小错误。
words.en: A minor is a person who is under the age at which they legally become an adult.

words.ex: The actual cost was lower than expected.
words.ex_cn: 实际成本比预期的低。
words.en: You use actual to emphasize that you are referring to something real or genuine.

words.ex: This is a genuine diamond.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石。
words.en: If something is genuine, it is real and exactly what it appears to be.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.ex: The magic show enthralls the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演让孩子们着迷。
words.en: If you are enthralled by something, you are so interested and excited by it that you give it all your attention.

words.tr: v. 诱骗；消遣；迷住；消磨
words.ex: He beguiles her with sweet words.
words.ex_cn: 他用甜言蜜语哄骗她。
words.en: If someone beguiles you, they charm you in a way that makes you trust them or like them, often so that they can deceive you.

words.tr:
v. 记录；准确地描述；俘虏；吸引；
n. 抓捕；
words.ex: The camera can capture the moment clearly.
words.ex_cn: 相机可以清晰地记录下这一瞬间。
words.en: To capture someone or something means to catch them, especially after a chase.

words.ex: The magic show captivates the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If you are captivated by someone or something, you find them fascinating and attractive.

words.tr: v. 强烈吸引住；使着迷；
words.ex: The magic show fascinated the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演深深吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If something fascinates you, it interests and delights you so much that your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

words.ex: The bright flowers attract bees.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的花朵吸引蜜蜂。
words.en: If something or someone attracts you, they have particular qualities which cause you to like or admire them.

words.tr:
v. 吸引；诱惑；引诱
n. 诱惑；诱饵；吸引力
words.ex: The bright colors lure the birds to the feeder.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引鸟类来到喂食器。
words.en: If you lure someone, you tempt them to do something or to go somewhere, especially by offering some form of reward.

words.tr: v. 诱惑；引诱；怂恿；劝诱；
words.ex: The smell of cookies tempted him to eat one.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味诱惑他吃了一块。
words.en: If something tempts you, it makes you want to have it or do it, even though you know you should not.

words.tr: phrase. 注册资本；登记资本；法定资本
words.ex: The company has a registered capital of 100,000 yuan.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的注册资本是10万元。
words.en: The amount of capital that a company is authorized to issue as stated in its memorandum of association and is registered with the appropriate government authority.

words.ex: He wants to register a trademark for his new brand.
words.ex_cn: 他想为他的新品牌注册商标。

words.tr: phrase. 注册；登记；报名参加（课程、活动等）
words.ex: Students need to register for their courses before the deadline.
words.ex_cn: 学生需要在截止日期前注册他们的课程。
words.en: To officially sign up or enroll in a course, event, or activity.

words.ex: He must register with the office before Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他必须在周一之前到办公室登记。
words.en: To officially record your name or the details of an event on a list.

words.tr:
v. 烤焦；烧灼
adj. 烧焦的；枯萎的
n. 烙印；焦痕
words.ex: He sears the steak on the grill.
words.ex_cn: 他在烤架上把牛排煎至表面焦黄。
words.en: To burn or scorch the surface of something with a sudden, intense heat.

words.ex: The sun makes the puddle evaporate quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳使水坑很快蒸发。
words.en: If a liquid evaporates, or if something evaporates it, it changes from a liquid state to a gas, because its temperature has increased.

words.ex: The apple shrivels in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 苹果在阳光下皱缩。
words.en: If something shrivels or if you shrivel it, it becomes dryer and smaller, often with lines in its surface, as a result of losing the water it contains.

words.ex: Water evaporation happens when the sun heats the lake.
words.ex_cn: 当太阳加热湖泊时，水就会蒸发。
words.en: Evaporation is the process by which a liquid turns into a gas.

words.tr: phrase. 极其悲惨的；像罪恶一样痛苦的
words.ex: He was as miserable as sin after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后极其悲惨。

words.ex: He felt guilt for his sin of lying.
words.ex_cn: 他因撒谎的罪行感到内疚。
words.en: Sin is an action or behaviour that is considered to be morally wrong according to religious or social laws.

words.tr: phrase. 可怜的失败者；惨败
words.ex: He is a miserable failure at keeping his promises.
words.ex_cn: 他是个连承诺都守不住的可怜的失败者。

words.ex: The rain was continuous all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都在下个不停。
words.en: Something that is continuous happens or exists without stopping or being interrupted.

words.tr:
n. 裂缝；噼啪声；
v. 破裂；
words.ex: There is a small crack in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有一条小裂缝。
words.en: If something hard cracks, or if you crack it, it becomes slightly damaged, with lines appearing on its surface.

words.ex: The apple is ripe and ready to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这个苹果熟了，可以吃了。
words.en: When fruit or crops are ripe, they are ready to be eaten or harvested because they have developed to the right stage.

words.tr:
n. 兽医；
v. 审查；
words.ex: The vet checked the dog's health.
words.ex_cn: 兽医检查了狗的健康状况。
words.en: A vet is a person who is qualified to treat sick or injured animals. As a verb, to vet means to examine something or someone carefully to make sure they are suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The veterinarian helps sick animals.
words.ex_cn: 兽医帮助生病的动物。
words.en: A veterinarian is a person who is qualified to treat sick or injured animals.

words.ex: They went on a long voyage across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 他们进行了一次横跨海洋的长途航行。
words.en: A voyage is a long journey, especially by sea or in space.

words.tr: phrase. 连续流动；不间断的流动
words.ex: The river has a continuous flow all year round.
words.ex_cn: 这条河全年都有连续流动。

words.tr: phrase. 连续放映影院；不间断放映的电影院
words.ex: The continuous performance cinema shows movies all day without breaks.
words.ex_cn: 这个连续放映影院全天不间断地播放电影。

words.tr: adv. 连续地；不断地；连续不断地；
words.ex: The machine works continuously without stopping.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器连续工作，不停止。
words.en: Without interruption; constantly.

words.tr:
adv. 好；对；满意地；
int. （用于表示惊讶，疑虑，接受等）好；
n. 井；
adj. 健康的；
words.ex: She sings well.
words.ex_cn: 她唱得很好。
words.en: In a good or satisfactory manner; in a thorough manner; in a manner that is appropriate or suitable.

words.ex: The sun well out in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在早上很好地出来了。

words.ex: The music accompanies the dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐伴随舞蹈。
words.en: To go somewhere with someone as a companion or escort; to play a musical accompaniment for.

words.ex: Honey is a viscous liquid.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是一种黏稠的液体。
words.en: A viscous liquid is thick and sticky and does not flow easily.
