words.en: A post graduate is a student who continues their education after completing a bachelor's degree, typically pursuing a master's or doctoral degree.

words.ex: He is an undergraduate student at Harvard.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的一名本科生。
words.en: An undergraduate student is a student in a university or college who has not yet received a first degree.

words.ex: The graduate student writes a thesis every year.
words.ex_cn: 这名研究生每年写一篇论文。
words.en: A graduate student is a student who continues studying after they have completed a first degree at a college or university.

words.ex: He is a postgraduate student in biology.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名生物学的研究生。
words.en: A postgraduate student is someone who is studying for a degree that is higher than the one they received as an undergraduate, typically a master's degree or a PhD.

words.tr: phrase. 本科院校；大学本科阶段的教育机构
words.ex: He graduated from undergraduate school in 2020.
words.ex_cn: 他于2020年从本科院校毕业。
words.en: The division of a university that provides bachelor's degree programs.

words.ex: He wants to go to graduate school after college.
words.ex_cn: 他想在大学毕业后读研究生院。
words.en: A graduate school is a school that awards advanced academic degrees (such as master's and doctoral degrees) with the general requirement that students must have earned a previous undergraduate (bachelor's) degree.

words.ex: He wants to go to postgraduate school after graduation.
words.ex_cn: 他毕业后想上研究生院。
words.en: A postgraduate school is an institution of higher education offering studies leading to a degree beyond the bachelor's degree.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；主要的；基本的；最好的；
words.ex: This is the prime reason for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 这是延误的首要原因。
words.en: Prime is used to describe something that is of the best possible quality, or the most important or basic part of something.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；小学的；初等的；原来的；最初的；
words.ex: Primary goal is to stay safe.
words.ex_cn: 首要目标是保持安全。
words.en: Something that is primary is more important than anything else.

words.ex: They settled in a small village after retirement.
words.ex_cn: 他们退休后在一个小村庄安顿下来。
words.en: To settle means to resolve or come to an agreement about a dispute, to establish a permanent home in a particular place, or to come to rest in a particular position.

words.tr:
adj. 犁过而未耕种的；休耕的；休闲中的
n. 休耕的田地；闲置；休整
v. 使（翻耕后的土地）休闲
words.ex: The farmer lets the field lie fallow this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年农夫让这块地休耕。
words.en: If land is fallow, it is not planted with crops, in order to improve the quality of the soil.

words.ex: The troupe performed a dance show in the town square.
words.ex_cn: 这个表演团在广场上演了一出舞蹈表演。
words.en: A troupe is a group of actors, singers, or dancers who work together.

words.ex: The premise of his argument is that everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他论点的前提是人人平等。
words.en: A premise is a statement or idea that forms the basis for a reasonable line of argument.

words.tr:
n. 前提；先决条件
v. 预先处理；事先准备
words.ex: You must finish homework as a precondition to play games.
words.ex_cn: 你必须完成作业才能玩游戏。
words.en: A precondition is something that must happen or exist before something else can happen.

words.tr: adj. 有辨别力的；能洞悉的；眼光敏锐的； v. “discern”的现在分词；
words.ex: She is a discerning shopper who always finds the best quality.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有辨别力的购物者，总是能找到最好的质量。
words.en: If you describe someone as discerning, you mean that they are able to judge which things of a particular kind are good and which are bad.

words.ex: He made a niggle about the coffee being too hot.
words.ex_cn: 他抱怨咖啡太烫了。
words.en: To niggle means to worry about or pay too much attention to small or unimportant details, or to cause someone to do this.

words.ex: The university sent me the prospectus for the course.
words.ex_cn: 大学给我寄了这门课程的简章。
words.en: A prospectus is a formal document that describes a new project, business, or product, especially one that is offered for sale or investment.

words.tr: v. 保持联络；做联系人；
words.ex: The manager liaises with the suppliers every week.
words.ex_cn: 经理每周与供应商保持联络。
words.en: To liaise means to act as a link to assist communication and cooperation between people or groups, especially in a professional context.

words.ex: The excavation revealed ancient pottery.
words.ex_cn: 挖掘发现了古代陶器。
words.en: The process of digging up and removing earth, especially at an archaeological site.

words.ex: The primal forest has never been touched by humans.
words.ex_cn: 这片原始森林从未被人类触碰过。
words.en: Primal means relating to an early stage in the development of something, or being the most important or basic part of something.

words.ex: The tribe lives in a primitive hut.
words.ex_cn: 这个部落住在原始的小屋里。
words.en: Belonging to a very early period in the history of the world, or to a time before modern things existed.

words.ex: The forest looked primeval and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林看起来远古而未被破坏。
words.en: relating to the earliest ages of the world or the universe; ancient or prehistoric.

words.ex: The captain sailed the ship across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 船长驾驶船穿越了海洋。
words.en: A captain is the person in charge of a ship or an aircraft, or a leader of a team or group.

words.tr: phrase. 定居；平静下来；专心于
words.ex: He wants to settle down with a family.
words.ex_cn: 他想安定下来组建家庭。
words.en: To settle down means to start living in a place where you intend to stay for a long time, usually after moving around a lot.

words.ex: The dogs had three offspring last spring.
words.ex_cn: 这些狗去年春天生了三只幼崽。
words.en: Someone's offspring are their children.

words.ex: He is a descendant of the first king.
words.ex_cn: 他是第一位国王的后裔。
words.en: A person, plant, or animal that is descended from a particular ancestor.

words.ex: The settler built a house near the river.
words.ex_cn: 这位定居者在河边建了一所房子。
words.en: A settler is a person who moves to a new place with the intention of staying there, especially in a previously uninhabited or sparsely inhabited area.

words.tr: n. 定居点；定居（过程）；协议；
words.ex: The small settlement near the river has five houses.
words.ex_cn: 河边的小定居点有五所房子。
words.en: A settlement is an official agreement intended to resolve a dispute or conflict.

words.ex: The overuse of plastic bags harms the environment.
words.ex_cn: 塑料袋的滥用对环境有害。
words.en: To use something too much or too often.

words.ex: The wheel rotates slowly.
words.ex_cn: 轮子缓慢地转动。
words.en: To rotate means to turn or cause to turn around an axis or center.

words.tr: v. 轮作作物；轮换种植农作物
words.ex: Farmers rotate crops to keep the soil healthy.
words.ex_cn: 农民轮作作物以保持土壤肥沃。

words.tr: n. 主要前提；主要论据
words.ex: The major premise is that all humans are mortal.
words.ex_cn: 主要前提是所有人都是会死的。

words.ex: The argument is based on a false premiss.
words.ex_cn: 这个论点基于一个错误的前提。
words.en: A statement or proposition put forward as a basis for reasoning, from which a conclusion can be drawn (variant spelling of 'premise').

words.ex: He made a hypothesis that plants grow faster in light.
words.ex_cn: 他提出一个假设，认为植物在光照下长得更快。
words.en: A hypothesis is an idea which is suggested as a possible explanation for a particular situation or condition, but which has not yet been proved to be correct.

words.ex: The difference is discernible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个差异肉眼可见。
words.en: able to be discerned; perceptible

words.ex: The two colors distinguish the two teams.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色使两个队伍有所不同。
words.en: If you can distinguish one thing from another, you can see or understand how they are different.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.ex: She wore a necklace made of jade.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条玉制的项链。
words.en: A hard, typically green stone used for ornaments and implements and consisting of the minerals jadeite or nephrite.

words.ex: She wore a ring with an emerald.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一枚镶有翡翠的戒指。
words.en: An emerald is a precious stone which is clear and bright green.

words.tr: n. 识别力；洞察力；眼力
words.ex: He showed good discernment in choosing his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择朋友时表现出了良好的判断力。
words.en: The ability to judge well.

words.ex: He wears a frown when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候会皱眉。

words.ex: He gave her a scowl when she was late.
words.ex_cn: 她迟到时，他皱了皱眉。
words.en: When someone scowls, they look at someone or something with an angry or irritated expression.

words.ex: A crow sat on the tree branch.
words.ex_cn: 一只乌鸦坐在树枝上。
words.en: A crow is a large black bird which makes a loud, harsh noise. If someone crows, they talk in a very proud way about something they have done or achieved.

words.ex: A large crowd gathered at the square.
words.ex_cn: 一大群人聚集在广场上。
words.en: A crowd is a large group of people who have gathered together, for example, to watch or listen to something interesting, or to protest about something.

words.ex: The baby is crawling on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在地板上爬。
words.en: To move slowly on hands and knees or by dragging the body close to the ground.

words.ex: He dig a hole in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园里挖了一个洞。
words.en: To dig means to break up, turn over, or remove earth, sand, etc., using a tool, a machine, or your hands. It can also mean to search for something by moving or looking through something, or to like or enjoy something very much.

words.tr: v. 摘下面纱；揭幕；揭露
words.ex: They will unveil the statue tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将摘下雕像的面纱。
words.en: If someone unveils something such as a new statue or painting, they show it to the public for the first time.

words.ex: He unraveled the knotted string.
words.ex_cn: 他把打结的绳子拆散了。
words.en: To unravel means to separate or disentangle the threads of a fabric or a rope, or to solve or explain something that is complicated or mysterious.

words.tr: adj. 欧洲大陆的；大陆的；
words.ex: He prefers continental breakfast with bread and coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他更喜欢欧洲大陆式的早餐，有面包和咖啡。
words.en: Continental is used to describe something that relates to or is characteristic of a continent, especially the mainland of Europe as distinct from the British Isles.

words.ex: The document is confidential and cannot be shared.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件是机密的，不能分享。
words.en: If you talk to someone in a confidential way, you talk to them quietly because what you are saying is secret or private.

words.tr: n. 现代主义；现代派；现代思想
words.ex: He likes modernism in art and design.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢艺术和设计中的现代主义。
words.en: Modernism is a style or movement in the arts that aims to break with classical and traditional forms.

words.ex: The artery carries blood from the heart.
words.ex_cn: 动脉将血液从心脏输送到身体。
words.en: An artery is a tube that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body.

words.tr: n. 额外费用；保险费；溢价；
words.ex: You need to pay a premium for faster delivery.
words.ex_cn: 你需要支付额外费用才能享受更快的配送。
words.en: A premium is an amount of money that you pay regularly to an insurance company for an insurance policy, or an amount of money that is more than usual for a product or service because it is of higher quality.

words.ex: The dress gave her a lot of glamour.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子给她增添了许多魅力。
words.en: If someone or something has glamour, they are attractive and exciting in a way that is not ordinary.

words.ex: We had a barbecue in the park last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们在公园举行了户外烧烤。
words.en: A barbecue is a meal or gathering at which meat, fish, or other food is cooked out of doors on a rack over an open fire or on a special appliance.

words.tr:
n. 材料；原料；
adj. 物质的；
words.ex: The table is made of wood material.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是由木头材料制成的。
words.en: Material refers to the substance or substances from which a thing is made or can be made, or information or ideas for use in creating a book or other work.

words.ex: He adapted to the new school quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就适应了新学校。
words.en: To make suitable to or fit for a specific use or situation.

words.ex: He gullibly believed the fake news.
words.ex_cn: 他轻信了那条假新闻。
words.en: In a manner that is easily persuaded to believe something; credulously.

words.ex: She sifts flour through a fine mesh.
words.ex_cn: 她用细网筛面粉。
words.en: To sift means to put a fine, loose, or powdery substance through a sieve so as to remove lumps or large particles. It can also mean to examine something thoroughly so as to isolate that which is most important or useful.

words.ex: He is a modernist who loves abstract art.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位喜欢抽象艺术的现代主义者。
words.en: A modernist is someone who follows or supports modern ideas, styles, or methods in art, literature, or religion.

words.ex: The army used artillery to attack the enemy base.
words.ex_cn: 军队用火炮攻击了敌方基地。
words.en: Artillery refers to large-caliber guns used in warfare on land.

words.tr:
n. 冠；花冠；冠状物
adj. 冠的；花冠的；头的
words.ex: The coronal suture in the skull is a key anatomical feature.
words.ex_cn: 头骨中的冠状缝是一个关键的解剖特征。
words.en: Relating to the crown or the top of the head, or to the corona of the sun or a flower.

words.tr:
n. 大炮；火炮
v. 猛撞；碰撞
words.ex: The soldiers fired the cannon at the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们向敌人开炮。
words.en: A cannon is a large, heavy piece of artillery which was used in wars to fire heavy metal balls or shells.

words.tr: 短语. 价格昂贵的；备受重视的；供不应求的
words.ex: Fresh water is at a premium in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 在沙漠中，淡水非常珍贵。
words.en: If something is at a premium, it is very valuable or in short supply.

words.tr: adj. 更老的；更旧的；更年老的；“old”的比较级；
words.ex: My older brother works as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 我哥哥年纪更大一些，是一名老师。
words.en: Comparative of old; having lived or existed for a longer time; more aged.

words.ex: He adapts to new rules quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快适应新规则。
words.en: If you adapt to a new situation or adapt yourself to it, you change your ideas or behaviour in order to deal with it successfully.

words.ex: He adapted from a book to make a movie.
words.ex_cn: 他从一本书改编来拍了一部电影。
words.en: To take something as a model or source for development or improvement.

words.ex: He is gullible and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易受骗，相信每一个他听到的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as gullible, you mean they are easily tricked because they are too trusting.

words.tr: n. 滤液；滤气; v. 过滤；筛选
words.ex: The filtrate is then collected in a separate container.
words.ex_cn: 滤液随后被收集在单独的容器中。
words.en: Filtrate is a liquid that has passed through a filter.

words.tr:
v. 过滤；
n. 过滤器；
words.ex: She filters the water before drinking it.
words.ex_cn: 她在喝水之前过滤水。
words.en: A filter is a device or a method that removes unwanted substances from something such as water, air, or light, by passing it through a special material or system.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；批判性的；关键的；危急的；临界的；
words.ex: Water is critical for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you are critical of someone or something, you show that you disapprove of them. In a critical situation, things are very serious and dangerous. A critical time or event is extremely important because it will affect future events.

words.tr: adj. 高度紧张的；兴奋的
words.ex: The child became hyper after drinking the sugary drink.
words.ex_cn: 那个孩子喝了含糖饮料后变得异常兴奋。
words.en: Excessively or extremely; over.

words.tr: adj. 苛求的；吹毛求疵的
words.ex: He is hypercritical about small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他对小错误非常吹毛求疵。
words.en: If you say that someone is hypercritical, you mean that they criticize things too much or too severely.

words.ex: He is hypocritical when he says he hates lying but lies all the time.
words.ex_cn: 他说他讨厌撒谎，却总是撒谎，这很虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being hypocritical, you mean that they pretend to have qualities, beliefs, or feelings that they do not really have.

words.tr: n. （用于筛撒粉状食物的）筛具，撒粉器; 滤器; 罗圈; 罗
words.ex: She used a sifter to evenly distribute the flour.
words.ex_cn: 她用筛子均匀地撒粉。
words.en: A sifter is a tool used to separate wanted elements from unwanted material or to break up clumps in dry ingredients such as flour.

words.ex: He is a hypocrite because he says he loves peace but fights often.
words.ex_cn: 他是个伪君子，因为他声称热爱和平，却经常打架。
words.en: A hypocrite is someone who pretends to have certain beliefs or opinions that they do not really have, especially in order to deceive people.

words.tr: adj. 过分活跃的；多动的；亢奋的
words.ex: The hyperactive child runs around the room all day.
words.ex_cn: 这个多动的孩子整天在房间里跑来跑去。
words.en: If someone is hyperactive, they are extremely active and find it difficult to relax or concentrate on one thing for very long.

words.ex: He gave a pseudo answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个假的答案。
words.en: Not genuine; sham.

words.ex: The hippo is sleeping in the river.
words.ex_cn: 河马正在河里睡觉。
words.en: A hippopotamus is a large, mostly herbivorous, semiaquatic mammal native to sub-Saharan Africa.

words.ex: The succession of rain made the ground wet.
words.ex_cn: 连续的雨水使地面变湿了。
words.en: A succession of things of the same kind is a number of them that exist or happen one after the other.

words.tr:
n. 火花；火星；
v. 激发；
words.ex: The match produced a small spark.
words.ex_cn: 火柴产生了一个小火花。
words.en: A spark is a small fiery particle thrown off from a fire, alight in ashes, or produced by striking together two hard surfaces such as stone or metal.

words.ex: I feel sympathy for the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 我对那些可怜的孩子感到同情。
words.en: If you have sympathy for someone who is in a bad situation, you are sorry for them, and show this in the way you behave towards them.

words.ex: She showed compassion for the homeless man.
words.ex_cn: 她对那个无家可归的人表示同情。
words.en: Compassion is a feeling of pity, sympathy, and understanding for someone who is suffering.

words.tr:
n. 寒冷；寒意；
v. 变冷；使冰冷；
words.ex: The chill of the morning made me wear a jacket.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的寒冷让我穿上了夹克。
words.en: A chill is a feeling of coldness, often accompanied by shivering. It can also refer to a feeling of fear or anxiety. As a verb, to chill means to make something cold, or to relax and take it easy.

words.ex: The multinational company has offices in five countries.
words.ex_cn: 这家跨国公司在五个国家设有办事处。
words.en: A multinational company or business operates in several different countries.

words.ex: The worker had long exposure to loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 这名工人长期暴露在噪音中。
words.en: The condition of being exposed to something, especially to something harmful or unpleasant.

words.ex: The fierce lion chased the deer.
words.ex_cn: 那只凶猛的狮子追赶着鹿。
words.en: A fierce animal or person is very aggressive or angry.

words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

words.tr:
adj. 极度的；
n. 极端；极端的事物；
words.ex: He felt extreme pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后感到极度疼痛。
words.en: If you describe something as extreme, you mean that it is very great in degree or intensity.

words.ex: The police caught the man for a serious crime.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓住了那个犯下严重罪行的人。
words.en: A crime is an illegal action or activity for which a person can be punished by law.

words.ex: Five apples constitute a basket.
words.ex_cn: 五个苹果构成一篮子。
words.en: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

words.tr: phrase. 连续地；接连地；一个接一个地
words.ex: He won three games in succession.
words.ex_cn: 他连续赢了三场比赛。
words.en: Following one after another without interruption.

words.tr:
n. 芯片；
v. 削成碎片；碎裂；
words.ex: The computer chip is very small.
words.ex_cn: 计算机芯片非常小。
words.en: A chip is a small piece which has been broken off something larger, or a small piece of silicon used to make computer parts.

words.ex: Ancient people used flint to make fire.
words.ex_cn: 古人用燧石生火。
words.en: Flint is a very hard greyish-black stone that was used in former times for making tools and weapons, and for starting fires.

words.tr: adj. 表面上的； v. “seem”的现在分词；
words.ex: His seeming kindness hid his true intentions.
words.ex_cn: 他表面上的善良掩盖了真实的意图。
words.en: appearing to be true or real but not necessarily so

words.ex: He felt great distress when he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 当他失去工作时，他感到非常忧虑。
words.en: Distress is a feeling of extreme worry, sadness, or pain.

words.ex: She generally wakes up at 7 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 她通常在早上七点起床。
words.en: In most cases; usually.

words.tr: n. 有价值的人或物；长处；
words.ex: He is an asset to the team because he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有价值的人，因为他工作努力。
words.en: An asset is something valuable that an individual, corporation, or country owns or controls with the expectation that it will provide a future benefit.

words.tr: n. 狂热的忠诚；强烈的忠心
words.ex: The dog showed fierce loyalty to its owner.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗对主人表现出狂热的忠诚。

words.ex: He got a penalty for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规则而受到惩罚。
words.en: A penalty is a punishment that is imposed on someone for doing something that is against the rules or the law.

words.tr: phrase. 校园犯罪；指在大学或学校校园内发生的违法行为
words.ex: The campus crime rate increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年校园犯罪率上升了。
words.en: Campus crime refers to criminal activities that occur on a college or university campus.

words.ex: The crime rate in this city is low.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的犯罪率很低。
words.en: The crime rate is the number of crimes that are committed in a particular area during a particular period of time.

words.ex: He committed a crime last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚犯下一桩罪行。
words.en: To do something illegal or wrong.

words.ex: He deceived his friend with a lie.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个谎言欺骗了朋友。
words.en: If you deceive someone, you make them believe something that is not true, usually in order to get some advantage for yourself.

words.tr:
v. 拖；拉；拖运；
n. 拖；拉；拖运；
words.ex: He hauled the heavy box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他把沉重的箱子拖过了房间。
words.en: To haul something means to pull it or carry it with a lot of effort.

words.ex: The factory reduces emission to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 工厂减少排放以保护环境。
words.en: An emission is the production and discharge of something, especially gas or radiation.

words.ex: The procession moved slowly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 行列缓缓沿着街道行进。
words.en: A procession is a group of people who are walking, riding, or driving in a line as part of a public event.

words.tr: n. 小饭店；小餐馆；小酒馆
words.ex: We had coffee at a small bistro near the park.
words.ex_cn: 我们在公园附近的一家小酒馆喝了咖啡。
words.en: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant or a small bar or nightclub.

words.tr:
n. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
v. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
words.ex: The car crash happened at the intersection.
words.ex_cn: 汽车碰撞发生在十字路口。
words.en: If a vehicle crashes or if the driver crashes it, it hits something and is damaged or destroyed.

words.tr: n. 劳动力；工人总数；职工总数；
words.ex: The factory needs a larger workforce to meet demand.
words.ex_cn: 工厂需要更多的劳动力来满足需求。
words.en: The workforce is the total number of people who are employed by a particular company or who are available to work in a particular country or area.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.ex: The car exceeded the speed limit.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车超过了限速。
words.en: To be greater in quantity, degree, or intensity than something else.

words.ex: He can deduce the answer from the clues.
words.ex_cn: 他能从线索中推断出答案。
words.en: If you deduce something or deduce that something is true, you reach that conclusion because of other things that you know to be true.

words.ex: He inferred that she was tired from her yawns.
words.ex_cn: 他从她的哈欠推断出她很累。
words.en: If you infer that something is the case, you decide that it is true on the basis of information that you already have.

words.tr: adj. 迷惑的；误导的；虚妄的
words.ex: The promise of quick riches is often delusive.
words.ex_cn: 迅速致富的承诺往往是欺瞒的。
words.en: Something that is delusive gives a false impression or leads you to believe something that is not true.

words.ex: The deceptive smile hid his true intentions.
words.ex_cn: 那欺骗性的微笑隐藏了他真正的意图。
words.en: If something is deceptive, it encourages you to believe something which is not true.

words.ex: He has a delusion that he is a famous singer.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种错觉，认为自己是一位著名歌手。
words.en: A delusion is a belief or impression that is firmly maintained despite being contradicted by what is generally accepted as reality or rational argument, typically a symptom of mental disorder.

words.ex: The mirror creates an illusion of a bigger room.
words.ex_cn: 镜子制造出房间更大的错觉。
words.en: An illusion is a false idea or belief, especially about yourself or your situation.

words.tr: v. 欺骗自己；自欺欺人
words.ex: He tries to deceive himself into thinking he is ready.
words.ex_cn: 他试图欺骗自己，让自己以为他准备好了。
words.en: To mislead or trick oneself into believing something that is not true.

words.ex: He deceived her into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他欺骗她签了那张纸。

words.tr: phrase. 温室效应气体排放
words.ex: Factories reduce greenhouse gas emission to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 工厂减少温室效应气体排放以保护环境。
words.en: The release of gases into the atmosphere that trap heat and contribute to the greenhouse effect, leading to global warming and climate change.

words.ex: He bought a zero-emission car to help the environment.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆零排放汽车来帮助保护环境。

words.tr:
n. 工序；过程；
v. 处理；加工；
words.ex: The factory improved the production process.
words.ex_cn: 工厂改进了生产工序。
words.en: A process is a series of actions which are carried out in order to achieve a particular result.

words.ex: He drew a straight line on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上画了一条直线。
words.en: A line is a long thin mark which is drawn or painted on a surface.

words.ex: The car crashed into the tree.
words.ex_cn: 汽车撞上了树。
words.en: To collide with something forcefully.

words.ex: He surmounted his fears to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了恐惧，在公众面前发言。
words.en: If you surmount a problem or difficulty, you deal successfully with it.

words.tr: v. 主持；指挥；担任会议主席
words.ex: He presides over the meeting every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周一主持会议。
words.en: To preside means to be in charge of a formal meeting, ceremony, or other event.

words.ex: He is taking sociology at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学里学习社会学。
words.en: Sociology is the study of society, patterns of social relationships, social interaction, and culture that surrounds everyday life.

words.ex: The violent storm destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场暴力的风暴摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If someone is violent, or if they do something that is violent, they use physical force or weapons to hurt, injure, or kill other people.

words.ex: She wore a long frock to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条长连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: A frock is a dress, especially one that is worn by women or girls.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.ex: He grabbed the ball quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速抓住了球。
words.en: If you grab something, you take it or pick it up suddenly and roughly.

words.ex: The kitchen has a new washing appliance.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里有一台新的洗衣机。
words.en: An appliance is a device or machine that is used to perform a particular task, especially in the home.

words.tr: n. 设施；特色功能；特定场所；资质；
words.ex: The school has a new sports facility.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个新的体育设施。
words.en: A facility is a place, building, or service that is designed for a particular purpose.

words.ex: Her hug was a consolation after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 在失败之后，她的拥抱是一种安慰。
words.en: Consolation is something that makes you feel better when you are sad or disappointed.

words.ex: He bought a new accessory for his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的手机买了一个新配件。
words.en: An accessory is something such as a bag or piece of jewelry that you wear or carry because it is attractive.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The flu is contagious and spreads easily.
words.ex_cn: 流感具有传染性，容易传播。
words.en: A contagious disease can be caught by touching someone who has the disease or by touching an infected object or by breathing in infected air.

words.ex: She tried to prevail on him to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 她试图劝服他改变主意。
words.en: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；盛行的；
words.ex: Smoking is prevalent in that country.
words.ex_cn: 在那个国家，吸烟很普遍。
words.en: If a condition, practice, or belief is prevalent, it is common or widespread.

words.tr: adj. 盛行的；有优势的；普遍的； v. “prevail”的现在分词；
words.ex: The prevailing weather today is sunny.
words.ex_cn: 今天盛行的天气是晴天。
words.en: The prevailing thing in a particular place or at a particular time is the one that is most common or strongest at that place or time.

words.ex: Too many rules can complicate the game.
words.ex_cn: 太多的规则会使游戏变得复杂。
words.en: To make something more difficult to understand or deal with by adding more parts or details.

words.tr: v. 解开；拆散；理清（纠结的线、绳等）
words.ex: He tried to ravel out the tangled string.
words.ex_cn: 他试图解开那团乱绳。
words.en: To untangle or unravel something that has become complicated or knotted, often metaphorically.

words.ex: The auctioneer brought the gavel down with a decisive strike.
words.ex_cn: 拍卖师果断地敲下小木槌。
words.en: A gavel is a small wooden hammer that a person in charge of a meeting or an auction hits against a wooden block to call for attention or order.

words.tr: v. 抓住某物（常指匆忙或试图抓住但不一定成功）
words.ex: The child grabbed at the balloon before it flew away.
words.ex_cn: 孩子匆忙伸手去抓那个气球，但气球飞走了。

words.tr: v. 抓取某物；试图抓住某物
words.ex: The child grabbed for the cookie on the table.
words.ex_cn: 孩子伸手去抓桌子上的饼干。

words.tr: adj. 待价而沽的；可争取的；尚未被占用的
words.ex: The job position is up for grabs.
words.ex_cn: 这个职位待价而沽。

words.tr: phrase. 家用电器（指家庭中使用的各种电器设备，如冰箱、洗衣机、微波炉等）
words.ex: She bought new household appliances for her kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 她为厨房买了新的家用电器。
words.en: Household appliances refer to electrical/mechanical machines which accomplish some household functions, such as cooking or cleaning.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；实际的；实践的；
words.ex: This tool is practical for everyday use.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具日常使用很实用。
words.en: relating to what is real rather than to what is possible or imagined; likely to succeed or be effective in real circumstances; involving or concerned with experience or actual use; not theoretical

words.tr: n. 通信设施；通讯设备
words.ex: The village has poor communication facilities.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄的通信设施很差。

words.ex: Dust particles float in the air.
words.ex_cn: 灰尘微粒漂浮在空气中。
words.en: A particle is a very small piece or amount of something.

words.ex: He got a consolation prize for trying hard.
words.ex_cn: 他因为努力尝试而得到了一个安慰奖。
words.en: A consolation prize is a prize given to someone who has not won a competition but is still recognized for their effort or participation.

words.tr:
v. 安慰；慰问
n. 控制台；操纵台
words.ex: She whispered kind words to console her crying friend.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声说些安慰的话来安抚哭泣的朋友。
words.en: If you console someone who is unhappy about something, you try to make them feel more cheerful.

words.tr: v. 使安静；安慰；使缓和
words.ex: She sang a song to soothe the baby.
words.ex_cn: 她唱了一首歌来安抚婴儿。
words.en: To soothe someone means to make them feel calmer and less anxious, upset, or angry.

words.ex: The soft chair gives me comfort.
words.ex_cn: 这把软椅子给我带来舒服。
words.en: If you comfort someone, you make them feel less worried, unhappy, or upset, for example by saying kind things to them.

words.ex: The weather is mild today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气温和。
words.en: Mild is used to describe something that is not extreme, severe, or strong, such as weather, taste, or behavior.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；宁静的；温和的；
words.ex: The lake was placid in the morning light.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的阳光下，湖面平静无波。
words.en: A placid person or animal is calm and does not easily become excited, angry, or upset.

words.ex: He unraveled the knotted string.
words.ex_cn: 他把打结的绳子拆散了。
words.en: To unravel means to separate or disentangle the threads of a fabric or a rope, or to solve or explain something that is complicated or mysterious.

words.ex: The texture of the bread is soft and fluffy.
words.ex_cn: 这种面包的质地柔软蓬松。
words.en: The feel, appearance, or consistency of a surface or a substance.

words.ex: The store sells many kinds of textile, like cotton and silk.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售多种纺织品，比如棉和丝绸。
words.en: Textiles are types of cloth or fabric, especially ones that have been woven.

words.tr: n. 织物；（建筑物的）结构；
words.ex: The dress is made of soft fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子是由柔软的织物制成的。
words.en: Fabric refers to cloth or other material produced by weaving together cotton, nylon, wool, silk, or other threads. It can also refer to the basic structure of a building or a system.

words.ex: His assumption was that the train would be on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是火车会准时。
words.en: An assumption is something that you assume to be the case, even without proof.

words.tr: n. 不满；令人不满的事物；
words.ex: He showed dissatisfaction with the new rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定表示不满。
words.en: Dissatisfaction is a feeling of not being satisfied or pleased with something.

words.tr: adj. 不满意的；不高兴的； v. “dissatisfy”的过去式；
words.ex: He was dissatisfied with the service.
words.ex_cn: 他对服务不满意。
words.en: If you are dissatisfied with something, you are not contented or pleased with it.

words.ex: The two events happened simultaneously.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件同时发生了。
words.en: Happening, existing, or done at the same time.

words.ex: The old sundial shows time by the sun's shadow.
words.ex_cn: 这个古老的日晷通过太阳的影子显示时间。
words.en: A sundial is a device that tells the time of day by the position of the sun. In common designs such as the horizontal sundial, the sun casts a shadow from its style (a thin rod or a sharp, straight edge) onto a flat surface marked with lines indicating the hours of the day. As the sun moves across the sky, the shadow edge aligns with different hour-lines.

words.tr: v. 解开；拆散；理清（纠结的线、绳等）
words.ex: He tried to ravel out the tangled string.
words.ex_cn: 他试图解开那团乱绳。
words.en: To untangle or unravel something that has become complicated or knotted, often metaphorically.

words.tr: v. 摘下面纱；揭幕；揭露
words.ex: They will unveil the statue tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将摘下雕像的面纱。
words.en: If someone unveils something such as a new statue or painting, they show it to the public for the first time.

words.ex: The shirt is made of synthetic fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫是合成纤维制成的。
words.en: Synthetic products are made from chemicals or artificial substances rather than from natural ones.

words.ex: I assume it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假定明天会下雨。
words.en: If you assume that something is true, you accept that it is true without proof.

words.ex: I presume he will arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假设他明天会到。
words.en: If you presume that something is the case, you think that it is the case, although you are not certain.

words.ex: I suppose he is late because of the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我认为他因为交通堵塞而迟到了。
words.en: If you suppose that something is true, you believe or imagine that it is true, although you may not have any proof.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.ex: Two events happen concurrently.
words.ex_cn: 两个事件同时发生。
words.en: Happening or existing at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 一致的；始终如一的；
words.ex: His answers are consistent with the data.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案与数据一致。
words.en: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

words.tr:
adj. 立即的；即时的；
n. 瞬间；立即；
words.ex: He wants an instant answer.
words.ex_cn: 他想要一个立即的回答。
words.en: An instant is a very short period of time, or a particular point in time.

words.ex: The car stopped in an instantaneous moment.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在瞬间停了下来。
words.en: Happening or done immediately.

words.tr: adj. 同时发生的；同时的
words.ex: The two events are coinstantaneous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件是同时发生的。
words.en: Occurring at the same instant in time; simultaneous.

words.ex: Dew forms on the grass in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨露水出现在草地上。
words.en: Dew is small drops of water that form on the ground and other surfaces outside during the night.

words.ex: The ground is damp after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后地面是潮湿的。
words.en: Something that is damp is slightly wet, often in a way that is unpleasant.

words.ex: The water is toxic to fish.
words.ex_cn: 这种水对鱼是有毒的。
words.en: If a substance is toxic, it is poisonous.

words.ex: We can utilise this tool to fix the problem.
words.ex_cn: 我们可以使用这个工具来解决问题。
words.en: To utilise something means to use it for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He showed conformity with the group's rules.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守了小组的规定。
words.en: Conformity is the act of matching attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors to group norms or standards.

words.ex: Don't overrate his skills; he is not that good.
words.ex_cn: 不要高估他的能力；他没那么好。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is overrated, you mean that people consider them to be better or more important than they really are.

words.tr: adj. 休眠的；蛰伏的；暂停活动的
words.ex: The volcano is dormant now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Something that is dormant is not active or growing but has the ability to be active at a later time.

words.tr: v. 取代；迫使…离开家园；
words.ex: The new robot will displace the workers on the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 这个新机器人将取代装配线上的工人。
words.en: To displace something or someone means to take their place or to force them to leave their usual place or role.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.ex: He engraves his name on the ring.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在戒指上。
words.en: To engrave means to cut or carve a design or letters into a hard surface, or to be strongly impressed in someone's memory.

words.tr:
v. 溢出；溅出
n. 溢出；溅出
words.ex: He spilled milk on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他把牛奶洒在了地上。
words.en: To cause or allow (a liquid, powder, etc.) to flow or fall out of a container, usually by accident.

words.ex: The smoke from the factory is noxious.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的烟雾是有害的。
words.en: Something that is noxious is harmful or poisonous.

words.ex: The frog is poisonous.
words.ex_cn: 这只青蛙是有毒的。
words.en: Something that is poisonous will kill you or make you ill if you eat it, drink it, or absorb it.

words.ex: The water has high toxicity.
words.ex_cn: 这种水有很高的毒性。
words.en: The degree to which a substance can damage an organism.

words.ex: The utilisation of solar energy is growing.
words.ex_cn: 太阳能的使用正在增加。
words.en: The act of using something in an effective way.

words.ex: The team was unanimous in choosing the new leader.
words.ex_cn: 团队在选择新领导时意见完全一致。
words.en: When a group of people are unanimous, they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.

words.ex: The team reached a consensus on the project plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队就项目计划达成了共识。
words.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

words.ex: They signed an agreement to share the costs.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份分担费用的协议。
words.en: An agreement is a formal decision about future action which is made by two or more people, groups, or organizations.

words.tr: n. 一致同意；全体赞同
words.ex: The team showed unanimity in voting for the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队在投票支持新计划时意见一致。
words.en: Unanimity is complete agreement among all members of a group.

words.ex: The dormant volcano has not erupted for 100 years.
words.ex_cn: 这座休眠火山已经100年没有喷发了。
words.en: A dormant volcano is a volcano that is not currently active but has the potential to erupt again.

words.tr: phrase. 潜伏；处于休眠状态；暂时不活动
words.ex: The seeds lie dormant in winter.
words.ex_cn: 种子在冬天休眠。
words.en: To remain inactive or in a state of suspension, often awaiting a future event.

words.ex: She gave a tearful farewell to her friends.
words.ex_cn: 她含泪向朋友们告别。
words.en: Someone who is tearful has tears in their eyes because they are sad, moved, or upset.

words.tr:
n. 坟墓；
adj. 严重的；
words.ex: They visited the grave of their grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了祖父的坟墓。
words.en: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried. When used as an adjective, grave means serious or solemn.

words.ex: The ceremony was solemn and quiet.
words.ex_cn: 仪式庄严而安静。
words.en: Solemn means very serious and not cheerful, often because something important or sad is happening or being remembered.

words.tr: adj. 严重的；认真的；严肃的；
words.ex: The accident caused a serious injury.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故造成了严重的伤害。
words.en: If you are serious about something, you are sincere about it and mean what you say.

words.tr: v. 被刻上某人的名字

words.w: He engraved a picture of himself
words.ex: He engraved a picture of himself on the wooden box.
words.ex_cn: 他把自画像雕刻在木盒上。

words.tr: v. 加浮雕花纹于；饰以浮饰；使凸出
words.ex: He embosses the card with his name.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字压印在卡片上。
words.en: To decorate a surface by making raised designs or patterns on it.

words.ex: The ancient stone has an inscription in Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这块古老的石头上有一段拉丁文碑文。
words.en: An inscription is a piece of writing or a short message that is written or carved on something, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.tr: n. 凹凸图案；浮雕效果；压花
words.ex: The paper has an embossment of flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这张纸上有花朵的凹凸图案。

words.ex: He gave a disrespectful answer to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师说了不尊重的话。
words.en: If you are disrespectful, you show no respect in the way that you speak or behave toward someone.

words.ex: The army tried to invade the neighboring country.
words.ex_cn: 军队试图侵犯邻国。
words.en: To enter a country, town, or region by force in order to take control of it.

words.tr:
v. 非法侵入；侵扰；冒犯
n. 非法进入；冒犯
words.ex: He trespasses on private land.
words.ex_cn: 他擅自进入私人土地。
words.en: To trespass is to enter someone's land or property without their permission.

words.tr: n. 拱廊；有拱廊的街道；游乐中心
words.ex: The old arcade has stone pillars and a tiled roof.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的拱廊有石柱和瓦片屋顶。
words.en: A covered passage with arches along one or both sides.

words.tr: n. 解说词；评论；实况报道；
words.ex: The commentator gave live commentary during the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 解说员在足球比赛期间进行了现场解说。
words.en: A commentary is a spoken or written description of an event or situation that is broadcast or published as it occurs.

words.ex: The movie recreates the battle of Waterloo.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影再现了滑铁卢战役。
words.en: To recreate something means to make it exist or happen again, or to make a copy of something that existed in the past.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄；
adj. 仿制的；
words.ex: They mock him for his accent.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他口音而嘲笑他。
words.en: To mock someone means to laugh at them, tease them, or make them look foolish, often by imitating their behavior or speech.

words.ex: They tease him because he wears funny hats.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他戴滑稽的帽子而戏弄他。
words.en: To tease someone means to make fun of them or try to provoke them in a playful way.

words.ex: The country expanded its territory after the war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在战争后扩大了它的领土。
words.en: An area of land that is controlled by a particular country, ruler, or military force.

words.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If a law or someone in authority prohibits something, they forbid it or make it illegal.

words.ex: He lives in Portugal.
words.ex_cn: 他住在葡萄牙。
words.en: Portugal is a country located on the Iberian Peninsula in southwestern Europe, known for its maritime history, cultural heritage, and as the birthplace of port wine.

words.ex: The cat ran down the alley.
words.ex_cn: 猫跑进了小巷。
words.en: An alley is a narrow passage between buildings or other structures.

words.ex: The bridge has a stone arch.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有一个石拱。
words.en: An arch is a structure that is curved at the top and is usually made of stone or brick. Arches are often used to support the weight of a bridge or the roof of a building.

words.ex: The invader came from a faraway land.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者来自一个遥远的地方。
words.en: An invader is someone who enters a place by force in order to conquer or occupy it.

words.ex: The invasion of privacy is a serious problem.
words.ex_cn: 侵犯隐私是一个严重的问题。
words.en: An invasion is an instance of invading a country or region with an armed force.

words.tr: adj. 对某事感到复杂的；对某事有心理负担的
words.ex: He is complex with his decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他对辞去工作的决定感到纠结。

words.tr: v. 作现场解说；进行实况报道
words.ex: He will commentate on the football match tonight.
words.ex_cn: 他今晚将为这场足球比赛做解说。
words.en: To commentate means to provide a spoken commentary on a sports match or other event as it happens, especially on television or radio.

words.ex: The commentator explained the game clearly.
words.ex_cn: 评论员清晰地解释了比赛。
words.en: A commentator is someone who gives a commentary on something such as a sports event or a television program.

words.tr:
adj. 第一手的
adv. 直接地
words.ex: He got first-hand information from the witness.
words.ex_cn: 他从目击者那里得到了第一手信息。
words.en: Obtained directly from the source or through personal experience.

words.tr:
adj. 嘲弄的
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄；（模仿）取笑；“mock”的现在分词
words.ex: His mocking laugh made her feel stupid.
words.ex_cn: 他嘲弄的笑声让她觉得自己很蠢。
words.en: Mocking is used to describe someone or something that makes fun of someone or something in a cruel way.

words.ex: The two countries argued over territorial rights.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家就领土权利发生了争执。
words.en: Relating to the ownership of an area of land or sea.

words.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。

words.ex: The prohibition of smoking in public places improved air quality.
words.ex_cn: 在公共场所禁止吸烟改善了空气质量。
words.en: Prohibition is the act of forbidding something, especially by law.

words.ex: The price of the phone is prohibitive for most students.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机的价格对大多数学生来说太贵了。
words.en: If the cost of something is prohibitive, it is so high that it prevents people from buying it or doing it.

words.ex: The shipment arrived on time.
words.ex_cn: 运输按时到达了。
words.en: The act of sending goods from one place to another, especially by ship.

words.ex: He checks the calendar every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都看日历。
words.en: A calendar is a chart or device which displays the date and the day of the week, and often the whole of a particular year divided up into months, weeks, and days.

words.tr:
n. 魔术；魔法；
adj. 魔术（似）的；神奇的；
words.ex: He performed magic at the birthday party.
words.ex_cn: 他在生日聚会上表演了魔术。
words.en: Magic is the power to use supernatural forces to make impossible things happen, such as making people disappear or controlling events in nature.

words.tr:
n. 纸片；
v. 滑倒；溜走；
words.ex: She found a slip of paper on the table.
words.ex_cn: 她在桌子上发现了一张纸片。
words.en: If you slip, you accidentally slide and lose your balance.

words.tr: v. 使粉碎；使破碎；使破灭；
words.ex: The stone shattered when it hit the ground.
words.ex_cn: 石头撞到地面时碎裂了。
words.en: If something shatters or is shattered, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.tr: n. 停战（协定）；休战（协定）
words.ex: The two sides agreed to a truce.
words.ex_cn: 双方同意停火。
words.en: A truce is an agreement between enemies or opponents to stop fighting or arguing for a certain time.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；
v. 不全信；不重视；
words.ex: The store gave a 20% discount on all shoes.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有鞋子提供了20%的折扣。
words.en: A reduction in the usual price of something, or the act of reducing the price.

words.tr: adj. 艰苦的；强硬的；严厉的；
words.ex: The hike was tough but beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 这次徒步旅行很艰苦但很美丽。
words.en: A tough person is strong and determined, and can tolerate difficulty or suffering.

words.tr:
n. 志愿者；
v. 自愿做；
words.ex: He is a volunteer at the local hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他是当地医院的一名志愿者。
words.en: A volunteer is someone who does work without being paid for it, especially work that involves helping people.

words.ex: The ship carries a large cargo of rice.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船运载了大量大米货物。
words.en: Cargo refers to the goods carried by a ship, aircraft, or other large vehicle.

words.ex: The freight train carried boxes to the city.
words.ex_cn: 货运列车把箱子运到了城市。
words.en: Freight refers to goods transported in bulk by truck, train, ship, or aircraft. It can also mean the charge for such transportation.

words.ex: The shop sold the clothes on consignment.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店以委托方式销售这些衣服。
words.en: A consignment is a quantity of goods that are sent somewhere, especially in order to be sold.

words.ex: He filled out a bank deposit slip at the ATM.
words.ex_cn: 他在自动取款机上填写了一张银行存款单。

words.tr: n. 沉积（物）；革职；宣誓证词；作证书
words.ex: Sediment deposition forms layers on the riverbed.
words.ex_cn: 沉积物在河床上形成层状结构。
words.en: The act of depositing something, especially a layer of a substance formed by natural processes, or the giving of testimony under oath.

words.ex: He disposed of the old books.
words.ex_cn: 他处理了那些旧书。
words.en: To dispose of something means to get rid of it, especially by throwing it away.

words.ex: His disposition is calm and kind.
words.ex_cn: 他的性情平静而善良。
words.en: Someone's disposition is the way that they tend to behave or feel.

words.ex: Children love playing games after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢放学后玩游戏。
words.en: Games are activities or sports that involve skill, chance, or endurance on the part of two or more persons who play according to a set of rules, usually for their own amusement or for that of spectators.

words.ex: The store makes a discount on clothes during the sale.
words.ex_cn: 商店在促销期间对衣服打折。

words.tr: phrase. 折扣商店；廉价商店
words.ex: I bought shoes at a discount store.
words.ex_cn: 我在折扣店买了鞋子。
words.en: A discount store is a retail establishment which sells products at prices lower than the usual market price.

words.tr: 短语. 打折；以折扣价
words.ex: He bought the shirt at a discount.
words.ex_cn: 他以折扣价买了这件衬衫。
words.en: If something is sold at a discount, it is sold at a price that is less than its usual price.

words.ex: The bank changed the discount rates for loans.
words.ex_cn: 银行调整了贷款的折现率。

words.tr: n. 难对付的人（或事）；棘手的问题
words.ex: Solving this math problem is a tough nut.
words.ex_cn: 解决这个数学问题是个难对付的难题。

words.ex: The volunteers for Olympic games help tourists find their way.
words.ex_cn: 奥运会志愿者帮助游客找到路。

words.ex: He did voluntary work at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院做志愿工作。
words.en: If something is voluntary, you do it because you choose to, and not because you have to.

words.ex: The volcano had a big eruption last week.
words.ex_cn: 上周这座火山发生了大喷发。
words.en: An eruption is a sudden, often violent, outburst or discharge, such as that of a volcano, emotion, or conflict.

words.tr: n. 养老金；退休金；抚恤金；
words.ex: He receives a monthly pension after retiring.
words.ex_cn: 他退休后每月领取养老金。
words.en: A pension is a sum of money which a retired, widowed, or disabled person regularly receives from the state or from a former employer.

words.ex: The teacher gave us a math assignment.
words.ex_cn: 老师给我们布置了一份数学作业。
words.en: An assignment is a task or piece of work that you are given to do, especially as part of your job or studies.

words.ex: The teacher will assign homework today.
words.ex_cn: 老师今天会布置作业。
words.en: To give someone a particular job or task; to allocate a resource or responsibility to a particular person or purpose.

words.ex: He bought a stainless steel knife.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一把不锈钢刀。
words.en: Stainless is used to describe something that does not rust or stain easily, especially stainless steel.

words.ex: This knife is rustless and stays shiny for years.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀不生锈，多年保持光亮。

words.ex: The teacher will distribute the books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将把书分发给学生。
words.en: If you distribute things, you hand them or deliver them to a number of people.

words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The teacher will allot five minutes for questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师会分配五分钟提问。
words.en: If something is allotted to someone, it is given to them as their share.

words.tr: adj. 神圣化的； 受崇敬的
words.ex: The hallowed ground is where the heroes rest.
words.ex_cn: 那片神圣的土地是英雄们安息的地方。
words.en: Something that is hallowed is respected and admired, usually because it is old, important, or has a good reputation.

words.ex: The temple is a sacred place for believers.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙对信徒来说是神圣的地方。
words.en: Something that is sacred is considered to be holy or connected with God or a god.

words.ex: The church is a holy place.
words.ex_cn: 教堂是一个神圣的地方。
words.en: If you describe something as holy, you mean that it is considered to be special because it is connected with God or a particular religion.

words.ex: Saint Francis loved animals and helped the poor.
words.ex_cn: 圣方济各热爱动物并帮助穷人。
words.en: A saint is a person who is recognized as having an exceptional degree of holiness, likeness, or closeness to God.

words.ex: The bus stops at the terminal at 9 PM.
words.ex_cn: 公交车晚上9点到达终点站。
words.en: A terminal is a place where vehicles, passengers, or goods begin or end a journey. It can also refer to a computer device at which a user enters data or commands.

words.ex: The climate in summer is very hot.
words.ex_cn: 夏天的气候非常炎热。
words.en: The climate of a place is the general weather conditions that are typical of it.

words.ex: The relevance of this topic is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这个主题的相关性是明显的。
words.en: The quality or state of being closely connected or appropriate.

words.tr: n. 按小时计酬的员工
words.ex: He is an hourly employee who works 30 hours a week.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名每周工作30小时的按小时计酬的员工。

words.ex: He lives on a pension after retiring.
words.ex_cn: 他退休后靠养老金生活。

words.tr: n. 按小时计酬的员工
words.ex: The store hires hourly employees to work during weekends.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店雇佣按小时计酬的员工在周末工作。

words.ex: He collates the papers before the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议前整理了这些文件。
words.en: To collate information or data means to collect it together and examine it carefully in order to compare it or find something out.

words.ex: The scientist calibrates the scale every morning.
words.ex_cn: 科学家每天早上标定秤。
words.en: To calibrate something means to mark or adjust it so that it can be used for measuring accurately.

words.tr: v. 使合乎标准；使合规格
words.ex: The school will standardize the test scores next month.
words.ex_cn: 学校下个月将统一评分标准。
words.en: To standardize something means to make it conform to a standard or norm, especially in order to ensure consistency and uniformity.

words.ex: He has the calibre to lead the team.
words.ex_cn: 他有领导团队的能力。
words.en: The quality of someone's character or the level of their ability; the diameter of the inside of a tube, especially of a gun barrel.

words.tr: v. 将某物分配给某人
words.ex: The teacher assigns homework to the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师给学生布置作业。
words.en: To allocate a particular thing or duty to a specific person.

words.tr: adj. 有硬皮的；有外壳的；执拗的；易怒的
words.ex: The bread has a crusty outside but a soft inside.
words.ex_cn: 这种面包外皮坚硬，但里面柔软。
words.en: If you describe someone as crusty, you mean they are easily irritated or get angry quickly, often in a way that is amusing or endearing.

words.ex: The old bike has rust on its chain.
words.ex_cn: 这辆旧自行车的链条上有锈。
words.en: Rust is a reddish-brown substance that forms on the surface of iron or steel when they are exposed to air and moisture, causing them to corrode.

words.ex: The old bike has a rusty chain.
words.ex_cn: 这辆旧自行车的链条生锈了。
words.en: If something is rusty, it is covered with rust or has become less good because it has not been used for a long time.

words.tr:
v. （使）发出沙沙；偷窃（牲口）
n. 沙沙声；瑟瑟声
words.ex: The wind rustled the leaves.
words.ex_cn: 风使树叶发出沙沙声。
words.en: If something rustles, it makes soft sounds as it moves lightly and gently, for example through the air or over dry leaves.

words.tr:
adj. 乡村的；纯朴的；土气的
n. 乡下人；乡巴佬
words.ex: They live in a rustic cabin near the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一间乡村小屋里。
words.en: Rustic is used to describe things that are typical of the countryside rather than the town, or things that are simple and old-fashioned in a way that is considered typical of the countryside.

words.ex: He bought a spoon made of stainless steel.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一个不锈钢勺子。
words.en: A type of steel that contains a large proportion of chromium, making it resistant to rust and corrosion.

words.ex: The tree has a hollow trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的树干是中空的。
words.en: If something is hollow, it has an empty space inside it.

words.ex: They hallow the old church on Halloween.
words.ex_cn: 他们在万圣节时敬拜那座老教堂。
words.en: To make holy or set apart as holy; to honor as sacred.

words.ex: The jet flew high above the clouds.
words.ex_cn: 喷气式飞机在云层上方飞行。
words.en: A jet is an aircraft that is powered by jet engines, allowing it to fly at high speeds. It can also refer to a stream of liquid or gas forced out of a small opening, or to travel by jet aircraft.

words.ex: He uses an ink jet printer to print photos at home.
words.ex_cn: 他用喷墨打印机在家打印照片。
words.en: A printing device that sprays microscopic droplets of ink onto paper to create text or images, known for its quiet operation and color accuracy.

words.ex: The ostrich runs very fast on the grassland.
words.ex_cn: 鸵鸟在草原上跑得很快。
words.en: An ostrich is a large African bird that cannot fly and has long legs and a long neck.

words.ex: He was reluctant to leave his home.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意离开家。
words.en: If you are reluctant to do something, you are unwilling to do it and hesitate before doing it, or do it slowly and without enthusiasm.

words.ex: The regularity of his daily routine helps him stay focused.
words.ex_cn: 他日常作息的规律性帮助他保持专注。
words.en: The quality or state of being regular; the condition of being governed by or according to rules, principles, or established customs.

words.ex: The child shows right laterality in writing.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子在写字时表现出右利性。
words.en: Laterality refers to the preference or dominance of one side of the body over the other, especially in the context of brain function and the use of limbs.

words.ex: The predominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的主导颜色是蓝色。
words.en: If something is predominant, it is more important, noticeable, or powerful than the other things in a situation.

words.tr:
n. 艰苦跋涉；
v. 长途跋涉；
words.ex: The trek across the mountains took five days.
words.ex_cn: 穿越群山的艰苦跋涉花了五天时间。
words.en: A trek is a long and often difficult journey, especially one made on foot.

words.tr:
v. 费力地做；苦干；跋涉
n. 苦工；劳累的工作
words.ex: He toils in the field every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天在田里辛苦劳作。
words.en: If you toil, you work very hard doing something that is difficult or tiring.

words.tr: v. 使气馁；使胆怯；吓倒
words.ex: The loud noise did not daunt her.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音并没有吓倒她。
words.en: If something daunts you, it makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.ex: We planned our itinerary before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们在旅行前规划了路线。
words.en: An itinerary is a plan of a journey, including the route and the places that you will visit.

words.ex: He acclimatise to the cold weather slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢适应了寒冷的天气。
words.en: to get used to a new place, situation, or climate

words.tr: n. 用右手或左手的习惯
words.ex: His handedness makes him write with his left hand.
words.ex_cn: 他的惯用手使他用左手写字。
words.en: The tendency to use one hand rather than the other, especially the right hand for most tasks.

words.tr: adj. 公正的；不偏不倚的；
words.ex: The judge was impartial in the trial.
words.ex_cn: 法官在审判中是公正的。
words.en: Someone who is impartial is not directly involved in a particular situation, and is therefore able to give a fair opinion or decision about it.

words.tr:
adj. 公平的；相当大的；合理的；
n. 集市；
words.ex: The teacher gave a fair grade to every student.
words.ex_cn: 老师给每个学生都给了一个公平的分数。
words.en: Fair means treating people equally without favouritism or discrimination.

words.ex: He only read the partial report.
words.ex_cn: 他只读了部分报告。
words.en: If you describe something as partial, you mean that it is not complete or whole.

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.ex: He has a preference for tea over coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他更喜欢茶而不是咖啡。
words.en: A preference is a greater liking for one alternative over another or others.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；杰出的；出类拔萃的
words.ex: He is a preeminent scientist in his field.
words.ex_cn: 他是该领域最杰出的科学家。
words.en: Standing out in importance or reputation; superior to all others.

words.ex: The sunset was spectacular.
words.ex_cn: 日落非常壮观。
words.en: Something that is spectacular is very impressive or dramatic.

words.ex: The small house is on a foothill near the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这栋小房子位于山脚下的山坡上。
words.en: A foothill is a low hill at the base of a mountain or mountain range.

words.ex: The dispute was settled through arbitral proceedings.
words.ex_cn: 争议通过仲裁程序得到了解决。
words.en: Relating to or involving arbitration.

words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.tr:
n. 大炮；火炮
v. 猛撞；碰撞
words.ex: The soldiers fired the cannon at the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们向敌人开炮。
words.en: A cannon is a large, heavy piece of artillery which was used in wars to fire heavy metal balls or shells.

words.ex: The army used artillery to attack the enemy base.
words.ex_cn: 军队用火炮攻击了敌方基地。
words.en: Artillery refers to large-caliber guns used in warfare on land.

words.ex: The river flows through a deep canyon.
words.ex_cn: 河流流经一个深峡谷。
words.en: A canyon is a large valley with very steep sides and usually a river flowing along the bottom.

words.ex: I can't travel now, but for the moment I must stay home.
words.ex_cn: 我现在不能旅行，但目前我必须待在家里。

words.ex: The mountain has two high points that are visible from far away.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有两个从远处都能看到的高点。

words.ex: The artery carries blood from the heart.
words.ex_cn: 动脉将血液从心脏输送到身体。
words.en: An artery is a tube that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body.

words.ex: The blood flows through arterial vessels.
words.ex_cn: 血液流经动脉血管。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the main route in a system of roads, railways, or rivers.

words.ex: He practices martial arts every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天练习武术。
words.en: Martial is used to describe things relating to soldiers or war.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生（或出版等）的；准备好的；
words.ex: The forthcoming book will be released next month.
words.ex_cn: 即将出版的这本书将在下个月发布。
words.en: If something is forthcoming, it is happening or coming soon.

words.tr:
n. 结构；建筑物；
v. 组织；
words.ex: The structure of the bridge is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。
words.en: The arrangement of and relations between the parts or elements of something complex.

words.ex: The quantity of water in the bottle is small.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子里的水量很少。
words.en: A quantity is an amount that you can measure or count.

words.ex: Honesty is an integral part of a good relationship.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是良好关系中不可或缺的一部分。
words.en: Something that is integral is very important or necessary. If something is an integral part of a whole, it is an essential part of that whole.

words.ex: He took an intensive English course last summer.
words.ex_cn: 去年夏天，他参加了一个密集的英语课程。
words.en: Intensive is used to describe something that involves a lot of effort, energy, or attention in a short period of time.

words.ex: He finally acknowledged his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: He bought a bottle of liquor for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为派对买了一瓶酒。
words.en: Liquor is an alcoholic drink that is made by distillation rather than by fermentation.

words.ex: His presence made everyone feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 他的存在让每个人都感到平静。
words.en: The state or fact of existing, occurring, or being present in a place or thing.

words.ex: The country is developing its economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正在发展它的经济。
words.en: To develop means to grow or cause to grow and become more mature, advanced, or elaborate.

words.tr: n. 管理结构；组织架构
words.ex: The company changed its management structure to improve efficiency.
words.ex_cn: 公司改变了管理结构以提高效率。

words.ex: The economic structure of the country has changed significantly over the last decade.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的经济结构在过去十年中发生了显著变化。
words.en: The arrangement of the various sectors of an economy, and the relationships between them, which determines the distribution of resources.

words.ex: He writes in his diary every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都写日记。
words.en: A diary is a book in which you write down your personal experiences and thoughts each day.

words.tr:
adj. 牛奶的；乳品的；
n. 乳品店；
words.ex: She bought dairy products from the local farm.
words.ex_cn: 她从当地农场买了乳制品。
words.en: A dairy is a place where milk and cream are kept or where butter and cheese are made.

words.ex: The integral number -5 is less than zero.
words.ex_cn: 整数 -5 小于零。

words.tr: adj. 必需的；基本的；本质的；
words.ex: Water is essential for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必需的。
words.en: Something that is essential is extremely important or absolutely necessary to a particular subject, situation, or activity.

words.ex: This is a basic math skill.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个基本的数学技能。
words.en: You use basic to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or necessary, and on which others depend.

words.tr: adj. 基本的；基础的；根本的；
words.ex: Water is a fundamental need for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本需求。
words.en: You use fundamental to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or essential. They affect the basic nature of other things or are the most important element upon which other things depend.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；小学的；初等的；原来的；最初的；
words.ex: Primary goal is to stay safe.
words.ex_cn: 首要目标是保持安全。
words.en: Something that is primary is more important than anything else.

words.tr: phrase. 强化训练；密集培训
words.ex: He does intensive training every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上进行高强度训练。
words.en: Intensive training refers to a concentrated and rigorous program designed to improve skills or knowledge in a specific area within a short period of time.

words.ex: He does intensive reading every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上进行精读。
words.en: Intensive reading refers to the thorough and detailed reading of texts, often with the aim of understanding and analyzing their content deeply.

words.tr: n. 演讲人；节目主持人；发言人；呈献者；
words.ex: The presenter told a funny story to the audience.
words.ex_cn: 演讲人给观众讲了一个有趣的故事。
words.en: A presenter is a person who introduces or hosts a television or radio program, or who introduces a speaker or performer at a public event.

words.ex: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun.
words.ex_cn: 天王星是离太阳第七远的行星。
words.en: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun in the Solar System. It has the third-largest planetary radius and fourth-largest planetary mass in the Solar System.

words.ex: The development of the town took many years.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇的发展花了许多年。
words.en: Development is the process of growth, progress, or making something more advanced.

words.ex: The village is still undeveloped with no roads or electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄仍然不发达，没有道路和电力。
words.en: An undeveloped area of land is one that has not been used for building or farming.

words.tr: v. 发展；发育；“develop”的现在分词； adj. 发展中的；
words.ex: The country is developing its economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正在发展它的经济。
words.en: A developing country or area of the world is poorer and has less advanced industries, especially in Africa, Latin America, or Asia.

words.tr: n. 一阵强劲的气流；爆炸；
words.ex: A blast of cold wind hit the window.
words.ex_cn: 一阵冷风击中了窗户。
words.en: A blast is a sudden loud noise or a strong gust of wind. It can also refer to an explosion or the act of blowing something up. As a verb, it means to explode or to criticize severely.

words.ex: He greatly improved his English.
words.ex_cn: 他的英语进步了很多。
words.en: To a great extent or degree; very much.

words.tr: adv. 间断发生地；零星地
words.ex: He visits his grandma sporadically.
words.ex_cn: 他偶尔去看望奶奶。
words.en: If something happens sporadically, it happens occasionally and not regularly or continuously.

words.ex: The child imitates her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If you imitate someone, you copy what they do or produce.

words.ex: The constitution protects the rights of all citizens.
words.ex_cn: 宪法保护所有公民的权利。
words.en: The constitution of a country or organization is the system of laws which formally states people's rights and duties.

words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.ex: The cost of maintenance is low for this car.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的维持费用很低。
words.en: The process of preserving a condition or situation or the state of being preserved.

words.ex: He bought a gift for his spouse.
words.ex_cn: 他给他的配偶买了一份礼物。
words.en: A spouse is a person's partner in marriage.

words.ex: The team went on an expedition to the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍去山上探险了。
words.en: An expedition is an organized journey that is made for a particular purpose such as exploration.

words.ex: The diameter of the circle is 10 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆的直径是10厘米。
words.en: A straight line passing from side to side through the center of a body or figure, especially a circle or sphere.

words.ex: The new policy has a wide radius of influence.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策的影响范围很广。
words.en: A straight line from the center to the circumference of a circle or sphere.

words.tr:
n. 一阵狂风；突然的一阵
v. （风）猛刮
words.ex: A sudden gust blew the hat off his head.
words.ex_cn: 一阵突然的风把他的帽子吹掉了。
words.en: A gust is a sudden, strong rush of wind.

words.ex: The table is made of granite.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是花岗岩做的。
words.en: Granite is a very hard rock that is often used in building.

words.ex: He climbed a big boulder near the river.
words.ex_cn: 他爬上了河边的一块大岩石。
words.en: A boulder is a large rounded rock.

words.ex: We have a blast at the park every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 我们每周末在公园都玩得很开心。
words.en: To have a very enjoyable time.

words.tr: 短语，一阵（尤指突然而强烈的风、声音或感觉）
words.ex: He got a blast of cold air when he opened the door.
words.ex_cn: 他开门时迎面吹来一阵冷风。
words.en: A sudden, intense burst of something, often wind, sound, or emotion.

words.tr: phrase. 全速地；全力地；以最大音量或强度
words.ex: The music was playing at full blast, making it hard to concentrate.
words.ex_cn: 音乐以最大音量播放，让人难以集中注意力。
words.en: At full blast means at maximum volume or intensity.

words.ex: The pencil is 15 centimeters long.
words.ex_cn: 这支铅笔有15厘米长。
words.en: A centimeter is a unit of length in the metric system equal to one hundredth of a meter.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: He threatened to call the police.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁要叫警察。
words.en: If someone threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.

words.ex: They have an intimate friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他们有着亲密的友谊。
words.en: having a close, friendly, or personal relationship with someone; private and personal

words.ex: They share intimacy through quiet talks at night.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过夜晚的安静交谈建立亲密感。
words.en: A close, familiar, and usually affectionate or loving personal relationship with another person or group.

words.ex: The teacher put emphasis on reading every day.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调每天都要阅读。
words.en: Special importance, value, or prominence given to something.

words.ex: The old church has strong masonry walls.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的教堂有坚固的石砖结构墙壁。
words.en: Masonry is the craft of building with stone, brick, or similar materials, often using mortar.

words.ex: He lives in a big mansion near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一座大宅子里。
words.en: A mansion is a very large, impressive house, especially one that is the home of a wealthy or important person.

words.tr: n. 汽车的维护；汽车的保养
words.ex: The maintenance of an automobile includes changing oil and checking tires.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的维护包括更换机油和检查轮胎。

words.ex: The birds mate in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟在春天交配。
words.en: A mate is a friend, someone you work with, or someone you are married to or in a sexual relationship with. As a verb, to mate means to have sex in order to produce young or to bring two animals together for breeding.

words.tr: 在前往……的考察/远征途中
words.ex: They are on an expedition to the North Pole.
words.ex_cn: 他们正在前往北极的考察途中。

words.tr: v. 出发进行探险；进行远征
words.ex: They will go on an expedition to the mountains next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将出发进行探险去山区。

words.tr: n. 一次购物远征；一次专门的购物之旅
words.ex: We went on a shopping expedition to buy new clothes.
words.ex_cn: 我们去进行了一次购物远征，买新衣服。

words.ex: He wants to expedite the process.
words.ex_cn: 他想加快这个过程。
words.en: To expedite something means to make it happen or be done more quickly.

words.ex: He made an expeditious decision to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速做出了离开的决定。
words.en: If you describe something as expeditious, you mean that it is done quickly and efficiently.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.ex: The navy launched a large fleet to protect the coast.
words.ex_cn: 海军派出了一支大型舰队来保护海岸。
words.en: A fleet is a group of ships or vehicles that are controlled by one company or organization and are used for a particular purpose.

words.tr:
adj. 引火的；燃烧的；纵火的；煽动的
n. 燃烧弹
words.ex: The incendiary device set the building on fire.
words.ex_cn: 这个引火装置把大楼点燃了。
words.en: An incendiary device is designed to cause fires. Incendiary remarks or actions are likely to cause anger or violence.

words.ex: The city's expansion caused more traffic.
words.ex_cn: 城市的扩张导致了更多的交通拥堵。
words.en: Expansion refers to the process of becoming larger or more extensive.

words.ex: The diamond is encased in glass.
words.ex_cn: 钻石被包裹在玻璃里。
words.en: To encase something means to cover or surround it completely in a case or close-fitting covering.

words.ex: The ticket is invalid because it expired.
words.ex_cn: 这张票无效，因为它已经过期了。
words.en: If something is invalid, it is not legally or officially acceptable, or it is not based on truth or reason.

words.ex: The judge gave an unbiased decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官作出了无偏见的判决。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unbiased, you mean they are fair and not likely to support one particular person or group involved in something.

words.ex: The swollen area is inflammatory and painful.
words.ex_cn: 这个肿胀的部位是发炎的，并且很痛。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behaviour as inflammatory, you mean that it is likely to cause people to react very angrily.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.ex: The shop tries to entice customers with cheap prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店试图以低价吸引顾客。
words.en: If you entice someone, you attract them to a particular place or activity by making it seem attractive or interesting.

words.tr:
n. 实验；试验；
v. 做试验；进行实验；
words.ex: The boy did a science experiment in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩在课堂上做了一个科学实验。
words.en: An experiment is a scientific procedure undertaken to make a discovery, test a hypothesis, or demonstrate a known fact.

words.tr: v. 骚扰；烦扰；屡次侵扰
words.ex: He harasses his coworkers with loud jokes.
words.ex_cn: 他用大声的笑话骚扰他的同事。
words.en: If someone harasses you, they trouble or annoy you, for example by attacking you repeatedly or by causing you as many problems as they can.

words.tr: n. 燃烧弹；纵火炸弹（一种设计用来引发火灾的爆炸装置）
words.ex: The plane dropped an incendiary bomb on the city.
words.ex_cn: 飞机向城市投下了一枚燃烧弹。
words.en: A bomb designed to cause fires and explosions.

words.tr: n. 弹幕射击；掩护炮火；拦河坝
words.ex: The soldiers faced a barrage of bullets.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们面对着一阵弹雨。
words.en: A barrage is a heavy and continuous bombardment of gunfire or a dam built across a river to control the flow of water.

words.ex: The tree produces a sticky resin.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树会分泌一种粘稠的树脂。
words.en: A sticky substance secreted by some trees, used in varnishes, adhesives, and plastics.

words.tr:
v. 渗出；流出；分泌出
n. 软泥；淤泥；泥浆
words.ex: Mud is oozing from the hole.
words.ex_cn: 泥巴正从洞里渗出来。
words.en: If a liquid oozes from something or if something oozes a liquid, the liquid flows from it slowly and in small quantities.

words.tr: v. 将某物包裹在某物中；把某物嵌入或装入某物内
words.ex: They encased the fragile vase in foam.
words.ex_cn: 他们把易碎的花瓶用泡沫包裹起来。

words.w: the resin oozed out of the tree
words.uk: ðə ˈrezɪn uːzd aʊt əv ðə triː
words.us: ðə ˈrezɪn ud aʊt əv ðə tri
words.ex: The resin oozed out of the tree after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴之后，树脂从树中渗出。

words.tr:
n. 跛子；（身体部分或全部肢体）有缺陷的人
v. 使成瘸子；严重损坏（削弱）
words.ex: The cripple walked slowly with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 那个跛子拄着拐杖慢慢走。
words.en: If someone is crippled by an injury, it is so serious that they can never move their body properly again. A cripple is a person who is severely disabled or unable to walk because of damage to their body.

words.tr:
adj. 有生理缺陷的；残疾的；弱智的
v. 妨碍；使不利；“handicap”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The school made the playground accessible for handicapped children.
words.ex_cn: 学校让操场方便残障儿童使用。
words.en: A handicapped person has a physical or mental disability.

words.tr:
adj. 跛腿的；残废的
v. 使成瘸子；严重损坏（削弱）；“cripple”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The crippled boy walked with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 这个跛腿的男孩拄着拐杖走路。
words.en: If someone is crippled, they are severely injured or disabled, especially in a way that makes it difficult for them to walk or move.

words.tr: adj. 残疾的； v. “disable”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The disabled man uses a wheelchair to move around.
words.ex_cn: 这位残疾人使用轮椅行动。
words.en: If someone is disabled, they are unable to use part of their body or mind properly, for example, because of injury or illness.

words.tr: adj. 无支持的；没有依据的
words.ex: The device is unsupported by the new software.
words.ex_cn: 这个设备不被新软件支持。
words.en: If something is unsupported, it is not supported or proved by evidence or facts.

words.ex: His fear is unfounded.
words.ex_cn: 他的恐惧是没有根据的。
words.en: If you describe a rumour, belief, or feeling as unfounded, you mean that it is wrong because it is not based on facts or evidence.

words.tr: n. 无效字符；不符合规范的字符
words.ex: The system rejected the password because it had invalid characters.
words.ex_cn: 系统拒绝了该密码，因为它包含无效字符。

words.tr: adj. 无力的；虚弱的；阳痿的
words.ex: He felt impotent after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到无能为力。
words.en: If someone feels impotent, they feel that they have no power to influence people or events.

words.tr: v. 创办；建立；“found”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He founded a school for poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一所为贫困儿童设立的学校。
words.en: If someone founds something such as a company, an organization, or an institution, they start it or create it.

words.tr: n. 客观的意见；无偏见的看法
words.ex: The judge gave unbiased opinions about the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官对这个案件给出了客观的意见。

words.ex: The strange noise confounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 奇怪的声音让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: To confuse and surprise someone, especially by being difficult to understand or deal with.

words.tr: adj. 困惑的；糊涂的；讨厌的；惊慌失措的; v. 使混淆（confound 的过去分词）
words.ex: The instructions were so confusing that I was utterly confounded.
