words.en: A tradition is a custom or belief that has existed for a long time among a particular group of people.

words.tr: v. 同意；继承；即位；加入
words.ex: He acceded to their request.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了他们的请求。
words.en: If you accede to someone's request, you do what they ask.

words.ex: The opening chapter introduces the main character.
words.ex_cn: 开篇章节介绍了主要角色。

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.tr: phrase. 分期付款的首次付款；预付定金
words.ex: He made a down payment on a new car.
words.ex_cn: 他为一辆新车付了首付款。
words.en: A down payment is a sum of money that you pay when you are buying something expensive such as a car or a house and cannot pay the full amount immediately. You pay the down payment first and then pay the rest later.

words.ex: He made an initial payment of $500 for the car.
words.ex_cn: 他为这辆车支付了500美元的首付款。

words.tr: phrase. 月付款；按月支付的款项
words.ex: He makes a monthly payment of $200.
words.ex_cn: 他每月支付200美元。
words.en: Monthly payment is a regular sum of money paid each month, typically for services, loans, or subscriptions.

words.ex: He discovered a new planet last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年发现了一颗新行星。
words.en: If you discover something that you did not know about before, you become aware of it or find it.

words.ex: Can you clarify your answer?
words.ex_cn: 你能澄清一下你的答案吗？
words.en: To clarify something means to make it easier to understand by explaining it more clearly.

words.ex: He tried to conceal the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图隐藏真相。
words.en: If you conceal something, you prevent it from being seen or known about.

words.tr:
v. 包括；遮盖；报道；
n. 遮盖物；庇护所；封面；
words.ex: The book covers basic math and science.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包括基础数学和科学。
words.en: If something covers something else, it has been placed over or upon it, usually in order to protect it or hide it.

words.ex: He dedicates his time to helping poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他致力于帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: If you dedicate yourself to something, you give all your attention and effort to it.

words.ex: His dedication to teaching helped many students succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他对教学的奉献帮助了许多学生取得成功。
words.en: The act of dedicating or the state of being dedicated; commitment.

words.tr: adj. 专注的；专用的；献身的； v. 奉献；“dedicate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is dedicated to his studies.
words.ex_cn: 他专注于学习。
words.en: If you say that someone is dedicated to something, you approve of the fact that they have committed to it and are willing to give a lot of time and energy to it.

words.tr: v. 对某事极为尊重；高度重视某事
words.ex: I have great esteem for this old tradition.
words.ex_cn: 我非常尊重这个古老的传统。

words.w: be held in high esteem by somebody
words.uk: biː hɛld ɪn haɪ ɪstɪːm baɪ ˈsʌmˌwʌn
words.us: biː hɛld ɪn haɪ ɪstɪm baɪ ˈsʌmˌwʌn

words.tr: adj. 专心致志于做某事；全心全意致力于做某事

v. 看待；有关；
n. 尊敬；致意；
words.ex: I regard him as a good friend.
words.ex_cn: 我把他看作好朋友。
words.en: If you regard someone or something as being a particular thing or as having a particular quality, you believe that they are that thing or have that quality.

words.tr:
n. 轻视；不尊重
v. 轻视；不尊重
words.ex: He feels disesteem from his coworkers.
words.ex_cn: 他感到同事们轻视他。
words.en: A lack of respect or regard; the state of being held in low esteem.

words.ex: He despises lying.
words.ex_cn: 他鄙视撒谎。
words.en: If you despise something or someone, you dislike them and have a very low opinion of them.

words.ex: He looked at the lie with contempt.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you have contempt for someone or something, you have no respect for them or think that they are unimportant.

words.ex: He detests eating broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌吃西兰花。
words.en: If you detest something, you dislike it intensely.

words.ex: There is a big difference between apples and oranges.
words.ex_cn: 苹果和橙子之间有很大的差异。
words.en: A difference is a way in which two or more things are not the same.

words.ex: There is a disparity in pay between men and women.
words.ex_cn: 男女之间的工资存在差异。
words.en: A disparity between two or more things is a noticeable difference between them.

words.ex: The two countries signed an accord to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项协议以停止战争。
words.en: An accord is an official agreement or treaty. It can also refer to a state of agreement or harmony.

words.ex: The decision was made in accordance with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定是按照规则做出的。
words.en: Agreement or harmony; conformity.

words.tr: n. 大麻吸食者；迷恋大麻的人
words.ex: He is a hophead who smokes marijuana every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每个周末都吸大麻的大麻吸食者。

words.ex: His benevolence helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的仁慈帮助了这个贫困家庭。
words.en: The quality of being well meaning; kindness.

words.ex: Her kindness helped me when I was sad.
words.ex_cn: 当我不开心时，她的善意帮助了我。
words.en: Kindness is the quality of being gentle, caring, and helpful.

words.ex: The malevolent wizard cast a dark spell.
words.ex_cn: 那个有恶意的巫师施了一个黑暗咒语。
words.en: Having or showing a wish to harm others; malicious.

words.ex: He did it out of spite.
words.ex_cn: 他出于恶意做了这件事。
words.en: If you do something out of spite, you do it because you want to hurt or upset someone.

words.ex: The company will downsize next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司下个月将裁员。
words.en: If a company or organization downsizes, it reduces the number of people it employs in order to reduce costs or improve efficiency.

words.ex: The lunar surface is covered with dust.
words.ex_cn: 月球表面覆盖着尘土。
words.en: Of or relating to the moon.

words.ex: The math problem is complicated.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学问题很复杂。
words.en: Involving many different and confusing aspects.

words.tr:
v. 处理；操纵；
n. 把手；柄；
words.ex: He can handle difficult problems easily.
words.ex_cn: 他能轻松处理难题。
words.en: To deal with or control a situation or problem.

words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.tr:
n. 闪耀；闪烁；小发光物
v. 闪耀；闪亮；流露（感情）
words.ex: The glitter of the stars lit up the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星的闪耀照亮了夜空。
words.en: If something glitters, light comes from or is reflected off different parts of it.

words.tr:
v. （突然）烧旺；闪耀；突然爆发；张开；加剧
n. 旺火；亮光
words.ex: The fire began to flare up suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 火突然燃了起来。
words.en: A flare is a sudden bright light or flame, or a sudden increase in something such as activity or trouble.

words.tr:
v. 闪烁；隐约闪现
n. 亮光；闪光
words.ex: The sun gleams on the water.
words.ex_cn: 阳光照在水面上，闪闪发亮。
words.en: A gleam is a small, bright light, especially one that shines for a short time.

words.ex: The wet stone has a soft sheen.
words.ex_cn: 湿石头有柔和的光泽。
words.en: A sheen is a soft, smooth, shiny quality on the surface of something.

words.ex: The candle's flicker lit up the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛的闪现照亮了黑暗的房间。
words.en: If a light or flame flickers, it shines unsteadily.

words.tr: n. 理事会；委员会；议会；
words.ex: The city council made a new rule about recycling.
words.ex_cn: 市政府理事会制定了关于回收的新规定。
words.en: A council is a group of people who are elected to govern a local area such as a city or, in Britain, a county.

words.tr:
n. 蔑视
v. 蔑视
words.ex: He looked at the lie with scorn.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you scorn someone or something, you feel or show contempt for them.

words.tr:
n. 日食；月食；黯然失色
v. 使失色
words.ex: We watched the solar eclipse last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚观看了日食。
words.en: An eclipse occurs when one celestial body moves into the shadow of another, temporarily obscuring it or cutting off its light.

words.ex: The moon turned red during the lunar eclipse.
words.ex_cn: 在月食期间，月亮变成了红色。
words.en: A lunar eclipse occurs when the Earth moves between the Sun and the Moon, blocking the Sun's light from reaching the Moon.

words.ex: He turned the door handle to open the door.
words.ex_cn: 他转动门把手来开门。
words.en: A door handle is a small round object or a lever that is attached to a door and is used to open or close it.

words.ex: I managed to finish my homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 我设法在晚饭前完成了作业。
words.en: To manage means to be in charge of or control something, especially a business or a group of people.

words.ex: The thermostat helps regulate the room temperature.
words.ex_cn: 恒温器有助于调节室温。
words.en: To regulate something means to control or manage it, especially by means of rules or laws.

words.tr: v. 处理不当；使用不当
words.ex: He mishandled the situation and made it worse.
words.ex_cn: 他处理不当，让情况变得更糟。
words.en: If you mishandle something, you deal with it badly or carelessly, often causing problems or damage.

words.tr: n. 媒合；配对；牵线搭桥
words.ex: She works in match-making for older people.
words.ex_cn: 她从事为老年人媒合的工作。

words.tr: phrase. 技术创新；科技革新
words.ex: The company focuses on technological innovation to grow faster.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司专注于技术创新以更快发展。
words.en: The process of translating an idea or invention into a good or service that creates value or for which customers will pay.

words.ex: The government announced a major reform in education.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布了教育方面的重大改革。
words.en: If someone reforms a system, they change or improve it.

words.tr:
adj. 平滑的；平坦的；
v. 使平滑；
words.ex: The glass surface is smooth.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃表面是平滑的。
words.en: Having an even and regular surface or consistency; free from projections, indentations, or roughness.

words.ex: The toy store sells many novelty items for children.
words.ex_cn: 玩具店出售许多为儿童设计的新奇物品。
words.en: The quality of being new, original, or unusual; something new, original, or unusual.

words.ex: The reformation improved the school's teaching methods.
words.ex_cn: 这场革新改善了学校的教学方法。
words.en: The act or process of improving or changing something, especially a system or organization, in order to make it more effective or appropriate.

words.ex: The surface of the table has been smoothed to perfection.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的表面已经被打磨得非常平滑。
words.en: Made smooth or smoother by rubbing or applying a liquid, or having an even and regular surface; free from projections or indentations.

words.tr: v. 散发；发射（光或热）；辐射
words.ex: The sun radiates heat and light.
words.ex_cn: 太阳散发出热量和光。
words.en: To send out rays or waves, especially of light or heat; to spread out from a central point.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: The president convoked an emergency meeting.
words.ex_cn: 总统召集了一次紧急会议。
words.en: To call together for a meeting or assembly.

words.tr: phrase. 安全理事会（通常指联合国安全理事会，负责维护国际和平与安全）
words.ex: The security council voted on the new peace plan.
words.ex_cn: 安全理事会投票通过了新的和平计划。
words.en: A permanent organ of the United Nations responsible for maintaining international peace and security.

words.ex: The teacher gave me feedback on my essay.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了我关于我作文的反馈。
words.en: Feedback is comments in the form of opinions about and reactions to something, intended to provide useful information for future decisions and development.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.ex: The rain was continuous all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都在下个不停。
words.en: Something that is continuous happens or exists without stopping or being interrupted.

words.ex: The plants grow in successional order.
words.ex_cn: 这些植物按 succession 的顺序生长。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by succession; following in order or sequence.

words.ex: He won three successive championships.
words.ex_cn: 他连续赢得了三届冠军。
words.en: Following one after the other without interruption.

words.tr: adj. 随之发生的；作为结果的；
words.ex: The rain was heavy, and the flood was consequent.
words.ex_cn: 雨下得很大，洪水随之发生。
words.en: Following as a result or effect.

words.ex: A shark swam near the beach.
words.ex_cn: 一条鲨鱼在海滩附近游动。
words.en: A shark is a large fish that lives in the sea and has very sharp teeth.

words.tr: adj. 分泌毒液的；有毒的；恶毒的
words.ex: The snake is venomous.
words.ex_cn: 这条蛇是有毒的。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as venomous, you mean that they show great bitterness and anger toward someone.

words.tr:
adj. 智力的；
n. 知识分子；
words.ex: He is an intellectual person who loves solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱解决数学问题的智力型人。
words.en: An intellectual is someone who spends a lot of time studying and thinking about complicated ideas.

words.tr:
n. 压力；（动植物的）品种；
v. 竭力；
words.ex: The job gave him a lot of strain.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作给他带来了很大的压力。
words.en: To strain means to make a great effort to do something, to pull or stretch something tightly, or to injure a muscle by stretching it too much.

words.ex: The doctor used medical terminology to explain the illness.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用医学术语来解释这种疾病。
words.en: The set of terms and expressions used in a particular subject, field, or profession.

words.tr:
adj. 一百年的
n. 百年纪念
words.ex: The city held a centennial parade to celebrate 100 years.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市举行了一场百年游行来庆祝一百周年。
words.en: A centennial is the one-hundredth anniversary of an event, or something that happens every hundred years.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.tr: phrase. 提供反馈；给予意见
words.ex: The teacher will provide feedback on your homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师会为你的作业提供反馈。
words.en: To give comments or advice about someone's work, performance, or behaviour.

words.tr: n. 对某事的反馈；对某事的评价或意见
words.ex: The teacher gave feedback on my essay.
words.ex_cn: 老师对我的作文给出了反馈。

words.tr: v. 实现；执行；实现( implement的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: The school implemented a new reading program.
words.ex_cn: 学校实施了一项新的阅读计划。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.ex: The rain stopped, and subsequent to that, the sun came out.
words.ex_cn: 雨停了，之后太阳出来了。

words.ex: The subsequent events surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 随后的事件让所有人都感到惊讶。

words.ex: He left the party, and subsequently went home.
words.ex_cn: 他离开了派对，随后回家了。
words.en: If something happens subsequently, it happens after something else.

words.tr: v. 大批出没于；成群滋扰；遍布于；寄生
words.ex: The bugs infest the old house.
words.ex_cn: 这些虫子侵袭了这栋老房子。
words.en: If creatures such as insects or rats infest a place, they are present in large numbers and usually cause damage or disease.

words.tr: v. 当心某物；警惕某事
words.ex: Beware of the dog near the gate.
words.ex_cn: 当心门口的狗。

words.tr: phrase. 毒蛇（指能分泌毒液并用毒牙攻击猎物或自卫的蛇类）
words.ex: The venomous snake slithered silently through the grass.
words.ex_cn: n. 毒蛇在草丛中悄无声息地滑行。
words.en: A venomous snake is a snake that uses modified saliva, venom, delivered through fangs to immobilize and digest prey, and for defense.

words.ex: Beware of the dog.
words.ex_cn: 当心那只狗。
words.en: to be cautious and alert to the dangers of.

words.ex: He shows high intelligence in solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决数学问题时表现出很高的智力。
words.en: The ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills.

words.tr: adj. 有才智的；聪明的；明智的；
words.ex: The intelligent boy solved the math problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个有才智的男孩很快解出了这道数学题。
words.en: Someone who is intelligent has the ability to think, understand, and learn things quickly and well.

words.tr: n. 智力测验；智力测试
words.ex: He took an intellectual test to measure his IQ.
words.ex_cn: 他参加了一项智力测验来测量他的智商。

words.ex: He tautened the rope before climbing.
words.ex_cn: 他在爬山前把绳子拉紧了。
words.en: To make or become taut.

words.tr:
adj. 紧张的；拉紧的；
n. 时态；
words.ex: He felt tense before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到紧张。
words.en: If you are tense, you are anxious and nervous and cannot relax.

words.tr: adj. 拉紧的；绷紧的；紧张的
words.ex: The sail was taut in the strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 帆在强风中绷得紧紧的。
words.en: If something such as a rope or wire is taut, it is stretched very tight. If muscles or parts of the body are taut, they are stretched tight, often because of physical effort or anxiety.

words.ex: A bright meteor flashed across the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 一颗明亮的流星划过夜空。
words.en: A meteor is a piece of rock or metal that burns very brightly when it enters the earth's atmosphere from space.

words.ex: He works in meteorology and predicts the weather.
words.ex_cn: 他从事气象学工作，预测天气。
words.en: Meteorology is the scientific study of the atmosphere and of atmospheric conditions, especially as they relate to weather and weather forecasting.

words.tr: n. 科学术语；科学领域的专业术语
words.ex: The book explains scientific terminology in simple words.
words.ex_cn: 这本书用简单的语言解释了科学术语。

words.tr:
n. 地中海；
adj. 地中海的；
words.ex: He sailed across the Mediterranean last summer.
words.ex_cn: 他去年夏天横渡了地中海。
words.en: relating to the Mediterranean Sea or the countries around it

words.ex: He outdid his brother in the math competition.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学竞赛中胜过了他的哥哥。
words.en: To outdo someone means to be more successful than them in a particular activity.

words.ex: The car exceeded the speed limit.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车超过了限速。
words.en: To be greater in quantity, degree, or intensity than something else.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.tr:
n. 纪律；学科；科目；训练；惩戒；
v. 约束自己；
words.ex: The teacher enforced discipline in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师在教室里维持纪律。
words.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

words.ex: The succession of rain made the ground wet.
words.ex_cn: 连续的雨水使地面变湿了。
words.en: A succession of things of the same kind is a number of them that exist or happen one after the other.

words.ex: He fulfilled his promise to help me.
words.ex_cn: 他履行了帮助我的承诺。
words.en: To fulfil means to do something that is expected, hoped for, or promised, or to cause it to happen.

words.ex: Water is made of two elements: hydrogen and oxygen.
words.ex_cn: 水由两种要素组成：氢和氧。
words.en: An element is a substance that cannot be separated into simpler substances by chemical means and is composed of atoms having the same number of protons.

words.ex: This segment of the book is very interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的这一部分非常有趣。
words.en: A segment of something is one of the parts into which it is divided or from which it is formed.

words.ex: He plays violin in a local orchestra.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个本地管弦乐队中拉小提琴。
words.en: An orchestra is a large group of musicians who play a variety of different instruments together. Orchestras usually play classical music.

words.ex: The turtle outlives the rabbit.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟比兔子活得长。
words.en: To live longer than someone else; to survive something.

words.ex: The decision was consequential for the future of the company.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来意义重大。
words.en: Something that is consequential is important or significant, often because it has effects on other things.

words.ex: He didn't study, consequently he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他没有学习，因此考试不及格。
words.en: As a result; therefore.

words.tr: v. 实现自我；充分发挥自己的潜力
words.ex: He paints every day to fulfil himself.
words.ex_cn: 他每天画画来实现自我。

words.ex: The old woman made a prophecy about the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预言了会有雨。
words.en: A prophecy is a statement that something will happen in the future, especially one made by someone with religious or magical powers.

words.tr:
v. 开始燃烧；开始烧
adj. 燃烧的；烧尽的
words.ex: The wood combusts quickly in the fire.
words.ex_cn: 木头在火中迅速燃烧。
words.en: To burn or cause to burn; to consume by fire.

words.tr:
adj. 易燃的；燃烧性的；易激动的
n. 燃质物；可燃物
words.ex: The wood is combustible and burns easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种木头是可燃的，容易燃烧。
words.en: A combustible material or gas catches fire and burns easily.

words.ex: The wood has high combustibility.
words.ex_cn: 这种木材具有很高的可燃性。
words.en: The ease with which a substance can be ignited and burned.

words.ex: Phosphorus is in some fertilizers.
words.ex_cn: 磷存在于一些肥料中。
words.en: Phosphorus is a chemical element with the symbol P and atomic number 15. It is a nonmetal that is essential for life, found in DNA, RNA, ATP, and the phospholipids that form all cell membranes.

words.ex: He is learning elementary math at school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校学习初级数学。
words.en: Elementary means relating to the simplest and most basic aspects of a subject.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.ex: He did a preliminary test before the main experiment.
words.ex_cn: 他在主要实验之前做了一个初步测试。
words.en: Preliminary means something that is done or happens before the main part or event, especially as an introduction or preparation.

words.ex: The essence of love is caring for others.
words.ex_cn: 爱的本质是关心他人。
words.en: The essence of something is its basic and most important characteristic which gives it its individual identity.

words.ex: The worm has a segmented body.
words.ex_cn: 这条蠕虫的身体是分割的。
words.en: Divided into or composed of segments or sections.

words.ex: He strengthened his muscle by lifting weights.
words.ex_cn: 他通过举重来增强肌肉。
words.en: Muscle is the tissue in the body that can contract to produce movement or maintain the position of parts of the body.

words.tr:
n. 功能；职责；
v. 起作用；
words.ex: The function of this button is to turn on the light.
words.ex_cn: 这个按钮的功能是打开灯。
words.en: A function is the purpose that something is designed to have or the job that someone is employed to do. It can also refer to a mathematical relationship or a social event.

words.ex: Calling time a thief is a metaphor.
words.ex_cn: 把时间称为小偷是一种隐喻。
words.en: A metaphor is a figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to an object or action to which it is not literally applicable.

words.ex: The manager will delegate the task to her assistant.
words.ex_cn: 经理将把这个任务委派给她的助手。
words.en: A delegate is a person who is chosen or elected to vote or make decisions on behalf of a group of people, especially at a conference or a meeting. As a verb, to delegate means to give a task or responsibility to another person, especially someone who is less senior than you.

words.tr: adj. 脆弱的；易碎的；不牢固的；
words.ex: The glass is fragile and might break easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃很脆弱，容易碎。
words.en: If something is fragile, it is easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.ex: The glass is brittle and breaks easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃很硬但容易碎。
words.en: If something is brittle, it is hard and easily broken.

words.ex: The old man is frail and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人瘦弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: Someone who is frail is not very strong or healthy.

words.tr: adj. 位于…的；处于…的境地的； v. 使位于；使坐落于；“situate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The house is situated near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子位于湖边。
words.en: If something is situated in a particular place or position, it is in that place or position.

words.ex: The invader came from a faraway land.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者来自一个遥远的地方。
words.en: An invader is someone who enters a place by force in order to conquer or occupy it.

words.tr:
adj. 完整的；完成的；
v. 完成；
words.ex: The book is complete with all chapters.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有所有章节，是完整的。
words.en: If you complete something, you finish doing, making, or producing it.

words.tr: phrase. 肌肉的运动；肌肉的收缩与舒张活动
words.ex: The movement of muscles helps us walk.
words.ex_cn: 肌肉的运动帮助我们行走。
words.en: The action or process of muscles moving or being moved.

words.ex: He exercises his leg muscles every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上锻炼腿部肌肉。

words.ex: He exercises his stomach muscles every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上锻炼腹部肌肉。
words.en: The muscles in the abdominal region, essential for core strength and stability.

words.tr: n. 生命功能；维持生命所必需的功能
words.ex: The heart and lungs perform vital functions.
words.ex_cn: 心脏和肺执行生命功能。

words.tr: n. 公共函数（编程术语，指在类中声明为 public 的函数，可被外部访问）
words.ex: The class has a public function to get the user name.
words.ex_cn: 这个类有一个公共函数用于获取用户名。

words.ex: The poem uses metaphorical language to express love.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗使用隐喻的语言来表达爱。
words.en: Using or containing metaphor; figurative.

words.ex: The manager delegated John to organize the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 经理委派约翰去组织会议。

words.ex: The vase remained intact after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 花瓶从高处摔下后依然完整无缺。
words.en: Something that is intact is complete and has not been damaged or changed.

words.tr: adj. 精致的；微妙的；易碎的；脆弱的；
words.ex: She wore a delicate lace dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精致的蕾丝连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is delicate is small and beautifully shaped. It can also be easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: This glass is unbreakable.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃不易破损。
words.en: If something is unbreakable, it cannot be broken or damaged.

words.ex: The table is made of sturdy wood.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是用坚固的木头做的。
words.en: Someone or something that is sturdy looks strong and is unlikely to be easily injured or damaged.

words.ex: The sun gives off radiation.
words.ex_cn: 太阳发出辐射。
words.en: Radiation is energy that comes from a source and travels through space at the speed of light. This energy has an electric field and a magnetic field associated with it, and has wave-like properties. You could also call radiation 'electromagnetic waves'.

words.ex: He bought a repair kit for his bike.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一套自行车维修工具。
words.en: A kit is a group of items that are kept together, often in the same container, because they are all used for similar purposes.

words.ex: The wind generates electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风产生电力。
words.en: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

words.tr:
adj. 偏远的；久远的；
n. 遥控器；
words.ex: The village is in a remote area far from the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于远离城市的偏远地区。
words.en: Remote areas are far away from cities and places where most people live, and are therefore difficult to get to.

words.ex: He avoids eating sugar to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他避免吃糖以保持健康。
words.en: If you avoid something, you take action in order to prevent it from happening to you.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.ex: His absenteeism caused the team to lose points.
words.ex_cn: 他的缺勤导致团队丢了分数。
words.en: Absenteeism is the habitual non-presence of an employee at their job.

words.ex: It is apparent that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is apparent, it seems to be true, although you cannot be certain that it is.

words.ex: The completion of the project took three months.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的完成花了三个月。
words.en: The act of finishing or making something whole or perfect.

words.ex: He completely forgot his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他完全忘记了钥匙。
words.en: In a way that is whole or entire; to the fullest extent.

words.ex: The plumber fixed the leaky pipe.
words.ex_cn: 水管工修好了漏水的管道。
words.en: A plumber is a person whose job is to connect and repair things such as water and drainage pipes, baths, and toilets.

words.ex: He keeps a first-aid kit in his car.
words.ex_cn: 他把急救包放在车里。
words.en: A first-aid kit is a collection of supplies and equipment that is used to give medical treatment.

words.tr:
v. 猛扭；扭伤；挣脱
n. 扳手；扳钳；（离别的）痛苦
words.ex: He wrenched the door open with all his strength.
words.ex_cn: 他用尽全力猛扭门，把它打开了。
words.en: A wrench is a tool used for gripping and turning nuts, bolts, pipes, etc. It can also refer to a sudden violent twist or pull, or a feeling of sadness or distress caused by separation.

words.tr: adj. 出去滑雪的；外出进行滑雪活动的
words.ex: They are out for skiing this weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他们这个周末出去滑雪。

words.tr: n. 螺丝刀；改锥；螺丝起子；伏特加橙汁鸡尾酒
words.ex: He used a screwdriver to tighten the loose screws.
words.ex_cn: 他用螺丝刀拧紧了松动的螺丝。
words.en: A screwdriver is a tool that is used for turning screws. It has a handle and a long metal part that fits into the top of the screw.

words.tr:
n. 螺丝钉；
v. 拧紧；
words.ex: He tightened the screw with a screwdriver.
words.ex_cn: 他用螺丝刀拧紧了螺丝钉。
words.en: A screw is a metal object similar to a nail, with a raised spiral line around it. Screws are used to fasten things together.

words.tr: 短语动词. 发电；产生电能
words.ex: The windmill can generate electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风车可以发电。
words.en: To produce electrical power, typically from sources like wind, solar, or fossil fuels.

words.ex: My generation grew up with smartphones.
words.ex_cn: 我们这一代人是伴随着智能手机长大的。
words.en: A generation is all the people in a group or country who are of a similar age, especially when they are considered as having the same experiences or attitudes.

words.ex: Lizards can regenerate their tails.
words.ex_cn: 蜥蜴可以再生尾巴。
words.en: To regenerate means to grow or form again, especially after being damaged or lost, or to improve a place or system by making it more active or successful.

words.ex: He uses the remote control to turn on the TV.
words.ex_cn: 他用遥控器打开电视。
words.en: A remote control is a device that allows you to operate a machine or apparatus from a distance, typically by using radio or infrared signals.

words.tr: n. 极小的可能性；几乎不可能发生的事
words.ex: There is a remote chance that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天下雨的可能性极小。

words.tr: n. 极小的可能性；几乎不可能的事
words.ex: There is a remote possibility that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天下雨的可能性极小。

words.tr: phrase. 遥感技术；通过卫星或飞机等远距离平台获取地球表面信息的技术
words.ex: Scientists use remote sensing technology to monitor forests from satellites.
words.ex_cn: 科学家使用遥感技术从卫星上监测森林。
words.en: Remote sensing technology refers to the acquisition of information about an object or phenomenon without making physical contact with the object, typically from aircraft or satellites.

words.ex: They traveled for days to reach a remote village in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他们旅行了几天才到达山里的一个偏远村庄。
words.en: A remote village refers to a small settlement located far away from urban areas, often characterized by limited access to modern amenities and services.

words.ex: He avoids eating too much sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他避免吃太多糖。
words.en: To refrain from performing a specific action.

words.tr: phrase. 避免错误；防止犯错
words.ex: He tries to avoid mistakes in his math homework.
words.ex_cn: 他努力在数学作业中避免错误。
words.en: To take action to prevent errors or incorrect actions.

words.tr: v. 损毁…的外形；使变丑
words.ex: The accident disfigured his face.
words.ex_cn: 那次事故使他的脸变形了。
words.en: To disfigure someone or something means to spoil their appearance.

words.ex: The landscape after the rain is very beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 雨后的景色非常美丽。
words.en: A landscape is all the visible features of an area of land, often considered in terms of their aesthetic appeal.

words.ex: He showed avoidance of difficult math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他回避困难的数学问题。
words.en: The act of keeping away from or preventing something from happening.

words.ex: He was dismissed for being late too often.
words.ex_cn: 他因经常迟到被解雇了。

words.ex: He was absent from school yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天缺席了学校。
words.en: If someone or something is absent from a place or situation where they should be or where they usually are, they are not there.

words.ex: He was an absentee from class yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天缺席了课程。
words.en: A person who is expected or required to be present at a place or event but is not.

words.ex: He succumbed to the illness after a long fight.
words.ex_cn: 经过长期抗争后，他最终死于疾病。
words.en: If you succumb to temptation, pressure, or something such as an illness, you do something that you want to do, or you give in to the pressure or illness, often after a period of trying not to.

words.tr:
v. 伸展；延伸；持续；
n. 一段；伸展；
words.ex: He stretches his arms every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上伸展手臂。
words.en: To stretch is to extend your body or a part of your body to its full length, or to extend something else to its full length or beyond its normal limits.

words.tr:
n. 光；灯；光线；
adj. 轻的；浅的；少量的；明亮的；
v. 点燃；照亮；
words.ex: The light from the window brightened the room.
words.ex_cn: 窗户透进来的光让房间变亮了。
words.en: Light is the natural agent that stimulates sight and makes things visible. It is also used to describe something that is not heavy or a source of illumination.

words.tr:
v. 生气；用烟熏；冒烟
n. 烟雾；烟气；愤怒；烦恼
words.ex: He fumed when he saw the mess.
words.ex_cn: 他看到一团糟时生气了。
words.en: Fume refers to gas, smoke, or vapor that smells strongly or is dangerous to inhale. It can also mean to emit gas, smoke, or vapor, or to be very angry.

words.tr: v. 熏蒸；（为灭虫或消毒而）熏烟
words.ex: They fumigate the house to kill bugs.
words.ex_cn: 他们对房子进行熏蒸以杀死害虫。
words.en: To disinfect or purify an area by exposing it to the fumes of certain chemicals.

words.ex: The injury caused necrosis in the tissue.
words.ex_cn: 受伤导致组织坏死。
words.en: The death of most or all of the cells in an organ or tissue due to disease, injury, or failure of the blood supply.

words.tr: phrase. 连续地；一口气地（指时间或动作不间断）
words.ex: He slept for five hours at a stretch.
words.ex_cn: 他一口气睡了五个钟头。
words.en: If you do something at a stretch, you do it continuously, without stopping.

words.ex: He ran at full stretch to catch the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他尽全力奔跑以赶上公交车。

words.ex: She decided to stretch out on the beach and enjoy the sun.
words.ex_cn: 她决定在沙滩上伸展身体，享受阳光。
words.en: To extend or lengthen one's body or a part of one's body to its full length.

words.tr: v. 延伸；伸展，拉紧；拉长；伸展，拉紧( stretch的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: He stretched his arms to reach the top shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他伸展手臂去够上面的架子。
words.en: Past tense and past participle of stretch: made or became longer or wider, often by pulling.

words.tr: adj. 清淡的；低盐的；精简的
words.ex: This lite beer has fewer calories than the regular one.
words.ex_cn: 这种清淡啤酒的卡路里比普通啤酒少。
words.en: Lite is used to describe something that is lighter or less heavy than usual, especially in terms of weight, calories, or complexity.

words.ex: The minister signed the new law.
words.ex_cn: 部长签署了新法律。
words.en: A minister is a person who is in charge of a particular government department or a member of the clergy in some Christian churches.

words.ex: The combustion of wood produces heat and smoke.
words.ex_cn: 木材的燃烧会产生热量和烟雾。
words.en: Combustion is a chemical process in which a substance reacts with oxygen to give off heat and light.

words.ex: He works at a veterinary clinic.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家兽医诊所工作。
words.en: Relating to the medical or surgical treatment of animals, especially domesticated animals.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.ex: The teacher elucidated the math problem with a simple diagram.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的图表阐明了这道数学题。
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by explaining or giving reasons.

words.ex: The pilot landed the plane safely.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员安全地降落了飞机。
words.en: A pilot is a person who operates the flying controls of an aircraft. Also, to pilot something means to test or introduce a new idea, product, etc., to see if it will be successful.

words.ex: The factory degasify the water before using it.
words.ex_cn: 工厂在使用水之前将其除气。

words.tr: v. 使气化，使变成气体
words.ex: The plant will gasify coal to make electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂将把煤转化为煤气来发电。
words.en: To convert a substance into a gas, especially by applying heat.

words.ex: The process of gasification converts solid fuels into gases.
words.ex_cn: 气化过程将固体燃料转化为气体。
words.en: The process of converting organic or fossil fuel based carbonaceous materials into carbon monoxide, hydrogen, and carbon dioxide.

words.tr: n. 燃烧室；内燃机中燃料燃烧的腔室
words.ex: The engine's combustion chamber gets very hot.
words.ex_cn: 发动机的燃烧室变得非常热。

words.ex: The wood has high combustibility.
words.ex_cn: 这种木材具有很高的可燃性。
words.en: The ease with which a substance can be ignited and burned.

words.ex: The new app is at pilot stage in three schools.
words.ex_cn: 这款新应用在三所学校处于试点阶段。

words.ex: He is a veteran player with many years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位经验丰富的老练球员。
words.en: A veteran is someone who has a lot of experience in a particular field or activity, especially in the armed forces.

words.ex: The veterinarian helps sick animals.
words.ex_cn: 兽医帮助生病的动物。
words.en: A veterinarian is a person who is qualified to treat sick or injured animals.

words.tr:
n. 兽医；
v. 审查；
words.ex: The vet checked the dog's health.
words.ex_cn: 兽医检查了狗的健康状况。
words.en: A vet is a person who is qualified to treat sick or injured animals. As a verb, to vet means to examine something or someone carefully to make sure they are suitable for a particular purpose.

words.tr: phrase. 兽医学；兽医治疗学
words.ex: She decided to study veterinary medicine because of her love for animals.
words.ex_cn: 她因为对动物的热爱决定学习兽医学。
words.en: Veterinary medicine is the branch of medicine that deals with the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of disease, disorder, and injury in animals.

words.tr: n. 检查员；巡视员；视察员；
words.ex: The inspector checked the building for safety.
words.ex_cn: 检查员检查了建筑物的安全性。
words.en: An inspector is a person whose job is to inspect something.

words.ex: The story has plausibility because it feels real.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事有合理性，因为它感觉真实。
words.en: The quality of seeming reasonable or probable.

words.tr: adj. 难以置信的；不像真实的；
words.ex: It seems implausible that he won the lottery twice.
words.ex_cn: 他中了两次彩票，这似乎难以置信。
words.en: If you describe something as implausible, you believe that it is unlikely to be true.

words.ex: The argument was a colorable imitation of the truth.
words.ex_cn: 这个论点是对真相的似是而非的模仿。
words.en: If something is colorable, it can be colored or it is plausible but not necessarily true.

words.tr: adv. 振振有词地；花言巧语地
words.ex: He plausibly explained why he was late.
words.ex_cn: 他合理地解释了自己迟到的原因。
words.en: In a way that seems reasonable or probable.

words.tr: adj. 表面可信的；貌似合理的；可着色的
words.ex: The map is colourable with three colors.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图可以用三种颜色着色。
words.en: Capable of being colored or appearing to have color; often used to describe something that is plausible but not genuine.

words.ex: The actual cost was lower than expected.
words.ex_cn: 实际成本比预期的低。
words.en: You use actual to emphasize that you are referring to something real or genuine.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.tr: v. 通过；递给；“pass”的现在分词； n. 流逝；通过； adj. 经过的；短暂的；过往的；
words.ex: He is passing the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他正在通过考试。
words.en: Going past or moving from one place to another; the act of passing something.

words.ex: He took a temporary job during summer.
words.ex_cn: 他在暑假期间做了一份短暂的工作。
words.en: Something that is temporary lasts for only a limited time.

words.tr: n. 公共卫生；卫生设施；
words.ex: The city improved sanitation to keep people healthy.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市改善了公共卫生以保障人民健康。
words.en: The conditions and processes that help maintain health and prevent disease, especially through cleanliness.

words.tr: n. 扭曲；歪曲；失真；畸变；
words.ex: The photo showed distortion in the lines.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片中的线条出现了扭曲。
words.en: A distortion is a change, twist, or exaggeration that makes something appear different from the way it really is.

words.ex: He gave his last dollar to the homeless man, showing an altruistic heart.
words.ex_cn: 他把最后一美元给了那个无家可归的人，表现出一颗无私的心。
words.en: If you describe someone as altruistic, you mean that they show unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

words.ex: She is selfless and always helps others.
words.ex_cn: 她很无私，总是帮助别人。
words.en: If you say that someone is selfless, you approve of them because they care about other people more than themselves.

words.ex: The climate in summer is very hot.
words.ex_cn: 夏天的气候非常炎热。
words.en: The climate of a place is the general weather conditions that are typical of it.

words.ex: The climatic changes affect the crops.
words.ex_cn: 气候的变化影响农作物。
words.en: Relating to the climate or weather conditions of a particular area.

words.tr: adj. 务实的；实事求是的；
words.ex: He took a pragmatic approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他采取了务实的方法来解决问题。
words.en: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way that is based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.

words.ex: The water in the pond dwindles in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天时，池塘里的水逐渐减少。
words.en: If something dwindles, it becomes smaller, weaker, or less in number.

words.ex: The company will downsize next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司下个月将裁员。
words.en: If a company or organization downsizes, it reduces the number of people it employs in order to reduce costs or improve efficiency.

words.ex: The noise will diminish after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜后噪音会减少。
words.en: If something diminishes, or if something diminishes it, it becomes reduced in size, importance, or intensity.

words.ex: He showed disdain for the lazy students.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些懒惰的学生表现出蔑视。
words.en: If you feel disdain for someone or something, you dislike them because you think that they are inferior or unimportant.

words.ex: He looked at the lie with contempt.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you have contempt for someone or something, you have no respect for them or think that they are unimportant.

words.ex: He despises lying.
words.ex_cn: 他鄙视撒谎。
words.en: If you despise something or someone, you dislike them and have a very low opinion of them.

words.ex: Some people look down upon others who have less money.
words.ex_cn: 有些人瞧不起那些钱少的人。
words.en: To regard someone or something as inferior or unworthy of respect.

words.tr:
n. 蔑视
v. 蔑视
words.ex: He looked at the lie with scorn.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you scorn someone or something, you feel or show contempt for them.

words.ex: The dog has a long pedigree from champion lines.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗有着来自冠军血统的悠久血统。
words.en: A pedigree is the recorded ancestry or lineage of a person or animal, often used to indicate purity of breed or high social status.

words.ex: The plane began its descent at 10,000 feet.
words.ex_cn: 飞机在一万英尺高度开始下降。
words.en: The act of moving or falling downward.

words.ex: He made a permanent change to his lifestyle.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的生活方式做出了永久的改变。
words.en: Something that is permanent exists or happens all the time, or exists for a long time without changing.

words.ex: The machine makes a perpetual noise.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器发出持续的噪音。
words.en: Something that is perpetual continues indefinitely or for a very long time without interruption.

words.ex: The nurse will sanitate the wound with clean water.
words.ex_cn: 护士会用干净的水清洁伤口。
words.en: To make sanitary; to clean or sterilize.

words.ex: His altruistic act of donating his entire salary to charity inspired many.
words.ex_cn: n. 他将全部工资捐给慈善机构的利他行为激励了许多人。
words.en: An altruistic act is a selfless action performed to benefit others without expecting anything in return.

words.ex: El Niño is a climatic phenomenon that affects weather worldwide.
words.ex_cn: 厄尔尼诺是一种影响全球天气的气候现象。

words.tr: v. 逐渐减少到；逐步缩减至
words.ex: The water in the bottle dwindled down to a few drops.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子里的水逐渐减少到只剩几滴。

words.tr: v. 逐渐消失；渐渐枯竭
words.ex: The sound of the music dwindled out as the night grew quiet.
words.ex_cn: 随着夜晚变得安静，音乐声逐渐消失了。

words.ex: The sun descends behind the hills.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在山后落下。
words.en: If you descend or if you descend a staircase, you move downwards from a higher to a lower level.

words.tr:
n. 成分；
adj. 构成的；
words.ex: Sugar is a constituent of soda.
words.ex_cn: 糖是苏打水的一种成分。
words.en: A constituent is a part of a whole. In politics, a constituent is a person who is represented by an elected official.

words.ex: The politician lost his constituency after the scandal.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客在丑闻后失去了他的支持者。
words.en: A constituency is a group of people in a country or area who are entitled to vote in an election, or the area itself.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.tr: n. 推进剂；发射药；火箭燃料
words.ex: The rocket uses a strong propellant to fly.
words.ex_cn: 火箭使用一种强大的推进剂来飞行。
words.en: A propellant is a substance that is used to move something forward, especially a rocket or a bullet, by creating a force that pushes it.

words.tr:
n. 鞭策；
v. 刺激；
words.ex: The competition served as a spur to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 竞争成了推动他更努力工作的鞭策。
words.en: A spur is something that makes you want to do something or that encourages you to do it. It can also refer to a sharp device worn on the heel of a rider's boot to urge a horse forward.

words.ex: The clay is malleable and easy to shape.
words.ex_cn: 这种黏土是可塑的，容易塑形。
words.en: If you say that someone is malleable, you mean that they are easily influenced or controlled by other people.

words.ex: The clay is mouldable when wet.
words.ex_cn: 当泥土是湿的时候，它是可塑的。
words.en: Capable of being shaped or formed.

words.ex: The renaissance brought new art and ideas to Europe.
words.ex_cn: 文艺复兴为欧洲带来了新的艺术和思想。
words.en: The Renaissance was a period in European history marking the transition from the Middle Ages to modernity and covering the 15th and 16th centuries, characterized by an effort to revive and surpass ideas and achievements of classical antiquity.

words.ex: The pink hat on the man looked like an incongruity.
words.ex_cn: 男人头上的粉红色帽子显得很不协调。
words.en: The state of being incongruous; incompatibility.

words.ex: The discordance between their opinions made the meeting very tense.
words.ex_cn: 他们意见之间的不一致使会议变得非常紧张。
words.en: Lack of agreement or harmony between people or things.

words.tr: adj. 不调和的；不一致的；不和谐的
words.ex: The two voices sounded discordant.
words.ex_cn: 这两声音听起来不和谐。
words.en: Something that is discordant is strange or unpleasant because it does not fit in with other things.

words.ex: Birds build nests by instinctual behavior.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类通过本能行为筑巢。
words.en: Relating to or prompted by instinct; done without conscious thought.

words.tr:
v. 扭打；混战
n. 扭打；混战
words.ex: The two boys had a scuffle over the ball.
words.ex_cn: 两个男孩为了球打了一架。
words.en: A scuffle is a short, confused fight or struggle at close quarters.

words.ex: Five apples constitute a basket.
words.ex_cn: 五个苹果构成一篮子。
words.en: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

words.ex: The constitution protects the rights of all citizens.
words.ex_cn: 宪法保护所有公民的权利。
words.en: The constitution of a country or organization is the system of laws which formally states people's rights and duties.

words.ex: He is studying constitutional law at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习宪法。
words.en: Relating to the constitution of a country or organization; in accordance with a political constitution.

words.ex: The assembly of the car took three days.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的装配花了三天时间。
words.en: An assembly is a group of people gathered together for a particular purpose, such as a meeting or a legislative session. It can also refer to the process of fitting together the component parts of a machine or other object.

words.tr: n. 制宪会议；制宪议会
words.ex: The constituent assembly wrote the new constitution.
words.ex_cn: 制宪会议起草了新宪法。

words.ex: A car has many components, like wheels and engines.
words.ex_cn: 汽车有许多部分，比如轮子和发动机。
words.en: A component is a part of a larger whole, especially a part that can be separated from or attached to a system.

words.ex: The insider told the news about the company's plan.
words.ex_cn: 这位局内人透露了公司计划的消息。
words.en: An insider is someone who is a member of a group or organization, and therefore has special knowledge about it.

words.ex: He tried to curb his horse with the reins.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用缰绳勒住马。
words.en: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

words.ex: He made an impetuous decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他冲动地决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impetuous, you mean that they are likely to act quickly and suddenly without thinking or being careful.

words.tr: adj. 凭冲动行事的；易冲动的
words.ex: He made an impulsive decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他一时冲动决定辞掉工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impulsive, you mean that they do things suddenly without thinking about them carefully first.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；性急的；易激动的
words.ex: He was too hotheaded to make a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 他太性急了，不适合做领导。
words.en: If you describe someone as hotheaded, you are criticizing them for acting too quickly, without thinking of the consequences.

words.tr: n. 少许；小块；片刻； v. “bite”的过去式；
words.ex: Can you give me a bit of sugar?
words.ex_cn: 你能给我一点点糖吗？
words.en: A bit is a small piece or quantity of something.

words.tr: v. 使粉碎；使破碎；使破灭；
words.ex: The stone shattered when it hit the ground.
words.ex_cn: 石头撞到地面时碎裂了。
words.en: If something shatters or is shattered, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.ex: He only understood bits of the story.
words.ex_cn: 他只理解了这个故事的一部分。
words.en: A bit is a small piece or amount of something, or the smallest unit of information in a computer.

words.ex: The revival of traditional music brought joy to many people.
words.ex_cn: 传统音乐的复兴给许多人带来了快乐。
words.en: The process of something becoming popular or active again after a period of inactivity or decline.

words.ex: The renewal of the contract took one week.
words.ex_cn: 合同的更新花了一周时间。
words.en: The act of making something valid for a further period of time after it has expired or been canceled.

words.ex: The idea of a resurgence in national pride began to take hold.
words.ex_cn: 民族自豪感复兴的想法开始深入人心。
words.en: If something resurges, it becomes stronger or more popular again after a period of being weak or not popular.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.ex: The decision was made in accordance with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定是按照规则做出的。
words.en: Agreement or harmony; conformity.

words.tr: v. （使）窒息而死；使呼吸困难；闷死
words.ex: The smoke is suffocating him.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾正在让他窒息。
words.en: To cause someone to die or to make it difficult for someone to breathe by preventing air from reaching the lungs.

words.ex: He wrote a treatise on ancient Chinese philosophy.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一部关于中国古代哲学的专著。
words.en: A treatise is a formal and systematic written discourse on some subject, generally longer and more detailed than an essay.

words.ex: It is a hypothetical situation.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个假设的情况。
words.en: A hypothetical situation, idea, or explanation is based on possible ideas or situations rather than actual ones.

words.tr: v. 厚厚地覆盖；使…窒息；闷死
words.ex: He tried to smother the fire with a blanket.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用毯子把火闷灭。
words.en: To smother someone or something means to kill them by covering their face so that they cannot breathe, or to put out a fire by covering it.

words.ex: The thief tried to choke the old man to death.
words.ex_cn: 小偷试图把老人掐死。

words.ex: He tried to strangle his enemy with a rope.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用绳子勒死他的敌人。
words.en: To strangle someone means to kill them by squeezing their throat tightly so that they cannot breathe.

words.tr:
n. 过量；过度；超过；
adj. 多余的；
words.ex: The excess of sugar in his diet caused health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他饮食中糖分过量导致了健康问题。
words.en: An excess of something is a larger amount than is needed, allowed, or usual.

words.ex: The boy hurt his spine when he fell from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 他从树上摔下来时伤到了脊柱。
words.en: The spine is the row of bones down the center of your back that supports your body and protects your spinal cord.

words.tr:
n. 压力；强调；
v. 着重；强调；
words.ex: He feels stress from too much work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为工作太多而感到压力。
words.en: Stress is a state of mental or emotional strain or tension resulting from adverse or demanding circumstances.

words.ex: She accentuates the first syllable when she says the word.
words.ex_cn: 她说这个词时重读第一个音节。
words.en: To accentuate something means to emphasize it or make it more noticeable.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.tr:
v. 突出；强调；高光；
n. 最突出的部分；
words.ex: The teacher highlighted the key words in the text.
words.ex_cn: 老师把文中的关键词突出了。
words.en: To highlight something means to make it stand out or to emphasize it, often because it is important or interesting.

words.ex: He emphasizes the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 他强调作业的重要性。
words.en: To give special importance or prominence to (something) in speaking or writing.

words.tr:
adj. 平滑的；平坦的；
v. 使平滑；
words.ex: The glass surface is smooth.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃表面是平滑的。
words.en: Having an even and regular surface or consistency; free from projections, indentations, or roughness.

words.ex: He incurred a fine for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他因超速而招致了一笔罚款。
words.en: If you incur something unpleasant, it happens to you because of something you have done.

words.tr:
v. 咯咯地笑
n. 咯咯笑；趣事
words.ex: The children giggle when they see the clown.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到小丑时咯咯笑。
words.en: To laugh in a silly, often high-pitched way, especially in a nervous or embarrassed manner.

words.tr:
v. 轻声笑；咯咯笑；暗自笑
n. 暗自发笑；咯咯声
words.ex: He chuckled when he saw the funny dog.
words.ex_cn: 他看到那只搞笑的狗时笑了起来。
words.en: To laugh quietly or inwardly.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

words.tr: v. 扔；抛；丢掷；放弃；离职
words.ex: He chucked the old book into the bin.
words.ex_cn: 他把那本旧书扔进了垃圾桶。
words.en: To throw something carelessly or casually; to give up or stop doing something.

words.tr: n. 涂层； v. “coat”的现在分词；
words.ex: The metal has a protective coating.
words.ex_cn: 这种金属有一层保护涂层。
words.en: A coating is a layer of a substance spread over a surface for protection or decoration.

words.tr: phrase. 超重行李；多余的负担（比喻义）
words.ex: He decided to leave behind his excess baggage before starting a new life.
words.ex_cn: 在开始新生活之前，他决定放下累赘。
words.en: Excess baggage refers to luggage that exceeds the weight or size limit allowed by an airline or other transport service without additional charges.

words.ex: He ate excessive amounts of candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了过多的糖果。
words.en: If you describe the amount or level of something as excessive, you disapprove of it because it is more or higher than is necessary or reasonable.

words.ex: He eats excessively sweets.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多甜食。
words.en: To an excessive degree; more than is necessary, normal, or desirable; inordinately.

words.ex: The weather is exceedingly cold today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气极其寒冷。
words.en: To a very great degree; extremely.

words.ex: He hurt his spinal cord in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中伤到了脊髓。
words.en: Relating to the spine or the spinal cord.

words.ex: He is the backbone of the team.
words.ex_cn: 他是团队的中坚。
words.en: The backbone is the most important part of something, providing support and strength.

words.ex: He handed out a leaflet about the event.
words.ex_cn: 他分发了一份关于该活动的传单。
words.en: A leaflet is a small sheet of printed paper that gives you information or advertises something.

words.ex: He wrote his name on a sheet of paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在一张纸上写了名字。
words.en: A sheet is a large piece of thin cloth used on a bed to lie on or under. It can also refer to a flat, thin piece of material, such as paper, metal, or glass.

words.tr:
adj. 手工的；体力的；
n. 说明书；
words.ex: He made a manual copy of the letter.
words.ex_cn: 他手工抄写了一封信。
words.en: A manual is a book which tells you how to do something or how a piece of machinery works.

words.ex: He handed me a pamphlet about the new park.
words.ex_cn: 他递给我一份关于新公园的小册子。
words.en: A pamphlet is a small book containing information on a particular subject or expressing political or religious views.

words.tr: phrase. 大量存在；充满；富于（某物）
words.ex: The forest abounds with birds and animals.
words.ex_cn: 森林里到处都是鸟和动物。
words.en: If things abound, or if a place abounds with things, there are very large numbers of them.

words.tr: phrase. 压力管理；应对压力的技巧与方法
words.ex: He practices yoga for stress management.
words.ex_cn: 他练习瑜伽来管理压力。
words.en: Stress management refers to the wide spectrum of techniques and psychotherapies aimed at controlling a person's levels of stress, especially chronic stress, usually for the purpose of improving everyday functioning.

words.ex: I paid the electric bill yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 我昨天付了电费账单。
words.en: A bill is a statement of money owed for goods or services, a proposed law presented to a legislature for approval, a piece of paper money, or the beak of a bird.

words.tr:
v. 转移；转让；调任；
n. 转移；转让；调任；
words.ex: He will transfer the money to his bank account.
words.ex_cn: 他将把钱转到他的银行账户。
words.en: If you transfer something or someone from one place to another, or they transfer from one place to another, they go from the first place to the second.

words.ex: The radio transmits music to listeners.
words.ex_cn: 收音机将音乐传递给听众。
words.en: To send or pass something from one person, place, or thing to another.

words.tr: n. 政治权力的平稳过渡
words.ex: The country achieved a smooth transfer of political power after the election.
words.ex_cn: 该国在选举后实现了政治权力的平稳过渡。

words.tr: n. 通过；通道；段落；短文；
words.ex: The passage of the train through the tunnel was quick.
words.ex_cn: 火车通过隧道的速度很快。
words.en: A passage is a long narrow space with walls or fences on both sides, which connects one place or room with another.

words.tr: phrase. 负债；产生债务；招致欠款
words.ex: If you spend more than you earn, you will incur debt.
words.ex_cn: v. 如果你花的比赚的多，你就会负债。
words.en: To incur debt means to become liable for or to take on debt, often as a result of borrowing money or making purchases on credit.

words.tr: v. 遭受损失；蒙受亏损
words.ex: The company incurred losses last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年遭受了损失。

words.ex: He went overdrawn on his bank account.
words.ex_cn: 他的银行账户透支了。
words.en: An overdraft occurs when money is withdrawn from a bank account and the available balance goes below zero.

words.tr: v. 透支；过度往后拉；过分描述
words.ex: He overdraws his bank account every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月都透支银行账户。
words.en: To overdraw means to withdraw more money from a bank account than the account holds, resulting in a negative balance. It can also mean to exaggerate or embellish in description or representation.

words.ex: The army launched a missile at the target.
words.ex_cn: 军队向目标发射了一枚导弹。
words.en: A missile is a weapon that is sent through the air and that explodes when it hits the thing it is aimed at.

words.tr: adv. 强制性地；禁不住地
words.ex: He checks his phone compulsively.
words.ex_cn: 他 compulsively 地查看手机。
words.en: If someone behaves compulsively, they have a very strong desire to do something and cannot stop themselves from doing it.

words.ex: She bought a warm wrap for the winter.
words.ex_cn: 她买了一件保暖的包裹（披肩）过冬。
words.en: To cover or enclose something in paper, cloth, or other material.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: He tries to restrain his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他努力克制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you restrain someone, you stop them from doing what they intended or wanted to do, usually by using your physical strength.

words.ex: The limitation of the phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的限制是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A limitation is a rule or situation that restricts what you can do or what can happen.

words.ex: The bike has a metal chain.
words.ex_cn: 这辆自行车有一条金属链条。
words.en: A chain consists of connected links which are typically made of metal, used for fastening or securing something, or for transmitting mechanical power.

words.tr:
n. 纸片；
v. 滑倒；溜走；
words.ex: She found a slip of paper on the table.
words.ex_cn: 她在桌子上发现了一张纸片。
words.en: If you slip, you accidentally slide and lose your balance.

words.tr:
n. 一小口；
v. 呷；啜；小口喝；
words.ex: He took a sip of water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一小口水。
words.en: To drink something slowly by taking small amounts into your mouth.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.tr: adj. 无聊的；令人厌倦的； v. “bore”的现在分词；
words.ex: The movie was boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很无聊。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as boring, you mean that they are not interesting and make you feel tired or impatient.

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.ex: He is studying pathology to understand diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习病理学以了解疾病。
words.en: Pathology is the study of the causes and effects of diseases, especially the branch of medicine that deals with the laboratory examination of samples of body tissue for diagnostic or forensic purposes.

words.tr: n. 弥赛亚（犹太人所期待的救世主）；救世主
words.ex: Many Jews are still waiting for the coming of the Messiah.
words.ex_cn: 许多犹太人仍在等待弥赛亚的到来。
words.en: In Judaism and Christianity, the messiah is the savior or liberator of a group of people, believed to be sent by God.

words.ex: He grinds the coffee beans into powder.
words.ex_cn: 他把咖啡豆碾成粉末。
words.en: To reduce something to small particles or powder by crushing it.

words.ex: He grinds his teeth when he is stressed.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到压力时，他会磨牙。

words.tr: adj. 无法控制行为的；禁不住的；
words.ex: He has a compulsive habit of checking the door lock.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种无法控制地检查门锁的习惯。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as compulsive, you mean that they cannot stop themselves doing or wanting something, even though it may be harmful or unreasonable.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet is compulsory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是必须的。
words.en: If something is compulsory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.tr: adj. 强制性的；义务的；必须的；
words.ex: Wearing a helmet is obligatory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是强制性的。
words.en: If something is obligatory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.ex: The athlete wore a mouthguard to protect his teeth during the game.
words.ex_cn: 运动员在比赛中戴上防护牙托以保护牙齿。
words.en: A protective device for the mouth that covers the teeth and gums to prevent injury during sports or other activities.

words.tr: phrase. 给（钟表等）上发条；使紧张；结束；最终导致
words.ex: He will wind up the clock every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都会给钟上发条。
words.en: To bring something to an end; to coil or twist something; to make someone nervous or excited.

words.tr: phrase. 结束；告终；意外到达
words.ex: He didn't plan to stay, but he ended up sleeping there.
words.ex_cn: 他本没打算留下，但最后在那里睡了。
words.en: If you end up in a particular place or situation, you are in that place or situation after a series of events, even though you did not originally intend to be.

words.tr: v. 被限制在某事物中；局限于某范围
在某物的界限之间；局限于某物的范围之内
words.ex: The children played between the confines of the fence.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在篱笆的界限之间玩耍。

words.tr: adv. 超出某物的范围或界限；超越某物的限制
words.ex: The birds flew beyond the confines of the forest.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿飞出了森林的范围。

words.tr: v. 限制自己做某事；局限于某事物
words.ex: He confined himself to reading books every night.
words.ex_cn: 他限制自己每天晚上只读书。

words.ex: The lion is at the top of the food chain.
words.ex_cn: 狮子处于食物链的顶端。
words.en: A food chain is a series of organisms each dependent on the next as a source of food.

words.ex: He told me a tedious story that made me fall asleep.
words.ex_cn: 他给我讲了一个枯燥乏味的故事，让我睡着了。

words.tr: v. 设置；放；“set”的现在分词； n. 环境；背景；
words.ex: He is setting the alarm for 6 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他正在把闹钟设置为早上6点。
words.en: The context and environment in which something is set or takes place.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.ex: The aridity of the desert makes it hard for plants to grow.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的干旱使植物难以生长。
words.en: Aridity is the state of being extremely dry, especially due to lack of rainfall.

words.ex: The drought made it hard to grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 旱灾使种植庄稼变得困难。
words.en: A drought is a long period of time during which no rain falls and hence there is a shortage of water.

words.ex: She has excellent night vision.
words.ex_cn: 她有很好的夜视能力。
words.en: Vision is the ability to see, the area that you can see, the ability to imagine how a country, society, industry, etc. could develop in the future and to plan in a suitable way, or an experience in which you see something that is not really there.

words.tr: n. 生物体；有机体；有机组织；
words.ex: A bacterium is a simple organism.
words.ex_cn: 细菌是一种简单的生物体。
words.en: An organism is a living thing that has an organized structure, can react to stimuli, reproduce, grow, adapt, and maintain homeostasis.

words.ex: The police used surveillance to watch the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察使用监视来观察那栋大楼。
words.en: The careful watching of a person or place, especially by the police or army, because of a crime that has happened or is expected.

words.tr:
adj. 资深的；高级的；年长的；
n. 年长者；大四学生；
words.ex: He is a senior engineer with 20 years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有20年经验的资深工程师。
words.en: Higher in rank, status, or importance; older in age.

words.ex: His answer was vague and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答不明确，难以理解。
words.en: If something written or spoken is vague, it does not explain or express things clearly.

words.tr:
adj. 有图画的；图示的
n. 画报
words.ex: The book has a pictorial guide to plants.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有一本植物的图解指南。
words.en: A pictorial representation or image is one that is made using pictures or shows things in a way that pictures do.

words.ex: The village by the lake is picturesque.
words.ex_cn: 湖边的村庄如画般美丽。
words.en: A picturesque place is attractive and interesting, especially in a way that is old-fashioned or unusual.

words.ex: He extinguished the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水把火扑灭了。
words.en: To extinguish a fire or a light means to stop it burning or shining.

words.tr: phrase. 扑灭；熄掉；伸出；发表；恼怒
words.ex: He put out the fire with a blanket.
words.ex_cn: 他用毯子扑灭了火。
words.en: To extinguish a fire or light; to publish or produce something; to extend or stretch out something.

words.ex: The extinct volcano has no lava now.
words.ex_cn: 这座死火山现在没有熔岩。
words.en: An extinct volcano is a volcano that is not expected to erupt again.

words.ex: The extinction of dinosaurs happened millions of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙的灭绝发生在数百万年前。
words.en: The state or process of a species, family, or larger group being or becoming extinct.

words.tr: adj. 繁荣的；旺盛的；兴旺的； v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；“thrive”的现在分词；
words.ex: The town is thriving because of its new factories.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇因为新的工厂而繁荣。
words.en: Prospering or flourishing; successful.

words.ex: The arid land has little rain and no trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片干旱的土地降雨稀少，没有树木。
words.en: An arid area of land has so little rain that it is very dry and cannot support much vegetation.

words.tr: n. （宗教等的）仪式；例行习惯；
words.ex: The village holds a ritual every spring to pray for good weather.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一个仪式，祈求好天气。
words.en: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

words.tr: adj. 虚拟的；几乎的；实际上的；事实上的；
words.ex: He played a virtual game on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他在电脑上玩了一个虚拟游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as virtual, you mean that it is so nearly true that for most purposes it can be regarded as true.

words.ex: The children learned through visual aids like pictures.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们通过图片等视觉辅助工具学习。
words.en: relating to seeing or to the eyes

words.tr: adj. 眼的；视觉的；光学的
words.ex: He wears optic glasses to see clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他戴光学眼镜以便看得清楚。
words.en: Relating to the eye or vision.

words.ex: Honesty is a great virtue.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种伟大的美德。
words.en: A virtue is a good quality or way of behaving.

words.tr: adj. 品行端正的；品德高的；
words.ex: He is a virtuous man who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个品行端正的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Having or showing high moral standards.

words.ex: She buys organic vegetables at the market.
words.ex_cn: 她在市场上买有机蔬菜。
words.en: Relating to or derived from living matter; denoting or characterized by a harmonious relationship between the elements of a whole.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.ex: The river water looked murky after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，河水看起来污浊。
words.en: If you describe something as murky, you mean that the details of it are not clear or that it is difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.ex: He can translate words into pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他能把词语转化为图画。
words.en: To translate means to change written or spoken words from one language into another, or to explain something in a way that is easier to understand.

words.ex: Many children suffer from poverty in poor countries.
words.ex_cn: 许多孩子在贫穷国家遭受贫困。
words.en: Poverty is the state of being extremely poor.

words.ex: He lived in indigence after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后生活贫困。
words.en: Indigence is the state of being extremely poor.

words.tr: n. 贫穷；致使贫乏或贫瘠之事物
words.ex: The war caused great impoverishment in the region.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争使该地区陷入极度贫困。
words.en: The act of making someone or something poor or in a worse condition.

words.ex: He will modify the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会更改计划。
words.en: To change something slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose.

words.tr:
adv. 顺时针方向地
adj. 顺时针方向的
words.ex: Turn the knob clockwise to open the jar.
words.ex_cn: 顺时针转动旋钮来打开罐子。
words.en: Moving in the same direction as the hands of a clock.

words.ex: The hospital will isolate the patient to stop the spread.
words.ex_cn: 医院将隔离这名病人以防止传播。
words.en: To isolate someone or something means to separate them from other people or things, often in order to protect them or to prevent the spread of something harmful.

words.ex: The teacher underlined the key point.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了这个关键点。
words.en: To draw a line under a word or phrase, especially in order to emphasize it.

words.ex: The teacher put emphasis on reading every day.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调每天都要阅读。
words.en: Special importance, value, or prominence given to something.

words.ex: The soil is moist after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后土壤是潮湿的。
words.en: Slightly wet; damp or humid.

words.ex: He threatened to call the police.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁要叫警察。
words.en: If someone threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.

words.ex: The broken bridge is a menace to drivers.
words.ex_cn: 这座破桥对司机来说是个危险物。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a menace, you mean that they are likely to cause serious harm.

words.ex: The manager yelled at his underling for making a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 经理因为下属犯了错误而对他大喊大叫。
words.en: An underling is a person who is lower in rank or position than someone else, especially in a work environment.

words.ex: The village suffered from famine last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个村庄遭受了饥荒。
words.en: A famine is a serious shortage of food in a country, which may cause many people to get sick or die.

words.tr: phrase. 生活在贫困中；过着贫穷的生活
words.ex: Many families live in poverty in rural areas.
words.ex_cn: 许多家庭在农村地区生活在贫困中。
words.en: To exist in a state of having little or no money and few or no material possessions.

words.tr: phrase. 贫困线；最低生活标准线
words.ex: Many families live below the poverty line.
words.ex_cn: 许多家庭生活在贫困线以下。
words.en: The poverty line is the minimum level of income deemed adequate in a particular country.

words.tr: phrase. 对抗贫困；与贫穷作斗争
words.ex: Governments around the world are implementing policies to combat poverty.
words.ex_cn: 世界各国政府正在实施政策以与贫困作斗争。
words.en: To fight against poverty; to take action to reduce or eliminate poverty.

words.ex: The soil has too much moisture.
words.ex_cn: 土壤中有太多湿气。
words.en: Moisture is tiny drops of water in the air, on a surface, or in a substance, that make it feel wet.

words.tr: phrase. 被以……相威胁；面临……的威胁
words.ex: He was threatened with fire if he did not leave.
words.ex_cn: 如果他不离开，就会被威胁用火烧他。
words.en: To be in a situation where someone or something is at risk of harm or danger.

words.ex: This small enterprise makes handmade toys.
words.ex_cn: 这家小企业生产手工玩具。
words.en: An enterprise is a company or business, often a large one, or a difficult or important project, especially one that involves a lot of planning and organization.

words.ex: The corporation sells smartphones worldwide.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司向全球销售智能手机。
words.en: A corporation is a large company or group of companies that is controlled together as a single organization.

words.ex: The corporate office is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的总部在纽约。
words.en: Corporate relates to large companies or to a particular large company.

words.tr: v. 构成…的基础（或起因）
words.ex: Poor diet underlies many health problems.
words.ex_cn: 不良饮食是许多健康问题的根源。
words.en: If something underlies a situation or activity, it is the cause or basis of it.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；潜在的； v. “underlie”的现在分词；
words.ex: The underlying cause of the problem is poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的根本原因是贫困。
words.en: An underlying thing is the thing that is the most important or basic, although it is not easily noticed or stated directly.

words.ex: The latent talent in the child became clear after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子潜在的才能在多年练习后显现出来。
words.en: Latent is used to describe something which is hidden and not obvious at the moment, but which may develop further in the future.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.ex: He noticed every detail of the painting.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了这幅画的每一个细节。
words.en: A detail is a small individual feature or element of something.

words.ex: He compiles data from many surveys.
words.ex_cn: 他汇编来自许多调查的数据。
words.en: To compile means to collect information from different places and arrange it in a book, report, or list.

words.ex: The induction of the new mayor will be held next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 新市长的就职典礼将在下周一举行。
words.en: Induction is the process or action of inducting someone to a position or organization, or the process of reasoning from specific cases to general rules.

words.tr:
n. 连接物；
v. 连接；联系；
words.ex: The chain has a broken link.
words.ex_cn: 这条链子有一个断了的连接物。
words.en: A link between two people, organizations, or places is a connection between them.

words.ex: The fishermen walk on the foreland at low tide.
words.ex_cn: 渔民在低潮时走在前沿地上。
words.en: A foreland is a piece of land that juts out into the sea, often forming a cape or headland.

words.ex: The town is near the frontier of the country.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇靠近国家的边境。
words.en: A frontier is a border between two countries or the area close to it. It can also refer to the limit of knowledge or the most advanced or recent stage in the development of something.

words.ex: Many people face unemployment during the economic crisis.
words.ex_cn: 在经济危机期间，许多人面临失业。
words.en: Unemployment refers to the state of being without a job, especially when one is actively seeking employment.

words.tr: adj. 可选择的；非强制的；
words.ex: The field trip is optional.
words.ex_cn: 这次郊游是可选的。
words.en: If something is optional, you can choose whether or not you do it or have it.

words.ex: You have three options to choose from.
words.ex_cn: 你有三个选项可以选择。
words.en: An option is something that you can choose to do in preference to one or more alternatives.

words.ex: The media reported the news quickly.
words.ex_cn: 媒介迅速报道了这则新闻。
words.en: The main means of mass communication (broadcasting, publishing, and the Internet), regarded collectively.

words.ex: She bought a medium sized shirt for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 她为旅行买了一件中等大小的衬衫。
words.en: Of an intermediate size, neither large nor small.

words.ex: He explained the plan in detail.
words.ex_cn: 他详细地解释了这个计划。
words.en: Including all the facts or aspects of a situation.

words.ex: He explicitly said no to the offer.
words.ex_cn: 他明确地拒绝了这个提议。
words.en: In a clear and detailed manner, leaving no room for confusion or doubt.

words.ex: The report comes with details of the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告带有事故的详细信息。

words.tr: adj. 诱导的；归纳的；感应的
words.ex: The scientist used inductive reasoning to form a hypothesis.
words.ex_cn: 科学家使用归纳推理来形成一个假设。
words.en: Inductive reasoning involves making broad generalizations from specific observations.

words.ex: He uses deductive reasoning to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他使用演绎推理来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Deductive reasoning is a logical process in which a conclusion is based on the concordance of multiple premises that are generally assumed to be true.

words.ex: His deduction was based on the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他的推论基于证据。
words.en: A deduction is a conclusion that you reach about something because of other things that you know to be true.

words.tr: v. 使正式就任；给予职位
words.ex: They inducted the new mayor with a ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过一场仪式使新市长正式就任。
words.en: To induct someone into a position or organization means to formally install them in that position or officially introduce them into that organization.

words.ex: He deducts tax from his salary every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每月从工资中扣除税款。
words.en: If you deduct an amount from a total, you subtract it from the total.

words.ex: He is a famous mathematician.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位著名的数学家。
words.en: A mathematician is a person who is an expert in mathematics, a field that uses numbers, formulas, and logical reasoning to solve problems.

words.tr: phrase. 把 A 与 B 联系起来；将 A 和 B 连接
words.ex: She links apple with orange in the chart.
words.ex_cn: 她在图表中把苹果和橙子联系起来。
words.en: To connect or associate one thing with another.

words.w: link between air pollution and heat disease
words.tr: n. 空气污染与热病之间的关联
words.uk: lɪŋk bɪˈtwiːn ɛə pəˈluːʃən ænd hiːt dɪˈziːz
words.us: lɪŋk bɪˈtwiːn er pəˈluːʃən ænd hiːt dɪˈziz
words.ex: There is a link between air pollution and heat disease.
words.ex_cn: 空气污染与热病之间存在关联。

words.ex: He found employment after graduating from university.
words.ex_cn: 他大学毕业后找到了工作。
words.en: the condition of having paid work

words.ex: The farmer owns five hectares of land.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民拥有五公顷土地。
words.en: A hectare is a unit of measurement of area, equal to 10,000 square metres or approximately 2.471 acres.

words.ex: He owns five acres of farmland.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有五英亩的农田。
words.en: A unit of area used in the US Customary and the British Imperial systems, equal to 4,840 square yards or 4,046.86 square meters.

words.ex: The company used a short slogan to attract customers.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司用了一个简短的口号来吸引顾客。
words.en: A short and striking or memorable phrase used in advertising or politics.

words.ex: Birds fly south by instinct.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类凭本能飞向南方。
words.en: An instinct is the natural tendency that a person or animal has to behave or react in a particular way.

words.ex: The birds live in a quiet marsh.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟生活在一片宁静的沼泽中。
