words.en: Something that is emotional is connected with people's feelings. If someone is emotional, they show their feelings very openly, especially because they are upset.

words.tr:
n. 性格外向者；爱交际的人
adj. 外向的
words.ex: He is an extrovert who loves talking to people.
words.ex_cn: 他是个外向的人，喜欢和人交谈。
words.en: An extrovert is someone who is very outgoing, sociable, and enjoys being around other people.

words.tr:
adj. 特别受喜爱的；
n. 特别喜爱的事物；
words.ex: Chocolate is my favourite dessert.
words.ex_cn: 巧克力是我最喜爱的甜点。
words.en: Something or someone that is preferred above all others.

words.tr:
v. 悬挂；吊；
n. 悬挂；
words.ex: He hangs a picture on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他把一幅画挂在墙上。
words.en: To hang something means to attach it to something else so that it is supported from above and does not touch the ground.

words.ex: The team works in harmony.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队合作得很和谐。
words.en: Harmony is the pleasant combination of different notes of music played at the same time. It can also refer to a situation in which people are peaceful and agree with each other, or when things seem right or suitable together.

words.ex: The climate is hospitable for growing oranges.
words.ex_cn: 这种气候适合种植橙子。
words.en: If someone is hospitable, they are friendly, welcoming, and generous to guests or strangers.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；使充气；夸口；吹嘘
words.ex: He tries to inflate the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用嘴把气球吹大。
words.en: To inflate something means to cause it to increase in size by filling it with air or gas. It can also refer to increasing the amount of money in circulation, leading to a decrease in its value.

words.ex: He is an influential teacher in our school.
words.ex_cn: 他是我们学校一位有影响力的老师。
words.en: Having great influence on someone or something.

words.tr: n. 优势；有利条件；好处；
words.ex: His height gives him an advantage in basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他的身高在篮球中给了他优势。
words.en: An advantage is a factor or circumstance that puts you in a favorable or superior position.

words.ex: They shouted, 'Welcome home!' when he walked through the door.
words.ex_cn: 当他走进门时，他们大喊：‘欢迎回家！’
words.en: A greeting used to express pleasure at someone's return to their home.

words.ex: He bought an extravagant car that cost too much money.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆奢侈的车，价格太贵了。
words.en: Spending much more than is necessary or wise; excessively expensive.

words.tr: n. 内向的人；不喜欢与人交往的人
words.ex: He is an introvert who likes reading alone.
words.ex_cn: 他是个喜欢独自读书的内向者。
words.en: An introvert is a person who tends to shrink from social contacts and to become preoccupied with their own thoughts.

words.tr: v. 和某人闲逛；和某人一起消磨时间
words.ex: I like to hang out with my friends after school.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢放学后和朋友们闲逛。

words.tr: phrase. 和睦相处；和谐共存；融洽地生活
words.ex: They live in harmony with their neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他们与邻居和睦相处。
words.en: To live in harmony means to coexist peacefully and cooperatively with others, often despite differences.

words.tr: phrase. 与...协调一致；与...和谐
words.ex: The painting is in harmony with the room's colors.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画与房间的颜色相协调。
words.en: If one thing is in harmony with another, the first thing suits the second or they seem right together.

words.tr: v. 使协调一致；使和谐；配上和音
words.ex: The two singers try to harmonize their voices.
words.ex_cn: 两位歌手试图让他们的声音和谐。
words.en: If two or more things harmonize, they combine in a pleasing way, or if you harmonize them, you make them combine in a pleasing way.

words.ex: The team worked in a harmonious way.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队以和谐的方式合作。
words.en: A harmonious situation, relationship, or agreement is one in which people are friendly and helpful to one another, and in which there is no serious disagreement or argument.

words.ex: They worked harmoniously together.
words.ex_cn: 他们和谐地一起工作。
words.en: In a way that is harmonious, showing a pleasing combination or arrangement of different elements.

words.tr: adj. 疯狂的；精神失常的；精神错乱的
words.ex: He thinks it's insane to drive without a license.
words.ex_cn: 他认为无证驾驶是疯狂的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as insane, you mean that they are very foolish or crazy.

words.ex: He inscribes his name on the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在石头上。
words.en: To write, mark, or engrave (words, symbols, etc.) on a surface, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.tr: n. （校外）学生宿舍；旅社；招待所；
words.ex: The students live in a cheap hostel near the university.
words.ex_cn: 学生们住在大学附近的一家便宜的学生宿舍里。
words.en: A hostel is a budget-oriented, shared-room accommodation that attracts a diverse clientele, including backpackers, students, and travelers seeking an economical place to stay.

words.ex: Water is a common substance.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的物质。
words.en: A substance is a particular kind of matter with uniform properties.

words.tr: v. 由于保险丝烧断而电路不通；熔接；结合；
words.ex: The light went out because the fuse blew.
words.ex_cn: 灯灭了，因为保险丝烧断了。
words.en: A fuse is a safety device consisting of a strip of wire that melts and breaks an electric circuit if the current exceeds a safe level. As a verb, it means to join or blend to form a single entity.

words.tr: adj. 现代的；当代的；同时代的；
words.ex: This museum displays contemporary art.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆展示现代艺术。
words.en: Belonging to or occurring in the present; or a person or thing living or existing at the same time as another.

words.ex: The continuity of the story made it easy to follow.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的连续性让它容易理解。
words.en: Continuity is the fact that something continues to happen or exist, with no great changes or interruptions.

words.ex: The colors from red to violet form a continuum.
words.ex_cn: 从红色到紫色的颜色构成一个连续体。
words.en: A continuum is a continuous sequence in which adjacent elements are not perceptibly different from each other, although the extremes are quite distinct.

words.ex: The duration of the movie is two hours.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的持续时间是两小时。
words.en: The duration of an event or state is the time during which it happens or exists.

words.tr: n. [英]地铁；管子；管状物；电视机；
words.ex: I take the tube to work every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我每天早上乘地铁去上班。
words.en: A tube is a long, hollow cylinder used for conveying or holding liquids or gases.

words.tr:
n. 损害；破损；
v. 损害；破坏；
words.ex: The storm caused serious damage to the house.
words.ex_cn: 风暴对房屋造成了严重损害。
words.en: Damage is physical harm that is caused to something which makes it less attractive, useful, or valuable.

words.tr: v. 加浮雕花纹于；饰以浮饰；使凸出
words.ex: He embosses the card with his name.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字压印在卡片上。
words.en: To decorate a surface by making raised designs or patterns on it.

words.ex: He craves chocolate when he is stressed.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到压力时，他渴望吃巧克力。
words.en: If you crave something, or crave for it, you want to have it very much.

words.ex: He carved the meat with a sharp knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用一把锋利的刀切开了肉。
words.en: To carve means to cut into a hard material in order to produce an object, design, or inscription.

words.ex: The ancient stone has an inscription in Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这块古老的石头上有一段拉丁文碑文。
words.en: An inscription is a piece of writing or a short message that is written or carved on something, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.ex: The student hostel is near the library.
words.ex_cn: 学生宿舍在图书馆附近。
words.en: A student hostel is a place where students live while they are studying at a university or college. It usually offers basic accommodation at a lower cost than private housing.

words.ex: The students stayed in a youth hostel during their trip.
words.ex_cn: 学生们在旅行期间住在青年旅舍。
words.en: A youth hostel is a place where young people, especially those who are traveling, can stay cheaply for short periods of time. It usually provides dormitory-style accommodation and shared facilities.

words.ex: The car had a malfunction in the engine.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的发动机出现了故障。
words.en: If a machine or device malfunctions, it fails to work properly.

words.tr:
n. 闻；气味；嗅觉；
v. 嗅；闻；散发气味；察觉；
words.ex: The smell of fresh bread made me hungry.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的香味让我饿了。
words.en: The faculty or power of perceiving odors or scents by means of the organs in the nose.

words.tr: v. 嗅；闻；散发气味；察觉；“smell”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He smelled the flowers before picking them.
words.ex_cn: 他在摘花之前先闻了闻。
words.en: To perceive or detect the odor or scent of something by means of the olfactory senses.

words.tr:
v. 熔炼；冶炼
v. 嗅；闻；散发气味；察觉；“smell”的过去式和过去分词
n. 胡瓜鱼
words.ex: They smelt iron ore to make steel.
words.ex_cn: 他们熔炼铁矿石来制造钢铁。
words.en: To smelt means to extract metal from ore by a process involving heating and melting.

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.tr:
v. （使）合并；（使）融合；（使）混合
n. 合并；混合
words.ex: He melds the two ideas into one.
words.ex_cn: 他把这两个想法融合成一个。
words.en: To combine or blend to form a single entity.

words.ex: She will divide the cake into two parts.
words.ex_cn: 她将把蛋糕分成两部分。
words.en: If you divide something, you separate it into two or more parts.

words.tr:
adj. 分开的；分离的；单独的；
v. 分离；隔离；
words.ex: They live in separate houses.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在分开的房子里。
words.en: To cause to move or be apart; to divide or keep apart.

words.tr:
v. 分开；分裂；
n. 划分；分歧；
words.ex: The tree split in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 那棵树在风暴中裂开了。
words.en: If something splits or if you split it, it is divided into two or more parts.

words.ex: Sugar dissolves in water.
words.ex_cn: 糖在水中溶解。
words.en: If a substance dissolves in liquid or if you dissolve a substance, it becomes mixed with the liquid and disappears.

words.ex: Salt is a solute in seawater.
words.ex_cn: 盐是海水中的溶质。
words.en: A solute is a substance that is dissolved in a solvent to form a solution.

words.tr: phrase. 与…整合；与…融合；使与…结合；与…集成
words.ex: The new app will integrate with your phone.
words.ex_cn: 这个新应用将与你的手机整合。
words.en: To combine one thing with another so that they become a whole.

words.ex: The music melds with the wind to create a calm sound.
words.ex_cn: 音乐与风融合，创造出宁静的声音。

words.ex: The workers did earthwork to build a new road.
words.ex_cn: 工人们进行了土方工程来修建一条新路。
words.en: An earthwork is a large artificial bank of soil, especially one built as a fortification.

words.ex: This house has a modern design.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子具有现代的设计。
words.en: Modern means relating to the present time, for example the present decade or present century.

words.tr:
adj. 当前的；流通的；
n. （水、气、电）流；趋势；
words.ex: The current weather is very hot.
words.ex_cn: 当前的天气非常热。
words.en: belonging to the present time; happening or being used or done now

words.ex: He hates the smell of durian.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌榴莲的气味。
words.en: A large, oval, tropical fruit with a hard, spiky shell and a strong, distinctive smell, which is either loved or hated by people.

words.ex: Phosphorus is in some fertilizers.
words.ex_cn: 磷存在于一些肥料中。
words.en: Phosphorus is a chemical element with the symbol P and atomic number 15. It is a nonmetal that is essential for life, found in DNA, RNA, ATP, and the phospholipids that form all cell membranes.

words.tr: adj. 自发的；自然产生的；
words.ex: The children gave a spontaneous cheer.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们自发地欢呼起来。
words.en: Something that is spontaneous is not planned but happens or is done because of a sudden impulse or natural feeling.

words.ex: The children laughed spontaneously when they saw the puppy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到小狗时自发地笑了。
words.en: If something happens spontaneously, it happens without being planned or organized, or without any external influence.

words.ex: Eating vegetables is beneficial to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吃蔬菜对你的健康有益。
words.en: Promoting or enhancing well-being; advantageous.

words.ex: The medicine helps inhibit pain.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物有助于抑制疼痛。
words.en: If something inhibits an event or process, it prevents it or slows it down.

words.ex: The phone vibrates when it receives a call.
words.ex_cn: 当手机收到电话时，它会震动。
words.en: To vibrate means to move rapidly to and fro or up and down; to oscillate.

words.ex: Her story inspires me to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 她的故事激励我更加努力。
words.en: If someone or something inspires you to do something new or unusual, they make you want to do it.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.ex: He punched the wall in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地打了墙一拳。
words.en: To punch means to hit someone or something hard with your fist, or to make a hole in something using a tool.

words.ex: The needle will pierce the skin.
words.ex_cn: 针会刺穿皮肤。
words.en: If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.

words.ex: The box has a rectangle shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是长方形的。
words.en: A rectangle is a four-sided flat shape where every interior angle is a right angle (90°). Opposite sides are parallel and of equal length.

words.ex: He will repay the loan next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月会偿还贷款。
words.en: If you repay a loan or a debt, you pay back the money that you owe to the person who you borrowed or took it from.

words.ex: They have mutual respect for each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此相互尊重。
words.en: Mutual is used to describe a situation, feeling, or action that is experienced, felt, or done by each of two or more parties towards the other or others.

words.ex: They have a reciprocal agreement to help each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们有一个互相帮助的互惠协议。
words.en: A reciprocal action or agreement involves two people or groups who do the same thing to each other or agree to help each other in a similar way.

words.tr: adj. 对某事有益的；对某物有好处的
phrase. 互惠互利的：指两个或多个人、组织或国家之间的关系，相互从中获益。
words.ex: The partnership was mutually beneficial, with both companies gaining significant market share.
words.ex_cn: 这种合作是互惠互利的，两家公司都获得了显著的市场份额。
words.en: If a situation or arrangement is mutually beneficial, it is advantageous to all the people or groups involved.

words.ex: It is advantageous to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 早起是有利的。
words.en: If something is advantageous to you, it is likely to benefit you.

words.ex: Smoking is harmful to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is harmful has a bad effect on something else, especially on a person's health.

words.ex: The baleful glare of the enemy sent shivers down their spines.
words.ex_cn: 敌人恶意的目光让他们不寒而栗。
words.en: Baleful means threatening harm or evil.

words.ex: It is disadvantageous to skip breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 不吃早餐是不利的。
words.en: If something is disadvantageous to you, it is likely to cause you difficulties or problems.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.tr:
n. 捆；束；包
v. 匆匆送走
words.ex: He bought a bundle of newspapers.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一捆报纸。
words.en: A bundle is a number of things that are tied or wrapped together so that they can be carried or stored easily.

words.ex: Rain can hinder our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨天会妨碍我们去徒步旅行的计划。
words.en: If something hinders you, it makes it more difficult for you to do something or make progress.

words.ex: The fallen tree obstructs the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树挡住了道路。
words.en: If something obstructs a road or path, it blocks it, stopping people or vehicles from getting past.

words.ex: The fallen tree impeded the car's path.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树阻碍了汽车的前进。
words.en: To impede something means to make its movement, development, or progress difficult.

words.ex: My teacher encourages me to speak English every day.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师鼓励我每天说英语。
words.en: If you encourage someone, you give them confidence, for example by letting them know that what they are doing is good and telling them that they should continue to do it.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；茂盛的；
words.ex: He is a vigorous man who runs every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的人，每天早上都跑步。
words.en: A vigorous person does things with great energy and enthusiasm. A vigorous campaign or activity is done with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 有活力的；精力旺盛的；
words.ex: The energetic boy ran around the park all afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 这个有活力的男孩整个下午都在公园里跑来跑去。
words.en: Someone who is energetic is very active and does not tire easily.

words.ex: The children are vibrant and full of energy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们充满活力。
words.en: If you describe something as vibrant, you mean that it is bright, lively, and full of energy.

words.ex: The rattlesnake hissed and shook its tail.
words.ex_cn: 响尾蛇嘶嘶作响并摇动尾巴。
words.en: A rattlesnake is a venomous snake known for the rattle at the end of its tail, which it uses as a warning signal to potential predators.

words.ex: The phone shows a small vibration when it rings.
words.ex_cn: 手机响时会轻微震动。
words.en: A vibration is a continuous slight shaking movement.

words.tr: adj. 保留的； v. 保留；“reserve”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The seats are reserved for students.
words.ex_cn: 这些座位是为学生保留的。
words.en: If something is reserved, it is kept specially for a particular purpose or person.

words.tr:
v. 打滑；侧滑
n. 打滑；侧滑
words.ex: The car skid on the wet road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在湿滑的路面上打滑了。
words.en: If a vehicle skids, it slides sideways or forwards while moving, usually because of bad weather conditions or because the driver is going too fast.

words.ex: He is a sociable man who likes to talk with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢和朋友聊天的外向的人。
words.en: A sociable person is friendly and enjoys being with other people.

words.tr:
adj. 相对的；相关联的；
n. 亲戚；
words.ex: His success is relative to his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的成功是相对于他的努力而言的。
words.en: A relative is someone who is part of your family. Parents, siblings, uncles, aunts, grandparents, cousins, nieces and nephews — they're all relatives.

words.ex: The new house has a spacious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所新房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A spacious room, building, or place is large in size or area, so that you can move around freely in it.

words.tr: adj. 容量大的；广阔的；宽敞的
words.ex: The capacious room can hold many people.
words.ex_cn: 这个宽敞的房间可以容纳很多人。
words.en: Capacious means having a lot of space inside; roomy.

words.ex: He practices his religion every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都实践自己的宗教信仰。
words.en: Religion is the belief in and worship of a superhuman controlling power, especially a personal God or gods.

words.tr: adj. 人口统计的；人口的；
words.ex: The survey collected demographic data like age and income.
words.ex_cn: 这项调查收集了年龄和收入等人口统计数据。
words.en: Relating to the structure of populations.

words.ex: He picked a random number to win the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他随意选了一个数字来赢得奖品。
words.en: If you describe something as random, you mean that it happens or is chosen without any definite plan, pattern, or purpose.

words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.tr:
n. 真空；空虚；
v. 用真空吸尘器打扫；
words.ex: The vacuum in space keeps no air.
words.ex_cn: 太空中的真空没有空气。
words.en: A vacuum is a space that contains no air or other gas, or a space from which most of the air or gas has been removed. It can also refer to a device that cleans floors and surfaces by sucking up dirt and dust.

words.ex: He uses a digital watch to tell time.
words.ex_cn: 他用一块数字手表看时间。
words.en: Digital systems, devices, or technology use electronic signals that are represented by the numbers 1 and 0, indicating 'on' or 'off'.

words.tr: n. 一个爱社交的孩子
words.ex: The sociable child plays with everyone at the park.
words.ex_cn: 这个爱社交的孩子在公园里和每个人玩耍。

words.tr: phrase. 亲近的亲属；直系亲属
words.ex: She invited all her close relatives to the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 她邀请了所有近亲参加婚礼。
words.en: Close relatives are people who are closely related by blood or marriage, such as parents, siblings, and children.

words.tr: phrase. 远亲；关系较远的亲戚
words.ex: She only sees her distant relatives at family reunions.
words.ex_cn: 她只在家庭聚会上见到她的远亲。
words.en: People who are related to you but are not closely connected, such as cousins, second cousins, etc.

words.ex: This room is relatively small.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间相对较小。
words.en: In comparison with other similar things or with what you expect.

words.ex: He visits a religious temple every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都去一座宗教寺庙。
words.en: Relating to or believing in a religion.

words.ex: The viability of the new business depends on customer demand.
words.ex_cn: 这个新企业的生存能力取决于客户需求。
words.en: The capacity of something to maintain its existence or to be successful.

words.tr: phrase. 胡乱地； 随便地
words.ex: He picked a number at random.
words.ex_cn: 他随机选了一个数字。
words.en: If you choose people or things at random, you do not use any particular method, so they all have an equal chance of being chosen.

words.tr: phrase. 随机选择；随机抽样
words.ex: The teacher uses random selection to choose a student to answer.
words.ex_cn: 老师用随机选择来挑选一名学生回答问题。
words.en: A method of sampling from a population in which each individual has an equal chance of being selected.

words.ex: The teacher uses random sampling to pick students for the quiz.
words.ex_cn: 老师用随机抽样来挑选学生参加测验。
words.en: A method of selecting individuals from a population where each has an equal chance of being chosen.

words.tr: n. 随机访问；直接存取
words.ex: The computer uses random access to read data quickly.
words.ex_cn: 计算机使用随机访问来快速读取数据。

words.tr:
n. 样品；样本；
v. 抽样；
words.ex: The scientist tested the sample from the river.
words.ex_cn: 科学家测试了来自河流的样品。
words.en: A sample is a small quantity of a product, especially food, given to customers so that they can try it before buying it.

words.ex: The shape has irregular sides.
words.ex_cn: 这个形状的边是不规则的。
words.en: Something that is irregular does not follow the expected pattern, plan, or method; it is not regular.

words.tr: v. 设计；“design”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 精心设计的；
words.ex: The house was designed for easy living.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子是为方便生活而设计的。
words.en: If something is designed for a particular purpose, it is intended for that purpose.

words.tr: v. 安排；“arrange”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 安排的；
words.ex: They arranged a meeting for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们安排了明天的会议。
words.en: If you arrange an event or meeting, you make plans for it to happen.

words.tr: adj. 放肆的；冒昧的；自以为是的
words.ex: He was presumptuous to ask for a raise after just one week.
words.ex_cn: 他才工作一周就要求加薪，太自以为是了。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as presumptuous, you disapprove of them because they are doing something that they have no right or authority to do.

words.ex: The boss is dictatorial and never listens to others.
words.ex_cn: 老板很专横，从不听别人的意见。
words.en: If you describe someone as dictatorial, you are criticizing them for behaving in a way that shows they expect to be obeyed without question.

words.tr: n. 真空干燥器；一种在减压条件下用于干燥或保存物质的密封容器
words.ex: The scientist placed the sample in a vacuum desiccator to remove moisture.
words.ex_cn: 科学家把样品放在真空干燥器中以去除水分。
words.en: A sealed container that uses a vacuum to remove moisture and preserve contents.

words.ex: The desiccant keeps the box dry.
words.ex_cn: 干燥剂使盒子保持干燥。
words.en: A desiccant is a substance that is used to induce or sustain a state of dryness (desiccation) in its vicinity.

words.ex: The sun will desiccate the leaves in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天阳光会把叶子晒干。
words.en: To remove the moisture from something, typically in order to preserve it.

words.tr: v. 使变小；使减少；使缩小
words.ex: The architect decided to minify the size of the building to fit the small plot of land.
words.ex_cn: 建筑师决定缩小建筑物的尺寸以适应这块小地块。
words.en: To reduce in size, amount, or degree; to make smaller or less significant.

words.ex: Try to lessen your sugar intake.
words.ex_cn: 试着减少你的糖摄入量。
words.en: If something lessens or you lessen it, it becomes smaller in size, amount, degree, or importance.

words.ex: The noise will diminish after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜后噪音会减少。
words.en: If something diminishes, or if something diminishes it, it becomes reduced in size, importance, or intensity.

words.tr: n. 长颈瓶；烧瓶；携带用扁瓶；保温瓶
words.ex: He poured the liquid into a glass flask.
words.ex_cn: 他把液体倒进了一个玻璃长颈瓶里。
words.en: A flask is a bottle or other container which is used in science laboratories and industry for holding liquids.

words.ex: He poured hot tea into the thermos.
words.ex_cn: 他把热茶倒进了保温瓶。
words.en: A thermos is a container which is used to keep hot drinks hot or cold drinks cold. It has two thin shiny glass walls with no air between them.

words.ex: The problem is a global issue.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题是一个全球性的问题。
words.en: relating to the whole world; worldwide

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.ex: The teacher gave us a handout about photosynthesis.
words.ex_cn: 老师发给我们一份关于光合作用的讲义。
words.en: A handout is a document which contains news or information about something and which is given, for example, to journalists or to people attending a talk or lecture.

words.ex: He handed out a leaflet about the event.
words.ex_cn: 他分发了一份关于该活动的传单。
words.en: A leaflet is a small sheet of printed paper that gives you information or advertises something.

words.tr: n. 帐篷外罩；防雨篷布
words.ex: The flysheet keeps rain off the tent.
words.ex_cn: 帐篷外罩防止雨水渗入帐篷。

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.ex: The helicopter flew over the city.
words.ex_cn: 直升机飞过了城市。
words.en: A helicopter is a type of aircraft that derives both lift and propulsion from one or more sets of horizontally revolving overhead rotors. It is capable of moving vertically and horizontally, the direction of motion being controlled by the pitch of the rotor blades.

words.ex: The city's sprawl has covered many farmlands.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的杂乱无序的拓展覆盖了许多农田。
words.en: If you sprawl somewhere, you sit or lie with your legs and arms spread out in a careless way.

words.tr: adj. 拥挤的；密集的； v. “crowd”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The bus was crowded during rush hour.
words.ex_cn: 高峰时段公交车很拥挤。
words.en: If a place is crowded, it is full of people.

words.tr: adj. 拥挤的；堵塞的； v. “congest” 的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The road was congested with cars during rush hour.
words.ex_cn: 高峰时段，这条路被汽车挤满了。
words.en: If a place is congested, it is extremely crowded and blocked with traffic or people.

words.ex: He turned the knob to adjust the volume.
words.ex_cn: 他转动旋钮来调节音量。
words.en: A knob is a round handle, or a round switch on a piece of equipment.

words.tr:
adj. 理想的；
n. 理想；典范；
words.ex: This is the ideal place to relax.
words.ex_cn: 这是放松的理想地方。
words.en: An ideal is a principle or value that one actively pursues as a goal, often in the context of ethics or morality.

words.ex: Global warming is making the Earth hotter.
words.ex_cn: 全球变暖正在让地球变得更热。
words.en: Global warming refers to the long-term increase in Earth's average surface temperature due to human activities, primarily fossil fuel burning, which increases heat-trapping greenhouse gas levels in Earth's atmosphere.

words.tr: phrase. 地球村（指因通信和交通发展使世界变得紧密相连，如同一个村庄）
words.ex: The internet makes the world a global village.
words.ex_cn: 互联网让世界成为一个地球村。
words.en: The term 'global village' refers to the idea that the world has become more interconnected due to the rapid advancement of communication and transportation technologies, making distances between people seem shorter.

words.tr: adj. 茅草盖的; 浓密的，毛茸茸的 vt. 用茅草覆盖(thatch的过去式形式) n. 茅草：
words.ex: The old house has a thatched roof.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子有一个茅草屋顶。
words.en: Covered or made with a roof or covering of straw, reeds, or similar materials.

words.ex: The old man lives in a thatched hut near the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人住在森林附近的一间茅草屋里。

words.tr: phrase. 茅草屋顶的小屋；茅舍
words.ex: They live in a thatched cottage near the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一座茅草屋子里。
words.en: A thatched cottage is a small house with a roof made of straw or reeds.

words.ex: They live in a small cottage near the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一座小村舍里。
words.en: A cottage is a small house, usually in the countryside.

words.ex: The children built a hut in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在树林里建了一间小屋。
words.en: A hut is a small, simple building, usually consisting of one room and made of materials such as wood, mud, or grass.

words.tr: n. 一组；一簇；（某物）的聚集
words.ex: A cluster of stars shone in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有一组星星闪耀。

words.ex: He handed me a pamphlet about the new park.
words.ex_cn: 他递给我一份关于新公园的小册子。
words.en: A pamphlet is a small book containing information on a particular subject or expressing political or religious views.

words.ex: He picked up a brochure about the city.
words.ex_cn: 他拿了一本关于这座城市的宣传小册子。
words.en: A brochure is a type of small magazine or booklet containing pictures and information about something or advertising something.

words.tr: v. 紧挨着某物；在某物旁边

words.ex: He walked home with his companion.
words.ex_cn: 他和同伴一起走回家。
words.en: A companion is someone who you spend time with or who you are travelling with.

words.tr: n. 一个理想的伴侣／同伴
words.ex: He is an ideal companion for long trips.
words.ex_cn: 他是长途旅行的理想伴侣。
words.en: A perfect partner or friend who is highly suitable or desirable.

words.ex: He is an idealistic young man who wants to change the world.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个理想主义的年轻人，想要改变世界。
words.en: If you describe someone as idealistic, you mean that they have ideals, and base their behaviour on these ideals, often in a way that is not practical.

words.ex: Ideally, we should finish the project by Friday.
words.ex_cn: 理想地，我们应该在周五前完成这个项目。
words.en: In an ideal or perfect way; in a way that would be best in an ideal world.

words.tr: adj. 唯物论的；物质至上主义的
words.ex: He is materialistic and only cares about money.
words.ex_cn: 他是个唯物论者，只关心钱。
words.en: If you describe a person or society as materialistic, you are critical of them because they attach too much importance to money and material possessions.

words.ex: He stood in the midst of the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他站在人群中间。
words.en: The middle part or point of something.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.ex: He wavers when choosing between two jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他在两个工作之间摇摆不定。
words.en: If you waver, you cannot decide about something or you are uncertain about what you should do.

words.ex: The weather varies from day to day.
words.ex_cn: 天气每天都在变化。
words.en: If things vary, they are different from each other in size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: His neglect of the project caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 他对项目的疏忽导致了延误。
words.en: If you neglect someone or something, you fail to give them the attention or care that they need.

words.ex: He overlooked the mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了报告中的错误。
words.en: If you overlook a fact or problem, you do not notice it, or do not realize how important it is.

words.ex: He ignored the warning sign.
words.ex_cn: 他忽视了警告标志。
words.en: If you ignore someone or something, you pay no attention to them.

words.ex: The drought made it hard to grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 旱灾使种植庄稼变得困难。
words.en: A drought is a long period of time during which no rain falls and hence there is a shortage of water.

words.ex: The dryness of the desert makes it hard for plants to grow.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的干燥使植物难以生长。
words.en: The state or quality of being dry.

words.ex: The aridity of the desert makes it hard for plants to grow.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的干旱使植物难以生长。
words.en: Aridity is the state of being extremely dry, especially due to lack of rainfall.

words.tr:
v. 拥抱；紧抱；抱有；挨着
n. 拥抱；搂抱
words.ex: She gave him a big hug when he arrived.
words.ex_cn: 他到达时，她给了他一个大大的拥抱。
words.en: To hug someone means to put your arms around them and hold them tightly, for example because you like them or are pleased to see them.

words.ex: The variability of weather makes it hard to plan outdoor events.
words.ex_cn: 天气的可变性使得计划户外活动很困难。
words.en: The quality or state of being subject to change or variation.

words.ex: The dark clouds are an indication of rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是下雨的迹象。
words.en: An indication is a sign which suggests, for example, what people are thinking or feeling.

words.ex: He inserts a coin into the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他把一枚硬币放进机器里。
words.en: To put or introduce something into something else.

words.tr: prep. 在...之中；在…的包围中；
words.ex: He stood amidst the trees, quiet and still.
words.ex_cn: 他站在树木之中，安静而静止。
words.en: In the middle of or surrounded by; among.

words.ex: We found a peaceful glade to rest in.
words.ex_cn: 我们找到了一个宁静的林间空地休息。
words.en: A glade is an open space in a forest.

words.tr: v. 玩忽职守；忽视自己的职责
words.ex: He neglects his duty by not showing up for work.
words.ex_cn: 他因不上班而玩忽职守。

words.tr: adj. 沉闷乏味的；忧郁的；凄凉的
words.ex: The weather was dreary and rainy all day.
words.ex_cn: 天气一整天都阴沉沉的，还下着雨。
words.en: If you describe something as dreary, you mean that it is dull, lifeless, or depressing.

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.tr: adj. 无聊的；令人厌倦的； v. “bore”的现在分词；
words.ex: The movie was boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很无聊。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as boring, you mean that they are not interesting and make you feel tired or impatient.

words.ex: She showed great affection for her little dog.
words.ex_cn: 她对她的小狗非常钟爱。
words.en: A feeling of liking and caring for someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 挚爱的；有深厚感情的；充满深情的
words.ex: She is affectionate with her little brother.
words.ex_cn: 她对弟弟很亲昵。
words.en: If you are affectionate, you show your love or fondness for another person in the way that you behave towards them.

words.ex: Her affectionateness made everyone feel loved.
words.ex_cn: 她的深情让每个人都感到被爱。

words.tr: n. 房间；室；腔；大会议室；
words.ex: He sat in the chamber and waited quietly.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在房间里安静地等待。
words.en: A chamber is a large room, especially one that is used for formal or public events.

words.tr:
v. 交配繁殖；饲养；
n. 品种；
words.ex: The farmers breed cows to get more milk.
words.ex_cn: 农民让奶牛交配繁殖以获得更多牛奶。
words.en: If you breed animals or plants, you keep them for the purpose of producing more animals or plants with particular qualities, in a controlled way.

words.tr: v. 沉思；闷闷不乐地想；n. 一窝幼崽；沉思的状态
words.ex: He sits by the window and broods over his failures.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边，为自己的失败而忧思。
words.en: If someone broods over something, they think about it a lot, seriously and often unhappily. A brood is a group of young birds all born at the same time to the same mother.

words.ex: The bird hatched her eggs after three weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟在三周后孵出了她的蛋。
words.en: To hatch means to cause an egg to break open so that a young animal can come out, or to plan secretly with other people to do something bad or illegal.

words.tr: n. 育幼室；蜂巢中用于哺育幼虫的蜂房
words.ex: Bees store honey in brood chambers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂在育幼室里储存蜂蜜。

words.ex: He received a certificate for completing the course.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了课程后获得了证书。
words.en: A certificate is an official document attesting a fact, in particular.

words.tr: adj. 严重的；严厉的；非常困难的；
words.ex: The storm caused severe damage to the houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对房屋造成了严重的破坏。
words.en: If something is severe, it is very bad or very serious.

words.ex: The baleful glare of the enemy sent shivers down their spines.
words.ex_cn: 敌人恶意的目光让他们不寒而栗。
words.en: Baleful means threatening harm or evil.

words.ex: The diameter of the circle is 10 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆的直径是10厘米。
words.en: A straight line passing from side to side through the center of a body or figure, especially a circle or sphere.

words.ex: He made a gesture of welcome with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用手做了一个欢迎的姿态。
words.en: A gesture is a movement that you make with a part of your body, especially your hands, to express emotion or information.

words.ex: He refused to disclose the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝透露这个秘密。
words.en: To disclose information means to make it known to the public.

words.ex: They enclose the garden with a wooden fence.
words.ex_cn: 他们用木栅栏把花园围起来。
words.en: If you enclose something with a letter, you put it in the same envelope as the letter.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.tr: phrase. 儿童保育设施；托儿所
words.ex: The parents drop their kids at the childcare facility every morning.
words.ex_cn: 父母每天早上把孩子送到托儿所。
words.en: A place where children are cared for while parents are at work or unavailable.

words.tr: n. 教师资格证书；教学证书
words.ex: He got a teaching certificate last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了教师资格证。
words.en: An official document certifying that an individual is qualified to teach in a school or institution.

words.ex: He needs a birth certificate to get a passport.
words.ex_cn: 他需要出生证明来办理护照。
words.en: An official document that proves a person's birth details.

words.tr: phrase. 结婚证书；婚姻登记证明
words.ex: They applied for a marriage certificate at the local government office.
words.ex_cn: 他们在当地政府办公室申请了结婚证书。
words.en: A marriage certificate is an official document that proves that two people are legally married.

words.tr: n. 托儿服务证书；儿童保育资格证书
words.ex: She earned a childcare certificate last year.
words.ex_cn: 她去年获得了托儿服务证书。

words.ex: Breaking the law can lead to severe consequence.
words.ex_cn: 违法可能会导致严重的后果。

words.ex: The severe storm broke many trees.
words.ex_cn: 这场猛烈的风暴吹倒了许多树。
words.en: A violent weather event with strong winds, heavy rain, or hail.

words.ex: He was severely injured in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中严重受伤。
words.en: If something is done severely, it is done in a very great or intense degree.

words.ex: The new policy has a wide radius of influence.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策的影响范围很广。
words.en: A straight line from the center to the circumference of a circle or sphere.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.ex: The soldier wore camouflage to hide in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 士兵穿着伪装服在森林中隐藏自己。
words.en: Camouflage is the way in which some animals are colored and shaped so that they cannot easily be seen in their natural surroundings.

words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.ex: The detective uncovered the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探揭开了真相。
words.en: To uncover something means to remove the cover from it or to reveal it by investigation or inquiry.

words.ex: He tried to conceal the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图隐藏真相。
words.en: If you conceal something, you prevent it from being seen or known about.

words.tr:
v. 隐藏；躲藏；
n. 兽皮；
words.ex: He hides the key under the mat.
words.ex_cn: 他把钥匙藏在垫子下面。
words.en: To conceal something or someone from view or discovery.

words.ex: It was sheer luck that he won the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢了比赛完全是运气。
words.en: Sheer is used to emphasize that a state or situation is complete and does not involve or is not mixed with anything else.

words.ex: He won three successive championships.
words.ex_cn: 他连续赢得了三届冠军。
words.en: Following one after the other without interruption.

words.ex: The rain was continuous all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都在下个不停。
words.en: Something that is continuous happens or exists without stopping or being interrupted.

words.tr:
n. 平衡；天平；秤；
v. （使）相抵；（使）平衡；
words.ex: She maintains a good balance between work and rest.
words.ex_cn: 她在工作和休息之间保持良好的平衡。
words.en: Balance is the ability to remain steady when you are standing up. Also, it refers to the state of having your weight spread equally so that you do not fall. In finance, it refers to the amount of money you have in a bank account.

words.tr: v. 调整；使适合；使适应；
words.ex: He adjusted the chair to sit comfortably.
words.ex_cn: 他调整了椅子以便坐得舒服。
words.en: To adjust something means to change it so that it is more effective or appropriate, or so that it fits better.

words.ex: This job requires patience.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作需要耐心。
words.en: If you require something, you need it or want it.

words.ex: The movie was fairly interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影相当地有趣。
words.en: To a moderately sufficient extent or degree.

words.ex: He gave a precise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了准确的答案。
words.en: If you give precise information or precise instructions, you give exact details so that there is no confusion about what should be done.

words.ex: He is colour-blind and cannot tell red from green.
words.ex_cn: 他是色盲，分不清红色和绿色。
words.en: Unable to distinguish certain colors, especially red and green, due to a deficiency in the eyes' color receptors.

words.ex: The colors from red to violet form a continuum.
words.ex_cn: 从红色到紫色的颜色构成一个连续体。
words.en: A continuum is a continuous sequence in which adjacent elements are not perceptibly different from each other, although the extremes are quite distinct.

words.ex: The succession of rain made the ground wet.
words.ex_cn: 连续的雨水使地面变湿了。
words.en: A succession of things of the same kind is a number of them that exist or happen one after the other.

words.ex: He loses balance when he walks on the narrow beam.
words.ex_cn: 当他走在窄梁上时，他会失去平衡。
words.en: To lose stability and be unable to stand upright.

words.tr: phrase. 保持平衡；维持均衡
words.ex: It is important to keep balance when you walk on a narrow path.
words.ex_cn: 当你走在狭窄的小路上时，保持平衡很重要。
words.en: To maintain an even distribution of weight enabling someone or something to remain upright and steady.

words.ex: The country's balance of payments showed a surplus last year.
words.ex_cn: n. 该国的国际收支平衡表去年显示有盈余。
words.en: The balance of payments is a record of all economic transactions between the residents of a country and the rest of the world in a particular period.

words.ex: The government will adjust a policy to help small businesses.
words.ex_cn: 政府将调整一项政策以帮助小企业。

words.tr: v. 调整支出以匹配收入
words.ex: He adjusts expenses to income every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月都调整支出以匹配收入。

words.ex: He adjusts a watch to match the clock.
words.ex_cn: 他调整手表以与钟表对时。

words.ex: He needs to adjust to the new school.
words.ex_cn: 他需要适应新学校。
words.en: If you adjust to a new situation or get used to it, you change your behaviour or ideas so that you can deal with it successfully.

words.tr: n. 需求；要求；必要条件；
words.ex: The job has a requirement of two years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作的要求是两年经验。
words.en: A requirement is something that is necessary or that must be done.

words.ex: To be precise, it was actually 3:15 when we arrived.
words.ex_cn: 确切地讲，我们到达时其实是3点15分。
words.en: Used to state something with exactness and clarity.

words.tr: phrase. 精确测量；精密测量
words.ex: The scientist made a precise measurement of the liquid.
words.ex_cn: 科学家对液体进行了精确的测量。
words.en: A precise measurement is an exact determination of the size, amount, or degree of something.

words.tr: n. 一个非常精确的人
words.ex: He is a very precise man who checks every number twice.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个非常精确的人，会核对每个数字两遍。

words.ex: The clock strikes precisely at noon.
words.ex_cn: 钟恰好在正午敲响。
words.en: In a precise manner; exactly.

words.ex: He is a trustworthy friend who always keeps his promises.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个值得信赖的朋友，总是信守承诺。
words.en: If you describe someone as trustworthy, you mean they are reliable, honest, and truthful.

words.tr:
v. 呕吐；吐出；喷涌出
n. 呕吐；呕吐物
words.ex: He felt sick and vomited on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他感到恶心，就在地上吐了。
words.en: To eject matter from the stomach through the mouth.

words.tr:
v. 摔跤；扭斗；奋力对付
n. 摔跤；角力；扭斗
words.ex: He tries to wrestle the dog away from the trash.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把狗从垃圾桶旁拉开。
words.en: To engage in a physical contest, typically involving grappling and trying to throw or immobilize the opponent, or to struggle with a difficult problem or decision.

words.ex: He was shy during his adolescence.
words.ex_cn: 他在青春期时很害羞。
words.en: Adolescence is the period in a person's life when they develop from a child into an adult.

words.ex: The lion lived in captivity for ten years.
words.ex_cn: 这只狮子被关押了十年。
words.en: The state of being imprisoned or confined.

words.ex: He was imprisoned for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷窃而被监禁。
words.en: To put someone in prison or keep them as a prisoner.

words.ex: The student was sent to detention for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这名学生因违反规则被留校滞留。
words.en: Detention is the act of detaining someone or the state of being detained in official custody, especially as a political prisoner.

words.ex: Small commerce helps local towns grow.
words.ex_cn: 小商业有助于小镇的发展。
words.en: Commerce is the activity of buying and selling things, especially on a large scale.

words.ex: The condensation of the report made it easier to read.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告的浓缩版更容易阅读。
words.en: Condensation is the process by which a gas changes into a liquid, or the liquid that results from this process.

words.ex: He has a facial scar from an accident.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上有一道因事故留下的疤痕。
words.en: Facial means relating to the face or designed for use on the face.

words.tr: adj. 不确切的；不精确的；
words.ex: His answer was imprecise and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答不确切，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as imprecise, you mean that it is not stated or done accurately or clearly.

words.tr: adj. 不活动的；不活跃的；怠惰的；
words.ex: The old man is inactive because of his illness.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人因为生病而不活动。
words.en: If someone or something is inactive, they are not doing anything or are not working.

words.ex: He ate too much and vomited up his dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多了，把晚饭都吐了出来。
words.en: To expel the contents of the stomach through the mouth; to vomit.

words.tr: v. 与某人搏斗；与某人激烈争斗；苦苦挣扎处理（某问题）
words.ex: He wrestled with his brother in the yard.
words.ex_cn: 他在院子里和他兄弟搏斗。

words.ex: He will tackle the problem tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会处理这个问题。
words.en: If you tackle a problem or task, you deal with it in a determined way. In sports such as football and rugby, a tackle is an act of trying to take the ball from a player on the other team.

words.ex: The police will detain the suspect for questioning.
words.ex_cn: 警察将扣留嫌疑人进行审问。
words.en: If someone is detained, they are officially held in a place, especially a prison, and are not allowed to leave.

words.tr: n. ……的所在地；……的中心（常用于指政府、权力或机构的所在地）
words.ex: Beijing is the seat of the Chinese government.
words.ex_cn: 北京是中国政府的所在地。

words.tr: phrase. 面部表情；脸上的神情变化，用以表达情绪或感觉
words.ex: He read her facial expressions to know how she felt.
words.ex_cn: 他通过她的面部表情来了解她的感受。
words.en: The movement or positioning of the facial muscles to communicate emotions or reactions.

words.ex: It is of great value to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 学习英语很有价值。

words.ex: She drinks herbal tea every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上喝草药茶。
words.en: Relating to or made from herbs, especially those used in medicine and cooking.

words.ex: The bird hovers above the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 鸟在花上空盘旋。
words.en: To remain in one place in the air, or to stay close to someone or something.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.ex: The ship's longitude is 45 degrees west.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船的经度是西经45度。
words.en: Longitude is the distance of a place east or west of the Greenwich meridian, measured in degrees.

words.ex: He always procrastinates doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他总是拖延做作业。
words.en: If you procrastinate, you keep leaving things you should do until later, often because you do not want to do them.

words.ex: The rarity of snow in this city surprises visitors.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市下雪的罕见现象让游客感到惊讶。
words.en: Something that is rare, or the state of being rare.

words.ex: He likes to seclude himself in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢把自己 secluded 在森林里。
words.en: To seclude means to keep someone away from other people, or to keep something away from other things.

words.tr: v. 隔离；使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘
words.ex: The walls insulate the house from cold air.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁将房子与冷空气隔离开。
words.en: To insulate something means to protect it from heat, cold, noise, or electricity by covering it in a material that prevents it from passing through.

words.ex: The hospital will isolate the patient to stop the spread.
words.ex_cn: 医院将隔离这名病人以防止传播。
words.en: To isolate someone or something means to separate them from other people or things, often in order to protect them or to prevent the spread of something harmful.

words.ex: The project is ongoing.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正在进行中。
words.en: An ongoing situation has been happening for quite a long time and seems likely to continue for some time in the future.

words.tr:
v. 喂；吃；
n. 饲养；喂养；
words.ex: She feeds the cat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上喂猫。
words.en: To give food to a person or an animal; to supply something to a machine or a system.

words.ex: The deer is a herbivore.
words.ex_cn: 鹿是食草动物。
words.en: An herbivore is an animal that gets its energy from eating plants, and only plants.

words.ex: The deer is herbivorous.
words.ex_cn: 这只鹿是食草的。
words.en: Herbivorous animals are those that feed on plants.

words.tr: n. 实践者；从业者；执业者；
words.ex: He is a medical practitioner who helps patients every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每天帮助病人的医疗实践者。
words.en: A practitioner is someone who works in a particular profession, especially one that requires special training and skills.

words.ex: Herbal medicine has been used for centuries to treat a variety of ailments.
words.ex_cn: 草药医学被用于治疗各种疾病已有数百年历史。
words.en: Herbal medicine refers to the use of plants and plant extracts for therapeutic purposes. It is a form of alternative medicine that has been practiced for centuries across various cultures.

words.tr: n. 草药医师；使用草药进行治疗的从业者
words.ex: The herbal practitioner gave her tea for stomach pain.
words.ex_cn: 草药医师给她开了治疗胃痛的草药茶。

words.ex: He lingered by the door, not wanting to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他逗留在门口，不想离开。
words.en: If you linger somewhere, you stay there for a longer time than is necessary, for example because you are enjoying yourself.

words.tr:
v. 振翼；颤动；飘动；挥动
n. 鼓翼；飘扬；激动不安
words.ex: The flag is fluttering in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 旗帜在风中飘扬。
words.en: If something thin or light flutters, or if you flutter it, it moves up and down or from side to side with a lot of quick, light movements.

words.tr:
v. 拍动；摆动；
n. 薄片；
words.ex: The bird flaps its wings to fly.
words.ex_cn: 鸟拍动翅膀飞翔。
words.en: A flap is a piece of cloth, paper, skin etc that is fixed at one edge to a surface, which you can lift up easily. If something such as a piece of cloth or paper flaps or if you flap it, it moves quickly up and down or from side to side.

words.ex: The city is at a latitude of 40 degrees north.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市位于北纬40度。
words.en: Latitude is the distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured in degrees.

words.ex: She led a reclusive life in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 她在山中过着隐居的生活。
words.en: If you describe someone as reclusive, you mean that they live alone and do not like seeing or talking to other people.

words.ex: The rule excludes children under 12.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则排除了12岁以下的孩子。
words.en: To exclude someone or something means to prevent them from entering a place or taking part in an activity.

words.tr:
adj. 僻静的；隐僻的； 退隐的
v. 隔离；隔绝；隐居；“seclude”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The cabin is secluded in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 小木屋坐落在树林中，十分僻静。
words.en: A secluded place is quiet, private, and not near people or things that disturb you.

words.tr: n. 隐居者；遁世者；隐士
words.ex: He lives as a recluse in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他住在树林里，过着隐居的生活。
words.en: A recluse is a person who lives alone and avoids other people.

words.ex: The data will feed into the system tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据明天将装入系统。
words.en: To flow or lead into something, especially in a way that contributes to it or affects it.

words.ex: Wolves feed on deer in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 狼以鹿为食。

words.ex: The mountain scenery is very beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 山景非常美丽。
words.en: The natural features of a landscape considered in terms of their appearance, especially when picturesque.

words.tr: v. （使）停滞；不发展；因不流动而变得污浊
words.ex: The economy began to stagnate after the crisis.
words.ex_cn: 经济在危机后开始停滞。
words.en: If something such as a business or project stagnates, it stops developing or making progress.

words.tr:
v. 利用；
n. 水龙头；轻拍；轻敲；轻击；
words.ex: The company tapped local talent to grow its business.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司利用本地人才来发展业务。
words.en: If you tap something, you hit it with a quick light blow or a series of quick light blows. A tap is a device that controls the flow of a liquid or gas from a pipe or container, for example on a sink.

words.ex: He owes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归功于努力工作。
words.en: If you owe money to someone, they have lent it to you and you have not yet paid it back. You can also say that you owe someone a debt of gratitude if they have helped you in a way that you feel you should thank them for.

words.ex: The ministry of education controls schools.
words.ex_cn: 教育部管理学校。
words.en: A ministry is a government department, especially in Britain, which is responsible for a particular area of administration, such as health or education.

words.tr:
n. 个人；
adj. 个别的；单独的；
words.ex: Each individual has the right to speak freely.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都有权自由发言。
words.en: An individual is a person considered separately from their society or community. As an adjective, it describes something that is single, separate, or unique to a person or thing.

words.ex: He joined a local book association.
words.ex_cn: 他加入了一个本地的图书协会。
words.en: An association is an official group of people who have the same job, aim, or interest.

words.tr: v. 诱惑；引诱；怂恿；劝诱；
words.ex: The smell of cookies tempted him to eat one.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味诱惑他吃了一块。
words.en: If something tempts you, it makes you want to have it or do it, even though you know you should not.

words.tr:
v. 吸引；诱惑；引诱
n. 诱惑；诱饵；吸引力
words.ex: The bright colors lure the birds to the feeder.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引鸟类来到喂食器。
words.en: If you lure someone, you tempt them to do something or to go somewhere, especially by offering some form of reward.

words.ex: He tried to seduce her with flowers and gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和礼物引诱她。
words.en: To seduce someone means to persuade them to do something, especially something wrong or unwise, by making it seem attractive or exciting.

words.ex: The bright flowers attract bees.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的花朵吸引蜜蜂。
words.en: If something or someone attracts you, they have particular qualities which cause you to like or admire them.

words.ex: The shop tries to entice customers with cheap prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店试图以低价吸引顾客。
words.en: If you entice someone, you attract them to a particular place or activity by making it seem attractive or interesting.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.ex: The cat is beneath the table.
words.ex_cn: 猫在桌子下面。
words.en: In or to a lower position than someone or something, under someone or something.

words.tr: adv. 自然地；理所当然地；
words.ex: Babies cry naturally when they are hungry.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿饿了时会自然地哭。
words.en: in a natural manner; as a matter of course; by nature

words.ex: They enjoy walking in the natural scenery.
words.ex_cn: 他们喜欢在自然风景中散步。
words.en: Natural scenery refers to the landscape that is not man-made, including mountains, rivers, forests, and other elements of the natural world.

words.ex: The mountain view shows magnificent scenery at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 日出时，山景展现出壮丽的景色。

words.tr: n. 令人印象深刻的风景
words.ex: The mountain view offered impressive scenery.
words.ex_cn: 山景提供了令人印象深刻的风景。

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.ex: There was a torrential rain last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚下了一场猛烈的雨。
words.en: Used to describe something that is like a torrent; very heavy or fast and powerful.

words.tr:
n. 地中海；
adj. 地中海的；
words.ex: He sailed across the Mediterranean last summer.
words.ex_cn: 他去年夏天横渡了地中海。
words.en: relating to the Mediterranean Sea or the countries around it

words.ex: The rain caused a torrent down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨在山间形成了一股急流。
words.en: A torrent is a fast-moving stream of water or other liquid.

words.ex: The subterranean tunnel connects two buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这条地下的隧道连接着两栋大楼。
words.en: Existing, occurring, or done under the earth's surface.

words.ex: The hikers struggled across the rough terrain.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者艰难地穿越了崎岖的地形。
words.en: Terrain is used to refer to an area of land or a type of land when you are considering its physical features.

words.tr: adv. 更确切地说；宁可；相当；
words.ex: I don't like coffee; rather, I prefer tea.
words.ex_cn: 我不喜欢咖啡；更确切地说，我更喜欢茶。
words.en: You use rather to indicate that something is true to a fairly great extent, especially when you are talking about something unpleasant or undesirable.

words.ex: His success came from individual effort.
words.ex_cn: 他的成功来自个人努力。

words.ex: He put his individual interest before the team's needs.
words.ex_cn: 他把个人利益放在团队需求之前。

words.w: the food is served in individual portions
words.uk: ðə fuːd ɪz sɜːvd ɪn ˌɪndɪˈvɪdʒuəl ˈpɔːʃənz
words.us: ðə fuːd ɪz sɜːrvd ɪn ˌɪndɪˈvɪdʒuəl ˈpɔːrʃənz
words.ex: The food is served in individual portions at the buffet.
words.ex_cn: 自助餐上食物以单人份供应。

words.ex: Each student must complete the task individually.
words.ex_cn: 每个学生必须单独完成任务。
words.en: If something is done individually, it is done separately to each person or thing in a group.

words.ex: He is an individualistic person who likes to work alone.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢独来独往的个人主义的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as individualistic, you mean that they like to think and do things in their own way, rather than imitating other people.

words.tr:
n. 吸引力；上诉；
v. 吸引；诉请；呼吁；
words.ex: The appeal of the beach drew many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 海滩的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them. If you appeal against a decision or sentence, you formally ask a court or other authority to change it. If something appeals to you, you like it or it interests you.

words.ex: The old estate has large gardens and a beautiful mansion.
words.ex_cn: 这个古老的庄园有大片花园和一座美丽的豪宅。
words.en: An estate is all the money and property that someone owns, especially everything that is left when they die.

words.ex: Don't discourage him from trying.
words.ex_cn: 不要阻止他尝试。
words.en: If someone or something discourages you, they cause you to lose your enthusiasm about your actions.

words.ex: He is a candidate for the mayor position.
words.ex_cn: 他是市长职位的候选人。
words.en: A candidate is someone who is being considered for a position, for example someone who is running in an election or applying for a job.

words.ex: The ice melts in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 冰在阳光下融化。
words.en: If a solid substance melts or if you melt it, it changes to a liquid, usually because it has been heated.

words.tr: phrase. （使）解冻；（使）融化；（尤指天气转暖后）变暖和
words.ex: The frozen river will thaw out in spring.
words.ex_cn: v. 春天时，冰冻的河流会解冻。
words.en: To thaw out means to become unfrozen or to cause something to become unfrozen. It can also mean to become more friendly or less formal.

words.tr:
v. 熔炼；冶炼
v. 嗅；闻；散发气味；察觉；“smell”的过去式和过去分词
n. 胡瓜鱼
words.ex: They smelt iron ore to make steel.
words.ex_cn: 他们熔炼铁矿石来制造钢铁。
words.en: To smelt means to extract metal from ore by a process involving heating and melting.

words.tr: v. 由于保险丝烧断而电路不通；熔接；结合；
words.ex: The light went out because the fuse blew.
words.ex_cn: 灯灭了，因为保险丝烧断了。
words.en: A fuse is a safety device consisting of a strip of wire that melts and breaks an electric circuit if the current exceeds a safe level. As a verb, it means to join or blend to form a single entity.

words.tr:
n. 耸肩
v. 耸肩
words.ex: He shrugged when asked why he was late.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到为什么迟到时，他耸了耸肩。
words.en: If you shrug, you raise your shoulders to show that you are not interested in something or that you do not know or care about something.

words.tr: adj. 惊吓的；受惊的；害怕的； v. “frighten”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The child was frightened by the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 孩子被巨大的噪音吓到了。
words.en: If you are frightened, you are anxious or afraid, often because of something that has just happened or that you think may happen.

words.ex: He listens to music to relax.
words.ex_cn: 他听音乐来放松。
words.en: If you relax or if something relaxes you, you feel more calm and less worried or tense.

words.ex: He works in the aerospace industry.
words.ex_cn: 他在航空航天行业工作。
words.en: The branch of technology and industry concerned with both aviation and space flight.

words.ex: I suppose he is late because of the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我认为他因为交通堵塞而迟到了。
words.en: If you suppose that something is true, you believe or imagine that it is true, although you may not have any proof.

words.tr: adj. 说得过去的；站得住脚的；可防守的
words.ex: His excuse was a little weak, but still tenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口有点牵强，但还是说得过去的。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or plan is tenable, it is reasonable and could be successfully defended against criticism.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有判断力的；恰当的；合理的；
words.ex: It is sensible to wear a coat in cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 在寒冷的天气里穿外套是明智的。
words.en: A sensible person is able to make good judgments and decisions based on reason rather than emotion.

words.ex: The estate agent showed us the house.
words.ex_cn: 房产中介带我们看了那所房子。
words.en: An estate agent is a person whose job is to sell houses and land for people.

words.ex: He works in real estate in New York.
words.ex_cn: 他在纽约从事房地产行业。
words.en: Real estate refers to property consisting of land or buildings.

words.ex: He is a candidate for the mayor position.
words.ex_cn: 他是市长职位的一个候选人。

words.tr: v. 融化；熔化；消散；“melt”的现在分词； adj. 融化的；
words.ex: The ice is melting in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 冰在阳光下融化。
words.en: Becoming liquid, especially as a result of heating.

words.ex: Sugar dissolves in water.
words.ex_cn: 糖在水中溶解。
words.en: If a substance dissolves in liquid or if you dissolve a substance, it becomes mixed with the liquid and disappears.

words.ex: Salt is a solute in seawater.
words.ex_cn: 盐是海水中的溶质。
words.en: A solute is a substance that is dissolved in a solvent to form a solution.

words.ex: The storm caused the train to halt.
words.ex_cn: 风暴使火车中断了。
words.en: Halting is used to describe something that is done in a hesitant or faltering manner, often because of uncertainty or lack of confidence.

words.tr:
v. 中断；暂停；
n. 停顿下来；
words.ex: The storm halted the flight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴中断了航班。
words.en: to bring or come to a stop; a temporary or permanent stop

words.ex: Reading a book gives me relaxation.
words.ex_cn: 读书让我放松。
words.en: Relaxation is the state or process of becoming less tense, anxious, or stressed.

words.tr: phrase. 被期望做某事；应该做某事；被安排做某事
words.en: To be expected or required to perform a specific action.

words.ex: The tenant pays rent every month.
words.ex_cn: 房客每个月支付租金。
words.en: A tenant is a person who rents land or property from a landlord.

words.tr: n. 承租人；租赁人；出租人
words.ex: The renter agreed to pay the monthly rent on time.
words.ex_cn: 这位租贷人同意按时支付每月租金。
words.en: A renter is a person who pays rent for the use of land or a building.

words.ex: Honesty is the main tenet of his life.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是他生活的宗旨。
words.en: A tenet is a principle or belief, especially one that is part of a larger system of beliefs.

words.ex: The church teaches its doctrine to all members.
words.ex_cn: 教会向所有成员传授它的教义。
words.en: A doctrine is a set of beliefs or principles that are taught or accepted by a particular group, especially in religion or politics.

words.tr: adj. 可触摸的；实际的；有形的；确凿的；
words.ex: The statue is tangible and can be touched.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像可以触摸，是实实在在的。
words.en: Something that is tangible is clear enough or definite enough to be easily seen, felt, or noticed.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

words.ex: The cow eats straw from the barn.
words.ex_cn: 牛吃谷仓里的稻草。
words.en: A straw is a thin tube of paper or plastic that you use to suck a drink into your mouth.

words.ex: The river forms the border between the two countries.
words.ex_cn: 这条河是两个国家的边界。
words.en: The edge or boundary of something, or the part near it; a dividing line.

words.tr: n. 药剂师；配药师；分配者；自动售货机
words.ex: The dispenser gave me medicine for my cough.
words.ex_cn: 药剂师给了我治疗咳嗽的药。
words.en: A dispenser is a machine or container that automatically provides a specific amount of a product, such as food, drink, or money, when you operate it.

words.ex: He picked up the receiver to answer the phone.
words.ex_cn: 他拿起听筒接电话。
words.en: A receiver is a person who receives something or a device that receives signals and converts them into sound or pictures.

words.ex: He has a monopoly on selling ice cream in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他在这座小镇上垄断了冰淇淋的销售。
words.en: If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.

words.tr: n. 官僚主义；官僚机构
words.ex: He hates the bureaucracy in government offices.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌政府办公室里的官僚主义。
words.en: Bureaucracy refers to a system of government or business that has many complicated rules and ways of doing things.

words.ex: The construction of the new bridge took two years.
words.ex_cn: 新桥的建筑花了两年时间。
words.en: The process or method of building or making something, especially buildings, bridges, etc.

words.ex: The coach endorses the new player.
words.ex_cn: 教练支持这位新球员。
words.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them.

words.tr: n. 会员资格；全体会员；
words.ex: He paid $50 to get membership of the gym.
words.ex_cn: 他支付了50美元以获得健身房的会员资格。
words.en: Membership is the state of being a member of a group or organization.

words.tr: v. 承受苦难；忍受艰难困苦
words.ex: He sustained hardships during the war.
words.ex_cn: 他在战争期间承受了苦难。

words.tr: v. 维持一个人的精神；鼓舞某人的士气
words.ex: Kind words can sustain a person's spirit during hard times.
words.ex_cn: 温暖的话语能在艰难时刻维持一个人的精神。

words.ex: The company works hard to sustain growth every year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司努力每年维持增长。

words.ex: We need sustainable energy to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要可持续的能源来保护环境。
words.en: If something is sustainable, it can be maintained or continued at a certain rate or level without causing damage or depletion of resources.

words.ex: He pushed the trolley to carry the groceries.
words.ex_cn: 他推着手推车来搬购物品。
words.en: A trolley is a small vehicle with wheels that can be pushed or pulled along and is used for carrying things.

words.ex: The farmer drove his cart full of apples to the market.
words.ex_cn: 农夫驾着装满苹果的运货马车去市场。
words.en: A cart is a vehicle with two or four wheels that is pulled by a horse or a person and is used for carrying goods.

words.ex: He pushes a barrow full of bricks.
words.ex_cn: 他推着一辆装满砖块的手推车。
words.en: A barrow is a large mound of earth that was used to cover a grave in ancient times. It can also refer to a small cart with two wheels that is used for carrying goods.

words.ex: He pushed the wheelbarrow full of dirt.
words.ex_cn: 他推着装满泥土的手推车。
words.en: A wheelbarrow is a small cart with one wheel and two handles, used for carrying things in the garden or on a building site.

words.ex: Bees help to fertilize flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂帮助花朵受精。
words.en: To fertilize means to make soil or land more fertile or productive by adding substances to it, or to cause an egg, female animal, or plant to develop a new individual by introducing male reproductive material.

words.ex: Farmers spread manure on the fields to help crops grow.
words.ex_cn: 农民把肥料撒在田里以帮助庄稼生长。
words.en: Manure is organic matter used as fertilizer in agriculture.

words.ex: He uses fertilizer to help his plants grow.
words.ex_cn: 他用肥料帮助植物生长。
words.en: A substance that is added to soil to improve the growth of plants.

words.tr:
v. 快步；小跑；骑马小跑
n. 小跑；快步走
words.ex: The horse trots slowly on the path.
words.ex_cn: 马在小路上慢跑。
words.en: To trot means to move at a pace faster than a walk, with the legs moving in diagonal pairs, but not as fast as a gallop.

words.ex: The teacher will assign homework today.
words.ex_cn: 老师今天会布置作业。
words.en: To give someone a particular job or task; to allocate a resource or responsibility to a particular person or purpose.

words.ex: The nurse will dispense medicine to the patients.
words.ex_cn: 护士将分发药品给病人。
words.en: To dispense means to distribute or provide something, especially in a systematic way, or to prepare and give out medicine.

words.ex: The teacher will distribute the books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将把书分发给学生。
words.en: If you distribute things, you hand them or deliver them to a number of people.

words.ex: The teacher will allot five minutes for questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师会分配五分钟提问。
words.en: If something is allotted to someone, it is given to them as their share.

words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.tr: phrase. 自动提款机；自动柜员机
words.ex: The cash dispenser was out of order, so I couldn't withdraw any money.
words.ex_cn: 取款机坏了，所以我无法取钱。
words.en: A machine from which you can obtain money by using a special plastic card.

words.ex: The iris of her eye is blue.
words.ex_cn: 她的眼睛虹膜是蓝色的。
words.en: The iris is a flat, colored, ring-shaped membrane behind the cornea of the eye, with an adjustable circular opening (pupil) in the center.

words.ex: The doctor checked his retina with a special light.
words.ex_cn: 医生用特殊的光检查了他的视网膜。
words.en: The retina is the layer at the back of the eyeball that is sensitive to light and sends signals to the brain about what is seen.

words.ex: The new plan incorporates feedback from students.
words.ex_cn: 新计划包含了学生的反馈。
words.en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

words.ex: The package includes a free book.
words.ex_cn: 这个套餐包括一本免费的书。
words.en: If one thing includes another, it has the other thing as one of its parts.

words.ex: The team comprises five players and one coach.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队包括五名球员和一名教练。
words.en: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.

words.tr:
n. 首都；财富；大写字母；
adj. 大写的；
words.ex: Beijing is the capital of China.
words.ex_cn: 北京是中国的首都。
words.en: The city or town that functions as the seat of government and administrative center of a country or region.

words.tr: n. 资本垄断；由资本控制的独家垄断
words.ex: The government broke up the capital monopoly to encourage competition.
words.ex_cn: 政府打破了资本垄断以鼓励竞争。

words.tr: v. 支持（某候选人）；背书（某候选人）
words.ex: He will endorse a candidate who cares about education.
words.ex_cn: 他将支持一位关心教育的候选人。

words.ex: The embryo grows inside the mother's womb.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎在母亲的子宫内生长。
words.en: An embryo is an unborn animal or human being in the very early stages of development.

words.ex: The fetus is growing inside the mother's womb.
words.ex_cn: 胎儿正在母亲的子宫内成长。
words.en: An unborn or unhatched offspring of a mammal, in particular an unborn human more than eight weeks after conception.

words.ex: The foetus is growing inside the mother.
words.ex_cn: 胎儿正在母亲体内发育。
words.en: An unborn or unhatched offspring of a mammal, in particular an unborn human more than eight weeks after conception.

words.ex: He shows high intelligence in solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决数学问题时表现出很高的智力。
words.en: The ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills.

words.tr:
adj. 成熟的；
v. 成熟；
words.ex: He is a mature student who works full-time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成熟的学生，全职工作。
words.en: When something or someone matures, they become fully grown or developed. In finance, a mature investment is one that has reached the end of its term and is ready to be paid out.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

words.ex: He abandoned his car in the snow.
words.ex_cn: 他把车抛弃在雪地里。
words.en: If you abandon a place, thing, or person, you leave the place, thing, or person permanently or for a long time, especially when you should not do so.

words.tr:
n. 烤肉；烘烤；
adj. 烤的；焙的；
v. 烤；烘烤；
words.ex: We had roast for dinner last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚我们吃了烤肉。
words.en: To cook food, such as meat, in an oven or over a fire.

words.ex: The police investigated the assault on the old man.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了对那位老人的攻击。
words.en: An assault is a physical attack on someone, or a military attack on a place.

words.tr: n. 掠夺者；捕食性动物；食肉动物；
words.ex: The lion is a predator that hunts deer.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是一种捕食鹿的掠夺者。
words.en: A predator is an animal that naturally preys on others.

words.ex: The embryonic stage is the earliest phase of development.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎阶段是发育的最早时期。
words.en: In an early stage of development; rudimentary.

words.tr: phrase. 在胚胎阶段；在萌芽状态；尚未成熟的
words.ex: The project is still in embryo, but it shows great potential.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目还处于初期阶段，但显示出巨大的潜力。
words.en: In the early stages of development; not yet fully formed or realized.

words.ex: The teacher gave a comprehensive review before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试前给了一个全面的复习。
words.en: Something that is comprehensive includes everything that is needed or relevant.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.ex: The teacher spoke in a comprehensible way.
words.ex_cn: 老师用容易理解的方式讲话。
words.en: If something is comprehensible, you can understand it.

words.tr:
adj. 智力的；
n. 知识分子；
words.ex: He is an intellectual person who loves solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱解决数学问题的智力型人。
words.en: An intellectual is someone who spends a lot of time studying and thinking about complicated ideas.

words.tr: adj. 有才智的；聪明的；明智的；
words.ex: The intelligent boy solved the math problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个有才智的男孩很快解出了这道数学题。
words.en: Someone who is intelligent has the ability to think, understand, and learn things quickly and well.

words.tr: phrase. 成年学生；大龄学生（通常指年龄超过传统大学入学年龄、重返校园或首次进入高等教育的学生）
words.ex: Mature students often work while they study.
words.ex_cn: 成年学生常常一边工作一边学习。
words.en: Mature students are students who begin their studies at a university or college after a period of time spent working or doing something else, rather than going straight from school.

words.ex: On mature consideration, he decided to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 经过深思熟虑后，他决定辞去工作。

words.tr: phr. 经过深思熟虑后；经过慎重考虑后
words.ex: On mature reflection, he decided to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 经过深思熟虑后，他决定辞职。
words.en: After careful and thorough consideration.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.tr: phrase. 攻击型航空母舰；两栖攻击舰（一种主要用于搭载和支援登陆作战的军舰，可搭载直升机或短距起降飞机）
words.ex: The navy launched an assault carrier to support the mission.
words.ex_cn: 海军派出一艘两栖攻击舰来支持任务。
words.en: A military ship designed to transport and launch aircraft.

words.tr: n. 攻击部队；突击力量
words.ex: The assault force moved forward at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 攻击部队在黎明时前进。

words.ex: He tried to curb his horse with the reins.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用缰绳勒住马。
words.en: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: He tries to restrain his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他努力克制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you restrain someone, you stop them from doing what they intended or wanted to do, usually by using your physical strength.

words.tr:
n. 攻击；袭击；
v. 攻击；袭击；
words.ex: The attack happened at night.
words.ex_cn: 这次攻击发生在夜晚。
words.en: To attack means to try to hurt or defeat someone or something by using force or violence.

words.ex: He is a carrier of the flu virus.
words.ex_cn: 他是流感病毒的携带者。
words.en: A carrier is a person or thing that carries, holds, or conveys something.

words.ex: The aircraft landed safely at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 这架航空器在机场安全着陆。
words.en: An aircraft is a vehicle which can fly, for example an aeroplane or a helicopter.

words.ex: The lion is a predatory animal.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是一种食肉动物。
words.en: Predatory animals live by killing and eating other animals. Predatory people or organizations are eager to gain something out of someone else's weakness or suffering.

words.tr: v. 使计算机化；用计算机做
words.ex: The school will computerize its records next year.
words.ex_cn: 学校明年将把记录电脑化。
words.en: To computerize something means to use computers to control or operate it, or to change something so that it can be controlled or operated by computers.

words.tr: v. 使通俗化；宣传；推广；使普及
words.ex: He wants to popularize science among children.
words.ex_cn: 他想在儿童中普及科学。
words.en: To make something known or liked by many people.

words.ex: The country tried to devalue its currency.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家试图使本国货币贬值。
words.en: If you devalue something, you cause it to be thought less impressive or less deserving of respect.

words.ex: We took the ferry to cross the river.
words.ex_cn: 我们乘渡船过河。
words.en: A ferry is a boat that transports passengers and sometimes also vehicles, usually across rivers or short stretches of sea.

words.ex: The bridge is made of iron.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥是用铁建造的。
words.en: Iron is a strong hard metal that is used to make steel and is also found in small quantities in blood and food.

words.ex: He bullies his little brother every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都欺负他的弟弟。
words.en: To bully someone means to use your strength or power to hurt or frighten them, often forcing them to do something they do not want to do.

words.tr:
v. （风）狂吹；咆哮；恫吓；咄咄逼人
n. 狂风声；咆哮；吓唬；夸口
words.ex: The wind blustered through the trees all night.
words.ex_cn: 风整晚狂吹着穿过树木。
words.en: If you say that someone is blustering, you mean that they are speaking aggressively but without authority, often because they are angry or offended.

words.tr:
v. 虚张声势；唬人
n. 虚张声势；吓唬；峭壁
adj. 直率的
words.ex: He used a bluff to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用虚张声势赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you bluff, you try to make someone believe that you will do something when you do not really intend to do it, or that you know something when you do not really know it.

words.ex: The company is undergoing computerization to improve efficiency.
words.ex_cn: 公司正在实施计算机化以提高效率。
words.en: The process of equipping a process, activity, or equipment with computers or of adapting something to the use of computers.

words.ex: The popularization of the internet has revolutionized communication.
words.ex_cn: 互联网的普及彻底改变了通信方式。
words.en: The act of making something widely known and accepted by the general public.

words.tr: adv. 公正地；正当地；应得地
words.ex: He was justly punished for lying.
words.ex_cn: 他因为撒谎而得到了应有的惩罚。
words.en: In a fair and deserved manner; rightly.

words.ex: He was unjustly punished for a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因一个错误而被不公正地惩罚了。
