words.en: In a manner that is not fair or just.

words.ex: The government announced a devaluation of the currency.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布货币贬值。
words.en: A reduction in the value of a currency with respect to other monetary units.

words.tr: v. 解决；消除（问题或分歧）；把某事彻底理顺
words.ex: They met to iron out the problems with the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他们见面解决了计划中的问题。

words.ex: The movie has a simple storyline.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影有一个简单的故事情节。
words.en: The plot or main story of a narrative, especially in a movie, novel, or play.

words.tr:
n. 轨道；
v. 绕...轨道而行；
words.ex: The moon moves around the Earth in an orbit.
words.ex_cn: 月亮围绕地球在轨道上运行。
words.en: An orbit is the curved path, usually elliptical, described by a planet, satellite, spaceship, etc., around a celestial body, as the sun.

words.tr:
v. 防止；战斗；抑制；
n. 战斗；
words.ex: The new law aims to combat pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律旨在防止污染。
words.en: Combat refers to fighting, especially during a war. It can also mean to try to stop something harmful from happening or increasing.

words.ex: He is slothful and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他懒惰，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as slothful, you mean that they are lazy.

words.tr: adj. 懒惰的；邋遢的；淫荡的
words.ex: He gave a sluttish performance, ignoring his duties.
words.ex_cn: 他表现得很懒惰，忽视了自己的职责。
words.en: If you describe a woman as sluttish, you mean that she is untidy, dirty, or behaves in a sexually immoral way.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；懒散的；马虎的
words.ex: He is lax about his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业很松懈。
words.en: If you say that a person's behaviour or a system is lax, you mean they are not careful or strict about maintaining high standards.

words.ex: The earthquake caused catastrophic damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: A catastrophic event or situation is one that causes great damage or suffering.

words.ex: You must abide by the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: If you can't abide someone or something, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: The allure of money made him take the risky job.
words.ex_cn: 金钱的诱惑让他接受了这份高风险的工作。
words.en: The quality of being powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.ex: Plants release oxygen into the air.
words.ex_cn: 植物向空气中释放氧气。
words.en: A colourless, odourless reactive gas, the chemical element of atomic number 8 and the life-supporting component of the air.

words.ex: The smell of flowers was pervasive in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花的香味遍布整个花园。
words.en: Something that is pervasive is present or noticeable throughout a place or thing.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: The combatant fought bravely in the battle.
words.ex_cn: 这名战斗人员在战斗中英勇作战。
words.en: A combatant is a person or country involved in fighting during a war.

words.ex: The pilot flew a fighter jet over the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员驾驶一架战斗机飞越了山脉。
words.en: A fighter is someone who fights in a battle or war, or someone who is determined to achieve something despite difficulties.

words.ex: He is combative in every meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在每次会议上都好斗。
words.en: Someone who is combative is aggressive and eager to fight or argue.

words.tr:
adj. 激进的；好战的
n. 激进；好战
words.ex: He is a militant who protests every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天抗议的激进分子。
words.en: A militant person is someone who is engaged in warfare or combat, or who is aggressively active in a cause.

words.ex: You must abide by the school rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守校规。
words.en: To accept or act in accordance with a rule, decision, or recommendation.

words.tr:
adj. 诱人的；迷人的；有吸引力的
v. 诱惑；吸引；“allure”的现在分词
words.ex: The city's nightlife is alluring to many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的夜生活对许多游客来说都极具诱惑力。
words.en: Something that is alluring is powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.ex: Her smile has a special charm.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑有一种特别的魅力。
words.en: If you say that someone has charm, you mean that they behave in a friendly and pleasant way that makes people like them. A charm is also a small ornament that is fixed to a bracelet or necklace.

words.ex: The bright flowers attract bees.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的花朵吸引蜜蜂。
words.en: If something or someone attracts you, they have particular qualities which cause you to like or admire them.

words.tr:
adj. 迷人的；吸引人的
v. 迷惑；吸引住；奴役；“enthrall”的现在分词
words.ex: The book was an enthralling tale of adventure.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是一个引人入胜的冒险故事。
words.en: If you describe something as enthralling, you mean it is so interesting and exciting that it holds your attention completely.

words.tr: adj. 引起兴趣的； v. 吸引；“appeal”的现在分词；
words.ex: The book has an appealing story.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有一个引人入胜的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as appealing, you mean that you like them or they make you want to have or do something.

words.tr: adj. 欺骗的；消遣的；令人陶醉的; v. 欺骗；使愉快地度过；迷住（beguile 的 ing ...
words.ex: The beguiling smile made him trust her.
words.ex_cn: 那迷人的微笑让他信任了她。
words.en: Something that is beguiling is charming and attractive, often in a way that is deceptive.

words.tr: n. 对老年人的歧视；年龄歧视
words.ex: He faced ageism when he applied for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他申请工作时遭遇了年龄歧视。
words.en: Ageism is prejudice or discrimination on the grounds of a person's age.

words.tr: v. 使根深蒂固；使处于牢固地位；用壕沟围住
words.ex: The habit entrenches itself over time.
words.ex_cn: 这个习惯随着时间的推移变得根深蒂固。
words.en: To establish something very firmly so that it is very difficult to change.

words.tr: adj. 确立的；根深蒂固的； v. “entrench”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The entrenched system is hard to change.
words.ex_cn: 这个已确立的制度很难改变。
words.en: If something is entrenched, it is firmly established and very difficult to change.

words.ex: The smell of bread pervades the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫在整个厨房里。
words.en: If something pervades a place or thing, it is present throughout it.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.ex: Water can penetrate the soil slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水可以慢慢渗透进土壤。
words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.tr: adj. 可渗透的；可渗入的；
words.ex: The soil is permeable, so water passes through easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种土壤是可渗透的，所以水很容易通过。
words.en: If a substance is permeable, it allows liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.tr: v. 侵入；侵占；侵犯；侵蚀
words.ex: The new building encroaches on the park.
words.ex_cn: 新建筑侵占了公园。
words.en: To gradually take something such as power or authority from someone else, often in a way that is not fair or legal.

words.ex: The movie was fantastic!
words.ex_cn: 这部电影极好！
words.en: If you describe something as fantastic, you are emphasizing that you think it is very good or that you like it a lot.

words.tr: adj. 可恶的；令人憎恶的；令人痛恨的
words.ex: He finds lying to friends abhorrent.
words.ex_cn: 他认为对朋友撒谎是令人厌恶的。
words.en: If something is abhorrent to you, you hate it very much, often because you think it is immoral or wrong.

words.tr: v. 把…强加给；使遭受；使承受
words.ex: The storm inflicted heavy damage on the village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给村庄造成了严重破坏。
words.en: If you inflict something unpleasant on someone, you make them suffer it.

words.ex: The government imposed a new tax on sugar.
words.ex_cn: 政府对糖征收了一项新税。
words.en: To impose means to officially force a rule, tax, punishment, etc. to be obeyed or received.

words.tr:
v. （使）倾斜；（使）偏向
n. 倾斜；企图
words.ex: The boy tilt the cup and spill the water.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把杯子倾斜，水洒了出来。
words.en: If you tilt an object or if it tilts, it moves into a sloping position with one end or side higher than the other.

words.tr: adj. 冒犯的；令人不快的；进攻性的；
words.ex: His offensive words made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他冒犯的话让她哭了。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as offensive, you mean that it is rude or insulting.

words.ex: He used too much jargon in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中用了太多行话。
words.en: Special words or expressions that are used by a particular profession or group and are difficult for others to understand.

words.ex: The movie was fantastically funny.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影极其搞笑。
words.en: In a manner that is extraordinarily good or attractive; in a way that is difficult to believe.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is marvelous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色极好。
words.en: If you describe something as marvelous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely good.

words.ex: He ate a super big pizza.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一块超大的披萨。
words.en: If you describe something as super, you mean that it is very good indeed.

words.tr:
adj. 糟糕的；可怕的；
adv. 非常；极其；
words.ex: The weather today is awful.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气很糟糕。
words.en: If you say that something is awful, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant, shocking, or bad.

words.tr: adj. 普通的；平常的；一般的；
words.ex: He wore an ordinary shirt to school.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件普通的衬衫去学校。
words.en: Something that is ordinary is not special or different in any way.

words.tr: v. 强行打扰某人；不请自来地纠缠某人
words.ex: He didn't want to inflict himself on his friends during the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 他不想在假期里强行打扰朋友。

words.ex: Please don't disturb me while I'm reading.
words.ex_cn: 我读书时请不要打扰我。
words.en: To disturb someone means to interrupt what they are doing and cause them inconvenience or annoyance.

words.ex: The problem recurs every week.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题每周都会再次出现。
words.en: If something recurs, it happens again, either once or several times.

words.ex: The recurrence of storms caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 风暴的反复出现造成了许多问题。
words.en: The return of a sign, symptom, or disease after a remission.

words.ex: The government's exchequer has been boosted by recent tax reforms.
words.ex_cn: 政府的财库因最近的税制改革而得到增强。
words.en: The Exchequer is the account at the Bank of England in which is held the Consolidated Fund, out of which most government payments are made.

words.ex: The government made a fiscal decision to lower taxes.
words.ex_cn: 政府做出了降低税收的财政决定。
words.en: Fiscal is used to describe something that relates to government money or public money, especially taxes.

words.ex: The infliction of pain is illegal.
words.ex_cn: 施加痛苦是非法的。
words.en: The act of imposing something unpleasant or painful on someone or something.

words.ex: His rude words were an offense to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话冒犯了所有人。
words.en: An offense is a crime or a violation of the law; it can also refer to a feeling of being upset or annoyed by something perceived as insulting or disrespectful.

words.tr: adv. 冒犯地；不愉快地；讨厌地
words.ex: He spoke offensively about her appearance.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的外貌出言不逊。
words.en: In a manner that causes someone to feel upset, annoyed, or resentful.

words.ex: The offensiveness of his words made everyone upset.
words.ex_cn: 他话语的冒犯性让所有人都感到不快。
words.en: The quality of being offensive or causing resentment.

words.tr: adj. 无害的；不触犯人的；不讨厌的
words.ex: He gave an inoffensive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个无害的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as inoffensive, you mean that they are not unpleasant or unacceptable in any way.

words.tr: n. 法律术语；法律行话
words.ex: The contract was full of legal jargon.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同充满了法律术语。

words.tr:
n. 术语；学期；期限；措辞；
v. 把…称作；把…叫做；
words.ex: The word 'algorithm' is a technical term in computer science.
words.ex_cn: ‘算法’是计算机科学中的一个术语。
words.en: A term is a word or expression used in relation to a particular subject, especially one that has a specific meaning, or a fixed period of time during which something lasts or is intended to happen.

words.ex: The doctor used medical terminology to explain the illness.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用医学术语来解释这种疾病。
words.en: The set of terms and expressions used in a particular subject, field, or profession.

words.ex: He bought an extravagant car that cost too much money.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆奢侈的车，价格太贵了。
words.en: Spending much more than is necessary or wise; excessively expensive.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏的；污秽的
v. （使）弄脏；（使）玷污；“begrime”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The old window was begrimed with dirt.
words.ex_cn: 那扇旧窗户被灰尘弄脏了。
words.en: Covered with dirt or soot; made dirty.

words.tr: v. 污染；弄脏；“contaminate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The river was contaminated by factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 河流被工厂废料污染了。
words.en: If something is contaminated, it has been made dirty or harmful, usually by the addition of something, especially chemicals or radiation.

words.tr: adj. 积满污垢的；肮脏的
words.ex: The boy's hands are grimy from playing in the dirt.
words.ex_cn: 男孩的手因为玩土变得脏兮兮的。
words.en: Something that is grimy is very dirty.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏恶臭的；
v. 对…犯规；
words.ex: The foul smell came from the garbage bin.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自垃圾桶。
words.en: If you describe something as foul, you mean it is dirty and smells or tastes unpleasant. In sports, a foul is an act that is against the rules of the game.

words.ex: The floor was filthy after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨过后，地板变得非常肮脏。
words.en: Something that is filthy is extremely dirty.

words.tr: adj. 无情的；冷酷的；残忍的；
words.ex: The ruthless boss fired employees without warning.
words.ex_cn: 这位无情的老板未经警告就解雇了员工。
words.en: If you say that someone is ruthless, you mean that you disapprove of them because they are very harsh or cruel, and will do anything that is necessary to achieve what they want.

words.tr: adj. 严厉的；严峻的；冷酷无情的；坚定的；可怕的
words.ex: He had a grim look on his face.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上带着严峻的表情。
words.en: If a situation or piece of news is grim, it is very serious, unpleasant, and depressing.

words.tr: adj. 不同的；多种多样的；
words.ex: The class has diverse students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级有来自许多国家的不同学生。
words.en: If a group or range of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things.

words.tr: adj. 各种各样的；不同的；各种的；
words.ex: He bought various fruits at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了各种各样的水果。
words.en: If you say that there are various things, you mean there are several different things of the type mentioned.

words.ex: He extinguished the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水把火扑灭了。
words.en: To extinguish a fire or a light means to stop it burning or shining.

words.ex: He estranged his brother with harsh words.
words.ex_cn: 他用刻薄的话与兄弟疏远了。
words.en: If you estrange someone, especially a member of your family, you cause them to stop being friendly or close to you.

words.ex: His rude behavior alienated his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的行为使朋友们疏远了他。
words.en: To cause someone to feel isolated or estranged; to transfer the ownership of property to another.

words.ex: The building has a neoclassical style with white columns.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑有着带有白色柱子的新古典主义风格。
words.en: Neoclassical refers to a revival of classical styles or influence in art, literature, architecture, or music.

words.tr: adj. 有偏见的； v. “bias”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The judge was biased against the defendant.
words.ex_cn: 这位法官对被告有偏见。
words.en: If someone is biased, they prefer one group of people to another, and behave unfairly as a result.

words.tr:
adj. 有偏见的；偏爱的；偏心的
v. 使有偏见；损害；“prejudice”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was prejudiced against people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对他国人民有偏见。
words.en: If someone is prejudiced, they have an unreasonable dislike of or preference for someone or something, especially based on their race, sex, religion, etc.

words.ex: The extravagant price of the diamond ring surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这枚钻石戒指的奢侈价格让所有人都感到惊讶。

words.tr: n. 奢侈的行为；挥霍无度的举动
words.ex: His extravagant act of buying a diamond watch shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他买钻石手表的奢侈行为让所有人都震惊了。

words.ex: He spent extravagantly on clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他花在衣服上的钱非常奢侈。
words.en: In a manner that is excessive or elaborate, especially in terms of spending money or using resources.

words.ex: He bought a luxury car as an extravagance.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆豪华汽车作为奢侈品。
words.en: Extravagance refers to the spending of more money than is reasonable or than you can afford, or the use of more of something than is necessary.

words.ex: He ate excessive amounts of candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了过多的糖果。
words.en: If you describe the amount or level of something as excessive, you disapprove of it because it is more or higher than is necessary or reasonable.

words.ex: His hands were begrimed with dirt from working in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园里干活，双手沾满了污垢。
words.en: To make something dirty, especially with soot or dirt.

words.ex: The river is contaminated by factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这条河被工厂废料污染了。
words.en: To contaminate something means to make it impure or polluted by contact or mixture with something unclean or harmful.

words.tr:
n. 漠视；忽视；
v. 漠视；不理会；不顾；
words.ex: His advice was met with disregard.
words.ex_cn: 他的建议遭到了漠视。
words.en: If you disregard something, you ignore it or do not take account of it.

words.tr: adv. 残忍地；冷酷地；无情地
words.ex: He ruthlessly fired the employee.
words.ex_cn: 他无情地解雇了那位员工。
words.en: If someone is ruthless, they are determined to get what they want and do not care if they hurt other people.

words.ex: The cruel king punished the innocent people.
words.ex_cn: 残酷的国王惩罚了无辜的人。
words.en: Someone who is cruel deliberately causes pain or distress to others or feels no concern about it.

words.tr: phrase. 多样的文化；不同的文化
words.ex: The city has diverse cultures from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市有来自许多国家的多元文化。
words.en: A variety of different cultural traditions, beliefs, and practices.

words.ex: The school values diversity in its students.
words.ex_cn: 学校重视学生的多样性。
words.en: The state of being diverse; variety.

words.ex: He tries to assimilate new words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力吸收新单词。
words.en: To assimilate means to take in and understand fully ideas, information, or culture, or to make something become part of a group or system.

words.ex: The stomach digests food into nutrients.
words.ex_cn: 胃将食物消化成营养物质。
words.en: To digest means to break down food in the stomach and intestines into substances that can be absorbed by the body. It can also mean to understand or assimilate information. As a noun, it refers to a compilation or summary of information.

words.ex: He drew a geometric shape on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上画了一个几何图形。
words.en: Relating to geometry, or according to its methods and principles.

words.ex: The grandeur of the palace amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿的宏伟让每个人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being grand or splendid in appearance or style.

words.tr:
n. 规模；等级；比例（尺）；刻度；秤；
v. 改变…大小；
words.ex: The scale of the project surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的规模让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A scale is a set of levels or numbers which are used in a particular system of measuring things or are used when comparing things.

words.ex: This chemical is an enhancer for plant growth.
words.ex_cn: 这种化学物质是植物生长的增强剂。
words.en: An enhancer is something that improves the quality, value, or extent of something else.

words.ex: His ulterior motive was to get money.
words.ex_cn: 他别有用心，目的是弄到钱。
words.en: If you say that someone has an ulterior motive for doing something, you believe that they have a hidden reason for doing it.

words.tr:
v. 使腐败；
adj. 腐败的；
words.ex: The official was corrupt by taking bribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员因收受贿赂而腐败。
words.en: If someone is corrupt, they do things that are dishonest or illegal in order to gain money or power.

words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.tr: adj. 刻板的；坚硬的；严格的；
words.ex: He has a rigid attitude toward rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的态度很刻板。
words.en: not able to be changed or adapted; not able to be bent or moved; stiff

words.tr: adj. 严格的；缜密的；严密的；
words.ex: The teacher is rigorous about homework deadlines.
words.ex_cn: 老师对作业截止日期要求严格。
words.en: If you are rigorous in something, you are very thorough and strict in the way you do it.

words.ex: My teacher is strict about homework deadlines.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师对作业截止日期要求很严格。
words.en: If someone is strict, they behave firmly and make sure that rules are obeyed.

words.ex: He is a novice at playing the guitar.
words.ex_cn: 他是个吉他新手。
words.en: A novice is someone who has just started learning or doing something and does not have much experience.

words.ex: He is a beginner in piano lessons.
words.ex_cn: 他是钢琴课的初学者。
words.en: A beginner is someone who has just started learning to do something and has not yet mastered it.

words.tr: phrase. 新手；生手；缺乏经验的人
words.ex: He is a green hand in the field of computer programming.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机编程领域是个新手。
words.en: A person who is new to or inexperienced in a particular activity or job.

words.ex: Rain can hinder our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨天会妨碍我们去徒步旅行的计划。
words.en: If something hinders you, it makes it more difficult for you to do something or make progress.

words.ex: The fallen tree impeded the car's path.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树阻碍了汽车的前进。
words.en: To impede something means to make its movement, development, or progress difficult.

words.tr:
v. 阻碍；妨碍
n. （带盖）篮子
words.ex: Rain hampered our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨妨碍了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If something hampers you, it makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.tr:
n. 大楼；大厦；块；街区；障碍物；
v. 阻塞；阻碍；
words.ex: The new block is next to the park.
words.ex_cn: 这栋新大楼就在公园旁边。
words.en: A block is a large solid piece of material with flat surfaces on each side. As a verb, to block means to prevent movement or progress.

words.ex: He is encumbered by too many debts.
words.ex_cn: 他被太多的债务拖累。
words.en: To encumber someone or something means to weigh them down or to block or hinder them.

words.ex: The tortoise moves slowly across the grass.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟慢慢地在草地上爬行。
words.en: A tortoise is a slow-moving land animal with a shell into which it can pull its head and legs for protection.

words.ex: She added a flavour enhancer to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 她往汤里加了一种增味剂。
words.en: A substance added to food to intensify its existing flavour.

words.ex: This food contains a harmless additive for flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这种食物含有用于调味的无害添加物。
words.en: An additive is a substance which is added in small amounts to something else in order to improve it, preserve it, or make it more effective.

words.ex: He has an ulterior motive for helping her.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助她是有隐秘的动机。

words.ex: He saved the file on the hard disk.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件保存在硬盘上。
words.en: A hard disk is a rigid magnetic disk fixed permanently within a drive unit and used for storing computer data.

words.ex: The computer's hard drive is full.
words.ex_cn: 电脑的硬盘已满。
words.en: A hard drive is a piece of hardware in a computer that stores and retrieves digital information using rapidly rotating disks coated with magnetic material.

words.tr: v. 阻止；妨碍（某人做某事）
words.ex: The rain hindered them from leaving the house.
words.ex_cn: 雨阻止了他们出门。

words.ex: The bird flew unhindered across the sky.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿毫无阻碍地飞过天空。
words.en: Not obstructed or impeded; free to move or progress.

words.ex: The rain was a hindrance to the game.
words.ex_cn: 雨水对比赛造成了妨碍。
words.en: A hindrance is a person or thing that makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.tr: adj. 穷困的；赤穷的；贫瘠的； v. “impoverish”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The impoverished family lived in a small house with no heating.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫困的家庭住在一个没有暖气的小房子里。
words.en: An impoverished person or area is very poor.

words.ex: The pond is shallow, so you can see the bottom.
words.ex_cn: 这个池塘很浅，所以你能看到底部。
words.en: If something is shallow, it does not extend far down from the top surface.

words.tr: v. 淹没；泛滥；使不胜负荷；使应接不暇
words.ex: The rain inundated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 大雨淹没了这个小镇。
words.en: To inundate means to flood or overwhelm something with a large amount of water or things.

words.tr: v. 侵蚀；腐蚀；逐渐丧失；削弱
words.ex: The wind erodes the sand slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢侵蚀着沙子。
words.en: If rock or soil erodes or is eroded by the weather, sea, or wind, it cracks and breaks so that it is gradually destroyed.

words.ex: The iron fence will corrode in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 铁栅栏在雨中会生锈。
words.en: If metal or stone corrodes, or if something corrodes it, it is gradually destroyed by a chemical reaction.

words.tr:
n. 厄运；毁灭；死亡
v. 注定；判决
words.ex: The old prophecy spoke of doom for the kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 古老的预言说这个王国将遭遇厄运。
words.en: Doom is a terrible fate or destiny that you cannot avoid, especially death or destruction.

words.ex: He commiserated with his friend after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 他在朋友失利后安慰了他。
words.en: If you commiserate with someone, you show them pity or sympathy because something unpleasant has happened to them.

words.tr:
n. 亡命之徒；逃犯；被剥夺法律权益者
v. 宣布…为非法；使…成为非法
words.ex: The police caught the outlaw last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚抓住了那个不法之徒。
words.en: An outlaw is a person who has broken the law and who is hiding or running away to avoid punishment. To outlaw something means to make it illegal.

words.tr:
adj. 疏远的；不合群的
v. 使疏远；离间；转让；“alienate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt alienated after his friends stopped talking to him.
words.ex_cn: 他的朋友们不再和他说话后，他感到被疏远了。
words.en: Feeling isolated or estranged from a group or activity to which one should belong or in which one should be involved.

words.ex: The long silence caused alienation between them.
words.ex_cn: 长久的沉默导致了他们之间的离间。
words.en: Alienation refers to the state or experience of being isolated from a group or an activity to which one should belong or in which one should be involved.

words.ex: He shows passion for playing basketball every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天对打篮球充满热情。

words.ex: She showed sympathy for the lost children.
words.ex_cn: 她对那些迷路的孩子表示同情。

words.tr: v. 对某事表示同情；怜悯某事
words.ex: She shows compassion for homeless people.
words.ex_cn: 她对无家可归的人表示同情。

words.tr: adj. 有同情心的；表示怜悯的；
words.ex: She is a compassionate teacher who helps struggling students.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位有同情心的老师，帮助学习困难的学生。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as compassionate, you mean that they feel or show pity, sympathy, and understanding for people who are suffering.

words.ex: Children play on the pavement after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在人行道上玩耍。
words.en: A pavement is a path with a hard surface, usually by the side of a road, that people walk on.

words.ex: The old computer is antiquated and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧电脑过时且缓慢。
words.en: Something that is antiquated is old-fashioned or outdated and no longer suitable for modern conditions or purposes.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；废弃的；淘汰的；
words.ex: This phone is obsolete because it doesn't work with new apps.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，因为它不能使用新应用。
words.en: Something that is obsolete is no longer needed because something better has been invented.

words.ex: The fish swim among the coral in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在海中的珊瑚间游动。
words.en: A hard stony substance secreted by certain marine coelenterates as an external skeleton, typically forming large reefs in warm seas.

words.tr: v. 焚化；焚毁；把…烧成灰烬
words.ex: The city will incinerate the trash tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市明天将焚烧垃圾。
words.en: To incinerate something means to burn it until it is reduced to ash.

words.tr: adj. 可更新的；可再生的；
words.ex: Solar energy is a renewable resource.
words.ex_cn: 太阳能是一种可更新的资源。
words.en: A renewable resource is a natural resource which will replenish to replace the portion depleted by usage and consumption, either through natural reproduction or other recurring processes in a finite amount of time in a human time scale.

words.ex: He hurt his shin while kicking the ball.
words.ex_cn: 他踢球时伤到了胫部。
words.en: The front part of the leg below the knee.

words.tr: v. 奴役；征服；使受控制
words.ex: The cruel king tried to enslave the villagers.
words.ex_cn: 这个残酷的国王试图奴役村民。
words.en: To make someone a slave; to take away someone's freedom.

words.ex: The timid boy whispered his answer.
words.ex_cn: 这个害羞的男孩小声说出了他的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or actions as timid, you are criticizing them for being too cautious or slow to act, because they are nervous about the possible consequences of their actions.

words.tr: adj. 糟糕透顶的；恶劣的；卑鄙的
words.ex: He said a vile thing to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友说了句卑鄙的话。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is vile, you mean that they are extremely unpleasant.

words.tr: v. 在街上奔波；四处奔波寻找工作或机会
words.ex: He pounded the pavement looking for a job.
words.ex_cn: 他四处奔波找工作。

words.ex: The book costs five pounds.
words.ex_cn: 这本书五英镑。
words.en: The pound is the unit of money used in Britain. It is also a unit of weight equal to 16 ounces or 0.4536 kilograms. As a verb, to pound means to hit something hard many times or to crush something into a powder or paste.

words.ex: He positively believes in his dream.
words.ex_cn: 他积极地相信自己的梦想。
words.en: In a positive manner; with certainty.

words.ex: The fish swim near the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在珊瑚礁附近游动。
words.en: A reef is a long line of rocks or sand, the top of which is just above or just below the surface of the sea.

words.tr: phrase. 珊瑚礁；由珊瑚虫的骨骼在海洋中堆积形成的岩石状结构
words.ex: Fish live in coral reefs.
words.ex_cn: 鱼生活在珊瑚礁中。
words.en: Underwater ecosystems built by colonies of tiny animals, known for their biodiversity.

words.ex: The factory uses renewable raw materials like bamboo and cotton.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂使用竹子和棉花等可再生的原材料。

words.tr: v. 用腿爬升（如爬杆或树）
words.ex: The boy shinned up the tree to get his kite.
words.ex_cn: 男孩用腿爬上了树去拿他的风筝。

words.tr: v. 沿着小腿下滑（非标准用法，无明确释义）
words.ex: The sweat began to shin down his leg after the long run.
words.ex_cn: 长时间跑步后，汗水开始沿着小腿下滑。

words.tr: n. 胫骨应力综合征；小腿疼痛综合征
words.ex: He stopped running because of shin splints.
words.ex_cn: 他因为胫骨应力综合征停止了跑步。

words.ex: The doctor put a splint on his broken arm.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他骨折的手臂上了夹板。
words.en: A splint is a long, thin piece of wood or metal that is used to hold a broken bone in place while it heals.

words.ex: His addiction led to the enslavement of his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他的上瘾导致了心灵的束缚。
words.en: The act of making someone a slave; the state of being a slave.

words.ex: His timidity made him afraid to speak in class.
words.ex_cn: 他的胆怯让他不敢在课堂上发言。
words.en: The quality or state of being timid; lack of courage or self-confidence.

words.ex: She timidly raised her hand to ask a question.
words.ex_cn: 她胆怯地举手问了一个问题。
words.en: In a manner that shows a lack of courage or confidence; shyly.

words.tr:
adj. 怯懦的；胆小的
adv. 胆怯地
words.ex: He was cowardly and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as cowardly, you disapprove of them because they are easily frightened and avoid dangerous or difficult situations.

words.ex: The shy boy didn't speak in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个害羞的男孩在课堂上没有说话。
words.en: If you are shy, you are nervous and uncomfortable in the company of other people.

words.ex: He gave a bold speech in front of the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前发表了大胆的演讲。
words.en: Someone who is bold is not afraid to do things which involve risk or danger.

words.ex: The vileness of his words made everyone upset.
words.ex_cn: 他话语的讨厌让每个人都感到不安。
words.en: The state or quality of being morally repulsive or extremely unpleasant.

words.tr: phrase. 保持低调；不引人注目
words.ex: In order to avoid unwanted attention, he decided to keep a low profile.
words.ex_cn: 为了避免不必要的关注，他决定保持低调。
words.en: To avoid attracting attention or publicity; to stay out of the public eye.

words.ex: The truck runs on diesel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车使用柴油运行。
words.en: Diesel is a type of heavy oil used as fuel in diesel engines.

words.tr: v. 狂吃暴饮；大吃大喝；大量消耗
words.ex: He guzzles soda every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都大口喝苏打水。
words.en: If you guzzle something, you drink it quickly and greedily.

words.tr:
n. 痛苦；折磨；令人痛苦的东西
v. 折磨；使痛苦；烦扰；纠缠；戏弄
words.ex: The loss of his dog was a deep torment.
words.ex_cn: 失去他的狗是一种深深的痛苦。
words.en: Torment refers to severe physical or mental suffering, or to cause someone to experience such suffering.

words.ex: The medicine helped revive the sick man.
words.ex_cn: 这剂药帮助这位病人恢复了生机。
words.en: To revive something means to bring it back to life, consciousness, or use, or to make it active or successful again.

words.ex: The city plan will revitalize the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市计划将使老城区复兴。
words.en: To revitalize something means to give it new life or energy.

words.ex: The prison conditions were inhumane.
words.ex_cn: 监狱的条件是不人道的。
words.en: If you describe something as inhumane, you mean that it is extremely cruel.

words.tr: adj. 野蛮的；无人性的；残忍的
words.ex: The prison conditions were inhuman.
words.ex_cn: 监狱的条件十分野蛮。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as inhuman, you mean that they are extremely cruel or unpleasant.

words.ex: Smoking can imperil your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会危及你的健康。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk of being harmed, damaged, or destroyed.

words.tr: v. 使遭危险或伤害；危害；危及
words.ex: Pollution can endanger animals.
words.ex_cn: 污染会危及动物。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk or in danger.

words.ex: The two roads diverge after the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 两条路在桥后分岔。
words.en: If one thing diverges from another similar thing, the first thing becomes different from the second or develops differently from it. You can also say that two things diverge.

words.ex: The truck is powered by a diesel engine.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车由柴油发动机驱动。
words.en: A diesel engine is an internal combustion engine in which ignition of the fuel is caused by the elevated temperature of the air in the cylinder due to the mechanical compression.

words.ex: He is a big guzzler of soda.
words.ex_cn: 他是个喝苏打水的大胃王。
words.en: A person or thing that consumes something in large, greedy amounts.

words.tr: v. 处于痛苦之中；备受折磨
n. 民间艺人；民俗艺术家
words.ex: The folk artist sang traditional songs at the village festival.
words.ex_cn: 这位民间艺人在村庄节日上演唱了传统歌曲。

words.ex: The revival of traditional music brought joy to many people.
words.ex_cn: 传统音乐的复兴给许多人带来了快乐。
words.en: The process of something becoming popular or active again after a period of inactivity or decline.

words.ex: He will restore the old bike.
words.ex_cn: 他将修复这辆旧自行车。
words.en: To restore something means to bring it back to its original condition or to a state of health, efficiency, or good management.

words.ex: He reverted to his old habits after the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 假期后，他恢复了旧习惯。
words.en: To return to a former state, practice, topic, etc.

words.tr: v. 衰弱；凋萎；憔悴；受折磨
words.ex: The prisoner languishes in a dark cell.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯在黑暗的牢房中饱受煎熬。
words.en: If someone languishes somewhere, they are forced to remain and suffer in an unpleasant situation.

words.tr: n. 血汗工厂； 活计苦累、工资低薄的工厂
words.ex: The documentary exposed the harsh conditions in sweatshops.
words.ex_cn: 这部纪录片揭露了血汗工厂的恶劣条件。
words.en: A sweatshop is a small factory where workers are paid very little and work long hours in poor conditions.

words.tr:
adj. 次要的；轻微的；小的；小调的；
n. 未成年人；
words.ex: The mistake was a minor error.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误是一个小错误。
words.en: A minor is a person who is under the age at which they legally become an adult.

words.ex: The war showed the inhumanity of violence.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争展现了暴力的非人性。
words.en: The quality of lacking compassion or kindness; cruelty.

words.ex: The norm in this school is to arrive on time.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的准则就是准时到校。
words.en: A norm is an official standard or level that organizations are expected to reach.

words.tr: v. 将某人的注意力从某事上转移开
words.ex: The loud music diverted her attention from the homework.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐将她的注意力从作业上转移开了。

words.tr: vi. 偏离常规；与标准不同
words.ex: His behavior diverges from the norm.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为偏离了常规。

words.ex: The divergence of opinions caused a big argument.
words.ex_cn: 意见的背离导致了一场激烈的争论。
words.en: A divergence is a difference between two or more things, attitudes, or opinions.

words.tr: adj. 分歧的；发散的；趋异的；
words.ex: The two friends had divergent opinions about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这两个朋友对这部电影的看法不同。
words.en: If two things diverge, they are different from each other, or they become different from each other.

words.ex: His refusal to listen is irrational.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝倾听是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings and behavior as irrational, you mean they are not based on logical reasons or clear thinking.

words.ex: He gave a verbal warning instead of a written one.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个口头警告，而不是书面的。
words.en: Relating to or in the form of words.

words.ex: The wound was cleaned with saline water.
words.ex_cn: 伤口用盐水清洗。
words.en: Saline is used to describe something that contains salt or is related to salt.

words.ex: The accident disabled him for life.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他终身残废。
words.en: If an injury or illness disables someone, it affects them so badly that it restricts the way that they can live their life.

words.ex: He tried to seduce her with flowers and gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和礼物引诱她。
words.en: To seduce someone means to persuade them to do something, especially something wrong or unwise, by making it seem attractive or exciting.

words.ex: The ad induced him to buy the product.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告诱使他购买了该产品。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.ex: The shop tries to entice customers with cheap prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店试图以低价吸引顾客。
words.en: If you entice someone, you attract them to a particular place or activity by making it seem attractive or interesting.

words.tr:
v. 吸引；诱惑；引诱
n. 诱惑；诱饵；吸引力
words.ex: The bright colors lure the birds to the feeder.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引鸟类来到喂食器。
words.en: If you lure someone, you tempt them to do something or to go somewhere, especially by offering some form of reward.

words.tr: v. 诱惑；引诱；怂恿；劝诱；
words.ex: The smell of cookies tempted him to eat one.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味诱惑他吃了一块。
words.en: If something tempts you, it makes you want to have it or do it, even though you know you should not.

words.ex: They decided to relocate to a quieter town.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定搬到一个更安静的城镇。
words.en: to move to a new place and establish one's home or business there

words.ex: The angle of the roof helps rain run off.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶的角度有助于雨水流下。
words.en: An angle is the space between two lines or surfaces that meet, measured in degrees.

words.tr: n. 非理性恐惧；毫无道理的害怕
words.ex: He has an irrational fear of dogs.
words.ex_cn: 他对狗有一种非理性的恐惧。
words.en: An intense, persistent, and irrational fear of a specific object, situation, or activity.

words.tr: v. <正>用言语表达（思想或感情）
words.ex: He cannot verbalise his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他无法用语言表达自己的感受。
words.en: To express something in words.

words.tr: v. 用言语（或文字）表达
words.ex: He can verbalize his thoughts clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: To verbalize means to express something in words, especially to articulate feelings or thoughts clearly.

words.ex: He can describe the picture in one sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他能用一句话描述这幅画。
words.en: If you describe a person, object, event, or situation, you say what they are like or what happened.

words.ex: The salinity of the sea water is too high for most fish.
words.ex_cn: 海水的盐分对大多数鱼来说太高了。
words.en: The concentration of salt in a solution, especially in water.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

words.ex: The company announced redundancy due to low profits.
words.ex_cn: 公司因利润低下宣布裁员。
words.en: Redundancy refers to the state of being not or no longer needed or useful; the inclusion of extra components which are not strictly necessary to functioning, in case of failure in other components; or the dismissal of employees from work for being no longer necessary.

words.tr: adj. 角的；有角的；尖角的；
words.ex: The angular shape of the triangle is clear.
words.ex_cn: 三角形的角形很清晰。
words.en: having angles or sharp corners; lean and bony

words.ex: The angular velocity of the wheel increased as the car sped up.
words.ex_cn: 随着汽车加速，车轮的角速度增加了。
words.en: The rate at which an object rotates around a specific axis, measured in radians per second.

words.ex: The spinning top keeps its angular momentum.
words.ex_cn: 旋转的陀螺保持其角动量。
words.en: The rotational motion of air around Earth's axis, conserved in the atmosphere and influencing wind patterns, especially in the upper troposphere.

words.tr: adj. 合法的；法律认可的；合理的；
words.ex: This contract is legitimate and signed by both parties.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同是合法的，并由双方签署。
words.en: Something that is legitimate is acceptable according to the law.

words.tr: adj. 需要久坐的；惯于久坐不动的；不爱活动的；
words.ex: His sedentary job makes him sit all day.
words.ex_cn: 他的久坐工作让他整天坐着。
words.en: Someone who has a sedentary lifestyle or job sits down a lot of the time and does not take much exercise.

words.tr: adj. 水上的；水运的；由水传播的
words.ex: The boat moved smoothly on the water-borne current.
words.ex_cn: 船在水上的水流中平稳前行。
words.en: Spread by or existing in water, especially as a means of transmission for diseases.

words.ex: The molten lava flowed down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 熔化的岩浆从山上流下。
words.en: Molten is used to describe substances that have been heated to a very high temperature and have turned into a liquid.

words.ex: The computer has a fast processor.
words.ex_cn: 这台电脑有一个快速的处理器。
words.en: A processor is a part of a computer that interprets and carries out instructions.

words.tr: v. 使浸透；使湿透；使满；使饱和
words.ex: The sponge will saturate if you pour too much water.
words.ex_cn: 如果你倒太多水，海绵会吸满。
words.en: To saturate something means to make it completely wet, or to fill it completely with something so that no more can be added.

words.tr:
n. 浸泡；
v. 吸收；
words.ex: The clothes went into a soak overnight.
words.ex_cn: 衣服泡了一整晚。
words.en: To soak something means to make it very wet by leaving it in a liquid, or to become very wet in this way. It can also mean to absorb or take in something.

words.tr:
v. 使湿透；浸透
n. 弄湿；浸液
words.ex: The rain drenched his clothes.
words.ex_cn: 雨把他的衣服淋湿了。
words.en: To drench something or someone means to make them completely wet.

words.tr: v. 使显得琐碎（或不重要、不难等）
words.ex: He trivializes serious problems by laughing at them.
words.ex_cn: 他通过嘲笑严重的问题来轻视它们。
words.en: If you say that someone trivializes something important, you disapprove of them because they make it seem less important, serious, or complex than it is.

words.tr: v. 制定法律；用立法规定
words.ex: The government will legislate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将制定新规则。
words.en: To legislate means to make or enact laws.

words.ex: He legitimately won the prize by following all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他通过遵守所有规则正当地赢得了奖品。
words.en: In a manner that is conforming to the law or to rules.

words.ex: The government's legitimacy depends on the people's trust.
words.ex_cn: 政府的合法性取决于人民的信任。
words.en: The quality or state of being legitimate.

words.ex: He hired a legal lawyer to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他请了一位法律律师来帮助他。
words.en: Relating to the law or to lawyers, or permitted or required by law.

words.tr: adj. 法律许可的；守法的；合法的
words.ex: He did a lawful job to help the community.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一份合法的工作来帮助社区。
words.en: If something is lawful, it is allowed by the law.

words.tr: phrase. 一种久坐不动的生活方式
words.ex: He has a sedentary lifestyle because he sits at a desk all day.
words.ex_cn: 他整天坐在办公桌前，过着久坐不动的生活。
words.en: A sedentary lifestyle: A way of life involving little physical activity or exercise.

words.ex: He got cholera from dirty water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了脏水染上了霍乱。
words.en: Cholera is an infectious and often fatal bacterial disease of the small intestine, typically contracted from infected water supplies and causing severe vomiting and diarrhea.

words.ex: He had diarrhea after eating bad food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了坏食物后得了腹泻。
words.en: A condition in which feces are discharged from the bowels frequently and in a liquid form.

words.tr:
v. 吼叫；咆哮
n. 吼叫；咆哮
words.ex: The lion let out a loud roar.
words.ex_cn: 狮子发出了一声响亮的咆哮。
words.en: If something roars, it makes a very loud noise, like the sound of a lion.

words.tr: phrase. 熔岩；火山喷出的炽热液态岩石
words.ex: The volcano spewed molten lava into the air.
words.ex_cn: 火山喷出了熔岩到空中。
words.en: Molten lava is the hot, fluid rock that erupts from a volcano or fissure in the Earth's surface.

words.tr: n. 咆哮； adj. 极大的； v. “roar”的现在分词；
words.ex: The lion's roaring echoed through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 狮子的咆哮在森林中回荡。
words.en: Making or uttering a loud, deep, or harsh prolonged sound.

words.tr: v. 用某物使某物饱和；彻底浸透某物
words.ex: The sponge was saturated with water.
words.ex_cn: 海绵被水浸透了。

words.ex: The obscene behavior shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这种可憎的行为让所有人都震惊了。
words.en: If you describe something as obscene, you mean it offends you because it relates to sex or violence in a way that you think is unpleasant and shocking.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏恶臭的；
v. 对…犯规；
words.ex: The foul smell came from the garbage bin.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自垃圾桶。
words.en: If you describe something as foul, you mean it is dirty and smells or tastes unpleasant. In sports, a foul is an act that is against the rules of the game.

words.ex: The floor was filthy after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨过后，地板变得非常肮脏。
words.en: Something that is filthy is extremely dirty.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏的；污秽的
v. （使）弄脏；（使）玷污；“begrime”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The old window was begrimed with dirt.
words.ex_cn: 那扇旧窗户被灰尘弄脏了。
words.en: Covered with dirt or soot; made dirty.

words.tr: adj. 积满污垢的；肮脏的
words.ex: The boy's hands are grimy from playing in the dirt.
words.ex_cn: 男孩的手因为玩土变得脏兮兮的。
words.en: Something that is grimy is very dirty.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.tr: adj. 公正的；正当的；正义的
words.ex: He is a righteous man who helps the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个帮助穷人的正直的人。
words.en: If you think that someone behaves or lives in a way that is morally good, you can say that they are righteous.

words.tr: adj. 司法的；法庭的；审判的；
words.ex: The judicial system protects people's rights.
words.ex_cn: 司法系统保护人民的权利。
words.en: Judicial means relating to the legal system and to judgments made in a court of law.

words.ex: The machine purifies water by removing dirt.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器通过去除杂质来净化水。
words.en: To purify something means to make it clean and pure by removing dirty or harmful substances from it.

words.ex: Dolphins are gregarious animals that swim in groups.
words.ex_cn: 海豚是群居动物，成群游泳。
words.en: Someone who is gregarious enjoys being with other people.

words.tr:
n. 哔哔声
v. 发哔哔声
words.ex: The machine bleeped when the button was pressed.
words.ex_cn: 当按钮被按下时，机器发出了哔哔声。
words.en: A bleep is a short high-pitched sound, especially one that is made by an electronic device.

words.ex: He shouted obscenely at the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他向人群下流地大喊。
words.en: In a manner that is extremely offensive or indecent.

words.tr: n. 色情；下流；猥亵的言行
words.ex: The movie was banned for containing obscenity.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因包含色情内容被禁播。
words.en: An obscenity is a word, phrase, or act that is considered extremely offensive, especially because it involves sex.

words.tr: phrase. 屏蔽（脏话等）；用蜂鸣声覆盖
words.ex: The radio will bleep out bad words.
words.ex_cn: 收音机会把脏话消音。
words.en: To replace a swear word or sensitive information in a broadcast with a bleep sound.

words.ex: This word derives from Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这个词源于拉丁语。

words.ex: We derive the answer from the formula.
words.ex_cn: 我们从公式中得到答案。
words.en: If you derive something such as pleasure or benefit from a person or from something, you get it from them.

words.ex: The authenticity of the ancient painting was confirmed by experts.
words.ex_cn: 这幅古画的真实性得到了专家的确认。
words.en: The quality of being genuine or not corrupted from the original.

words.tr: v. 证明…是真实的；鉴别
words.ex: He must authenticate his identity with a password.
words.ex_cn: 他必须用密码验证自己的身份。
words.en: To authenticate something means to prove or confirm that it is genuine or true.

words.tr: adj. 真实的；真的；真正的；
words.ex: This is a real diamond, not fake.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石，不是假的。
words.en: Something that is real actually exists and is not imagined, invented, or theoretical.

words.ex: This is a genuine diamond.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石。
words.en: If something is genuine, it is real and exactly what it appears to be.

words.ex: The flowers in the garden are artificial.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的花是人造的。
words.en: Made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally, especially as a copy of something natural.

words.tr:
v. 伪造；假装；冒充；
adj. 假的；冒充的；伪造的；
words.ex: He faked a signature to get the money.
words.ex_cn: 他伪造了一个签名来拿到钱。
words.en: If something is fake, it is not real, genuine, or true, but is made to appear so.

words.ex: He tried to justify his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由来证明自己的错误是正当的。
words.en: To justify something means to show or prove that it is reasonable, necessary, or correct.

words.tr: v. 证明...正当；“justify”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 有正当理由的；
words.ex: He justified his actions by telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他通过讲真话来证明自己的行为是正当的。
words.en: If you describe a decision, action, or idea as justified, you think it is reasonable and acceptable because it is based on facts or good reasons.

words.ex: The purification of water removes harmful bacteria.
words.ex_cn: 水的净化可以去除有害细菌。
words.en: The act of making something pure by removing dirty or harmful substances.

words.tr: n. 纯粹主义者；语言纯正癖者
words.ex: He is a purist who only drinks black coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他是个纯粹主义者，只喝黑咖啡。
words.en: A purist is someone who insists on following traditional rules or styles, especially in the arts, and who believes that these should not be changed or mixed with modern elements.

words.ex: He uses soap to cleanse his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用肥皂洗手。
words.en: To cleanse something means to make it extremely clean, especially by using a special substance or process.

words.ex: He refines his writing every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天完善自己的写作。
words.en: To refine something means to make it purer or to improve it, especially by removing unwanted substances or by making small changes.

words.ex: The river is contaminated by factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这条河被工厂废料污染了。
words.en: To contaminate something means to make it impure or polluted by contact or mixture with something unclean or harmful.

words.ex: He gave a heartless reply to her plea.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的恳求给出了无情的答复。
words.en: If you describe someone as heartless, you mean that they are cruel and unkind, and have no sympathy for anyone or anything.

words.tr: v. 逐步渗透；逐渐灌输
words.ex: Parents try to instill good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To instill something in someone means to gradually but firmly establish an idea or attitude in their mind.

words.ex: He infringes the rules by arriving late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而违反了规则。
words.en: To infringe means to violate or break a law, agreement, or right.

words.tr: v. 侵入；侵占；侵犯；侵蚀
words.ex: The new building encroaches on the park.
words.ex_cn: 新建筑侵占了公园。
words.en: To gradually take something such as power or authority from someone else, often in a way that is not fair or legal.

words.tr:
n. 连环漫画；
adj. 滑稽的；
words.ex: He reads a comic every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上读一本连环漫画。
words.en: A comic is someone who entertains people by making them laugh, especially a professional comedian.

words.tr:
v. 移栽；移植；
n. 移植；
words.ex: He will transplant the flowers to the garden tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天要把这些花移栽到花园里。
words.en: To transplant something means to move it from one place to another. In medicine, to transplant an organ, piece of skin, etc. means to use it to replace a damaged part in someone's body.

words.ex: The gardener did a graft on the apple tree.
words.ex_cn: 园丁在苹果树上进行了嫁接。
words.en: Graft can refer to the act of joining parts from different plants so that they grow as one plant, or to the act of transferring living tissue from one part of the body to another. It can also refer to the practice of using one's position to gain money or advantages dishonestly.

words.tr:
n. 鞭策；
v. 刺激；
words.ex: The competition served as a spur to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 竞争成了推动他更努力工作的鞭策。
words.en: A spur is something that makes you want to do something or that encourages you to do it. It can also refer to a sharp device worn on the heel of a rider's boot to urge a horse forward.

words.ex: The barbaric act shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个野蛮的行为震惊了所有人。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as barbaric, you mean that it is extremely cruel or uncivilized.

words.tr:
adj. 失职的；违法的；拖欠债务的
n. 违犯者；少年罪犯；违法者
words.ex: The delinquent worker ignored his duties.
words.ex_cn: 这位失职的员工忽视了他的职责。
words.en: A delinquent is someone, especially a young person, who commits a crime or breaks the law.

words.tr: adj. 懒惰的；邋遢的；淫荡的
words.ex: He gave a sluttish performance, ignoring his duties.
words.ex_cn: 他表现得很懒惰，忽视了自己的职责。
words.en: If you describe a woman as sluttish, you mean that she is untidy, dirty, or behaves in a sexually immoral way.

words.ex: He is slothful and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他懒惰，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as slothful, you mean that they are lazy.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；懒散的；马虎的
words.ex: He is lax about his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业很松懈。
words.en: If you say that a person's behaviour or a system is lax, you mean they are not careful or strict about maintaining high standards.

words.tr:
v. （使）滴下；流口水；运球
n. 点滴；少量；口水
words.ex: The tap continues to dribble water.
words.ex_cn: 水龙头一直在滴水。
words.en: If a liquid dribbles somewhere, or if you dribble it, it drops down slowly or flows in a thin stream. In sports such as football and basketball, if you dribble the ball, you keep kicking or tapping it in order to keep it moving.

words.ex: He infringed a rule by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了规定。

words.tr: phrase. 违反法律；侵犯法规
words.ex: He will go to jail if he infringes a law.
words.ex_cn: 如果他违反法律，就会坐牢。
words.en: To break or violate a law, often by encroaching on rights or regulations.

words.tr:
n. 长条；条状；
v. 剥去；剥夺；
words.ex: He cut a strip of paper to wrap the gift.
words.ex_cn: 他剪了一条纸来包装礼物。
words.en: To remove a layer from something, or to take off your clothes.

words.tr: phrase. 连环漫画；漫画专栏
words.ex: He draws a comic strip every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每周末画一幅连环漫画。
words.en: A sequence of drawings arranged in interrelated panels to display brief humor or form a narrative, often serialized, with text in balloons and captions.

words.ex: The hospital performed a kidney transplantation last week.
words.ex_cn: 医院上周进行了肾脏移植手术。
words.en: The act or process of moving an organ, tissue, or living thing from one place or person to another.

words.ex: The heart is transplantable to another person.
words.ex_cn: 这颗心脏可以移植给另一个人。
words.en: Capable of being transplanted.

words.tr:
v. 转移；转让；调任；
n. 转移；转让；调任；
words.ex: He will transfer the money to his bank account.
words.ex_cn: 他将把钱转到他的银行账户。
words.en: If you transfer something or someone from one place to another, or they transfer from one place to another, they go from the first place to the second.

words.tr:
adj. 青少年的；幼稚的；
n. 少年；
words.ex: The book is written for juvenile readers.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是为青少年读者撰写的。
words.en: A juvenile is a child or young person who is not yet old enough to be considered an adult.

words.tr: adj. 淫荡的；放荡的；行为放荡的
words.ex: Her sluttish behaviour shocked the whole class.
words.ex_cn: 她淫荡的行为让全班震惊。

words.ex: The turtle moves in a sluggish way.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟移动得很缓慢。
words.en: If you describe something as sluggish, you mean that it is moving or working more slowly than usual.

words.tr: n. 迟缓的节奏；缓慢的步调
words.ex: The economy has been moving at a sluggish pace this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年经济一直以迟缓的节奏发展。

words.ex: He tried to retaliate by spreading rumors.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过散布谣言来报复。
words.en: If you retaliate when someone harms or annoys you, you do something which harms or annoys them in return.

words.ex: He was arrested for perpetrating a fraud.
words.ex_cn: 他因实施诈骗而被逮捕。
words.en: If someone perpetrates a crime or any other immoral or harmful act, they do it.

words.ex: He worked hard and prospered in business.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，在商业上取得了成功。
words.en: If people or businesses prosper, they are successful and do well.

words.ex: The ship dropped its anchor in the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船在港口放下了锚。
words.en: An anchor is a heavy object that is dropped from a boat or a ship into the water to prevent the vessel from moving.

words.tr: v. 抢劫；掠夺；蹂躏；破坏
words.ex: The invaders despoiled the village.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者抢劫了村庄。
words.en: To despoil something means to steal from it or damage it, especially in a violent or destructive way.

words.tr:
v. 掠夺；抢劫
n. 掠夺物；掠夺；赃物
words.ex: The pirates plundered the ship.
words.ex_cn: 海盗劫掠了那艘船。
words.en: If someone plunders a place or plunders things from a place, they steal things from it.

words.ex: The thieves robbed the bank last night.
words.ex_cn: 小偷昨晚抢劫了银行。
words.en: To rob someone or somewhere means to take money or property illegally from them, often using force.

words.tr: adj. 不礼貌的；失礼的；粗鲁的
words.ex: He was discourteous to the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 他对服务员无礼。
words.en: If you say that someone is discourteous, you mean that they are rude and have no consideration for the feelings of other people.

words.tr: adj. 懒惰的；懒散的；好逸恶劳的
words.ex: He is indolent and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他很懒，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as indolent, you mean that they are lazy.

words.tr:
v. 促进；使增长；
n. 提高；增强；
words.ex: Exercise can boost your energy.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进你的精力。
words.en: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.

words.ex: They persecute people for their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们因人们的信仰而迫害他们。
words.en: If someone is persecuted, they are treated cruelly and unfairly, often because of their race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: He decided to retaliate against his persecutor by reporting him to the police.
words.ex_cn: 他决定向警察举报他的迫害者来报复。

words.tr: v. 报复攻击；对袭击进行反击
words.ex: He decided to retaliate against an attack by calling the police.
words.ex_cn: 他决定对这次攻击进行报复，于是报了警。

words.ex: He was courteous to everyone he met.
words.ex_cn: 他对遇到的每个人都很有礼貌。
words.en: Someone who is courteous is polite and respectful to other people.

words.ex: Companies should carry out social responsibility by helping poor communities.
words.ex_cn: 公司应该通过帮助贫困社区来履行社会责任。

words.tr: n. 后援者；援助者；升压器；助力器
words.ex: He is a booster of the local football team.
words.ex_cn: 他是当地足球队的后援者。
words.en: A booster is something that increases the power, effectiveness, or success of something else. It can also refer to a person who promotes or supports something enthusiastically.

words.tr:
v. 涂抹；弄脏；中伤；诽谤
n. 污迹；污渍；丑化；诽谤
words.ex: He smeared butter on the bread.
words.ex_cn: 他在面包上涂抹了黄油。
words.en: To spread a liquid or a thick substance over a surface, or to damage someone's reputation by telling lies about them.

words.tr:
n. （文字）诽谤
v. 发表文字诽谤（某人）
words.ex: He wrote a false story about her, and it was libel.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于她的虚假文章，这是诽谤。
words.en: A libel is a published false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation; a written defamation.

words.tr:
v. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
n. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
words.ex: He spread slander about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: Slander is the action or crime of making a false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation.

words.ex: She has a slender figure.
words.ex_cn: 她身材苗条。
words.en: Someone or something that is slender is thin and graceful.

words.tr: adj. 苗条的；纤细的；微小的；
words.ex: She has a slim figure.
words.ex_cn: 她身材苗条。
words.en: If someone is slim, they are thin in an attractive way.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.ex: The benevolent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位慈善的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: If you describe a person in authority as benevolent, you mean that they are kind and fair.

words.ex: The shirt is made of synthetic fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫是合成纤维制成的。
words.en: Synthetic products are made from chemicals or artificial substances rather than from natural ones.

words.tr: v. 制定（法律）；通过（法律）；扮演（角色）
words.ex: The government will enact a new law next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将颁布一项新法律。
words.en: To enact a law or rule means to make it official by passing it through a legislative body.

words.ex: He resents being ignored by his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他怨恨被老板忽视。
words.en: If you resent someone or something, you feel bitter and angry about them.

words.ex: The affluent family bought a big house by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这个富裕的家庭在湖边买了一栋大房子。
words.en: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

words.ex: There is ample food for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都有足够的食物。
words.en: If there is an ample amount of something, there is enough of it and usually some extra.

words.ex: The palace had opulent carpets and golden chandeliers.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿里有华丽的地毯和金色的吊灯。
words.en: Having or displaying great wealth or richness.

words.tr: n. 树干；大衣箱；象鼻子；
words.ex: The elephant held the branch with its trunk.
words.ex_cn: 大象用它的鼻子抓住树枝。
words.en: The main stem of a tree, below the branches, and above the ground; the main part of the body, excluding the head, arms, and legs; the long, flexible nose of an elephant; a large, strong box used for transporting or storing clothes and other personal possessions.

words.ex: The judge showed leniency toward the first-time offender.
words.ex_cn: 法官对初犯表现出了宽大。
words.en: Leniency is the quality of being more merciful or tolerant than expected.

words.ex: His benevolence helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的仁慈帮助了这个贫困家庭。
words.en: The quality of being well meaning; kindness.

words.tr: phrase. 合成纤维；人造纤维
words.ex: This jacket is made from synthetic fibre.
words.ex_cn: 这件夹克是由合成纤维制成的。
words.en: A synthetic fibre is a fibre made by humans through chemical synthesis, as opposed to natural fibres that are directly derived from living organisms.

words.tr: n. 合成材料；人造材料
words.ex: The jacket is made of synthetic material.
words.ex_cn: 这件夹克是用合成材料做的。
words.en: A man-made substance, not occurring naturally.

words.ex: This dress is colored with a synthetic dye.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子是用合成染料染色的。
words.en: A synthetic dye is a man-made substance used to add color to materials, differing from natural dyes which are derived from plants or animals.

words.ex: He crushed the can with his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他用手把罐子压碎了。
words.en: To crush something means to press it very hard so that its shape is destroyed or so that it breaks into pieces. It can also mean to defeat someone completely, or to make someone feel extremely upset or disappointed.

words.ex: The material is synthetically produced in a lab.
words.ex_cn: 这种材料是在实验室中综合生产的。
words.en: In a synthetic manner; by synthesis or artificial combination.

words.ex: He never disparages his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他从不贬低他的同学。
words.en: If you disparage someone or something, you speak about them in a way which shows that you do not have a good opinion of them.

words.tr: n. 局外人；无取胜希望者；
words.ex: He felt like an outsider at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上感觉像个局外人。
words.en: An outsider is someone who does not belong to a particular group or organization.

words.tr: phrase. 插嘴；打断；超车抢档
words.ex: He cut in while I was talking.
words.ex_cn: 我正在说话时，他插嘴了。
words.en: To interrupt someone who is speaking, or to move into a line of traffic by driving in front of someone else.

words.tr:
adj. 蔑视的；毁谤的；轻视的
v. 轻视；蔑视；贬损；“disparage”的现在分词
words.ex: He made a disparaging comment about his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友说了句贬低的话。
words.en: If you are disparaging about someone or something, or make disparaging comments about them, you say things which criticize them and show that you do not have a good opinion of them.

words.tr: n. 主席；主持人；董事长；
words.ex: The chairman called the meeting to order.
words.ex_cn: 主席宣布会议开始。
words.en: A chairman is a man who is in charge of a meeting, committee, or organization.

words.ex: He buys lunch in the school canteen.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校食堂买午餐。
words.en: A canteen is a place in a factory, office, or school where meals are served, often at a lower cost than in restaurants. It can also refer to a small container for carrying water or other drinks.

words.ex: The children play near the fountain in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园的喷泉附近玩耍。
words.en: A fountain is a structure that squirts water into the air to create a visual or auditory effect, or a natural source of water.

words.tr: n. 丰沛的喷泉；富足的源泉
words.ex: The garden has an affluent fountain that flows all day.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园有一个终日流淌的丰沛喷泉。

words.ex: The white poplar grows near the river.
words.ex_cn: 白杨树长在河边。

words.ex: The poplar trees grow tall by the river.
words.ex_cn: 白杨树在河边长得很高。
words.en: A poplar is a type of tree that grows quickly and is often planted for its wood or to provide shade.

words.ex: The speaker eulogized the bravery of the soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者颂扬了士兵们的英勇。
words.en: To speak or write in praise of someone or something highly.

words.ex: His hard work received much praise from the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力工作得到了老师的许多赞美。
words.en: If you praise someone or something, you express approval for their achievements or qualities.

words.ex: Cats and dogs can coexist in the same house.
words.ex_cn: 猫和狗可以在同一个房子里共存。
words.en: To exist together at the same time or in the same place.

words.tr: n. 航空；航空学；飞行（术）；
words.ex: He works in aviation as a pilot.
words.ex_cn: 他作为一名飞行员从事航空工作。
words.en: Aviation is the operation and production of aircraft.

words.tr: adj. 泛滥的；猖獗的；蔓生的
words.ex: Rumors are rampant in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在这个小镇上四处流传。
words.en: If you describe something bad, such as a crime or disease, as rampant, you mean that it is very common and is increasing in an uncontrolled way.

words.ex: The prolonged rain caused flooding.
words.ex_cn: 持久的降雨引发了洪水。
words.en: Something that is prolonged continues for a long time, or longer than expected.

words.tr: v. 挤压；压碎；“crush”的现在分词；
words.ex: The machine is crushing the cans.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器正在挤压罐子。
words.en: If you describe something as crushing, you mean that it is very severe or intense.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.ex: This broken phone is useless.
words.ex_cn: 这部坏掉的手机毫无用处。
words.en: If something is useless, it is not able to do what it is supposed to do or is not effective.

words.ex: Good teachers edify their students with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 好老师用智慧启发学生。
words.en: To edify someone means to improve their mind or character by teaching them something.

words.tr: adj. 庸俗的；粗俗的；粗野的；下流的
words.ex: He used a vulgar word in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上说了一个粗俗的词。
words.en: If you describe something as vulgar, you mean that it is in bad taste or of poor quality.

words.ex: The sandpaper feels coarse to the touch.
words.ex_cn: 这张砂纸摸起来很粗糙。
words.en: Coarse things have a rough texture because they consist of thick threads or large pieces.

words.ex: This contract is prolongable by mutual agreement.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同经双方同意可以延长。
words.en: Capable of being extended or prolonged in duration.

words.ex: The prolongation of the meeting made everyone tired.
words.ex_cn: 会议的延长让每个人都累了。
words.en: The act of prolonging something; extension.

words.ex: The artist elongated the figure to create a sense of grace.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家拉长了人物形象，以创造出一种优雅的感觉。
words.en: To elongate something means to make it longer, especially by stretching it.

words.ex: They will extend the deadline by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他们将截止日期延长一周。
words.en: To extend something means to make it longer or larger, or to spread it over a larger area.

words.ex: We need to shorten the meeting to one hour.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要把会议缩短到一小时。
words.en: To make something shorter in length, duration, or extent.

words.tr: n. 船坞；造船厂；修船厂；船舶修理所
words.ex: The shipyard builds large boats for the navy.
words.ex_cn: 造船厂为海军建造大型船只。
words.en: A shipyard is a place where ships are built or repaired.

words.ex: He rebut the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据反驳了这一说法。
words.en: If you rebut a charge or criticism that is made against you, you give reasons why it is untrue or unacceptable.

words.ex: He refuted the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据驳斥了这一说法。
words.en: To prove a statement or theory to be wrong or false; to deny the truth or accuracy of something.

words.tr:
v. 反驳；回嘴
n. 反驳；顶嘴
words.ex: He gave a quick retort when she criticized him.
words.ex_cn: 当她批评他时，他迅速回了一句。
words.en: If you retort, you reply angrily to someone.

words.ex: He gave a strong rebuttal to the claim.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个说法给出了有力的反驳。
words.en: A rebuttal is a statement or piece of evidence that contradicts or opposes a previous statement or evidence.

words.ex: He spoke in a hoarse voice after shouting all day.
words.ex_cn: 他喊了一整天后，声音变得沙哑。
words.en: If your voice is hoarse or if you are hoarse, your voice sounds rough and unclear, for example because your throat is sore.

words.tr: adj. 精美的；细腻的；强烈的
words.ex: She wore an exquisite dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精美的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is exquisite is extremely beautiful or pleasant, especially in a delicate or refined way.

words.ex: He likes movies with vulgar tastes.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢有低俗品味的电影。

words.tr: n. 粗俗的笑话；低俗的段子
words.ex: He told vulgar jokes at the party, and everyone felt uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上讲了粗俗的笑话，大家都感到不舒服。

words.ex: The vulgarity of his language shocked everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他粗俗的语言震惊了房间里的每一个人。
words.en: The quality or state of being vulgar, especially in the sense of being coarse or lacking refinement.

words.tr: adv. 粗俗地；庸俗地；通俗地
words.ex: He spoke vulgarly to the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 他对服务员粗俗地说话。
words.en: In a crude, offensive, or sexually explicit manner.

words.ex: She wore an elegant dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条优雅的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe a person or thing as elegant, you mean that they are pleasing and graceful in appearance or style.

words.tr:
n. 核；核心；重点；
adj. 核心的；
words.ex: The core of the apple is not edible.
words.ex_cn: 苹果的核心不能吃。
words.en: The central or most important part of something.

words.tr: adj. 天生的；先天的；天赋的
words.ex: He has an inborn talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 他天生就有音乐才能。
words.en: An inborn quality or ability is one that you have had naturally since birth.

words.ex: Honesty is an inherent quality of a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是好领导固有的品质。
words.en: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

words.tr: adj. 固有的；内在的；本身的；
words.ex: Honesty is an intrinsic part of her character.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是她性格中固有的部分。
words.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

words.tr: adj. 适合居住的；可居住的；
words.ex: The planet is habitable because it has water and air.
words.ex_cn: 这颗行星有水和空气，适合居住。
words.en: A place that is habitable is suitable or good enough for people to live in.

words.ex: This park is an ecological habitat for many birds.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园是许多鸟类的生态栖息地。
words.en: Relating to or concerned with the relation of living organisms to one another and to their physical surroundings.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.tr: v. 使（尤其是坏事）合法化；正式批准（或认可）
words.ex: The law will legitimize this practice.
words.ex_cn: 法律将使这种做法合法化。
words.en: To legitimize something means to make it legal or acceptable according to the law.

words.tr: v. 结晶；定形；（使）具体化；变明确
words.ex: The idea began to crystallize after many talks.
words.ex_cn: 经过多次讨论，这个想法开始明朗起来。
words.en: To crystallize means to cause something to form into crystals or to become clear and definite in form.

words.ex: The house uses solar-powered lights.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子使用太阳能供电的灯。
words.en: Powered by solar energy.

words.ex: The small room was cosy with a warm blanket and a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 这个小房间铺着温暖的毯子，喝着热茶，非常舒适。
words.en: A place or situation that is cosy is comfortable and warm.

words.ex: The little cabin is cozy and warm.
words.ex_cn: 这座小木屋舒适又温暖。
words.en: A place that is cozy is comfortable and warm.

words.ex: He refused the money purely because it was wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他纯粹是因为觉得不对才拒绝了那笔钱。
words.en: In a pure manner; without admixture or adulteration.

words.tr: phrase. 彻头彻尾地；从核心上；从根本上
words.ex: She was British to the core.
words.ex_cn: 她是个彻头彻尾的英国人。
words.en: Completely or thoroughly.

words.ex: The habitant lives in a small house near the river.
words.ex_cn: 这个居民住在河边的一所小房子里。
words.en: A habitant is someone who lives in a particular place.

words.tr:
adj. 居住的；常驻的；
n. 常住居民；
words.ex: The resident population grew last year.
words.ex_cn: 居住人口去年增加了。
words.en: A resident is someone who lives in a particular place or a person who has their home in a place.

words.tr: n. 栖息地；居留地；产地；
words.ex: The panda's habitat is in the mountains of China.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫的栖息地在中国的山区。
words.en: The natural environment in which a species or group of species lives.

words.ex: You must comply with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: To act in accordance with a wish, command, or rule.

words.ex: You must abide by the school rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守校规。
words.en: To accept or act in accordance with a rule, decision, or recommendation.

words.tr: phrase. 与……一致；符合；相协调
words.ex: His actions do not accord with his words.
words.ex_cn: 他的言行不一致。
words.en: To be in agreement or harmony with something.

words.ex: The painter used a roller to apply the paint.
words.ex_cn: 油漆工用滚筒来涂油漆。
words.en: A roller is a cylinder that rotates around a central axis and is used in various machines and devices to move, flatten, or compress something.

words.ex: He wound the fishing line onto the reel.
words.ex_cn: 他把鱼线绕在卷筒上。
words.en: A reel is a cylinder on which film, wire, thread, or other flexible materials can be wound. It can also refer to a lively Scottish or Irish dance, or to the act of staggering or lurching violently.

words.ex: The kitchen was unsanitary and dirty.
words.ex_cn: 厨房不卫生且脏乱。
words.en: If you describe a place as unsanitary, you mean that it is dirty, and likely to cause disease.

words.ex: The teacher will not condone cheating in exams.
words.ex_cn: 老师不会容忍考试作弊。
words.en: To condone something means to accept or allow behavior that is considered wrong.

words.ex: I forgive you for being late.
words.ex_cn: 我原谅你迟到了。
words.en: If you forgive someone who has done something bad or wrong, you stop being angry with them and stop blaming them.

words.ex: The storm bereaved the village of its power.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴使村庄失去了电力。
words.en: To deprive someone of a loved one through death.

words.tr: adj. 有缺陷的；有故障的；有错误的；
words.ex: The faulty phone keeps turning off.
words.ex_cn: 这部有缺陷的手机总是自动关机。
words.en: If you describe something as faulty, you mean that it is not perfect or it has some weaknesses.

words.ex: The ancient symbol remains an enigma.
words.ex_cn: 这个古代符号仍然是一个谜。
words.en: An enigma is something that is mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.tr:
v. 抽出；节省；
adj. 备用的；多余的；空闲的；
words.ex: Can you spare a few minutes to help me?
words.ex_cn: 你能抽出几分钟帮我吗？
words.en: If you have something such as time, money, or space to spare, you have some extra time, money, or space that you have not used or which you do not need.

words.ex: The children play at Nursery 796.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在796号托儿所玩耍。
words.en: A nursery is a place where young children are cared for during the day while their parents are at work.

words.ex: The word 'bank' has different semantic meanings.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'bank' 有不同的语义含义。
words.en: Semantic is used to describe something that relates to the meanings of words and sentences.

words.w: I can not find my bearings
words.tr: 我找不到方向；我迷失了方向（比喻在情况或环境中失去判断或定位）
words.uk: aɪ kæn nɒt faɪnd maɪ ˈbɛərɪŋz
words.us: aɪ kæn nɑt faɪnd maɪ ˈbɛrɪŋz
words.ex: I can not find my bearings in the dark forest.
words.ex_cn: 我在黑暗的森林里找不到方向。

words.w: have a strong bearing on something
words.tr: v. 对某事有重大影响
words.uk: hæv ə strɒŋ ˈbɛərɪŋ ɒn ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: hæv ə strɔːŋ ˈbɛrɪŋ ɑːn ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: The weather has a strong bearing on the crop yield.
words.ex_cn: 天气对农作物产量有重大影响。

words.tr: n. 影响；方位；轴承；举止； v. 忍受；“bear”的现在分词；
words.ex: The new policy has a big bearing on our daily lives.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对我们日常生活有很大影响。
words.en: The manner in which one conducts or carries oneself, including posture and gestures; also refers to a machine part that supports another part and reduces friction.

words.tr: n. 流血；杀戮；流血事件
words.ex: The war caused much bloodshed.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争造成了大量流血。
words.en: Bloodshed is the killing or wounding of people, usually during fighting or a war.

words.tr:
v. 使脱落；去除；
n. 棚屋；
words.ex: The tree sheds its leaves in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在秋天落叶。
words.en: A shed is a small building, usually made of wood, used for storing things such as garden tools. When something sheds, it loses its covering, such as leaves or hair, or it gets rid of something it no longer needs.

words.ex: He sent a letter of condolence to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他给朋友寄了一封慰问信。
words.en: An expression of sympathy, especially on the occasion of a death.

words.ex: He condescended to explain the simple math to his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他屈尊向弟弟解释了简单的数学。
words.en: If someone condescends to do something, they agree to do it in a way which shows that they think they are superior to the people they are doing it for.

words.ex: He bought a spare part for his car.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的车买了一个备件。
words.en: A spare part is a component that can be used to replace a broken or worn-out part in a machine or piece of equipment.

words.ex: He reads books in his spare time.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间读书。
words.en: Spare time refers to the time when one is not working or occupied; leisure time.

words.ex: The nursery teacher sings songs with the children every morning.
words.ex_cn: 幼儿园教师每天早上和孩子们一起唱歌。

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.tr: adj. 无结果的；无成效的；
words.ex: The meeting was fruitless because no decisions were made.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议毫无结果，因为没有做出任何决定。
words.en: If an action or attempt to do something is fruitless, it is unsuccessful or produces nothing of value.

words.tr: adj. 传导的；能传导（热、电）的
words.ex: Copper is conductive and used in wires.
words.ex_cn: 铜具有导电性，用于电线。
words.en: Having the property of conducting something (especially heat or electricity).

words.ex: He is an eccentric man who wears socks with sandals.
words.ex_cn: 他是个古怪的人，穿着袜子配凉鞋。
words.en: If you say that someone is eccentric, you mean that they behave in a strange way, and have habits or opinions that are different from those of most people.

words.ex: He wore a weird hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶怪异的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as weird, you mean that they are strange, unusual, or mysterious.

words.tr: adj. 奇怪的；奇数的；余的；
words.ex: He wore an odd hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇怪的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odd, you mean that they are strange or unusual.

words.ex: This product is inferior to the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这个产品比另一个差。
words.en: If one person or thing is inferior to another, they are not as good, important, or valuable as the other person or thing.

words.ex: The wind began to slacken after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风速开始减缓。
words.en: If something slackens or if you slacken it, it becomes slower, less active, or less intense.

words.ex: My mentor helped me choose my career path.
words.ex_cn: 我的导师帮助我选择了职业道路。
words.en: A mentor is a person who gives a younger or less experienced person help and advice over a period of time, especially at work or school.

words.tr:
n. 垫；爪垫；便笺簿
v. 放轻脚步走
