words.ex: He asked a rhetorical question to make a point.
words.ex_cn: 他问了一个修辞性的问题来阐明观点。
words.en: A rhetorical question is one which is asked in order to make a statement rather than to get an answer.

words.tr: n. 空洞的言辞；毫无实质内容的华丽辞藻
words.ex: His speech was just empty rhetoric.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲只是空洞的言辞。

words.tr: n. 政治口号的修辞；政治宣传口号所使用的言辞技巧
words.ex: The rhetoric of political slogans often simplifies complex issues.
words.ex_cn: 政治口号的修辞常常简化复杂的问题。

words.ex: He is a veteran player with many years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位经验丰富的老练球员。
words.en: A veteran is someone who has a lot of experience in a particular field or activity, especially in the armed forces.

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；积习难改的
words.ex: He is an inveterate smoker who cannot quit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个根深蒂固的吸烟者，无法戒掉。
words.en: If you describe someone as, for example, an inveterate liar or smoker, you mean that they have lied or smoked for a long time and are not likely to stop doing it.

words.ex: The actors had a rehearsal before the play.
words.ex_cn: 演出前，演员们进行了一次排练。
words.en: A rehearsal of a play, dance, or piece of music is a practice of it in preparation for a performance.

words.tr: adv. 马上；迅速地；准时地；
words.ex: He answered the call promptly.
words.ex_cn: 他马上接了电话。
words.en: If you do something promptly, you do it immediately.

words.tr: n. 分子云；由气体和尘埃组成的星际云，是恒星形成的场所
words.ex: The molecular cloud is where stars are born.
words.ex_cn: 分子云是恒星诞生的地方。

words.ex: The molecular structure of water consists of two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.
words.ex_cn: 水的分子结构由两个氢原子与一个氧原子结合而成。
words.en: The arrangement of atoms within a molecule, including the type of bonds that hold the atoms together.

words.ex: The looming crisis is making everyone worried.
words.ex_cn: 即将到来的危机让每个人都感到担忧。

words.tr:
n. 秘密；
adj. 秘密的；
words.ex: He kept the secret from everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他把秘密藏了起来，谁也没告诉。
words.en: If something is secret, it is known about by only a small number of people, and is not told or shown to anyone else.

words.ex: The doctor checked his bowel for signs of infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的肠是否有感染迹象。
words.en: The lower part of the alimentary canal from the end of the stomach to the anus.

words.ex: The intestine helps digest food.
words.ex_cn: 肠道帮助消化食物。
words.en: The part of the alimentary canal between the stomach and the anus.

words.ex: The doctor checked his intestinal health.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的肠道健康。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the intestines.

words.ex: The gland produces a secretion to help digestion.
words.ex_cn: 腺体分泌一种物质以帮助消化。
words.en: The process by which substances are produced and discharged from a cell, gland, or organ for a particular function in the organism or for excretion.

words.ex: The dog left excrement on the grass.
words.ex_cn: 狗在草地上留下了粪便。
words.en: Excrement is waste matter that is excreted from the body, especially feces.

words.ex: The dog left its excreta on the grass.
words.ex_cn: 狗在草地上留下了排泄物。
words.en: Waste matter discharged from the body, especially feces and urine.

words.tr:
n. 动物的粪便
v. 施粪肥于
words.ex: The cow left dung on the grass.
words.ex_cn: 牛在草地上留下了粪便。
words.en: Dung is the excrement of animals, used as manure.

words.ex: The tricky question eluded even the best students.
words.ex_cn: 这道难题难倒了即使是最优秀的学生。
words.en: If something that you want eludes you, you fail to obtain it. If you elude someone or something, you avoid them or escape from them.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
n. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
words.ex: They stroll in the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们晚饭后在公园里闲逛。
words.en: If you stroll somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；漫步
n. 闲逛；漫步
words.ex: We decided to saunter along the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定沿着海滩漫步。
words.en: If you saunter somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.ex: The cat likes to roam around the garden.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫喜欢在花园里游荡。
words.en: To roam means to move about or travel without any definite purpose or destination.

words.ex: He likes to wander in the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢晚饭后在公园里徘徊。
words.en: If you wander in a place, you walk around there in a casual way, often without intending to go in any particular direction or to any particular place.

words.tr: n. 改造（工程）；建筑改造；整修；
words.ex: The refurbishment of the old school took six months.
words.ex_cn: 这所旧学校的改造工程花了六个月。
words.en: The process of repairing and redecorating something, especially a building, to make it more attractive or functional.

words.ex: Scientists work at the observatory to study stars.
words.ex_cn: 科学家在天文台工作以研究恒星。
words.en: A building or place equipped for observation of natural phenomena (as in astronomy); also : an institution whose primary purpose is making such observations.

words.tr: adj. 极好的；令人震惊的； v. “stun”的现在分词；
words.ex: She wore a stunning dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件极好的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Extremely impressive or attractive.

words.ex: He wore a ceremonial robe for the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他为婚礼穿了一件仪式性的长袍。
words.en: relating to or used in a ceremony; formal

words.ex: Legends say that some heroes are immortal.
words.ex_cn: 传说有些英雄是不死的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as immortal, you mean that they are so famous or popular that they will be remembered for a very long time.

words.ex: The baby's neural connections are developing fast.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿的神经连接正在迅速发展。
words.en: Neural relates to a nerve or the nervous system.

words.ex: He is bullying his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他正在欺负他的弟弟。
words.en: The use of strength or influence to harm or intimidate those who are weaker.

words.ex: The baby ingests milk every few hours.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿每隔几小时喝奶。
words.en: To ingest means to take food, drink, or another substance into your body, usually by swallowing.

words.ex: He swallowed the pill with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水吞下了药片。
words.en: To swallow means to make food or drink go down your throat and towards your stomach. It can also mean to accept something without protest or to believe something too easily.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌烦的；令人烦恼的；
words.ex: The loud noise is bothersome.
words.ex_cn: 这嘈杂的声音令人厌烦。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as bothersome, you mean that they cause bother or difficulties.

words.ex: The cat got entangled in the string.
words.ex_cn: 猫被绳子缠住了。
words.en: If something is entangled in something else, it is caught or twisted around it, or mixed with it so that it is difficult to separate the two things.

words.ex: The house was refurnished with modern furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这栋房子用现代家具重新装备了。
words.en: To furnish or decorate a place again, especially with new furniture.

words.tr: v. 重新刷新；翻新；整修
words.ex: They will refurbish the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新这栋老房子。
words.en: To refurbish something means to clean it, decorate it, and provide it with new equipment or facilities, especially so that it is more attractive or more useful.

words.ex: The park is closed for refurbishment this week.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园本周因翻新而关闭。

words.ex: The company will reimburse you for your travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司会报销你的旅行费用。
words.en: If you reimburse someone for something, you pay them back the money that they have spent or lost because of it.

words.ex: He asked for reimbursement for his travel costs.
words.ex_cn: 他要求报销旅行费用。
words.en: The act of compensating someone for an expense or loss incurred.

words.ex: The children built a mound of sand at the beach.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在海滩上堆了一个沙土墩。
words.en: A mound is a large pile of earth or stones; it can also refer to the action of piling up earth or stones.

words.ex: He left a heap of clothes on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他把一堆衣服扔在地上。
words.en: A heap of things is a pile of them, especially a pile arranged in a rather untidy way.

words.ex: She wrote a poetic letter to her friend.
words.ex_cn: 她给朋友写了一封诗意的信。
words.en: Something that is poetic is very beautiful and expresses emotions in a sensitive or moving way.

words.tr:
n. 工序；过程；
v. 处理；加工；
words.ex: The factory improved the production process.
words.ex_cn: 工厂改进了生产工序。
words.en: A process is a series of actions which are carried out in order to achieve a particular result.

words.tr: n. 神经过程；指神经系统中发生的生理或电化学活动过程
words.ex: The neural process helps the brain send signals to the body.
words.ex_cn: 神经过程帮助大脑向身体发送信号。

words.tr: v. 使变得不相似；使同化；使失去特征
words.ex: The two groups dissimilate over time.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体随着时间推移变得越来越不同。
words.en: To make or become different or dissimilar.

words.ex: The stomach digests food into nutrients.
words.ex_cn: 胃将食物消化成营养物质。
words.en: To digest means to break down food in the stomach and intestines into substances that can be absorbed by the body. It can also mean to understand or assimilate information. As a noun, it refers to a compilation or summary of information.

words.ex: He tries to assimilate new words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力吸收新单词。
words.en: To assimilate means to take in and understand fully ideas, information, or culture, or to make something become part of a group or system.

words.ex: He takes an antacid when his stomach hurts.
words.ex_cn: 当他胃痛时，他会服用抗酸药。
words.en: A substance that neutralizes stomach acidity and is used to relieve heartburn, indigestion, or an upset stomach.

words.ex: The teacher stopped the school bullying immediately.
words.ex_cn: 老师立即制止了校园欺凌。
words.en: School bullying refers to the repeated aggressive behavior by students intended to harm others physically or emotionally, often occurring within the school environment.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed a peptic medication to aid digestion.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一种助消化的药物来帮助消化。
words.en: Relating to or aiding digestion.

words.ex: He got entangled in a legal problem.
words.ex_cn: 他卷入了一场法律纠纷。

words.tr: n. 化妆品；美容品；“cosmetic”的复数；
words.ex: She buys cosmetics at the drugstore.
words.ex_cn: 她在药店买化妆品。
words.en: Substances or treatments used to enhance or alter the appearance of the face or body.

words.tr: n. （船只）搁浅；（船只）搁浅 v. 使滞留，使搁浅( strand的现在分词 )；
words.ex: The storm caused the ship's stranding on the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 风暴导致船只在岩石上搁浅。
words.en: The act of leaving someone or something in a place from which it is difficult to escape or be rescued, especially a place that is isolated or inaccessible.

words.tr: adj. 虚拟的；几乎的；实际上的；事实上的；
words.ex: He played a virtual game on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他在电脑上玩了一个虚拟游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as virtual, you mean that it is so nearly true that for most purposes it can be regarded as true.

words.ex: The refugees lived in abject poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这些难民过着凄惨的贫困生活。
words.en: Abject means extremely bad, unpleasant, and degrading.

words.ex: The aboriginal people live in the forests of Australia.
words.ex_cn: 土著居民生活在澳大利亚的森林里。
words.en: An aboriginal person or thing is one that has been in a country or region from the earliest known times or from before the arrival of colonists.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

words.tr: v. 使适应（新气候或环境）
words.ex: He needs to acclimatize to the hot weather.
words.ex_cn: 他需要适应炎热的天气。
words.en: To acclimatize means to adjust to a new climate, environment, or situation.

words.ex: He showed great capability in solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决数学问题上展现了很强的能力。
words.en: The ability or qualities necessary to do something.

words.ex: The uptake of nutrients by plants is important for growth.
words.ex_cn: 植物对营养物质的摄取对生长很重要。
words.en: The process by which substances are taken into a cell, organism, or system; the understanding or comprehension of information.

words.ex: The sponge absorbs water quickly.
words.ex_cn: 海绵很快吸收水。
words.en: If something absorbs a liquid, gas, or other substance, it soaks it up or takes it in.

words.tr: phrase. 拿起；开始从事；接受（提议）；占用
words.ex: He took up the book from the table.
words.ex_cn: 他从桌子上拿起了书。
words.en: To begin to do or deal with something; to occupy or fill a particular amount of time or space; to accept an offer or challenge.

words.tr:
adj. 可变的；易变的；
n. 变量；
words.ex: The weather is variable in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天的天气是多变的。
words.en: A variable is something that is likely to vary; something that is subject to variation.

words.ex: The cosmic rays come from outer space.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙射线来自外太空。
words.en: Relating to the universe or cosmos, especially as distinct from the earth.

words.ex: He loves to watch the cosmos at night.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在夜晚观看宇宙。
words.en: The cosmos refers to the universe seen as a well-ordered whole, or to any system or structure that is complex and orderly.

words.tr: n. 化妆包；用于存放化妆品的小包
words.ex: She keeps her lipstick and mirror in a cosmetic bag.
words.ex_cn: 她把口红和镜子放在化妆包里。

words.ex: The tribe lives in a primitive hut.
words.ex_cn: 这个部落住在原始的小屋里。
words.en: Belonging to a very early period in the history of the world, or to a time before modern things existed.

words.tr: adj. 原始的；远古的；最初的
words.ex: The primordial soup formed the first life on Earth.
words.ex_cn: 原始汤形成了地球上的最初生命。
words.en: Primordial means existing at or from the beginning of time; primeval.

words.ex: The forest looked primeval and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林看起来远古而未被破坏。
words.en: relating to the earliest ages of the world or the universe; ancient or prehistoric.

words.ex: The primal forest has never been touched by humans.
words.ex_cn: 这片原始森林从未被人类触碰过。
words.en: Primal means relating to an early stage in the development of something, or being the most important or basic part of something.

words.tr:
v. 使滞留；使搁浅；
n. 方面；
words.ex: The storm stranded the travelers on the island.
words.ex_cn: 风暴使旅行者滞留在岛上。
words.en: If someone is stranded, they are left in a place that is difficult for them to get away from. A strand of something such as hair, wire, or thread is a single thin piece of it.

words.ex: Oil spills can lead to stranding and death of sea turtles.
words.ex_cn: 石油泄漏会导致海龟搁浅和死亡。

words.ex: He is virtually always on time.
words.ex_cn: 他几乎总是准时。
words.en: In effect though not formally recognized; practically.

words.ex: He is wearing a headset to experience virtual reality.
words.ex_cn: 他戴着头盔体验虚拟现实。
words.en: Virtual reality is an artificial environment that is created with software and presented to the user in such a way that the user suspends belief and accepts it as a real environment.

words.ex: The children learned through visual aids like pictures.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们通过图片等视觉辅助工具学习。
words.en: relating to seeing or to the eyes

words.ex: The project was an abject failure, resulting in significant financial losses.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目彻底失败了，导致了重大的财务损失。
words.en: An abject failure is a complete and utter failure, often resulting in humiliation or disgrace.

words.tr: phrase. 原住民文化；指一个地区原始居民的传统、信仰、语言和生活方式
words.ex: The elders teach the children about aboriginal culture.
words.ex_cn: 长老们教孩子们关于原住民文化。
words.en: The traditional customs, beliefs, and social structures of the original inhabitants of a region.

words.tr: v. 使自己适应某物；适应（环境、气候等）
words.ex: He tried to acclimatize himself to the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 他努力让自己适应寒冷的天气。

words.tr:
n. 艰苦跋涉；
v. 长途跋涉；
words.ex: The trek across the mountains took five days.
words.ex_cn: 穿越群山的艰苦跋涉花了五天时间。
words.en: A trek is a long and often difficult journey, especially one made on foot.

words.tr:
v. 费力地做；苦干；跋涉
n. 苦工；劳累的工作
words.ex: He toils in the field every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天在田里辛苦劳作。
words.en: If you toil, you work very hard doing something that is difficult or tiring.

words.ex: He works at a veterinary clinic.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家兽医诊所工作。
words.en: Relating to the medical or surgical treatment of animals, especially domesticated animals.

words.tr:
n. 兽医；
v. 审查；
words.ex: The vet checked the dog's health.
words.ex_cn: 兽医检查了狗的健康状况。
words.en: A vet is a person who is qualified to treat sick or injured animals. As a verb, to vet means to examine something or someone carefully to make sure they are suitable for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. 资深员工；有经验的雇员
words.ex: The veteran employee gave advice to new workers.
words.ex_cn: 这位资深员工给新员工提供了建议。
words.en: An experienced worker who has been with a company for a long time.

words.tr: n. 研究能力；科研能力
words.ex: The university improved its research capacity last year.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学去年提高了其研究能力。

words.tr: phrase. 研究能力；科研能力
words.ex: He has strong research capability.
words.ex_cn: 他有很强的研究能力。
words.en: The capacity or facilities available for conducting scientific study and investigation.

words.tr: n. 氧气摄取；机体吸收氧气的能力
words.ex: Athletes train to improve their oxygen uptake.
words.ex_cn: 运动员训练以提高氧气摄取。

words.tr: n. 若干变量；多个变量
words.ex: The equation has a number of variables to solve.
words.ex_cn: 这个方程有若干变量需要求解。

words.ex: This apple is a variant of the red delicious.
words.ex_cn: 这种苹果是红富士的一个变体。
words.en: A variant is something that is slightly different from other similar things.

words.tr: adj. 各种各样的；不同的；各种的；
words.ex: He bought various fruits at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了各种各样的水果。
words.en: If you say that there are various things, you mean there are several different things of the type mentioned.

words.tr: adj. 不同的；多种多样的；
words.ex: The class has diverse students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级有来自许多国家的不同学生。
words.en: If a group or range of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things.

words.ex: He has awareness of the environmental problems.
words.ex_cn: 他意识到环境问题。
words.en: Knowledge or perception of a situation or fact.

words.ex: The auditory system helps us hear sounds.
words.ex_cn: 听觉系统帮助我们听到声音。
words.en: Relating to the sense of hearing.

words.ex: The room has good acoustic properties.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有良好的声音效果。
words.en: Relating to sound or the sense of hearing.

words.tr: n. 情况；事例；案件；外壳；容器（箱，盒）；
words.ex: In this case, we should wait longer.
words.ex_cn: 在这种情况下，我们应该再等一会儿。
words.en: A particular situation or example of something.

words.ex: The dissonant notes made the music sound unpleasant.
words.ex_cn: 这些不和谐的音符让音乐听起来很难听。
words.en: If something is dissonant, it is not harmonious or consistent; it may refer to sounds that are harsh and unpleasant or to ideas, opinions, or elements that are in disagreement.

words.tr: v. 使根深蒂固；使处于牢固地位；用壕沟围住
words.ex: The habit entrenches itself over time.
words.ex_cn: 这个习惯随着时间的推移变得根深蒂固。
words.en: To establish something very firmly so that it is very difficult to change.

words.ex: He is an artistic boy who loves to draw.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢画画的艺术型男孩。
words.en: Someone who is artistic is good at drawing or painting, or arranging things in a beautiful way.

words.tr: n. 锦标赛；冠军赛；冠军的身份；
words.ex: He won the championship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年赢得了锦标赛。
words.en: A championship is a competition to find the best player or team in a particular sport or game.

words.ex: He works in financial planning.
words.ex_cn: 他从事财政规划工作。
words.en: Relating to finance or the management of large amounts of money.

words.ex: The government made a fiscal decision to lower taxes.
words.ex_cn: 政府做出了降低税收的财政决定。
words.en: Fiscal is used to describe something that relates to government money or public money, especially taxes.

words.ex: He read a historical book about ancient Rome.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于古罗马的历史书。
words.en: Historical means relating to the study of history or connected with the past.

words.ex: The small village is idyllic with green fields and quiet streams.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄有着绿色的田野和宁静的溪流，十分宁静美好。
words.en: An idyllic place or experience is extremely pleasant, beautiful, and peaceful, often in a way that seems too good to be true.

words.tr: phrase. 自我意识；自知之明；对自身思想、情绪和行为的觉察能力
words.ex: He has self awareness and knows his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他有自我意识，知道自己的感受。
words.en: Conscious knowledge of one's own character, feelings, motives, and desires.

words.tr: n. 增强的意识；警觉性提高
words.ex: The accident led to heightened awareness of road safety.
words.ex_cn: 这起事故增强了人们对道路安全的意识。
words.en: An increased level of consciousness or attention towards a particular subject.

words.ex: He uses optical lenses to see small objects.
words.ex_cn: 他使用光学镜片来看小物体。
words.en: Relating to sight, especially in relation to the physical action of light.

words.tr: n. 听觉通道；听觉通路
words.ex: The auditory channel helps us hear sounds around us.
words.ex_cn: 听觉通道帮助我们听到周围的声音。
words.en: A pathway or channel for sound, especially the ear canal.

words.tr: n. 听觉问题；听觉障碍
words.ex: He has an auditory problem and needs a hearing aid.
words.ex_cn: 他有听觉问题，需要助听器。
words.en: A difficulty or disorder affecting the ability to hear, such as hearing loss or tinnitus.

words.ex: The school concert was held in the auditorium.
words.ex_cn: 学校的音乐会是在礼堂举行的。
words.en: An auditorium is the part of a theatre, concert hall, or other public building in which the audience sits.

words.tr: phrase. 在所有情况下；无论如何；一律
words.ex: In all cases, safety must come first.
words.ex_cn: 在所有情况下，安全必须放在第一位。
words.en: Under any circumstances; always.

words.tr: phrase. 假使；如果；万一；以防
words.ex: Keep a flashlight in case of power outage.
words.ex_cn: 以防停电，准备一个手电筒。
words.en: used to describe what should be done if a particular situation, especially a bad one, occurs

words.tr: n. 不协和音乐；音调不和谐的音乐
words.ex: The composer used dissonant music to create tension.
words.ex_cn: 作曲家使用不协和音乐来制造紧张感。
words.en: Music that is harsh, discordant, or lacking in harmony, creating an unsettling effect.

words.tr: adj. 确立的；根深蒂固的； v. “entrench”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The entrenched system is hard to change.
words.ex_cn: 这个已确立的制度很难改变。
words.en: If something is entrenched, it is firmly established and very difficult to change.

words.ex: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一个宁静的村庄在日落时分的景象。
words.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

words.tr: v. 深陷于；根深蒂固于；牢固地扎根于
words.en: To be firmly established or deeply rooted within a system, practice, or belief.

words.tr: phrase. 艺术表达；艺术表现形式
words.ex: The painting is a powerful example of artistic expression.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是艺术表现的一个有力例子。
words.en: Artistic expression refers to the various ways in which individuals create and share art to communicate ideas, emotions, or a worldview.

words.tr: n. 艺术天赋基因；具有艺术才能的遗传特质
words.ex: His artistic genes make him draw beautifully.
words.ex_cn: 他的艺术天赋基因让他画得非常美。

words.tr: phrase. 艺术风格；指艺术作品在形式、手法、色彩、构图等方面所表现出的独特特征和整体风貌
words.ex: The museum features a wide range of artistic styles from different periods.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆展出了来自不同时期的各种艺术风格。
words.en: A distinctive manner or method of expression in any art.

words.ex: They tease him because he wears funny hats.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他戴滑稽的帽子而戏弄他。
words.en: To tease someone means to make fun of them or try to provoke them in a playful way.

words.tr: v. （以可望而不可及之物）逗引；使干着急
words.ex: The smell of cookies tantalize him.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味让他垂涎欲滴。
words.en: If someone or something tantalizes you, they make you feel hopeful and excited about getting what you want, usually before disappointing you by not letting you have it.

words.tr: n. 奇事；巧合；怪癖；奇行
words.ex: His habit of talking to his plants is a strange quirk.
words.ex_cn: 他跟植物说话的习惯是一个奇怪的奇事。
words.en: A quirk is a peculiar habit or aspect of a person's character, or an unexpected twist in a situation or story.

words.tr: phrase. 全国冠军赛；全国锦标赛
words.ex: Winning the national championship was the highlight of his career.
words.ex_cn: 赢得国家锦标赛是他职业生涯的亮点。
words.en: A competition held to determine the best in a particular sport or game at a national level.

words.w: by a tantalizing quirk of fate
words.tr: adv. 凭命运一个诱人的巧合
words.uk: baɪ ə ˈtæn.təl.aɪ.zɪŋ kwɜːk əv feɪt
words.us: baɪ ə ˈtæn.təl.aɪ.zɪŋ kwɜːrk əv feɪt
words.ex: By a tantalizing quirk of fate, she found her lost wallet at the bus stop.
words.ex_cn: 凭命运一个诱人的巧合，她在公交站找到了丢失的钱包。

words.tr: phrase. 经济负担；财务压力
words.ex: The loan created a financial burden for her family.
words.ex_cn: 这笔贷款给她的家庭带来了经济负担。
words.en: A heavy load of financial responsibility or debt.

words.tr: phrase. 金融危机；金融崩溃
words.ex: The bank failed after a financial meltdown.
words.ex_cn: 金融危机发生后，这家银行倒闭了。
words.en: A severe and sudden collapse of financial systems or markets.

words.tr: phrase. 财务指标；用于衡量企业财务状况和经营绩效的量化标准
words.ex: The company tracks key financial metrics like profit and revenue.
words.ex_cn: 公司追踪关键的财务指标，如利润和收入。
words.en: Quantitative data used to assess the financial health and performance of a business.

words.tr: phrase. 财务支持；经济援助
words.ex: He got financial support from his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他从父母那里获得了经济支持。
words.en: Financial support refers to the provision of money or resources to help someone or something, especially in the context of education, business, or personal needs.

words.ex: He studied metrics to write better poetry.
words.ex_cn: 他学习韵律学以写出更好的诗歌。
words.en: Metrics are standards of measurement by which efficiency, performance, progress, or quality of a plan, process, or product can be assessed.

words.ex: The country uses metric units for weight and distance.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家使用米制单位来衡量重量和距离。
words.en: A metric is a system of measurement that uses meters, liters, and grams as its basic units.

words.tr: n. 历史框架；历史背景结构
words.ex: The book uses a historical framework to explain the war.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使用历史框架来解释这场战争。
words.en: A structure of past events, ideas, or conditions used to understand or analyze a subject.

words.tr: phrase. 历史遗迹；历史文物
words.ex: The museum displays ancient historical relics.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆展出了古代的历史文物。
words.en: Historical relics refer to objects, artifacts, or sites that have survived from past times and are of historical interest or significance.

words.ex: The idyllic blue ocean stretched endlessly under the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 田园诗般的蓝色海洋在日落下无尽延伸。

words.ex: He works on an agricultural farm.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个农场工作。
words.en: Relating to the science or practice of farming, including cultivation of the soil for the growing of crops and the rearing of animals to provide food, wool, and other products.

words.tr: adj. 按时间先后顺序排列的
words.ex: The events are listed in chronological order.
words.ex_cn: 这些事件按时间顺序列出。
words.en: If things are described or shown in chronological order, they are described or shown in the order in which they happened.

words.tr: adj. 即刻的；立即的；紧接的；最近的；
words.ex: He needs immediate help.
words.ex_cn: 他需要即刻的帮助。
words.en: An immediate action, event, or situation happens or exists without any delay.

words.ex: He practices martial arts every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天练习武术。
words.en: Martial is used to describe things relating to soldiers or war.

words.ex: He immersed the cloth in water.
words.ex_cn: 他把布浸在水里。
words.en: To immerse something or someone means to put them into a liquid so that they are completely covered by it. It can also mean to involve oneself deeply in a particular activity or interest.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.ex: He is proficient in playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他弹钢琴很熟练。
words.en: If you are proficient in something, you can do it well because you have learned how to do it.

words.ex: Children develop cognitive skills as they grow.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在成长过程中发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognitive means relating to the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.

words.ex: Farmers plant agriculture crop every spring.
words.ex_cn: 农民每年春天种植农作物。

words.tr: n. 农用车辆；用于农业作业的专用车辆
words.ex: The farmer drives an agricultural vehicle to plow the field.
words.ex_cn: 农民驾驶农用车辆耕田。
words.en: A machine used in farming, such as a tractor or combine harvester.

words.tr: phrase. 按时间顺序地；以年代先后排列
words.ex: The events were listed in chronological order.
words.ex_cn: 这些事件按时间顺序列出。
words.en: In the order in which events happened.

words.tr: n. 按时间顺序的发展； chronological development 指按照事件发生的时间先后顺序进行排列或发展的过程
words.ex: The book shows the chronological development of computers.
words.ex_cn: 这本书展示了计算机的 chronological 发展过程。
words.en: The sequence in which events or developments occur over time.

words.tr: phrase. phr. 在不久的将来；在最近的未来
words.ex: He will start his new job in the immediate future.
words.ex_cn: 他将在不久的将来开始他的新工作。
words.en: In the very near future; soon.

words.ex: He left the room immediately after the bell rang.
words.ex_cn: 铃声一响，他就立即离开了房间。
words.en: If something happens immediately, it happens without any delay.

words.tr:
n. 元帅；高级军官；典礼官；消防局长
v. 整理；集结
words.ex: The marshal led the army into battle.
words.ex_cn: 元帅率领军队上战场。
words.en: A marshal is a high-ranking officer in the armed forces, especially in the army or air force, or a person who arranges or directs a public event.

words.tr: n. 军乐；具有军事风格的音乐
words.ex: The soldiers marched to martial music.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们随着军乐行进。
words.en: Music composed for military purposes, often played by bands during ceremonies or parades.

words.tr: phrase. 使自己沉浸于；专心于；埋头于
words.ex: He likes to immerse himself in simple books every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢每天晚上沉浸在简单的书籍中。
words.en: To involve oneself deeply in a particular activity or interest.

words.ex: The judge will summon him tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 法官明天将传唤他。
words.en: If you summon someone, you order them to come to you.

words.tr: v. 擅长于某事；精通某事
n. 认知与神经系统的组合，指大脑中负责处理信息、感知、记忆、学习和决策等心理功能的神经结构与机制
words.ex: The brain's cognitive and neurological systems help us remember names and make choices.
words.ex_cn: 大脑的认知与神经系统的组合帮助我们记住名字并做出选择。

words.tr: phrase. 认知行为；指个体在思维、感知和理解过程中表现出的行为模式
words.ex: He changed his cognitive behaviour to feel happier.
words.ex_cn: 他改变了认知行为以感觉更快乐。
words.en: A therapeutic approach that focuses on changing unhelpful patterns of thinking and behaviour.

words.tr: adj. 逻辑上的；合乎逻辑的；
words.ex: His argument is logical and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点合乎逻辑，容易理解。
words.en: In accordance with the principles of logic; reasonable.

words.ex: The weather is unpredictable today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气不可预测。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unpredictable, you mean that you cannot tell what they are going to do or how they are going to behave.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.ex: It is rational to save money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 为未来存钱是合理的。
words.en: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.

words.ex: He visits a religious temple every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都去一座宗教寺庙。
words.en: Relating to or believing in a religion.

words.tr: adj. 习惯的；惯常的； v. “accustom”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is accustomed to waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 他习惯早起。
words.en: If you are accustomed to something, you know it so well or have experienced it so often that it seems natural, unsurprising, or easy to deal with.

words.ex: They collaborate to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作完成这个项目。
words.en: to work jointly with others or together especially in an intellectual endeavor

words.tr: n. 始终一贯；前后一致；
words.ex: His consistency in studying every day helped him pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他每天学习的一贯坚持帮助他通过了考试。
words.en: Consistency is the quality or condition of being consistent, especially in achieving a level of performance or behavior that does not vary greatly in quality over time.

words.tr: phrase. 逻辑一致性；逻辑上的连贯性
words.ex: The argument shows logical consistency throughout.
words.ex_cn: 这个论点在整个过程中保持了逻辑一致性。
words.en: The quality of being free from contradictions in reasoning or argument.

words.tr: phrase. 逻辑思维；逻辑思考
words.ex: He uses logical thinking to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用逻辑思维解决数学问题。
words.en: Logical thinking involves the process of reasoning in a structured and coherent manner to solve problems or make decisions.

words.ex: The unpredictable noise from the old machine scared the children.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧机器发出的难以预测的噪音吓到了孩子们。
words.en: Sound that is irregular, unpredictable, and difficult to anticipate.

words.tr: phrase. 对某事感到惊叹；对某事感到惊奇
words.ex: We marvel at the beauty of the stars.
words.ex_cn: 我们对星空的美丽感到惊叹。

words.tr: phrase. 建筑奇迹；宏伟的建筑作品
words.ex: The pyramids are architectural marvels of ancient Egypt.
words.ex_cn: 金字塔是古埃及的建筑奇迹。

words.tr: phrase. 理性决定；基于理性的判定
words.ex: The company's success was due to its rational determination in resource allocation.
words.ex_cn: 公司的成功归功于其在资源分配上的理性决策。
words.en: The exercise of logic and reason to make firm, well-considered decisions and pursue goals with determination.

words.tr: n. 基本原理；基础理论；
words.ex: The rationale for the new rule is to save time.
words.ex_cn: 这个新规则的基本原理是节省时间。
words.en: The fundamental reasons or logical basis for a course of action or belief.

words.tr:
n. 圣歌；赞美诗；喊叫
v. 吟唱；诵扬；反复叫喊
words.ex: The monks sang a traditional chant during the morning prayer.
words.ex_cn: 修道士们在晨祷时唱了一首传统圣歌。
words.en: A chant is a word or group of words that is repeated over and over again. It can also refer to a simple song, especially one that is sung in a religious service.

words.tr: phrase. 宗教颂歌；宗教吟唱
words.ex: The monks sang a religious chant every morning.
words.ex_cn: 僧侣们每天早上唱一首宗教颂歌。
words.en: A rhythmic vocal expression used in religious ceremonies.

words.tr: phrase. 宗教事务；宗教问题
words.ex: The government does not interfere in religious matter.
words.ex_cn: 政府不干涉宗教事务。
words.en: An issue or topic related to faith, spirituality, or religious practice.

words.ex: He cooks dinner on a gas stove.
words.ex_cn: 他用煤气灶做晚饭。
words.en: A gas stove is a stove that is fuelled by combustible gas such as natural gas, propane, butane, liquefied petroleum gas or other flammable gas.

words.tr: phrase. 习惯于某事；适应某事
words.ex: He got accustomed to waking up early for work.
words.ex_cn: 他习惯了早起上班。

words.ex: They collaborate with each other on science projects.
words.ex_cn: 他们一起合作做科学项目。

words.ex: The family reduced their monthly expenditure.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭减少了每月的开支。
words.en: Expenditure is the spending of money on something, or the money that is spent on something.

words.tr: adj. 公正的；不偏不倚的；
words.ex: The judge was impartial in the trial.
words.ex_cn: 法官在审判中是公正的。
words.en: Someone who is impartial is not directly involved in a particular situation, and is therefore able to give a fair opinion or decision about it.

words.ex: He felt satisfaction after finishing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他完成作业后感到满意。
words.en: The feeling of pleasure that you have when you do or get something that you wanted or needed.

words.ex: The operation of the machine is very smooth.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的运行非常顺畅。
words.en: An operation is a planned activity involving many people performing various tasks.

words.tr:
n. 决策人；行政官；管理人员；
adj. 行政的；决策的；
words.ex: The executive decided to launch the new product.
words.ex_cn: 这位决策人决定推出新产品。
words.en: An executive is a person who has a senior management position in a business or other organization.

words.tr:
v. 增加；增多；
n. 增加；增长；
words.ex: The company increased its profits last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年增加了利润。
words.en: To increase something means to make it larger in size, amount, or degree.

words.tr:
n. 包；包裹；
v. 包装；
words.ex: He bought a package of cookies.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一包饼干。
words.en: A package is a wrapped container or a set of objects wrapped in paper or packed in a box.

words.ex: The artist interweaves colors to make a beautiful pattern.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家将颜色交织在一起，创造出美丽的图案。
words.en: To interweave means to weave or blend together two or more things so that they cannot be separated easily.

words.ex: The child mimics her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If someone or something mimics another person or thing, they try to be like them or copy their behavior or characteristics.

words.ex: The country saw a rise in overall tourism expenditure last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年该国的总体旅游支出有所增加。
words.en: The total amount of money spent by visitors on tourism-related activities, services, and goods within a specific period.

words.tr: n. 公正的看法；不偏不倚的视角
words.ex: He gave an impartial view of both sides.
words.ex_cn: 他对双方都给出了公正的看法。
words.en: An unbiased or neutral perspective on a subject.

words.ex: The park improved visitor satisfaction by adding more rest areas.
words.ex_cn: 公园通过增加更多休息区提高了游客满意度。
words.en: The degree of contentment experienced by guests or users of a service or location.

words.tr:
n. 抢救；
v. 打捞；挽救；抢救；
words.ex: The salvage of the ship took three days.
words.ex_cn: 对这艘船的抢救花了三天时间。
words.en: To salvage something means to retrieve or preserve it from loss or destruction, especially from a shipwreck or fire. It can also refer to the act of saving or rescuing something from a difficult situation.

words.tr: n. 制造运营；生产操作
words.ex: The factory improved its manufacturing operation to save time.
words.ex_cn: 工厂改进了其制造运营以节省时间。

words.tr: phrase. 打捞作业；救援行动
words.ex: The salvage operation recovered the sunken ship.
words.ex_cn: 打捞作业打捞了沉没的船只。
words.en: An operation to recover something valuable from a place where it has been lost or damaged.

words.tr: phrase. 销售主管；市场总监
words.ex: She was recently promoted to the position of marketing executive.
words.ex_cn: 她最近被提升为市场营销主管。
words.en: A marketing executive is a person responsible for the marketing activities of a company or organization, including planning, executing, and monitoring marketing campaigns to promote products or services.

words.ex: The plants grew artificially under blue lights.
words.ex_cn: 这些植物在蓝光下人工生长。
words.en: In a way that is made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally, especially as a copy of something natural.

words.tr: v. 人工延长白昼时间
words.ex: Farmers use lights to increase day length artificially for plants.
words.ex_cn: 农民使用灯光人工延长植物的白昼时间。

words.ex: The smallholder grows vegetables on his farm.
words.ex_cn: 这位小农户在他的农场种植蔬菜。
words.en: A smallholder is a person who owns or rents a small piece of land and grows crops or keeps animals on it, often as a means of subsistence.

words.tr: v. 增加小农户的脆弱性
words.ex: Climate change can increase smallholder vulnerability to droughts.
words.ex_cn: 气候变化会增加小农户对干旱的脆弱性。

words.tr: phrase. 旅游套餐；包含交通、住宿等服务的旅行打包产品
words.ex: He booked a travel package for his vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他为假期预订了一个旅行套餐。
words.en: A travel package is a combination of travel services such as transportation, accommodation, and sometimes meals and activities, sold together at a single price.

words.tr: v. 与某物交织在一起；把某物与另一物紧密地编织或融合
words.ex: The story interweaves with real history.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事与真实历史交织在一起。

words.tr: phrase. 模仿人类能力；模拟人类技能
words.ex: Robots are designed to mimic human abilities in various tasks.
words.ex_cn: 机器人被设计用来模仿人类在各种任务中的能力。
words.en: To imitate or replicate the capabilities of humans, often in the context of technology or artificial intelligence.

words.ex: The child mimics her mother's actions when she cooks.
words.ex_cn: 当妈妈做饭时，孩子模仿她的行为。
words.en: To copy or imitate the behavior or movements of another person.

words.tr:
adj. 集体的；
n. 集体；
words.ex: The collective decision was made by all members.
words.ex_cn: 这个集体决定是由所有成员做出的。
words.en: done or shared by all members of a group of people

words.ex: They have a good relationship with their neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他们和邻居关系很好。
words.en: A relationship is the way in which two or more people or things are connected, or the state of being connected.

words.ex: He uses scientific methods to test his idea.
words.ex_cn: 他用科学方法来测试他的想法。
words.en: Scientific means relating to science or using the methods of science.

words.ex: The virus can mutate quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以迅速变异。
words.en: If an animal or plant mutates, or something mutates it, it develops different characteristics as the result of a change in its genes.

words.ex: Children develop perceptual skills by playing with toys.
words.ex_cn: 儿童通过玩玩具发展知觉能力。
words.en: Relating to the ability to interpret or become aware of something through the senses.

words.tr: n. 术语；条款；期间；学期；“term”的复数；
words.ex: The book explains the terms of computer science.
words.ex_cn: 这本书解释了计算机科学的术语。
words.en: Terms refer to the conditions that are set for an agreement or the words used to describe specific things in a particular field.

words.tr:
v. 看待；有关；
n. 尊敬；致意；
words.ex: I regard him as a good friend.
words.ex_cn: 我把他看作好朋友。
words.en: If you regard someone or something as being a particular thing or as having a particular quality, you believe that they are that thing or have that quality.

words.tr: n. 马达；发动机；机动车；
words.ex: The car has a strong motor.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有一个强大的马达。
words.en: A motor is a device that changes energy into mechanical motion, especially such a device that provides power for a vehicle or for another device with moving parts.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet can prevent head injuries.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔可以防止头部受伤。
words.en: To prevent something means to stop it from happening or to stop someone from doing something.

words.tr:
n. 大师；主人；
v. 掌握；精通；
words.ex: He is a master of classical piano.
words.ex_cn: 他是古典钢琴的大师。
words.en: A master is someone who has control over something or someone; a person who is highly skilled in a particular area; or a degree awarded by a university or college.

words.tr: n. 集体成就；共同完成的成果
words.ex: The team's collective accomplishment won them the award.
words.ex_cn: 团队的集体成就为他们赢得了奖项。
words.en: An achievement resulting from the combined effort of a group.

words.tr: n. 集体协议；劳资双方达成的集体合同
words.ex: The workers signed a collective agreement with their employer.
words.ex_cn: 工人与雇主签署了集体协议。

words.ex: The ever-shifting sands make it difficult to build a permanent structure.
words.ex_cn: 不断变化的沙子使得建造永久性建筑变得困难。
words.en: Constantly changing or moving.

words.ex: Their ever-shifting relationship made it hard to trust each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们不断变化的关系让他们难以互相信任。
words.en: A relationship that is constantly changing or adapting over time.

words.ex: Good interpersonal relationship helps people work together.
words.ex_cn: 良好的人际关系有助于人们共同工作。
words.en: The way in which two or more people or groups regard and behave towards each other.

words.tr: phrase. 科学进步；科学进展
words.ex: The scientific progress in medicine has led to the development of new treatments.
words.ex_cn: 医学上的科学进步已经导致了新治疗方法的发展。
words.en: Scientific progress refers to the advancement of knowledge and technology through systematic study and experimentation.

words.ex: His converse was the opposite of what he said earlier.
words.ex_cn: 他的相反言论与他之前说的话相反。
words.en: To engage in conversation; to talk informally with someone.

words.tr:
n. 反面；
v. 使倒转；（使）倒车；撤销；
words.ex: The reverse of the coin has a picture of a tree.
words.ex_cn: 硬币的反面有一棵树的图案。
words.en: If you reverse the order of a set of things, you arrange them in the opposite order, so that the first thing comes last.

words.tr: v. 变异为某种事物；转变为某种形式
words.ex: The virus can mutate into something more dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以变异为更危险的东西。

words.ex: He converted into a teacher after working in business.
words.ex_cn: 他在从事商业工作后转变为一名教师。

words.tr: n. 知觉决策；基于感知信息做出的判断
words.ex: The child made a perceptual decision about which color was brighter.
words.ex_cn: 孩子做出了关于哪种颜色更亮的知觉决策。
words.en: The process of making a judgment based on sensory information.

words.tr: phrase. 感知信息；通过感官获取并经过大脑加工处理的信息
words.ex: The child uses perceptual information to recognize shapes.
words.ex_cn: 孩子使用感知信息来识别形状。
words.en: Information that is received and interpreted through the senses, such as sight, sound, or touch.

words.tr: phrase. 宽泛地讲；总体来说
words.ex: In broad terms, he likes sports.
words.ex_cn: 总的来说，他喜欢运动。
words.en: If you describe something in broad terms, you describe it in a general way, without giving details.

words.tr: phrase. 就...而言；在...方面；根据
words.ex: In terms of cost, this phone is cheaper.
words.ex_cn: 从成本来看，这部手机更便宜。
words.en: used to indicate what aspect of a subject you are talking about

words.ex: Vaccines help build immunity against diseases.
words.ex_cn: 疫苗有助于增强对疾病的免疫力。
words.en: Immunity is the state of being immune from or insusceptible to a particular disease or the legal status of being exempt from certain obligations or penalties.

words.ex: The child received immunization against measles.
words.ex_cn: 孩子接种了麻疹疫苗。
words.en: The process by which an individual's immune system becomes fortified against an agent (known as the immunogen).

words.ex: The doctor will immunize the child against measles.
words.ex_cn: 医生会给这个孩子接种麻疹疫苗。
words.en: To immunize someone or something means to protect them against a disease by giving them a vaccine.

words.tr: phrase. 在这方面；就这一点而言
words.ex: He didn't finish the report. In this regard, he needs more time.
words.ex_cn: 他没有完成报告。在这方面，他需要更多时间。
words.en: used to refer to something that has just been mentioned, especially when you are going to say something more about it

words.tr: prep. 关于某事；就某事而言
words.ex: He spoke with regard to the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 他谈到了新政策。

words.tr: v. 把某物视为某物；认为某物是某物
words.ex: They regard him as a hero.
words.ex_cn: 他们把他视为英雄。

words.tr: adj. 有免疫力的；免疫的；不受影响的；
words.ex: Children are immune to this disease after vaccination.
words.ex_cn: 儿童接种疫苗后对这种疾病有免疫力。
words.en: If you are immune to a particular disease, you cannot be affected by it. If you are immune to something such as criticism, it does not affect you.

words.ex: His motive was to help his family.
words.ex_cn: 他的动机是帮助家人。
words.en: Your motive for doing something is your reason for doing it.

words.ex: The technician fixed the motor circuits in the factory machine.
words.ex_cn: 技工修好了工厂机器中的电动机电路。

words.ex: He drives a motor vehicle to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天开车去上班。
words.en: A motor vehicle is a self-propelled road vehicle, commonly wheeled, that does not operate on rails, such as trains or trams, and is used for the transportation of passengers or cargo.

words.tr: n. 回路；环行；电路；巡回；
words.ex: The battery connects to the circuit to make the light work.
words.ex_cn: 电池连接到回路，使灯亮起来。
words.en: A circuit is a roughly circular line, route, or movement that starts and finishes at the same place. It can also refer to the complete path that an electric current travels along.

words.ex: Planting trees can prevent desertification.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以防止荒漠化。
words.en: Measures taken to stop fertile land from becoming desert, often through sustainable land management.

words.ex: The fence prevents children from falling into the pool.
words.ex_cn: 围栏防止孩子们掉进游泳池。
words.en: To stop someone from performing an action.

words.tr: phrase. 大师级工匠；技艺精湛的匠人
words.ex: The master craftsman carved the wooden statue by hand.
words.ex_cn: 这位大师级工匠用手雕刻了这尊木雕。
words.en: A highly skilled artisan who has achieved mastery in a specific craft.

words.ex: He earned a master's degree in engineering.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了工程学的硕士学位。
words.en: A master's degree is an advanced academic degree awarded by universities or colleges upon completion of a course of study demonstrating mastery or a high-order overview of a specific field of study or area of professional practice.

words.tr:
v. 定罪；宣判有罪
n. 罪犯；囚犯
words.ex: The court convicted him of theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院判定他犯有盗窃罪。
words.en: If someone is convicted of a crime, they are found guilty of that crime in a court of law.

words.ex: The police caught the culprit who stole the bike.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓住了偷自行车的罪犯。
words.en: A culprit is someone who has done something wrong or illegal.

words.tr:
adj. 犯罪的；
n. 罪犯；
words.ex: He made a criminal mistake by stealing money.
words.ex_cn: 他偷钱犯了一个犯罪的错误。
words.en: A criminal is a person who has committed a crime.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.tr: adj. 有独创性的；巧妙的；
words.ex: The child came up with an ingenious way to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子想出了一个有独创性的方式来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

words.ex: He works in the sales department.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售部工作。
words.en: A department is one of the sections in an organization such as a government, business, or university.

words.tr:
n. 计划；节目；程序；
v. 编程；
words.ex: He made a programme to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个存钱的计划。
words.en: A programme is a plan of activities designed to achieve a particular result.

words.ex: The teacher gave clear instruction on how to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了如何解决这个问题的明确教授。
words.en: Detailed information telling how something should be done, operated, or assembled.

words.tr: adj. 群体的；社区的；公有的；
words.ex: They share a communal kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 他们共用一个群体厨房。
words.en: Communal means relating to or shared by all the members of a community.

words.tr:
n. 叙述；叙事；
adj. 叙述性的；
words.ex: He told a simple narrative about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他童年的简单故事。
words.en: A narrative is a story or an account of a series of events.

words.tr:
adj. 依靠的；依赖的；
n. 受赡养者；
words.ex: The child is dependent on his parents for food.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子依靠父母提供食物。
words.en: A dependent person or thing is one that needs the support of another person or thing in order to exist or be successful.

words.ex: The fireworks at night were a beautiful spectacle.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的烟花是一场美丽的奇观。
words.en: A spectacle is a visually striking performance or display.

words.ex: The jury decided the man was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团裁定这个人无罪。
words.en: A jury is a group of people who are chosen to decide whether someone is guilty or not guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.tr: v. 判定（某人）犯有（罪行）
words.ex: The court convicted him of theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院判定他犯有盗窃罪。
words.en: To find someone guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.tr: phrase. 消除饥荒；根除饥饿
words.ex: The government wants to eradicate famine in the region.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消除该地区的饥荒。
words.en: Completely eliminate widespread food scarcity.

words.ex: He is a genius in math.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面是个天才。
words.en: Someone who is a genius is a person who is exceptionally intelligent or talented, especially in a particular field.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

words.tr: v. （使）杂交繁育；杂交繁育; n. （动植物的）杂交品种
words.ex: Farmers crossbreed cows to get better milk.
words.ex_cn: 农民杂交奶牛以获得更好的牛奶。
words.en: To crossbreed animals or plants means to breed them from parents of different breeds or varieties.

words.ex: The broken glass is a hazard.
words.ex_cn: 碎玻璃是危险。
words.en: A hazard is something which could be dangerous to you, your health or safety, or your plans or reputation.

words.tr: adj. 泛滥的；猖獗的；蔓生的
words.ex: Rumors are rampant in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在这个小镇上四处流传。
words.en: If you describe something bad, such as a crime or disease, as rampant, you mean that it is very common and is increasing in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr: n. 一项真正巧妙的发明
words.ex: The robot is a truly ingenious invention.
words.ex_cn: 这个机器人是一项真正巧妙的发明。

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.ex: Bees pollinate flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂给花园里的花授粉。
words.en: To pollinate means to transfer pollen from the male part of a flower to the female part, enabling fertilization and the production of seeds.

words.ex: Bees are important pollinators for flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂是花朵的重要传粉者。
words.en: A pollinator is an animal that moves pollen from the male part of a flower to the female part of a flower, thus enabling fertilization and the production of seeds.

words.ex: She bought a pink orchid for her mother.
words.ex_cn: 她为母亲买了一朵粉色的兰花。
words.en: A plant with complex flowers that are often brightly coloured, grown especially for its beautiful flowers.

words.ex: He plays violin in a local orchestra.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个本地管弦乐队中拉小提琴。
words.en: An orchestra is a large group of musicians who play a variety of different instruments together. Orchestras usually play classical music.

words.tr: v. 改编为管弦乐；策划；精心安排
words.ex: He orchestrated the folk song for a symphony orchestra.
words.ex_cn: 他将这首民歌改编为管弦乐。
words.en: To orchestrate something means to organize or arrange it in a very detailed and carefully planned way, especially in order to achieve a particular effect or result.

words.tr: adj. 教育性的；有启发的；有益的
words.ex: The movie is instructive for children.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影对孩子们很有教育意义。
words.en: Providing useful or interesting information or knowledge.

words.tr: n. 单元住宅；公寓住宅；
words.ex: He lives in a small apartment near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他住在公园附近的一间小公寓里。
words.en: An apartment is a set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a large building.

words.ex: He walks in the orchard every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都在果园里散步。
words.en: An orchard is an area of land where fruit trees are grown.

words.ex: The education department sends books to schools.
words.ex_cn: 教育部门向学校发送书籍。
words.en: The department of a government or organization responsible for the administration and oversight of education systems and policies.

words.ex: He watches television programmes every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上看电视节目。
words.en: Shows broadcast on television.

words.tr: phrase. 建立；创立；设立；架起；提出
words.ex: He set up a small shop last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年开了一家小商店。
words.en: To set up something means to establish it or arrange it.

words.tr: phrase. 共同活动；集体活动
words.ex: Cooking a meal together is a simple communal activity.
words.ex_cn: 一起做饭是一项简单的集体活动。
words.en: An activity that is shared or done by a group of people, especially those living in the same community.

words.tr: n. 共同决策；集体决策
words.ex: The village uses communal decision-making to choose their leader.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄通过共同决策来选择他们的领导人。
words.en: A process where a group collectively reaches a decision.

words.tr: n. 叙事史；以故事形式叙述的历史
words.ex: He wrote a narrative history of the American Revolution.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一部关于美国革命的叙事史。

words.tr: v. 依赖某物；取决于某物
adj. 依赖于某物；依靠某事物
n. 天文奇观；壮观的天文现象
words.ex: The total solar eclipse was an astronomical spectacle.
words.ex_cn: 日全食是一场天文奇观。
words.en: A visually striking display in the sky, often awe-inspiring, like the Northern Lights.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.ex: The sunset was spectacular.
words.ex_cn: 日落非常壮观。
words.en: Something that is spectacular is very impressive or dramatic.

words.ex: He felt psychological stress before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到心理压力。
words.en: Relating to the mental and emotional state of a person.

words.ex: They communicate well with each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此沟通得很好。
words.en: To communicate means to share or exchange information, news, or ideas, especially by speaking or writing.

words.ex: The motif of love appears in many poems.
words.ex_cn: 爱的主题出现在许多诗歌中。
words.en: A motif is a design or pattern that is used in a piece of art or music, or a theme that is repeated in a work of literature.

words.ex: The unfair verdict caused public outrage.
words.ex_cn: 不公正的判决引发了公众的愤怒。
words.en: An outrage is an extremely strong reaction of anger, shock, or indignation.

words.tr: adj. 有竞争力的；竞争的；
words.ex: She is a competitive runner who wins many races.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有竞争力的跑步者，赢得了许多比赛。
words.en: Competitive is used to describe situations or activities in which people or firms compete with each other.

words.ex: He wears a helmet to protect his head.
words.ex_cn: 他戴头盔来保护头部。
words.en: If you protect someone or something, you prevent them from being harmed or damaged.

words.ex: The stray dog wandered into the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 这只走失的狗走进了后院。
words.en: If someone or something strays, they wander away from where they are supposed to be.

words.tr: adj. 自发的；自然产生的；
words.ex: The children gave a spontaneous cheer.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们自发地欢呼起来。
words.en: Something that is spontaneous is not planned but happens or is done because of a sudden impulse or natural feeling.

words.ex: The dove is a symbolic bird of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征性鸟类。
words.en: If you describe an event, action, or procedure as symbolic, you mean that it represents an important change, although it has little practical effect.

words.tr:
v. 意思是说；表示…的意思；
n. 手段；方法；收入；
words.ex: This sign means you cannot park here.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志意思是说这里不能停车。
words.en: Means refers to a method or way of doing something, or the resources or assets available for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He resisted the temptation to eat cake.
words.ex_cn: 他抵制了吃蛋糕的诱惑。
words.en: If you feel you want to do something or have something, even though you know you really should avoid it, you can refer to this feeling as temptation.

words.tr: phrase. 心理因素；影响行为或心理状态的心理学变量
words.ex: Stress is a psychological factor that affects sleep.
words.ex_cn: 压力是一个影响睡眠的心理因素。
words.en: A psychological factor is an element that influences the mental state or behavior of an individual or group.

words.tr: phrase. 心理疾病；精神疾病；心理障碍
words.ex: The treatment of psychological illness often involves a combination of medication and therapy.
words.ex_cn: 心理疾病的治疗通常涉及药物和疗法的结合。
words.en: A condition that affects a person's thinking, feeling, behavior or mood. These conditions may affect someone's ability to relate to others and function each day.

words.tr: n. 心理学原理；心理规律
words.ex: The psychological principle of reward helps children learn better.
words.ex_cn: 奖励的心理学原理帮助孩子学得更好。
words.en: A fundamental concept or theory in psychology that explains human behaviour, thought, or emotion.

words.tr: phrase. 心理测验；心理测试
words.ex: He took a psychological test to understand his emotions.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一项心理测试来了解自己的情绪。
words.en: A psychological test is a standardized measure used to assess an individual's mental abilities, personality traits, or emotional state.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人交流；与某人沟通
words.ex: I can communicate with my friend in English.
words.ex_cn: 我能用英语和我的朋友交流。
words.en: To share or exchange information, news, or ideas with someone.

words.ex: She bought some cloth to make a dress.
words.ex_cn: 她买了一些布来做裙子。
words.en: Cloth is fabric which is made by weaving or knitting cotton, wool, silk, or other threads. Cloth is used especially for making clothes.

words.ex: He bought new clothing for the winter.
words.ex_cn: 他为冬天买了新衣服。
words.en: Clothing refers to items worn on the body. Clothing is typically made of fabrics or textiles but over time has included garments made from animal skin or other thin sheets of materials put together.

words.tr: n. 动物图案；以动物为主题的装饰纹样
words.ex: The pottery has an animal motif on its surface.
words.ex_cn: 陶器表面有一个动物图案。

words.tr: phrase. 突出主题；显著母题；鲜明主旨
words.ex: The salient motif in the artist's work is the use of vibrant colors.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家作品中的突出主题是使用鲜艳的色彩。
words.en: A salient motif is a prominent or recurring theme, idea, or pattern in a work of art, literature, or music.

words.tr: adj. 具有竞争力的全球市场
words.ex: The company works hard to succeed in a competitive global market.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司努力在具有竞争力的全球市场中取得成功。
words.en: An international marketplace where businesses compete for customers and resources.

words.tr: phrase. 保护某人免受某事物的伤害（或危险、损失等）
words.ex: A umbrella can protect you from the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨伞可以保护你免受雨淋。
words.en: To keep someone or something safe from harm, injury, damage, or loss.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The virus is infectious and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒具有传染性，传播迅速。
words.en: An infectious disease can be passed from one person to another, especially through the air they breathe.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The flu is contagious and spreads easily.
words.ex_cn: 流感具有传染性，容易传播。
words.en: A contagious disease can be caught by touching someone who has the disease or by touching an infected object or by breathing in infected air.

words.tr: v. 偏离；远离某物；走离正道
words.ex: Don't stray away from the path.
words.ex_cn: 不要偏离路径。

words.ex: He subconsciously picked up his pencil when he thought.
words.ex_cn: 当他思考时，他下意识地拿起了铅笔。
words.en: If you do something subconsciously, you do it without realizing that you are doing it.

words.tr: adj. 下意识的；潜意识的；
words.ex: The ad used subliminal messages to influence buyers.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告使用了下意识的信息来影响买家。
words.en: Subliminal refers to something that is below the threshold of sensation or consciousness; it is perceived by or affecting someone's mind without their being aware of it.

words.ex: The car stopped in an instantaneous moment.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在瞬间停了下来。
words.en: Happening or done immediately.

words.tr: n. 弦外之音；言外之意；暗示
words.ex: His smile had an overtone of sadness.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑中带着一丝悲伤。
words.en: An overtone is a subtle or subsidiary quality, implication, or connotation.

words.ex: He gave spontaneous criticism during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上发表了即兴的批评。
words.en: Spontaneous criticism refers to unplanned and immediate critique or feedback, often arising naturally in a discussion or situation.

words.ex: The dove is a symbolic meaning of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征性代表。
words.en: Symbolic meaning refers to the significance or representation of something beyond its literal sense, often used to convey ideas, values, or emotions through symbols.

words.ex: He cleaned the floor by means of a mop.
words.ex_cn: 他用拖把打扫了地板。
words.en: If you do something by means of a particular method, instrument, or process, you do it using that method, instrument, or process.

words.ex: He is by no means lazy.
words.ex_cn: 他绝对不懒。
words.en: You use 'by no means' to emphasize that something is not true or is definitely not the case.

words.tr: phrase. 无论如何；务必；在任何情况下
words.ex: I will finish this task by any means.
words.ex_cn: 我无论如何都会完成这个任务。
words.en: Using any method possible, regardless of the difficulty or cost.

words.tr: adj. 压倒的；无法抗拒的；势不可挡的； v. “overwhelm”的现在分词；
words.ex: The crowd's cheers were overwhelming.
words.ex_cn: 人群的欢呼声压倒了一切。
words.en: If something is overwhelming, it affects you very strongly, and you do not know how to deal with it.

words.ex: The vote was overwhelmingly in favor of the new law.
words.ex_cn: 投票压倒性地支持这项新法律。
words.en: In a way that is very great or very strong; so powerful that you cannot resist it or decide how to react.

words.tr: n. 令人难以抗拒的诱惑
words.ex: He felt an overwhelming temptation to eat the chocolate cake.
words.ex_cn: 他感到一种难以抗拒的吃巧克力蛋糕的诱惑。
words.en: A desire or urge so strong that it is difficult to resist.

words.tr: adj. 有极大诱惑力的；不可抵抗的；
words.ex: The chocolate cake looked irresistible.
words.ex_cn: 那块巧克力蛋糕看起来极具诱惑力。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as irresistible, you mean that they are so good or attractive that you cannot stop yourself from liking them or wanting them.

words.tr:
v. 努力；斗争；挣扎；
n. 努力；斗争；难事；
words.ex: He struggles to finish his homework every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都努力完成作业。
words.en: If you struggle to do something, you try hard to do it, even though it is difficult or other people are making it difficult for you.

words.ex: The room was devoid of any furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间里全无家具。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is devoid of a quality or thing, you are emphasizing that they have none of it.

words.ex: The loud noise scared the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音吓到了孩子。
words.en: If something scares you, it frightens or worries you.

words.tr: adj. 欠缺的；过小的；少量的
words.ex: He had scanty food for the whole day.
words.ex_cn: 他一整天的食物很少。
words.en: If something is scanty, there is not enough of it or it is too small in amount.

words.ex: The water supply is insufficient for the whole village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对整个村庄来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is insufficient, it is not enough for a particular purpose.

words.tr: adj. 不足的；缺乏的；有缺陷的
words.ex: The plant is deficient in sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物缺乏阳光。
words.en: If someone or something is deficient in a particular thing, they do not have the full amount of it that they need.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏的；不足的；稀有的；
words.ex: Water is scarce in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很缺乏。
words.en: If something is scarce, there is not enough of it.

words.ex: He has a scar on his arm from the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他手臂上有一道事故留下的伤疤。
words.en: A mark left on the skin after a wound or injury has healed, or the act of causing such a mark.

words.ex: The prospect of a better job makes him happy.
words.ex_cn: 更好工作的前景让他感到高兴。
words.en: A prospect is the possibility that something will happen, or a view of a wide area.

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.ex: He is prone to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If you are prone to a particular problem or characteristic, you are likely to be affected by it or to have it.

words.ex: He strives to finish his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力完成作业。
words.en: If you strive to do something or strive for something, you make a great effort to do it or get it.

words.ex: The weather can dictate what we wear each day.
words.ex_cn: 天气可以支配我们每天穿什么。
words.en: To dictate means to say or read something aloud for someone else to write down, or to give orders in an authoritative manner.

words.ex: The court will prosecute him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将因盗窃罪起诉他。
words.en: To prosecute means to institute legal proceedings against someone or to carry on a legal action against a defendant in a court of law. It also means to continue with or carry on an activity or enterprise.

words.ex: He will sue the company for damages.
words.ex_cn: 他将起诉这家公司要求赔偿。
words.en: To sue means to start a legal case against someone, usually to claim money from them because they have caused you harm or loss.

words.ex: The court will indict him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将对他提起盗窃指控。
words.en: If someone is indicted for a crime, they are officially charged with it.

words.tr: v. 报告某人；向当局举报某人
words.ex: He reported somebody for stealing his bike.
words.ex_cn: 他举报了偷他自行车的人。

words.tr: v. 反映；反射；反省；思考；仔细考虑；
words.ex: The mirror reflects the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 镜子反射阳光。
words.en: If a surface reflects light, heat, sound, or an image, it sends the light, etc. back and does not absorb it. If something is reflected in a mirror or in water, you can see its image in the mirror or in the water.

words.tr: phrase. 与某事作斗争；努力应对某事；艰难处理某事
words.ex: He struggles with math homework every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都在为数学作业发愁。
words.en: To try very hard to do something that is difficult or that involves problems.

words.tr: adj. 完全缺乏某种东西的；无...的
words.ex: The room was devoid of any furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间完全没有任何家具。

words.tr: phrase. 就业前景；工作前景；职业前途
words.ex: He wants to improve his job prospect by learning new skills.
words.ex_cn: 他想通过学习新技能来改善就业前景。
words.en: The possibility or likelihood of future success in a job or career.

words.tr:
v. 密谋；激起…的兴趣
n. 阴谋诡计；密谋策划
words.ex: They intrigue to take over the company.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋接管这家公司。
words.en: If something intrigues you, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

words.tr: adj. 感兴趣的；策划阴谋（intrigue 的过去式和过...； v. 引起……的兴趣；
words.ex: I was intrigued by the strange story.
words.ex_cn: 我对这个奇怪的故事感到感兴趣。
words.en: If you are intrigued by something, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

words.tr: n. 精细的装饰性雕塑
words.ex: The museum displays an intricate decorative sculpture from the 18th century.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆展出了一件18世纪的精细装饰性雕塑。
words.en: A complex and finely detailed ornamental carving or model.

words.ex: The company underwent radical changes to improve its performance.
words.ex_cn: 公司经历了根本性的变化以提高其表现。
words.en: Radical changes refer to fundamental or thorough changes that affect the core or essence of something.

words.ex: He ordered fried prawn for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚餐点了炸对虾。
words.en: A prawn is a small shellfish with a long tail and many legs, which can be eaten.

words.ex: This job is apt for someone who loves quiet work.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作适合喜欢安静工作的人。

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.ex: She wears a white apron while cooking.
words.ex_cn: 她做饭时穿着一件白色围裙。
words.en: An apron is a piece of clothing that you wear over the front of your normal clothes and tie round your waist, especially when you are cooking, in order to prevent your clothes from getting dirty.

words.ex: He lay supine on the couch, staring at the ceiling.
words.ex_cn: 他仰卧在沙发上，盯着天花板。
words.en: If you are supine, you are lying on your back. It can also describe someone who is passive or not willing to act.

words.tr: phrase. 倾向于做某事；容易做某事
words.ex: He is prone to make mistakes when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，他容易出错。
words.en: To have a natural tendency or inclination to do something.

words.ex: He is liable to make mistakes when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，容易出错。
words.en: If someone or something is liable to something, they are likely to experience it or do it.

words.tr: v. 努力争取某物；竭力追求某事
words.ex: He strives for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他努力争取更好的生活。

words.tr: v. 规定价格；强制定价
words.ex: The government can dictate price for essential medicines.
words.ex_cn: 政府可以规定基本药品的价格。
words.en: To set or determine the price of something, often with authority or control.

words.ex: The teacher gave a dictation of five sentences.
words.ex_cn: 老师进行了一次五句话的听写。
words.en: Dictation is the speaking or reading aloud of words for someone else to write down.

words.ex: The government will prosecute criminal activity to keep society safe.
words.ex_cn: 政府将起诉犯罪行为以维护社会安全。
words.en: To initiate legal proceedings against someone for committing a crime.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

words.ex: The government made a new regulation to control pollution.
words.ex_cn: 政府出台了一项新管理措施来控制污染。
words.en: A regulation is an official rule or order.

words.tr: adj. 有（法律）责任的；有…倾向的；
words.ex: He is liable for the damage caused by his car.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的车造成的损害负有责任。
words.en: If you are liable for something such as a debt or a duty, you are legally responsible for it. If something is liable to happen, it is very likely to happen.

words.tr:
n. 种类；类别；
v. 理清；解决；把…分类；拣选；
words.ex: This store sells all sorts of fruits.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售各种各样的水果。
words.en: A sort is a kind or category of things or people which have similar characteristics.

words.ex: He made a proposition to lower taxes.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了降低税收的建议。
words.en: A proposition is a statement or an idea that people can consider or discuss to decide whether it is true.

words.ex: He is stubborn and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很顽固，不肯改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is stubborn is determined to do what they want and is very unwilling to change their mind.

words.tr:
n. 珍宝；宝物；财富；
v. 珍惜；
words.ex: The old map showed where the treasure was buried.
words.ex_cn: 那张旧地图显示了珍宝埋藏的地方。
words.en: If you treasure something that you have, you keep it or care for it carefully because it gives you great pleasure and you think it is very special.

words.ex: The document is confidential and cannot be shared.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件是机密的，不能分享。
words.en: If you talk to someone in a confidential way, you talk to them quietly because what you are saying is secret or private.

words.ex: The trip is contingent on the weather.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行取决于天气情况。
words.en: A contingent event or situation depends on something else in order to happen or exist.

words.tr: v. 反思某事；仔细思考某事
words.ex: He sat quietly to reflect on his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他静静地坐着反思自己的错误。

words.ex: He sat by the window to ponder his future.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边深思自己的未来。
words.en: If you ponder something, you think about it carefully.

words.tr: v. 苦思冥想某事；反复思考某事
words.ex: He puzzled over the math problem for hours.
words.ex_cn: 他苦思冥想这道数学题好几个小时。

words.tr: v. 沉思；冥想；考虑；仔细计划
words.ex: He meditates every morning to feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冥想以保持平静。
words.en: To meditate means to spend time in quiet thought for religious purposes or relaxation.

words.ex: He was triumphant after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后非常成功。
words.en: If you are triumphant, you have achieved a great victory or success, often making you feel very proud and happy.

words.tr: phrase. 一种胜利感；一种成就感；一种 triumph 的感觉
words.ex: He felt a sense of triumph after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后感到一种胜利的喜悦。
words.en: A feeling of satisfaction and pride from achieving a difficult goal.

words.tr: n. 全面的监管；大规模的规制
words.ex: The government introduced full-scale regulation of the financial market.
words.ex_cn: 政府对金融市场实施了全面的监管。

words.tr: phrase. 交通规则；交通法规
words.ex: The police enforce traffic regulation to keep roads safe.
words.ex_cn: 警察执行交通法规以保障道路安全。
words.en: A rule or set of rules governing the movement of vehicles on a road.

words.ex: The violator must pay a fine.
words.ex_cn: 违规者必须支付罚款。
words.en: A violator is someone who breaks a law, rule, or agreement.

words.ex: He accepted liability for the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他承担了事故的责任。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a liability, you mean that they cause a lot of problems or embarrassment.

words.tr: phrase. 有可能做某事；易于发生某事
words.ex: He is liable to lose his temper when he's tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累的时候容易发脾气。
words.en: If someone is liable to do something, they are likely to do it because of their character or situation.

words.ex: He will sort out his books tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会整理好他的书。
words.en: To sort something out means to organize or arrange it, or to solve a problem or difficulty.

words.tr: phrase. 仔细检查并分类；整理（物品、文件等）
words.ex: He needs to sort through the papers on his desk.
words.ex_cn: 他需要整理桌上的文件。
words.en: To sort through something means to look at a number of things in a group and decide which ones you want or need, and which ones you do not.

words.ex: He propose to go to the park after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他提议午饭后去公园。
words.en: If you propose something, you suggest it as a plan or course of action.

words.ex: He made a proposal to improve the school lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了一个改善学校午餐的提案。
words.en: A proposal is a plan or suggestion, especially a formal one that is put forward for people to think about and decide upon.

words.tr: phrase. 价值主张；指企业向客户提供的产品或服务所能带来的独特价值或利益
words.ex: The company's value proposition is to provide high-quality products at affordable prices.
words.ex_cn: 该公司的价值主张是以合理的价格提供高质量的产品。
words.en: A value proposition refers to a promise of value to be delivered to a customer, a belief from the customer that value will be experienced from the use of a product or service.

words.tr: phrase. 固执的问题；难缠的问题
words.ex: He keeps asking the same stubborn question.
words.ex_cn: 他一直问同一个固执的问题。
words.en: A problem or issue that is difficult to resolve due to its complexity or resistance to change.

words.ex: He found a trove of old coins in the attic.
words.ex_cn: 他在阁楼上发现了一堆古钱币珍藏。
words.en: A trove is a valuable collection of objects.

words.ex: He amass wealth by working hard.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作积累财富。
words.en: If you amass something such as money or information, you gradually collect a large amount of it.

words.ex: The old attic was a treasure trove of vintage toys.
words.ex_cn: 那个旧阁楼是古董玩具的宝库。
words.en: A treasure trove is a collection of valuable or interesting things, especially one that has been hidden or discovered by chance.

words.ex: He amassed many books over ten years.
words.ex_cn: 他在十年间收集了大量书籍。
words.en: To gather together or accumulate (a large amount or number of valuable material or things) over a period of time.

words.tr: n. 机密事项；保密事务
words.ex: He kept all confidential matters secret.
words.ex_cn: 他将所有机密事项保密。

words.tr: v. 取决于某事；以某事为条件

words.ex: The class analyzed statistical data from the survey.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级分析了调查的统计数据。
words.en: Relating to the use of statistics or statistical methods.

words.ex: He will surrender when he sees the police.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到警察时，他会投降。
words.en: If you surrender, you stop fighting or resisting someone and agree that you have been beaten.

words.tr: adj. 残疾的； v. “disable”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The disabled man uses a wheelchair to move around.
words.ex_cn: 这位残疾人使用轮椅行动。
words.en: If someone is disabled, they are unable to use part of their body or mind properly, for example, because of injury or illness.

words.tr:
adj. 有生理缺陷的；残疾的；弱智的
v. 妨碍；使不利；“handicap”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The school made the playground accessible for handicapped children.
words.ex_cn: 学校让操场方便残障儿童使用。
words.en: A handicapped person has a physical or mental disability.

words.tr:
adj. 瘸的；跛的；站不住脚的；无说服力的
v. 变跛；瘸行
words.ex: The lame dog walked slowly on three legs.
words.ex_cn: 那只瘸狗用三条腿慢慢走。
words.en: If someone is lame, they are unable to walk properly because of damage to one or both of their legs. A lame excuse, explanation, etc. is one that is weak and difficult to believe.

words.ex: The painting is considered a masterpiece by art critics.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画被艺术评论家视为杰作。
words.en: A masterpiece is a work of art such as a painting, film, or book that is made with great skill and is considered to be the best work of a particular artist or writer.

words.tr: adj. 独自的；单独的；孤寂的；
words.ex: He lives in a solitary house far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 他住在离城镇很远的独自一人的房子里。
words.en: A solitary person or thing is the only one in a place.

words.tr: n. 统计测量；统计量测
words.ex: The teacher used statistical measurement to check student scores.
words.ex_cn: 老师使用统计测量来检查学生成绩。
words.en: A quantifiable value or metric derived from data analysis, used to summarize or describe a set of observations.

words.ex: The results were statistically significant.
words.ex_cn: 这些结果在统计上是显著的。
words.en: In a way that relates to statistics or the use of statistics.

words.ex: The trees surround the house.
words.ex_cn: 树木环绕着房子。
words.en: If something or someone is surrounded by something, that thing is situated all around them.

words.ex: They enclose the garden with a wooden fence.
words.ex_cn: 他们用木栅栏把花园围起来。
words.en: If you enclose something with a letter, you put it in the same envelope as the letter.

words.ex: The army besiege the small town.
words.ex_cn: 军队围攻这座小镇。
words.en: To surround a place with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender; to overwhelm someone with requests or complaints.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.tr:
n. 圆；圈；
v. 圈出；环绕；
words.ex: The child drew a circle with a pen.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用笔画了一个圆。
words.en: A circle is a shape consisting of a curved line completely surrounding an area. Every part of the line is the same distance from the centre of the area.

words.tr:
n. 坟墓；
adj. 严重的；
words.ex: They visited the grave of their grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了祖父的坟墓。
words.en: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried. When used as an adjective, grave means serious or solemn.

words.ex: He had to surrender individual properties to pay his debts.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不放弃个人财产来偿还债务。

words.ex: The detective tried to ascertain the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探试图查明真相。
words.en: If you ascertain the truth about something, you find out what it is, especially by making a deliberate effort to do so.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.tr: v. 慷慨陈词；高声朗诵
words.ex: He likes to declaim poetry in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在全班面前朗诵诗歌。
words.en: To declaim means to speak or recite something in a dramatic or impassioned way, often in public.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.tr:
v. 声称；索赔；
n. 声称；索要；
words.ex: He claims that he saw a UFO last night.
words.ex_cn: 他声称自己昨晚看到了不明飞行物。
words.en: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.

words.ex: The president will declare a holiday next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将在下周宣布放假。
words.en: If you declare something, you state it formally, publicly, or officially.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.ex: The novel is an acclaimed masterpiece praised by critics worldwide.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说是一部广受赞誉的杰作，受到全球评论家的称赞。
words.en: A work of art or literature that has received widespread praise and recognition.

words.tr: n. 单独监禁；隔离关押
words.ex: He was put in solitary confinement for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因为违反规定被关进单独监禁。
words.en: The isolation of a prisoner in a separate cell, with minimal human contact, as a form of punishment.

words.tr:
adj. 唯一的；
n. 鞋底；
words.ex: He is the sole owner of the shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是这家商店唯一的主人。
words.en: If you describe something as the sole thing of a particular kind, you mean that it is the only one of that kind.

words.ex: The workers showed solidarity during the strike.
words.ex_cn: 工人们在罢工期间表现出团结。
words.en: Solidarity is unity or agreement of feeling or action, especially among individuals with a common interest; mutual support within a group.

words.ex: The team showed unity in winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 团队在赢得比赛时展现了统一。
words.en: Unity refers to the state of being united or joined as a whole.

words.ex: He was under confinement for breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 他因违法而被拘禁。
words.en: Confinement is the state of being forced to stay in a place, especially a prison, or the time when a woman gives birth to a baby.

words.ex: She led a reclusive life in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 她在山中过着隐居的生活。
words.en: If you describe someone as reclusive, you mean that they live alone and do not like seeing or talking to other people.

words.tr: adj. 喜隐居的；爱孤独的；隐退性的
words.ex: She led a seclusive life in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 她在山中过着隐居的生活。
words.en: Preferring to be alone, away from the company of others.

words.w: Do not surrender your own feelings and intuitions
words.tr: 不要放弃你自己的情感和直觉
words.uk: dəʊ nɒt səˈrendə yɔːr əʊn ˈfiːlɪŋz ænd ˌɪntjuˈɪʃənz
words.us: doʊ nɑːt sərˈrendər jɔːr ɔːn ˈfiːlɪŋz ænd ˌɪntuˈɪʃənz
words.ex: Do not surrender your own feelings and intuitions, even when others disagree.
words.ex_cn: 即使别人不同意，也不要放弃你自己的情感和直觉。
